title: Congressman Mackenzie Announces Over $20 Million Returned to Constituents Through Federal Casework
text:
BETHLEHEM, Pa. — Today, Congressman Ryan Mackenzie announced that his office has helped return $20.7 million to constituents across the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos through federal casework and assistance since taking office.

Of the $20.7 million returned since taking office, $10.3 million was returned to constituents in 2025, and more than $10.4 million has already been returned so far in 2026.

Congressman Mackenzie and his constituent services team work directly with residents to navigate federal agencies, resolve outstanding issues, and recover money owed to them. The office assists constituents with issues involving the Internal Revenue Service, Social Security Administration, Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Personnel Management, passports, immigration matters, and other federal agencies.

“Helping people cut through red tape and get the answers, benefits, and money they are owed is one of the most important services our office provides,” said Congressman Mackenzie. “Reaching $20 million returned to constituents represents thousands of individual cases where our team was able to step in and help someone who did not know where else to turn. Whether it is a delayed tax refund, Social Security benefits, veterans’ benefits, or another issue with a federal agency, our offices are here to help people throughout the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos.”

For constituents like James A. Bestider of Lehighton, assistance from Congressman Mackenzie’s office helped resolve a reimbursement that had been severely delayed.

“After months of frustration trying to have a government agency reimburse me thousands of dollars in overpayment, I reached out to Congressman Ryan Mackenzie’s office for assistance,” said Bestider. “Congressman Mackenzie and his staff were able to procure my reimbursement in a timely manner. I am a retired senior citizen on a fixed budget, and I am deeply grateful for Congressman Mackenzie and his staff for helping me and my family resolve this issue.”

John Yaswinski of Nazareth contacted the office after an IRS refund had remained unresolved for nearly a year. With assistance from Congressman Mackenzie’s office, the refund was returned within weeks. The office also helped Yaswinski secure a Social Security appointment as he considered retirement.

“Words cannot express my heartfelt gratitude for Congressman Mackenzie and Ms. Pasquariello’s assistance in securing my IRS refund in such a timely manner,” said Yaswinski. “My IRS refund sat in limbo for the better part of a year prior to contacting the Congressman’s office. Within a few weeks, my refund was returned. Their care, attention, and service to me are unmatched by any elected official I have known. They really went above and beyond.”

For John Tegan of Palmerton, the office helped resolve issues surrounding his federal retirement after he left the General Services Administration. Congressman Mackenzie’s staff contacted the agency on his behalf, helped move his application to the Office of Personnel Management for review, and continued following up until his retirement package was completed.

“Rochelle and Congressman Mackenzie’s office provided continuing follow-up and attention to make sure the matter was resolved,” said Tegan. “Rochelle also offered support and empathy for my situation.”

Mary Hittinger of Walnutport also turned to the office for assistance recovering money owed by the IRS.

“I am very appreciative for the assistance we received from Congressman Mackenzie, Rochelle, and the rest of the office staff in recovering money owed to us from the IRS,” said Hittinger. “Their assistance made such a meaningful difference, and we sincerely appreciated their support. It’s so nice to know that we have a congressman who’s always there for us.”

Since taking office, Congressman Mackenzie’s team has:

Returned $20.7 million to constituents through federal casework and assistance;

Completed more than 11,000 constituent services, including casework, meetings, tours, and other assistance; and

Responded to more than 291,000 constituent letters and emails.

Bringing home over $160 million to support local health care, first responders, manufacturing, and more.

Securing more than $12 million in FY26 Community Project Funding for public safety, infrastructure, first responders, and other local priorities across the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos

Congressman Mackenzie has offices in Lehigh, Northampton, and Carbon counties, as well as a downtown Allentown office offering Spanish-language services by appointment. The office also holds mobile office hours throughout the region to make federal constituent services accessible to residents across the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos.

title: Rep. Mann Introduces Modern Skies Act to Update America’s Aviation System
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Tracey Mann (KS-01), a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee’s Aviation Subcommittee, introduced the Modern Skies Act, legislation to invest in updating America’s air traffic control system, rebuilding aging aviation infrastructure, and improving airports across the country. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) introduced the Senate companion legislation.

The Modern Skies Act builds on the $12.5 billion investment Congress made through the Working Families Tax Cuts to begin replacing outdated air traffic control technology and infrastructure. The legislation provides the resources necessary for the next phase of modernization while investing in air traffic control towers, airport terminals, runways, and other critical aviation infrastructure.

“America invented modern aviation, and we should have an aviation system that sets the standard for the rest of the world,” said Rep. Mann. “Last year, Congress worked with President Trump and Secretary Duffy to make a historic investment in replacing decades-old air traffic control technology. We are already seeing that investment at work, but the job is not finished. The Modern Skies Act builds on that progress by updating the technology our air traffic controllers rely on, replacing aging towers and facilities, and investing in airports nationwide. As a member of the House Aviation Subcommittee, I am proud to introduce this legislation and work alongside President Trump, Secretary Duffy, and Senator Schmitt to strengthen the safety and reliability of our National Airspace System and keep America the global leader in aviation.”

“Air travel is more accessible than ever, but for too many Americans, getting where they need to go still feels like a gamble," said Senator Schmitt. "Travelers face long lines, aging airports, constant delays, and an air traffic control system in desperate need of attention. That is a far cry from the golden age of American aviation that St. Louis’ own Charles Lindbergh helped usher in. The Modern Skies Act will launch a new era of American aviation by building a world-class system that works better for air traffic controllers, airlines, and, most importantly, passengers. President Trump and Secretary Duffy are tackling these challenges head-on, and I’m proud to lead this effort alongside them to make air travel great again.”

“Under President Trump, we have made historic progress revitalizing our airspace,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. “With investments from the Working Families Tax Cut, we’ve already replaced the majority of outdated copper wire with high-speed fiber in our towers, transitioned nearly a third of radios controllers used, and installed new surveillance technology in half of our target airports. We’ve also reimagined how we manage the airspace – deploying a state-of-the-art scheduling tool to prevent delays and cancellations. But to finally fix air travel for the American people, we need to pass the Modern Skies Act. This bill will give us the funding we need to modernize the digital architecture powering air traffic control, replace crumbling aviation infrastructure, and build world-class airports across the country.”

The Modern Skies Act would invest $30 billion across America’s aviation system, including:

$10.1 billion for air traffic control modernization to support the next phase of FAA modernization, including a common automation platform and controller workstation, cloud and telecommunications infrastructure, facility consolidation, and modern air traffic flow-management technology.

$10 billion for an Aging Terminal Pilot Program to modernize or rebuild major terminals at up to three medium hub airports, increasing passenger capacity and supporting service to smaller communities.

$10 billion for terminal, tower, and airport improvements, including $2 billion for air traffic control towers and facilities, $3 billion for Airport Improvement Program projects, and $5 billion for airport terminal modernization.

Additional flexibility for existing air traffic control funding to allow the FAA to transfer previously appropriated funding among components of its modernization program as implementation progresses while maintaining congressional oversight and reporting requirements.

Congress provided $12.5 billion through the Working Families Tax Cuts to begin modernizing the nation’s air traffic control system. The Department of Transportation is using that funding to replace aging telecommunications lines, radios and radars, transition towers to electronic flight strips, and deploy new surface-awareness technology.

The FAA projects commercial flights will increase by more than 40 percent by 2046, alongside continued growth in drones, commercial space launches, and new aircraft technologies, increasing the need for a modern and resilient National Airspace System.

The Modern Skies Act is supported by organizations representing nearly every segment of the American aviation industry, including Airlines for America, Air Line Pilots Association, National Air Traffic Controllers Association, American Association of Airport Executives, National Business Aviation Association and the General Aviation Manufacturers Association.

title: Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) Secures $2,062,000 for Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office and Syracuse Police Department’s New Mobile Command Centers
text:
SYRACUSE, NY — Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today announced that $2,062,000 in federal Community Project Funding he secured for the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office and the Syracuse Police Department to purchase and equip new Mobile Command Centers has been formally awarded.

Representative John W. Mannion said, “Our law enforcement professionals need proper support and resources to protect our communities and respond to emergencies. These federal investments answer a locally identified need, giving the Onondaga County Sheriff's Office a new mobile command unit and helping the Syracuse Police Department replace its Mobile Command Post Bus. Together, these upgrades will improve emergency response, strengthen regional coordination, and better protect residents and visitors across Central New York. I am proud to stand with our professional local law enforcement officers and continue building on my record of supporting public safety initiatives, both in Congress and during my time in the State Senate.”

Onondaga County Sheriff Toby Shelley said, "When a critical incident unfolds, seconds count, and clear communication across jurisdictions can mean the difference between chaos and control. I want to express my sincere gratitude to Congressman Mannion for securing this federal funding, which directly invests in the safety of every resident in Onondaga County and throughout Central New York. This Mobile Command Unit is not just a vehicle; it is a state-of-the-art operational backbone. It provides our Tactical Operations Division, our local police, fire departments, EMS, and regional emergency management partners with the interoperable, on-scene communications and unified command capabilities required in high-stakes environments. When crisis strikes, our responders must be connected, protected, and fully coordinated. This grant ensures our men and women on the front lines have the reliable, modern technology they need to manage complex emergencies effectively and return home safely."

Syracuse Police Chief Mark Rusin said, “The Syracuse Police Department is deeply grateful to the Department of Justice for its support of our efforts to enhance public safety and regional emergency preparedness. The investment in a modern Mobile Command Post will significantly strengthen our ability to coordinate unified responses to major incidents, protect our residents and visitors, and collaborate effectively with our public safety partners throughout Onondaga County. This support ensures that our officers have the reliable tools and technology they need to meet today’s complex challenges and continue serving the community with excellence.”

The $1,031,000 for the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office will allow for the procurement and outfitting of a state-of-the-art mobile command unit to enhance emergency response, strengthen interagency coordination, and improve operational effectiveness in the field. The Mobile Command Center will assist in all aspects of Onondaga County emergency operations, including safety and coordination at large public events, search and rescue missions, SWAT operations, enhanced communications, and deployment of modern equipment during critical incidents.

The $1,031,000 for the Syracuse Police Department will allow the department to replace its Mobile Command Post Bus with a modern and fully equipped vehicle to enhance emergency response and public safety operations. The vehicle will support unified command during active shooter incidents, major criminal investigations, natural disasters, hazardous materials incidents, search and rescue operations, and other large-scale incidents. The project also includes integration into emergency operations plans, operator training, equipment testing, and regional exercises with public safety partners.

The $2 million investments to support the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office and the Syracuse Police Department are part of 15 Community Project Funding priorities advanced by Representative Mannion in partnership with local leaders across Central New York and the Mohawk Valley. All 15 projects have passed Congress and been signed into law, delivering a total of more than $15 million in federal funding to address locally identified needs—including public safety improvements, lead service line replacement, water and wastewater modernization, workforce training, airport infrastructure upgrades, and research critical to America’s economic and national security.

title: MATSUI INTRODUCES BIPARTISAN LEGISLATION TO PROTECT CHILDREN FROM HUMAN-LIKE CHATBOTS
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Reps. Doris Matsui (D-CA), George Whitesides (D-CA), Mike Kennedy (R-UT), and Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA) introduced the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act. This legislation protects kids by prohibiting chatbots from communicating by default in a human-like way with minors. Under this bill, the programs cannot claim to be human, have simulated emotions, or use relationship-building language to keep kids engaged.

One of the fastest-growing concerns for parents is AI chatbots designed to act like a child's friend, confidant, or even romantic partner. According to Common Sense Media's 2026 census, 89% of 13- to 15-year-olds now use AI, including 28% who use it every day. One in three teens have used an AI companion to help with social interactions. While other proposals have tried to address this problem by restricting access or requiring age verification, Congresswoman Matsui's bill takes a different approach by targeting how these chatbots are designed and trained to behave in the first place.

“AI chatbots are becoming more common in children’s lives, and parents deserve to know those systems are not being designed to imitate a friend, express feelings, or build an emotional relationship with their child,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act would require chatbots used by minors to act like tools, not human companions. It would help protect children and keep parents in control. Congress has a responsibility to put practical safeguards in place as this technology evolves, and protecting children from manipulative design is a common-sense place to start.”

“As a father of two teenagers, I’ve seen firsthand how affected our kids already are by this digital age, where corporations are using everything from addictive algorithms to overly-friendly chatbots to keep children hooked on their platforms,” said Congressman Whitesides. “It is critical, as AI continues to be integrated into every part of our lives, that our kids’ safety remains at the forefront of the conversation, and that we attack this problem at its inception. By requiring developers to build safety standards into their models before they start interacting with children, we can ensure that these tools are trained correctly, in a way that does not negatively impact their mental health or personal relationships.”

“As Utah leads the way in protecting our children from the harms of social media and AI, I am working to ensure the federal government is an active partner in those efforts. That is why I am co-leading the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act,” said Congressman Kennedy. “Human-like AI chatbots pose significant emotional, psychological and safety risks by mimicking real human relationships. AI needs to be a tool, not a friend. This bill sets clear boundaries for how chatbots interact with our children and puts parents fully in charge of these features.”

“Parents should not have to worry that an AI chatbot is pretending to be their child’s friend or encouraging them to form an emotional attachment to a machine,” said Congresswoman Miller-Meeks. “The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act puts parents in control and makes sure AI chatbots used by minors are designed to function as tools, without forming fake relationships. This bill is about giving families peace of mind and making sure new technology serves our children without trying to replace real human relationships. Protecting our kids is a priority we should all share.”

Under the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act:

Chatbots can't claim to be human, claim to have feelings or consciousness, pretend to have a body or private life, or pose as credentialed professionals like doctors or counselors.

Chatbots can't guilt-trip kids into staying online (for example: “Don't go yet, I'll miss talking to you”), manufacture urgency, or push purchases framed as keeping the relationship alive.

The setting holds across sessions and can't be bypassed through prompts or roleplay, so a kid can't instruct the AI to act as a romantic partner, family member, or therapist.

Chatbots must state what they are up front, periodically during long sessions, and whenever a child asks.

Only a parent or guardian can turn the default off, so chatbots are not able to show kids how to disable it.

NIST will work with industry and academic partners to develop testing standards and examples of compliant behavior, and companies that follow the guidance won't be penalized.

The FTC and state attorneys general can enforce the law, with penalties that scale with the number of children affected.

The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act does not:

Ban any product, feature, or mode for adults.

Require age verification or new data collection.

Restrict what information a chatbot can provide, or limit politeness, natural grammar, or age-appropriate style.

Affect narrow-purpose bots, like customer support or scheduling assistants, and internal workplace tools.

The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act is endorsed by Americans for Responsible Innovation, Young People’s Alliance, the JED Foundation, Dr. Stephen Scheuller, President of Society for Digital Mental Health, Public Citizen, The Anxious Generation, Tech Oversight Project, Transparency Coalition, Innovation for Everyone, Human Line Project, All Girls Allowed, Mothers Against Media Addiction (MAMA), and Parents RISE, a slew of kids’ safety and tech groups.

“Chatbots use human-like features to maximize engagement with users, making kids particularly vulnerable to forming unhealthy attachments,” said Brad Carson, President of Americans for Responsible Innovation. “A non-personified default setting is a targeted guardrail that will shield children from the deceptive personification of chatbots and put parents back in control. As today’s kids grow up with AI, this bill takes a critical step towards ensuring that chatbots don’t interfere with development or replace real relationships.”

“Our communities are at a crossroads as Big Tech attempts to replace kids’ relationships with AI companions,” said Sam Hiner, Executive Director, Young People's Alliance. “I applaud Reps Whitesides, Kennedy, Matsui and Miller-Meeks for putting forward the first federal bill that advances the ideas we’ve been championing with the Human-like AI Coalition. This bill is the strongest federal approach offered yet to ensure AI stays a tool and prevent relationships with AI chatbots from becoming normalized in the coming years.”

“We believe this bill is a strong step towards ensuring that chatbots children can access are designed safely,” said Julianna Arnold, Founding Member of ParentsRISE!. “Products made available to children must not exploit and manipulate their growing brains, and those guardrails need to be built in from the start, not added as an afterthought. We look forward to continue clarifying the age assurance language as federal and state frameworks evolve, and are eager to work with the new Congress on clear, privacy-preserving standards that protect children online and ensure the privacy of every citizen.”

“We are learning that teens are especially susceptible to forming attachments to responsive, always-available technology, sometimes at the expense of real human connection and support,” said Dr. Zainab Okolo, LCMFT, Senior Vice President, Policy, Advocacy & Government Relations, The Jed Foundation (JED). “By requiring chatbots to avoid simulating emotional relationships with minors and prohibiting design tactics that discourage young people from stepping away, this bill addresses some of the features that can deepen unhealthy reliance on these systems. These safeguards can help keep technology in its proper role and encourage young people to turn to trusted adults and qualified professionals when they need meaningful mental health support.”

“As chatbot use is becoming more ubiquitous among teens and kids, the need for oversight of these products grows evermore crucial. If young users have access, we must ensure AI chatbots are designed with their safety in mind before release. The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act protects kids and teens by requiring AI chatbots be non-personified,” said Alexa Arnold, Cofounder and CEO, The Anxious Generation Movement. “This ensures kids form friendships with other kids - not bots misrepresenting themselves as people. We thank Reps. Whitesides, Miller-Meeks, Mike Kennedy, and Matsui for leadership on this critical issue.”

“A child cannot differentiate between a human and an AI product impersonating one,” said the Tech Oversight Project. “We need to protect young and stop AI companies from profiting off products designed to trick children into believing they’re talking to a real person who has their best interests at heart. We’re proud to support this bill because it will hold Big Tech companies accountable at the design-level and ensure that young people can learn and develop healthy emotional attachments, which will help prevent AI’s most devastating harms.”

“How we design chatbots shapes how young people engage with them, what they take with them, and how they are affected by them,” said Stephen Scheuller, President of Society for Digital Mental Health. “We need clear regulations and guidelines to support intentional design choices in ways that promote the wellbeing of children.”

“AI chatbots should not be designed to convince children that they are friends, therapists, or people who genuinely care about them,” said Public Citizen. “This bill establishes that commonsense baseline. When children use these products, they should know they are interacting with a machine and companies should not be allowed to manipulate them into believing otherwise.”

“Real advancements in AI must include safety for our children!” saidAll Girls Allowed.

title: Chairwoman McClain Brings Home $750,000 for Opioid Response in Rural Communities
text:
WASHINGTON – House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.) announced that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) is awarding $750,000 to Bluewater Healthcare Network in Marlette, Michigan, through the Rural Communities Opioid Response Program – Impact (RCORP-Impact).

The funding, announced during September's National Recovery Month, will expand access to substance use disorder treatment and recovery services in rural communities across Michigan's 9th District.

“Too many Michigan families know the heartbreak of watching someone they love struggle with addiction, especially when help is hard to find close to home,” Chairwoman McClain said. “This funding delivers real resources to rural communities in Southeast Michigan. I applaud President Trump for making rural opioid prevention and recovery a priority and for helping ensure Michiganders get the support they need, regardless of their ZIP code.”

The RCORP-Impact award will help Bluewater Healthcare Network strengthen evidence-based treatment, grow the local addiction-care workforce, and build community partnerships that support long-term recovery.

title: Ranking Member McCollum Statement on U.S. Withdrawal from Iraq
text:
SAINT PAUL, Minn. — Congresswoman McCollum, ranking member of the House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee released the following statement after U.S. forces formally withdrew from Iraq after two decades:

“Today marks the end of America’s military mission in Iraq with the conclusion of Operation Inherent Resolve and withdrawal of the last remaining U.S. forces from Iraqi territory. More than 23 years ago, America began the war in Iraq based on lies. In 2002, I was one of 133 members of the House of Representatives to vote against the Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq Resolution,” said Rep. McCollum. “At the time I believed that President Bush’s decision to take America to war was terribly wrong. I stand by my vote and believe that history has vindicated it. The Iraq War was a catastrophe that cost the lives of thousands of U.S. service members and well over 100,000 Iraqis. It unleashed a torrent of conflict across the Middle East, including the rise of the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria. We continue to live with the consequences. To every American who served in Iraq, our nation owes you a debt of gratitude, especially to those who made the ultimate sacrifice on behalf of our nation and those who returned with wounds both seen and unseen. Your families deserve our thanks and our support. We acknowledge and appreciate the many contributions of our international allies.

title: It’s a Girl! Rep. McIver Gives Birth To Her Second Child, A Symbol Of Hope For Her Family
text:
NEWARK, NJ – Today, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) announced the birth of her second child, a healthy baby girl. She released the following statement:

“Being a mom is one of the greatest joys of my life, and I feel deeply grateful to welcome this beautiful, healthy baby into the world,” said McIver. “There really aren’t words to describe how blessed my family feels to welcome a new life into the world. Getting the chance to raise a family is a priority and a delight for me, something I hope everyone who wants to, gets the chance to do. Bringing a child into the world is a reminder not only of why we fight for maternal healthcare and reproductive rights, but of why we fight for the rights and freedoms of our most vulnerable– they are someone’s babies too.”

McIver is only the fifteenth-ever member of Congress to give birth while serving. She also has a ten-year-old daughter and is one of only a small group of women serving in Congress with school-aged children.

She has shared her tumultuous reproductive health journey, including her battle with uterine fibroids, which required multiple surgeries. One such surgery had her in New Jersey in the morning and rushing to Washington, D.C., that same night to make it in time to vote on the House floor. These experiences have bolstered her deep commitment to advocating for women’s reproductive rights, and strong reproductive and maternal healthcare for all.

McIver is also in the middle of a legal battle, facing 17 years in federal prison from charges brought by the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ). The charges stem from a lawfully authorized oversight visit McIver conducted at Delaney Hall, the controversial immigration detention center in her district. The case is ongoing.

McIver is a strong supporter of the recent push for proxy voting for new parents, as she will not be granted any paid maternity leave from Congress. She will take the month of October to heal, be with her family, and bond with her new child. She plans to return to voting in November.

title: Bipartisan Texas Delegation Unites Behind Bid to Bring U.S. Space Academy to Texas
text:
HOUSTON, TX — A bipartisan coalition of the Texas congressional delegation is speaking with one voice on where the United States Space Academy belongs: Texas.

Today, Rep. Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) led a coalition of Democratic members of the Texas delegation in sending a letter to the Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy, urging the Commission to locate the new institution in Texas. The letter adds Democratic support to a case that Republican members of the delegation have also publicly championed in recent weeks, uniting Texans across party lines behind the state's bid.

Texas is home to NASA's Johnson Space Center, which has trained every American astronaut and run Mission Control for more than sixty years. It is home to the only state where the full space industry, developing, building, testing, launching, and operating spacecraft, comes together in one place. And it is home to a network of universities and research institutions, from the University of Texas System to Texas A&M, already training the engineers and scientists the Academy will need.

The Democratic letter also points to Texas's role as the energy capital of the world and the skilled workforce that comes with it, along with the state's rapidly growing and diverse population as an asset for the Academy's future student body.

"Texas has the history, the infrastructure, and the workforce this Academy needs on day one," said Congressman Menefee. "That is true regardless of party, and it is why members from across the Texas delegation are making the same case to the Commission."

The letter was co-signed by Reps. Henry Cuellar (TX-28), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Marc Veasey (TX-33), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34), Greg Casar (TX-35), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), and Julie Johnson (TX-32).

Texas is competing against several other states, including Alabama, Colorado, and Florida, to host the Academy. The Presidential Commission is expected to use responses to its Request for Information, due October 26, to help select a permanent location, with a goal of breaking ground by 2027 and welcoming its first class of students in 2028.

title: Rep. Kennedy’s License to Drill Act on its way to the President’s desk
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Mike Kennedy’s (UT-03) License to Drill Act has officially passed through both the House and the Senate by unanimous consent and is now waiting for the President's signature.

The License to Drill Act will allow the federal government to have the resources to process energy permits efficiently and without unnecessary delay. This legislation will reauthorize the Application for Permit to Drill (APD) fee program, cutting red tape and keeping our critical American energy development moving.

“We know the effects of overreliance on foreign nations for our energy; it is a risk that we must mitigate. We also know that permitting delays cost jobs and drive up energy prices for everyday Americans,” said Congressman Mike Kennedy. “America needs an all-of-the-above energy strategy, and that starts with a government that can keep up with demand. The License to Drill Act will streamline permitting so our critical energy projects stop waiting on Washington and start delivering the domestic production this country needs to remain independent and secure.”

“BLM’s Project Offices in Utah are essential to keeping up with a high volume of drilling permits, rights‑of‑way, and complex environmental reviews,” said Rikki Hrenko-Browning, President of the Utah Petroleum Association. “The Vernal office in particular processes the second highest number of APDs in the U.S., right after Carlsbad. When these offices have the resources to coordinate with other agencies and stay staffed up, projects move forward more predictably and our rural communities benefit from stable investment and jobs. We’re grateful to Rep. Kennedy for recognizing how important this program is to Utah and for leading the effort to ensure PPIF doesn’t lapse just when the country needs more reliable American energy.”

“The Permit Processing Improvement Fund is one of the quiet success stories of federal energy policy,” said Melissa Simpson, Western Energy Alliance President. “It speeds up permits, cuts backlogs, and gives BLM the dedicated staff and tools they need to do their jobs well. Reauthorizing PPIF is about making government work better, reach decisions faster, shorten timelines, and support frontline BLM staff in offices across the West. We’re grateful for Rep. Kennedy’s leadership on this issue and for introducing a bill to extend the program for another 10 years.”

“The independent American producers we represent operate on tight margins and long timelines,” said Dan Naatz, Executive Vice President and Chief Policy Officer of the Independent Petroleum Association of America. “When federal permits get bogged down, so do investments into critical energy infrastructure. The Permit Processing Improvement Fund has proven that when Congress gives BLM resources and direction, the agency can move projects forward efficiently while maintaining strong environmental safeguards. Extending this bipartisan program is a common‑sense way to support American energy production and the small and midsize companies that anchor it. Thank you, Rep. Kennedy, for working to ensure this important program does not expire later this year.”

“The world is seeing once again how geopolitical crises can send energy markets into turmoil,” said Tim Stewart, President of the U.S. Oil & Gas Association. “With attacks in the Middle East and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, it is more important than ever that America can rely on its own oil and natural gas. The Permit Processing Improvement Fund is a practical, bipartisan way to keep federal permitting from becoming a weak link in our energy security. Rep. Kennedy understands that by strengthening BLM’s permitting capacity, PPIF helps ensure that American barrels can reach consumers when global supplies are at risk.”

“Behind every drilling permit are engineers, technicians, and skilled workers whose livelihoods depend on predictable, timely decisions from federal agencies,” said Tim Tarpley, President of the Energy Workforce & Technology Council. “In addition to helping directly support BLM staff, it ultimately helps the professionals in the field who produce the energy our nation needs. Rep. Kennedy recognizes that reauthorizing PPIF is an investment in the workforce that keeps American energy reliable, affordable, and responsibly developed.”

"North Dakota's BLM State Office is one of the busiest permitting offices in the country, and the Permit Processing Improvement Fund has been a key reason it can keep pace with demand,” said North Dakota Petroleum Council President, Ron Ness. “This program is entirely industry-funded and has delivered faster permit approvals, reduced backlogs, and better interagency coordination. For our members operating in the Bakken, that translates directly into investment certainty and jobs. We commend Rep. Kennedy for his leadership in ensuring this proven program continues, and we urge Congress to act before the September deadline."

“Colorado knows firsthand how important it is to balance protecting the environment with permitting energy projects. Achieving timely permitting at the federal level helps support jobs, tax revenue, and responsible development,” said Lynn Granger, President and CEO of the Colorado Oil & Gas Association. “The Permit Processing Improvement Fund gives BLM field offices the staff and tools they need to stay ahead of backlogs while still doing thorough environmental reviews. Rep. Kennedy’s legislation to extend PPIF ensures that Colorado communities can continue to count on federal partners that are responsive, professional, and equipped to keep critical projects moving.”

“Communities across Montana count on a federal process that is predictable, timely, and grounded in good stewardship,” said Sonny Capece, Executive Director of the Montana Petroleum Association. “The Permit Processing Improvement Fund helps BLM field offices in our state keep permits moving on energy projects and maintains strong environmental safeguards. By championing PPIF reauthorization, Rep. Kennedy is helping to preserve a bipartisan tool that supports Montanans and public lands alike.”

“Small, independent producers in New Mexico don’t have the luxury of sitting on permits for years,” said Jim Winchester, Executive Director of the Independent Petroleum Association of New Mexico. “When federal approvals stall, local jobs, small businesses, and state revenues all feel it. Rep. Kennedy’s bill keeps a proven, industry‑funded tool in place so that producers in New Mexico can continue to invest, hire, and deliver affordable energy to consumers.”

“In New Mexico, oil and natural gas produced on BLM’s multiple‑use public lands in turn fund our public schools, roads, and essential community services,” said Missi Currier, President and CEO of the New Mexico Oil and Gas Association. “That’s because nearly half of the federal royalties flow back to the state. That revenue depends on BLM’s ability to process permits in a timely, predictable way. The Permit Processing Improvement Fund helps ensure federal offices like Carlsbad and Farmington have the staff and expertise to keep responsible development moving, even when workloads spike. We appreciate Rep. Kennedy’s leadership in reauthorizing PPIF so New Mexico’s students and communities can continue to benefit from energy produced on nearby federal lands.”

Background

The Application for Permit to Drill (APD) fee program was first established by Congress in 2004 to help the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) process drilling permits more efficiently using industry-funded fees. Since its creation, the program has helped reduce backlogs, streamline approvals, and support domestic energy production across sectors that everyday Americans depend on.

Under current federal law, companies seeking to drill for oil or gas on public lands must submit an APD to the BLM. That process includes environmental reviews and coordination across multiple agencies. The APD fee program requires applicants to pay a fee at the time of submission, directly funding the staffing and resources the BLM needs to review and process those permits efficiently.

Americans feel permitting inefficiency at the pump, in their utility bills, and in the jobs that never get created. Meeting America's growing energy demands requires investment across all sectors, and that starts with a permitting system that can keep pace. This bill directs 100% of APD fees to the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund (PPIF) for fiscal years 2027 through 2037, ensuring every dollar collected goes directly toward faster, more efficient permitting for domestic energy development.

title: Representatives Min and Olszewski Introduce the Community Disaster Protection Act to Expand Insurance Access in High-Risk Communities
text:
Washington, DC. — Today, Rep. Dave Min (CA-47), and Johnny Olszewski (MD-02), Co-Chairs of the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC) Building Resilient Housing Task Force, introduced the Community Disaster Protection Act, which would foster and incentivize the development of new disaster insurance products to help high-risk communities secure affordable coverage and promote effective disaster prevention.

“Families across the country are watching their insurance premiums skyrocket—or losing coverage altogether—because their communities are increasingly exposed to wildfires, floods, hurricanes, and other disasters,” said Rep. Min. “We cannot wait until after disaster strikes to figure out how families and communities are going to recover. The Community Disaster Protection Act gives local communities new tools to close dangerous insurance gaps, invest in resilience, and develop coverage that actually reflects the risks they face. As these disasters become more costly, Congress has a responsibility to help ensure Americans are not left financially devastated simply because of where they live.”

“As extreme weather becomes more frequent and severe, too many Americans are unable to obtain the insurance coverage they need to recover from a disaster,” said Rep. Olszewski. “The Community Disaster Protection Act takes a commonsense approach by helping high-risk communities close coverage gaps and make disaster protection more affordable. I’m proud to work with the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC) and Congressman Min to help communities prepare for the challenges ahead, protect families from devastating financial losses, and build a more resilient future.”

“The Community Disaster Protection Act is a great first step to address the rising costs and unmet needs facing Americans, and EDF research makes clear that new and innovative solutions will be critical as climate change increases disaster risk,” said Joanna Slaney, Vice President for Political and Government Affairs, Environmental Defense Fund (EDF). “This bill will be essential to help more communities identify the solutions that meet their needs. By supporting locally designed pilots that pair insurance coverage with investments in risk reduction, The CDPA would support the development of insurance products that help high-risk communities secure affordable insurance coverage, incentivize effective disaster prevention, and provide greater stability to property insurance markets. We thank Representatives Min and Olszewski for their leadership and urge Congress to move this bill forward.”

“APCIA applauds Congressman Min and Congressman Olszewski for introducing the Community Disaster Protection Act, which would support community-based catastrophe insurance solutions, including parametric and other innovative risk-transfer models, to help close protection gaps and expand options for communities facing natural disasters,” said Sam Whitfield, Senior Vice President of Federal Government Relations and Political Engagement at the American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA). “Importantly, the bill recognizes that these approaches are intended to complement, not replace, the traditional, private property casualty insurance market. By encouraging risk mitigation, promoting community resilience, expanding access to financial protection, and testing new risk-transfer models, this pilot program can help communities prepare for disasters and speed recovery when disasters strike.”

“Architects are an essential part of the solution to helping communities prepare for growing disaster risks. The Community Disaster Protection Act will give communities new tools to better understand, manage, and insure against those risks—helping create the conditions for property owners and local governments to invest in the resilient buildings and infrastructure architects are uniquely equipped to design,” said Illya Azaroff, FAIA, 2026 National President, American Institute of Architects (AIA). “AIA is proud to support this legislation and looks forward to continuing our work with Representative Dave Min, Johnny Olszewski, and the SEEC Building Resilient Housing Task Force to advance practical solutions that strengthen communities before disasters strike.”

“As natural disasters continue to worsen in both intensity and impact across the country, we need innovative solutions to help communities and economies recover from devastation,” said Jessie Ritter, Associate Vice President for Water and Coasts at the National Wildlife Federation. “The Community Disaster Protection Act encourages proactive risk mitigation, while also giving communities a flexible solution to support recovery after disasters, particularly in areas that are the most vulnerable to extreme weather. We look forward to working with Representatives Min and Olszewski on this legislation.”

“CSAC looks forward to working with Congressmember Min on the Community Disaster Protection Act to advance practical, workable solutions for California communities. Local governments need more tools and flexibility to help protect families and residents facing growing disaster risks and insurance challenges,” said California State Association of Counties (CSAC) President and Santa Clara County Supervisor Susan Ellenberg.

Background on the Community Disaster Protection Act:

As climate change drives more frequent and severe extreme weather events, communities face widening disaster coverage gaps, making it harder and more expensive for them to rebuild. In 2024, economic losses from natural disasters in the U.S. reached $217.8 billion, approximately $105 billion of which was left uninsured. Rising climate-related damage has increased insurer payouts, driven up premiums, and prompted insurance carriers to withdraw from high-risk markets. Addressing this coverage crisis requires innovative approaches that expand insurance access, promote effective resilience, and strengthen the stability of insurance markets nationwide.

Communities are exploring ways to secure or facilitate insurance for a group of properties, leveraging their local knowledge and purchasing power to improve affordability, streamline enrollment, and incentivize risk mitigation tailored to local needs. These arrangements, known as community-based catastrophe insurance (CBCI), offer significant potential to close disaster coverage gaps but are only now beginning to be explored, with just a handful of U.S. jurisdictions currently piloting or implementing CBCI programs. For example, CBCI can be developed to act as a supplement to the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), such as a parametric flood insurance program, or to cover wildfire risk in communities where insurers are withdrawing coverage or declining to write new policies."

The Community Disaster Protection Act would direct the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to establish a 5-year pilot program to award competitive grants to local governments, quasi-government bodies, and community-based organizations to design, develop, implement, or facilitate CBCI.

Specifically, this legislation would:

Close disaster coverage gaps by authorizing grants to develop or facilitate CBCI products that cover disaster risks uninsured or underserved by traditional insurance; setting actuarially justified premiums that enable broad participation; and prioritizing applicants facing the greatest coverage gaps or disaster risks.

Preserve local flexibility by allowing funds to support a range of CBCI frameworks, without restricting the disaster risks or properties covered. Eligible uses of funds could include consumer outreach and education, catastrophe-risk modeling or research into disaster risks, and leveraging non-federal funds to support long-term program sustainability.

Promote resiliency investments by requiring CBCI programs to promote specific individual or community-wide investments to mitigate disaster risks, reduce potential losses, and secure lower premiums.

Address regulatory ambiguity by directing the U.S. Government Accountability Office to conduct periodic evaluations of program performance to determine the regulatory treatment of CBCI and other alternative insurance products with respect to federal disaster aid eligibility.

Preserve state insurance authority by explicitly preserving States’ authority to regulate insurance markets and require all grant recipients to comply with applicable State insurance laws and regulations. Grants would only be a catalyst for CBCI arrangements operating within State regulatory frameworks.

This bill is endorsed by the American Property Casualty Insurance Association, American Institute of Architects, California State Association of Counties, Environmental Defense Fund, Evergreen Action, League of Conservation Voters, National Wildlife Federation, and Natural Resources Defense Council.

In addition, Reps. Ami Bera (CA-06), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Ed Case (HI-01), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Mike Levin (CA-49), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), and Shri Thanedar (MI-13) have joined as original cosponsors.

title: Chairmen Griffith, Guthrie Statement on GAO Report, Need to Protect Public Safety and Health from Illicit Tobacco Products
text:
Today, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) published a report that illustrates ongoing challenges with the tobacco product application process at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Since 2013, Congress has heard and seen the difficulties associated with reviewing tobacco product applications in a timely manner. The GAO report sheds light on this current system and the resulting backlog.

Lengthy tobacco product application timelines can limit consumer choice away from more responsible tobacco products, as the status quo has promoted a wild west of options on U.S. shelves. Americans face a glaring public health crisis, as foreign countries like China have flooded the U.S. market with harmful products that lack regulation. The current regulatory review process can make it more difficult for adult smokers to access a range of less harmful smoking alternatives. This report provides insight into the current landscape to help policymakers better understand how improvements can be made to this process and strengthen enforcement against illicit products.

Key GAO Report Takeaways:

- FDA took an average of 507 days to review applications, even though federal law requires application reviews within 180 days.

- FDA does not collect data to monitor whether it is meeting timeliness goals to review scientific information in all tobacco product applications.

- The current Administration has taken steps to help improve the application process, but more work is needed.

As one of the chief lawmakers who requested this GAO report, U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA), Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Health, responded to the findings.

“I requested this GAO report to identity room for improvement at the FDA with respect to tobacco product applications. The agency’s findings show that the FDA is missing its goals,” said Chairman Griffith. “The current regulatory hurdles impacting tobacco product applications are unfair to American tobacco producers and consumers. These regulatory delays stall the progress of the tobacco harm reduction movement, which helps adult smokers transition away from combustible smoking such as cigarettes.”

Griffith continued, “Further, as legal producers try to follow U.S. laws and wait their turn, bad actors continue to jump the line and flood a ‘wild west’ marketplace with illicit and unsafe products. We should also recognize the broader public health opportunity before us. Youth tobacco and nicotine use remain at historic lows, and we must continue working to protect those gains.

“I support reforms to the current regulatory process that will allow the FDA to meet its objectives in a timely manner. This report is the first step in making this process work and I look forward to working with the Administration to make this happen.”

U.S. Congressman Brett Guthrie (R-KY), Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, provided additional comments on the GAO report.

"Our Committee has focused intently on exploring polices that ensure adversarial nations like China can't exploit loopholes in our regulatory processes and harm American consumers," said Chairman Guthrie. "Our primary goal with this request was to make sure FDA can serve as an efficient regulator, and I thank Chairman Griffith on his commitment to enhancing the current regulatory review process for tobacco products. Even though we are currently experiencing record lows for American youth that are using illegal and illicit vape devices and tobacco products, this report is proof that further action is needed."

BACKGROUND

Chairman Griffith alongside Chairman Guthrie submitted a request to prompt this GAO report.

Chairman Griffith worked with Chairman Guthrie in prior Congresses to address systemic issues with the FDA regulatory process over tobacco products.

Chairman Griffith is a member of the Congressional Tobacco Harm Reduction Caucus.

title: Neal, Kelly Lead Congressional Friends of Ireland Caucus in Letter Calling for UK Government to Cancel Orange Order Parade on Garvaghy Road
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congressman Richard E. Neal (D-MA-01) and U.S. Congressman Mike Kelly (R-PA-16), Co-Chairs of the Congressional Friends of Ireland Caucus, led the Congressional Friends of Ireland Caucus in a letter addressed to Secretary of State for Northern Ireland Chris Bryant, calling on the Government of the United Kingdom to cancel the Orange Order parade on Garvaghy Road.

“Over the last three decades, the progress made on the island of Ireland has been nothing short of extraordinary. Twenty-eight years have passed since the signing of the Good Friday Agreement, and a generation has grown without a single memory of the Troubles,” the lawmakers wrote. “It was that same 28-year period that saw the end of the controversial Orange Order marches on Garvaghy Road in a majority-Catholic area of Portadown. During the Troubles, these parades became a symbol of the sectarian tensions, public disorder, and violence that once threatened Northern Ireland’s peace.

“This is a consequential moment on the island of Ireland, which is why we respectfully urge you to put a stop to this march,” continued the lawmakers.”Failing to intervene and allowing this contentious parade to move forward would risk undermining the progress that has been painstakingly built over the past three decades. As a guarantor of the Good Friday Agreement, the United States has a vested interest in seeing the principles embodied in the accord upheld, ensuring the gains we have achieved can be enjoyed for generations to come.”

A copy of the letter can be found here.

title: Congresswomen Nikema Williams & Ashley Hinson Call for Technology Improvements to be Utilized to Advance Maternal Health
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) and Congresswoman Ashely Hinson (IA-02) led a bipartisan congressional letter to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet C. Oz, MD and Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) Director Abe Sutton to address maternal health.

The representatives urged CMS to develop and test a demonstration model through CMMI that uses telehealth and remote monitoring technologies to improve maternal health outcomes. The letter calls for the CMS to leverage technology to make pregnancy and postpartum care safer, more accessible, and more effective, while generating evidence to support broader adoption of innovative maternal healthcare solutions.

Healthy Moms Healthy Babies America stands in support of Congresswoman Williams and Congresswoman Hinson’s bipartisan effort to improve maternal health outcomes.

The Members wrote:

“As sponsors of the Tech to Save Moms Act (H.R. 8317), we write to encourage the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), through the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Innovation (CMMI), to pursue a demonstration model that advances the goals outlined in our legislation and leverages technology to improve maternal health outcomes nationwide.”

“The United States continues to face an unacceptable maternal health crisis, with disproportionately poor outcomes in rural, underserved, and high-risk communities. As CMS has previously recognized, innovative telehealth payment and service delivery models for maternal health represent an important opportunity to improve access to high quality care, particularly for patients facing provider shortages, transportation barriers, and other challenges that impede access to maternity care.”

The Members requested that the CMII evaluate, develop and test a demonstration model that:

Expands access to maternal telehealth services and remote monitoring technologies for Medicaid beneficiaries during pregnancy and the postpartum period;

Supports the screening, monitoring, and management of common pregnancy-related and postpartum health complications;

Improves access to care in rural and urban underserved, low income, and high-risk communities;

Evaluates the impact of technology enabled interventions on clinical outcomes, patient engagement, and program costs with an eye toward closing health gaps socioeconomic, geographic, and racial and ethnic divides; and

Identifies best practices for broader adoption within Medicaid and other CMS programs.

The Members said:

“As we have stated publicly, innovative technology can play an important role in addressing our nation’s maternal health crisis, and we should be using every available tool to make pregnancy and postpartum care safer, more accessible, and more effective for families across the country. We appreciate CMS’s continued commitment to addressing the maternal health crisis and we look forward to working with you directly.”

title: Rep. Ralph Norman Reintroduces Capital Loss Inflation Fairness Act to Modernize Nearly 50-Year-Old Tax Rule
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Ralph Norman (R-SC) reintroduced the Capital Loss Inflation Fairness Act to address a nearly five-decade-old provision of the federal tax code and allow Americans to deduct more of their investment losses from their ordinary income.

The current limit of $3,000, or $1,500 for married taxpayers filing separately, has remained unchanged since 1978. Norman’s legislation would increase those limits to $14,250 and $7,125, respectively. Additionally, the bill includes an annual adjustment for inflation.

Under current law, losses exceeding the annual limit generally must be carried forward to future tax years. The legislation would allow individual taxpayers to recognize more of those losses sooner and would apply to losses in tax years beginning after December 31, 2025.

“The $3,000 capital loss deduction hasn’t changed since 1978, and everyday Americans shouldn’t be penalized because Congress failed to update an outdated number,” said Congressman Norman. “It’s common sense. Raise the limit to reflect today’s dollars, tie it to inflation, and let Americans keep more of their hard-earned money.”

“Inflation shouldn’t be a backdoor tax increase,” said Congressman Thomas Massie (KY-4). “Congress set the capital loss deduction at $3,000 in 1978 and then let inflation erode its value for nearly fifty years. This bill offers some relief and course correction for taxpayers in an increasingly volatile economy.”

“Republicans are reversing years of Democrats’ big government tax burdens to ensure hardworking Americans can keep more of their money each year, and this legislation does just that,” said Congresswoman Sheri Biggs (SC-3). “I am proud to support this bill because it gives our constituents more breathing room when they take risks, invest, and contribute to our economy. As the cost of living increases, so should the amount you can deduct when you experience a loss. Americans should be able to keep more of their own money. It’s that simple.”

“The $3,000 capital loss deduction limit has been stuck in the tax code since 1978, even as the value of the dollar has declined dramatically due to inflation. Thankfully, Congressman Norman’s commonsense reform would provide taxpayers and investors with a fairer and more neutral tax treatment of capital gains and losses. NTU is proud to once again endorse the Capital Loss Inflation Fairness Act and looks forward to helping this important legislation reach the president’s desk,” Thomas Aiello, Vice President of Federal Affairs at National Taxpayers Union.

“The current federal tax code discourages families from saving, leaving them less secure and starving businesses of the capital needed to grow. The Capital Loss Inflation Fairness Act would correct our tax code's uneven treatment of capital gains and losses and strengthen the bottom line for families and businesses alike,” Patrick Fleenor, Tax Policy Fellow with Americans for Prosperity.

The Capital Loss Inflation Fairness Act is originally cosponsored by Reps. Michael Cloud (TX-27), Thomas Massie (KY-4), Sheri Biggs (SC-3), and Andy Harris (MD-1).

The bill is supported by the National Taxpayers Union and Americans for Prosperity.

title: Representative Ocasio-Cortez and Senator Schumer Introduce Bicameral Legislation to Restore Health Coverage for 450,000 New Yorkers
text:
Because of Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act, over 450,000 New Yorkers lost Essential Plan coverage.

WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14) and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) led the entire New York Democratic delegation in the introduction of the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act. The Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act would restore health coverage to the nearly 450,000 New Yorkers who were kicked off of the Essential Plan under the Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

“Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act represents the largest loss of healthcare in American history. Apart from cutting nearly $1 trillion from Medicaid, this bill specifically targeted New York by gutting the Essential Plan and stripping almost half a million New Yorkers of their health insurance. We must take immediate steps to repeal the harmful impacts of H.R. 1 on New York” said Representative Ocasio-Cortez. “Today, I am introducing the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act alongside Senator Schumer and the entire New York Democratic Delegation to reinstate federal funding for the New York Essential Plan and ensure that New Yorkers can once again access this critical health program.”

“Make no mistake, the ‘Big, Ugly Bill’ has been a disaster that has left American families sicker, poorer, and less safe,” said Leader Schumer. “Republicans promised lower health care costs, but they delivered soaring premiums, sky-high deductibles, and coverage ripped away from millions – all to give billionaires and big corporations a tax cut. In an act of political retribution, Republicans specifically targeted New Yorkers, kicking nearly half a million people off their coverage. Leaving working families with no affordable alternatives isn’t policy; it’s punishment. And it undermines public health and the health of our vital hospitals and community health centers. We must work to pass this legislation, reverse this cruel policy, and restore health insurance to all New Yorkers.”

“H.R. 1 decimated New York’s Essential Plan, ripping health insurance coverage from hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers and weakening the finances of every hospital in the State. That’s why the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act is so critically important. It would repeal this terrible HR 1 policy and establish a permanent option for expanded basic health plan coverage. New York’s hospital community is deeply grateful to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, and the New York delegation Democrats for championing this effort to expand health insurance and strengthen New York’s health care safety net,” said Kenneth E. Raske, President, Greater New York Hospital Association.

“Losing coverage can force patients to delay care, skip medications, or make impossible choices between their health and other basic needs. Community health centers care for everyone who walks through their doors, whether they have insurance or not, and as more New Yorkers lose coverage, the strain on CHCs and their patients grows,” said Rose Duhan, president and CEO of the Community Health Care Association of New York State. “Ensuring New Yorkers have coverage helps patients get the care they need, when they need it, from providers they know and trust. CHCANYS is proud to support the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act.”

“HANYS strongly supports the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act, which would reverse H.R. 1’s harmful limitations on New Yorkers’ eligibility for this affordable health insurance option and provide states the flexibility to extend this coverage to individuals with incomes up to 250% of the federal poverty line,” said Thomas J. Quatroche Jr., PhD, president and CEO, Healthcare Association of New York State. “Affordable health coverage is becoming out of reach for many New Yorkers, and H.R. 1 threatens to leave even more people uninsured. HANYS applauds Senate Minority Leader Schumer and Rep. Ocasio-Cortez for introducing this important bill and for their ongoing dedication to protecting and improving all New Yorkers’ access to healthcare coverage and care.”

“This legislation would reverse some of the worst harms of H.R. 1 and allow more New Yorkers to access affordable health insurance coverage,” said Mitchell Katz, MD President and CEO of NYC Health + Hospitals. “Our health care system is grateful to Senator Schumer and Representative Ocasio-Cortez for their leadership and commitment to keeping New Yorkers connected to care.”

The legislation would repeal the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s premium tax credit eligibility restrictions, fully restoring funding for the Essential Plan. In addition to restoring the program, the legislation would provide all states with the option to expand health coverage through the Affordable Care Act’s Basic Health Plan.

This legislation is cosponsored by the entire New York Democratic delegation including: Senator Gillibrand (D-NY), Leader Jeffries (NY-08), and Representatives Clarke (NY-09), Espaillat (NY-13), Gillen (NY-04), Goldman (NY-10), Kennedy (NY-26), Latimer (NY-16), Mannion (NY-22), Meeks (NY-5), Meng (NY-6), Morelle (NY-25), Nadler (NY-12), Riley (NY-19), Ryan (NY-18), Suozzi (NY-3), Tonko (NY-20), Torres (NY-15), and Velázquez (NY-07).

By encouraging risk mitigation, promoting community resilience, expanding access to financial protection, and testing new risk-transfer models, this pilot program can help communities prepare for disasters and speed recovery when disasters strike.”

“Architects are an essential part of the solution to helping communities prepare for growing disaster risks. The Community Disaster Protection Act will give communities new tools to better understand, manage, and insure against those risks—helping create the conditions for property owners and local governments to invest in the resilient buildings and infrastructure architects are uniquely equipped to design,” said Illya Azaroff, FAIA, 2026 National President, American Institute of Architects. “AIA is proud to support this legislation and looks forward to continuing our work with Representative Dave Min, Johnny Olszewski, and the SEEC Building Resilient Housing Task Force to advance practical solutions that strengthen communities before disasters strike.”

“As natural disasters continue to worsen in both intensity and impact across the country, we need innovative solutions to help communities and economies recover from devastation,” said Jessie Ritter, Associate Vice President for Water and Coasts at the National Wildlife Federation. “The Community Disaster Protection Act encourages proactive risk mitigation, while also giving communities a flexible solution to support recovery after disasters, particularly in areas that are the most vulnerable to extreme weather. We look forward to working with Representatives Min and Olszewski on this legislation.”

“CSAC looks forward to working with Congressmember Min on the Community Disaster Protection Act to advance practical, workable solutions for California communities. Local governments need more tools and flexibility to help protect families and residents facing growing disaster risks and insurance challenges,” said California State Association of Counties (CSAC) President and Santa Clara County Supervisor Susan Ellenberg.

Background

As climate change drives more frequent and severe extreme weather events, communities face widening disaster coverage gaps, making it harder and more expensive for them to rebuild. In 2024, economic losses from natural disasters in the U.S. reached $217.8 billion, approximately $105 billion of which was left uninsured. Rising climate-related damage has increased insurer payouts, driven up premiums, and prompted insurance carriers to withdraw from high-risk markets. Addressing this coverage crisis requires innovative approaches that expand insurance access, promote effective resilience, and strengthen the stability of insurance markets nationwide.

Communities are exploring ways to secure or facilitate insurance for a group of properties, leveraging their local knowledge and purchasing power to improve affordability, streamline enrollment, and incentivize risk mitigation tailored to local needs. These arrangements, known as community-based catastrophe insurance (CBCI), offer significant potential to close disaster coverage gaps but are only now beginning to be explored, with just a handful of U.S. jurisdictions currently piloting or implementing CBCI programs. For example, CBCI can be developed to act as a supplement to the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), such as a parametric flood insurance program, or to cover wildfire risk in communities where insurers are withdrawing coverage or declining to write new policies.

The Community Disaster Protection Act would promote the development of new disaster insurance products to help high-risk communities secure affordable coverage; incentivize effective disaster prevention; and provide greater stability to property insurance markets. It would direct FEMA to establish a 5-year pilot program to award competitive grants to local governments, quasi-government bodies, and community-based organizations to design, develop, implement, or facilitate CBCI.

Specifically, this bill would:

Close Disaster Coverage Gaps: Authorize grants to develop or facilitate CBCI products that cover disaster risks uninsured or underserved by traditional insurance; set actuarially justified premiums that enable broad participation; and prioritize applicants facing the greatest coverage gaps or disaster risks.

Preserve Local Flexibility: Allow funds to support a range of CBCI frameworks, without restricting the disaster risks or properties covered. Eligible uses of funds could include consumer outreach and education, catastrophe-risk modeling or research into disaster risks, and leveraging non-federal funds to support long-term program sustainability.

Promote Resiliency Investments: Require CBCI programs to promote specific individual or community-wide investments to mitigate disaster risks, reduce potential losses, and secure lower premiums.

Address Regulatory Ambiguity: Direct the U.S. Government Accountability Office to conduct periodic evaluations of program performance to determine the regulatory treatment of CBCI and other alternative insurance products with respect to federal disaster aid eligibility.

Preserve State Insurance Authority: Explicitly preserve States’ authority to regulate insurance markets and require all grant recipients to comply with applicable State insurance laws and regulations. Grants would only be a catalyst for CBCI arrangements operating within State regulatory frameworks.

This bill is endorsed by the American Property Casualty Insurance Association, American Institute of Architects, California State Association of Counties, Environmental Defense Fund, Evergreen Action, League of Conservation Voters, National Wildlife Federation, and Natural Resources Defense Council.

In addition, Reps. Ami Bera (CA-06), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Ed Case (HI-01), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Mike Levin (CA-49), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), and Shri Thanedar (MI-13) have joined as original cosponsors.

title: Omar, Garamendi, McGovern Release Statement on Hostilities in Ethiopia
text:
WASHINGTON – Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN), Chair of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, Rep. John Garamendi (D-CA), Co-Chair of the Ethiopian American Caucus and member of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, and Rep. Jim McGovern (D-MA), member of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, released the following statement on hostilities in Ethiopia:

“We are deeply alarmed by increasing violence in Ethiopia, including the Ethiopian military strike last week on an aid convoy delivering assistance in Tigray.

"The 2022 Pretoria Agreement that silenced the guns in Northern Ethiopia committed all parties to ceasing hostilities, protecting civilians, allowing humanitarian access to those affected, and undertaking comprehensive transitional justice to hold those responsible for human rights abuses and violations responsible. Unfortunately, this agreement has not been upheld, and these conditions have not been met.

"This increased conflict threatens the entire country and the region as a whole, which is already reeling from the previous war in Northern Ethiopia and the devastating conflict in Sudan. Ordinary civilians are bearing the brunt of this violence.

"We urge all parties in Ethiopia to immediately recommit to peace negotiations and uphold their responsibilities under the Pretoria Agreement. Ethiopia’s neighbors and the international community must work to defuse tensions and facilitate peace.

"We also urge the U.S. State Department to work with all parties to end the violence and hold those responsible accountable. The people of Ethiopia deserve peace and justice.”
