title: King, Curtis Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Increase Affordable Housing Across the United States
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Angus King (I-ME) and John Curtis (R-UT) are introducing bipartisan legislation to increase affordable housing across the United States. The Build American Efficiency Act would streamline the process for home builders to determine and locate domestically sourced materials that comply with the Build America, Buy American Act (BABA). This small legislative step would help homebuilders cut costs and avoid bureaucracy as they work to address the national housing shortage.

To accomplish its goals, the Build American Efficiency Act would encourage the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to share industry-led initiatives to certify products and facilities that comply with BABA requirements. The BABA standards were passed in the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. In addition to King and Curtis, the legislation is cosponsored by Senators Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) and Peter Welch (D-VT).

“Despite our country’s desperate need for additional affordable housing options, American homebuilders face steep costs and bureaucratic red tape,” said Senator King. “The Build American Efficiency Act would empower the Department of Housing and Urban Development to share information to help builders, manufacturers, and housing providers navigate complicated compliance requirements and identify verified American-made products. Eliminating this time-consuming and costly additional step for homebuilders will allow them to build more homes faster. It’s a three-page bill that amounts to a common-sense helping hand.”

“Utah’s impressive growth has unfortunately brought with it the strain of rising housing costs—which has already been made worse by unnecessary federal red tape,” said Senator Curtis. “This bipartisan bill is a commonsense fix that makes it easier for builders to identify American-made materials, cut through bureaucracy, and get more affordable homes built faster.”

More specifically, the Build American Efficiency Act would:

Clarify that the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development has the authority to recognize auditable and verifiable systems that document products that comply with Build America, Buy America domestic content requirements

Allow HUD to treat documentation generated under the Make It American Process Standard, or similar standards that provide an auditable and verifiable certification process, as sufficient evidence for domestic content certification

Help manufacturers, builders, and funding recipients more easily determine which products comply with BABA requirements

Reduce time spent navigating waiver requests, duplicative paperwork, and uncertainty over which products have or have not been approved

Preserve flexibility by ensuring the bill does not mandate the use of any one database or prohibit recipients from using other lawful methods to certify compliance.

In Maine, the Build American Efficiency Act is supported by Avesta Housing and Evernorth.

"The Build American Efficiency Act is an important step forward that will help Avesta, and creators of affordable housing everywhere, move ahead with creating desperately needed new homes for individuals and families. By streamlining and simplifying domestic purchasing provisions through clear, verifiable lists of compliant components, this bill removes a significant challenge to building housing that is now causing serious delays, increasing costs of construction, and putting the viability of needed developments at risk," said Jennifer Hawkins, President and CEO of Avesta Housing. "We deeply appreciate the leadership of Sen. King to bring this bipartisan bill forward to address this critical issue and for his unwavering support of housing for Maine people."

“Evernorth is proud to endorse the Build American Efficiency Act. This commonsense legislation is an important first step toward reducing the compliance burden and delays that are making it harder and more expensive to build the affordable homes our communities need,” said Nancy Owens, President of Evernorth.

Nationwide, the bill is supported by ABB, Alliance for American Manufacturing, Associated General Contractors, Eaton, Bipartisan Policy Center Action, Inclusive Abundance Action, Maine Affordable Housing Coalition, National Association of Electrical Distributors, National Association of Manufacturers, National Association of Realtors, National Association of State Housing Agencies, National Electrical Contractors Association, National Electrical Manufacturers Association, Prysmian, Schneider, Siemens, and Southwire.

Senator King has long been committed to ensuring Maine people across the state can access safe and affordable housing and has worked with his colleagues on creative solutions to combat the housing shortage. He introduced the Farmhouse-to-Workforce Housing Act, which would expand the existing Housing Preservation Grants program so rural homeowners can create more housing on their property — such as an attached apartment unit or a small home nearby — to be available for rent. Additionally, King has sponsored the bipartisan Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act to create nearly two million new affordable homes across the country — including thousands in Maine. He also worked with his Republican colleagues to improve affordability of rural homes and farms through the Access to Credit for our Rural Economy (ACRE) Act of 2023.

title: Klobuchar Recognizes Crystal and Justin Kasmiskie as this Year's Angels in Adoption Minnesota Honorees
text:
The Kasmiskie family and Senator Amy Klobuchar at the Angels in Adoption annual celebration in Washington, D.C.

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Coalition on Adoption, spoke at the annual Angels in Adoption celebration hosted by the Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute and recognized Crystal and Justin Kasmiskie from Shakopee, Minnesota, as this year’s Angels in Adoption Minnesota honorees, alongside their adopted sons.

The Kasmiskies adopted their two-year-old twins in December of 2025 but trouble with their visas delayed their travel. The Kasmiskies were faced with a horrible choice: leave one of their twins behind or stay and risk losing both before the visa ban went into effect. They chose to stay with the kids. Ultimately, with Klobuchar’s help, the family received their approved visas and safely departed Liberia.

“Every child deserves a loving home, a nurturing family, and a bright future,” said Klobuchar. “When Crystal and Justin first encountered a technical visa error, they worried they wouldn't be able to bring their sons home before a visa ban was set to take effect. Our office was able to push their visas through and on January 20th, one day before the ban affected visas from Liberia, they departed for home. Since then, their boys have started preschool, spent lots of time with family, and even went apple picking!”

In her role as co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Coalition on Adoption, Klobuchar has been a leader in the fight to give every child a permanent home. The Congressional Coalition on Adoption is the largest bipartisan, bicameral caucus in Congress. To date, Klobuchar’s office has assisted more than 1,500 Minnesota families with their adoption cases.

In response to the visa ban in January, Klobuchar has advocated for adoption visas to be exempted from the travel ban, as well as guidance for families on how to move forward.

In January 2026, Klobuchar led a letter with her Adoption Caucus Co-Chairs, Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND), Rep. Robert Aderholt (R-AL), and Rep. Danny Davis (D-IL), to the State Department requesting immediate guidance and permanent exemptions for adoption visas.

title: Bipartisan Lummis-Kelly MORE American Fuel Act Passes U.S. Senate
text:
Washington D.C. — The U.S. Senate last night passed the Modernizing Outdated Regulations to Expand American Fuel Act of 2026 (MORE American Fuel Act). The bipartisan bill was introduced by Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) and Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ).

The MORE American Fuel Act modernizes outdated Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) licensing requirements for uranium enrichment facilities and aligns them with the process already used for other nuclear facilities and reactors. The bill lets enrichment companies begin construction at their own risk instead of waiting years for a construction license before breaking ground, while preserving public participation and the NRC’s rigorous safety standards.

“Senator Kelly and I agree on something simple: we can keep the NRC’s high safety standards and still stop making enrichment companies wait years just to break ground,” said Lummis. “Wyoming’s uranium and Wyoming’s workers are ready to help secure this nation’s nuclear fuel supply now. I want to thank Senator Kelly for working with me, and I’m pleased that the Senate has agreed it’s time to cut the red tape holding back American enrichment. I urge the House to act swiftly and send this legislation to President Trump’s desk as soon as possible.”

“Nuclear power is a reliable source of energy. Outdated regulations should not hold back production of the enriched uranium needed to power our nuclear reactors,” said Kelly. “This bill will help us improve our energy security while maintaining strong safety and environmental standards, and I’m glad to see it one step closer to becoming law.”

Background:

Nuclear power provides about 18 percent of total U.S. electricity generation, yet U.S. operators import roughly 80 percent of their enriched uranium. That leaves ratepayers exposed to foreign price swings and to dependence on adversarial suppliers, including Russia.

Senator Lummis cosponsored Senator Barrasso’s Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act, signed into law in 2024. The law banned Russian uranium imports beginning in August 2024, and the ban becomes absolute in 2028 when the Department of Energy’s limited waiver authority expires.

Wyoming is home to the nation’s largest uranium reserves and a skilled energy workforce, positioning the state to lead a domestic nuclear fuel buildout.

The MORE American Fuel Act passed the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee by a vote of 18-1 in September.

title: U.S. Senate Passes Lummis, Barrasso, Hageman Legislation to Modernize Wyoming School Trust Fund Investments
text:
Washington D.C. — The U.S. Senate last night passed the Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act, legislation led by Senators Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) and John Barrasso (R-WY) that would give Wyoming’s permanent school land fund greater investment flexibility and potentially increase annual returns for K-12 education.

“Last night, the U.S. Senate passed a bill that will put Wyoming’s school trust fund to better work for our students,” said Lummis. “The fund holds $5.4 billion but earns only about 5 percent, because it’s still bound by investment rules written in 1890. This bill keeps the principal fully protected while allowing modern investment tools that could raise returns. That means millions of additional dollars for Wyoming classrooms every year, with no new taxes. I thank my Senate colleagues for their support, and I urge the House to act quickly so we can get this to President Trump’s desk.”

“Wyoming has made smart, sustained investments in the future of our students. The Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act will give our state more flexibility in how it manages and grows our permanent school land fund,” said Barrasso. “Diversifying this vital fund will help generate greater returns for students and teachers across Wyoming. With Senate passage, this bill is one step closer to becoming law.”

Background:

Congress established Wyoming’s State Act of Admission upon statehood in 1890, and it governs how the state manages its federally granted school lands. Proceeds from school trust land sales, exchanges, or disposals must be deposited into a permanent land fund under strict federal regulation. Current law prohibits investing the principal, and only accrued interest can be used to fund K-12 education.

Wyoming’s permanent school trust fund currently holds $5.4 billion and generates roughly 5 percent annually under these restrictions. The legislation passed by the Senate would modernize the fund’s investment policies, potentially raising returns from 5% to 8.3% and significantly boosting annual education funding without touching the principal.

The bill preserves all constitutional protections for education funding and maintains principal protection. Only investment returns can be spent, all existing controls on land disposal and exchanges remain unchanged, and the longtime permanent trust fund structure stays fully intact.

The Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act was introduced by Senators Lummis and Barrasso, and Representative Harriet Hageman in July 2025.

title: Senator Marshall Praises Forbes Field Being Named Candidate Location for KC-46A Mission
text:
Topeka – U.S. Senator Roger Marshall, M.D. (R-Kansas), praised the Air National Guard’s decision to identify Forbes Field Air National Guard Base in Topeka as one of four candidate locations for its next KC-46A Pegasus mission.

“This is great news for Kansas and well-deserved recognition of the men and women of the 190th Air Refueling Wing,” said Senator Marshall. “Forbes Field has the infrastructure, the experience and, most importantly, the outstanding Airmen needed to take on this next-generation mission.”

The Secretary of the Air Force approved Forbes Field, along with Bangor Air National Guard Base in Maine, Key Field Air National Guard Base in Mississippi, and Rickenbacker Air National Guard Base in Ohio, as candidate locations for Mission Operations Base 9. The selected location is slated to receive eight KC-46A aircraft.

“Forbes Field is the absolute right place for basing the KC-46A Pegasus,” Brig. Gen. Paul Schneider, the adjutant general, said. “The Kansas Airmen of the 190th Air Refueling Wing continue to set the standard for excellence, as demonstrated by their flawless execution during Operation Epic Fury, their ability to maintain personnel strength above 100% of authorized, and remarkable maintenance record. As the Secretary of the Air Force moves forward with the MOB 9 strategic basing process, the 190th stands ready to recapitalize their legacy KC-135s with the modern capability of eight KC-46A aircraft, ensuring Kansas remains the premier hub for global reach.”

In the coming weeks, the Air National Guard’s Basing and Conversions Division will conduct town halls with the four candidate locations to discuss site-survey criteria and upcoming milestones.

title: Merkley Blasts Senate Republicans for Blocking His Bill to Ban Congressional Stock Trading
text:
Washington, D.C. – Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley released the following statement after Senate Republicans blocked his Ending Trading and Holdings in Congressional Stocks (ETHICS) Act:

“Members of Congress are elected to serve the people, not their portfolios.

“Rather than crack down on Congressional stock trading, Senate Republicans not only blocked my comprehensive legislation to ban this deeply corrupt practice, but they also put up a partisan, fatally flawed bill that doesn’t cover the President and would only prevent members of Congress from buying stocks, allowing them to still sell and hold stocks and perpetuating a clear conflict of interest.

“There should be no question about whether a lawmaker is voting on or writing legislation in the best interest of their constituents or the best interest of their investments. We need a real ban on Congressional stock trading, and I urge my colleagues on the other side of the aisle to work with us on meaningful and decisive action to ban this flagrant conflict of interest once and for all.”

On Wednesday, Merkley took to the Senate Floor in an attempt to pass his ETHICS Act, which would ban members of Congress, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children from buying, selling, and holding stocks and other covered investments. Full text of the ETHICS Act can be found by clicking here.

Merkley has been leading the charge to end Congressional stock trading for over a decade. In 2012, Merkley and former Senator Sherrod Brown (D-OH) led an effort to add an amendment to the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge (STOCK) Act banning trading by members of Congress.

In 2023, Merkley first introduced the ETHICS Act, which later became the first-ever bill banning Congressional stock trading to advance out of a Senate committee. The ETHICS Act was the basis for similar bipartisan legislation that also advanced out of committee in the Republican-controlled Senate this Congress.

title: Wyden, Merkley Introduce Bill to Extend Secure Rural Schools Funding
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, both D-Ore., today were joined by their colleagues Mike Crapo and Jim Risch, both R-Idaho, in introducing legislation that would extend funding for the Secure Rural Schools (SRS) program for three years, and clarify congressional intention for distribution of funding for counties in Oregon with Bureau of Land Management lands.

Funding for the program expired yesterday, September 30, 2026.

“Secure Rural Schools is a lifeline for rural Oregon,” Wyden said. “I’ll be working as hard as I can to get this bill across the finish line, but the well-being of rural America shouldn’t be dependent on Congress getting its act together to renew this funding every few years. It’s past time to get rural communities off the financial rollercoaster and deliver a permanent funding solution.”

“The SRS program provides crucial payments that are a lifeline for rural communities here in Oregon and across America—keeping schools open, maintaining roads, restoring watersheds, and providing funding for police officers and firefighters to keep families safe,” said Merkley. “A three-year extension of the program and these common-sense updates are critical to ensuring the federal government upholds its promise to our communities and that local governments can reliably access these important resources.”

Wyden co-authored the SRS law in 2000, and it has brought nearly $4 billion to Oregon counties since then. Funding for the program lapsed in September 2023 and resumed two years later in September 2025, depriving rural counties across the country of critical funding for schools, law enforcement, and infrastructure projects.

title: Wyden, Merkley Press Officials for Answers on UAS Testing Pauses in Pendleton, McMinnville and Tillamook
text:
Oregon senators: “Our constituents have expressed concerns about how the ongoing pause affects the local economies across the state where UAS testing takes place, and they seek a timely resolution”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley today asked the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and its designated administrator of unmanned aircraft system (UAS) test sites in Pendleton, McMinnville and Tillamook for an update about the recent suspension of all flight operations at those three Oregon locales.

The Oregon senators said their letter comes after operations at those three UAS test sites were paused on Sept. 11 due to concerns at the University of Alaska Fairbanks UAS test site, which serves as the FAA’s designated administrator to test and develop UAS technology, and to oversee operations for test sites across the West.

“While we understand that the pause was necessary due to the FAA’s concerns regarding safety practices, oversight, and documentation, the situation has disrupted flight activity at all other test sites that operate under the University of Alaska Fairbanks,” Wyden and Merkley wrote FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and Dr. Catherine F. Cahill, Director of the Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft System Integration. “In Oregon, this pause delays testing and development for aerospace and defense contractors, federal customers, and commercial UAS companies who operate at the Pendleton UAS Range, Northwest UAV in McMinnville, and Tillamook UAS Test Range.”

Wyden and Merkley wrote that the testing pause has created significant uncertainty for Oregon communities, noting for example that the Pendleton UAS range generates roughly $2.4 million annually for the Eastern Oregon Regional Airport – roughly 82 percent of the airport’s total revenue at the airport.

“Our constituents have expressed concerns about how the ongoing pause affects the local economies across the state where UAS testing takes place, and they seek a timely resolution,” the senators wrote. “We appreciate the FAA’s efforts to review safety practices and conduct oversight. We also recognize the timeliness and importance of resuming operations at all test sites that have been impacted by the pause.”

The senators asked for responses to their letter by Oct. 7, given the significant economic uncertainty facing the test sites.

The entire letter is here.

title: VIDEO: In Homeland Security Subcommittee, Senator Moody Questions Witnesses on Potential Threats posed to America’s Children and Seniors From AI
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody discussed the dangers of AI, especially when it comes to protecting children and seniors, yesterday in a Homeland Security Subcommittee.

“As a mom, one of my top concerns is the impact AI is having on our children – especially as the technology is ingrained more and more into daily life. We cannot allow Congress to stall, cross its fingers, and hope that everything pans out for the best, because the dark side of AI is being utilized to scam seniors, facilitate addictive algorithms, and steal the image and likeness of our children. We must continue our work in Congress to ensure it never gets out of control. We must win the AI race against China, but we need to do it in a way that protects America’s most vulnerable from AI’s dangerous potential,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

As Florida’s Attorney General, Senator Moody warned about the dangers of AI and worked to protect Floridians:

Ran the “Summer Scams Series: Tech Traps,” warning Floridians about AI voice-cloning “grandparent” scams, ChatGPT-generated phishing, and AI-assisted sextortion schemes targeting teens.

Publicly highlighted how generative AI made sextortion more believable and scalable.

Launched investigations into Meta and Instagram, as well as took legal action, over the platform’s algorithms and practices that sought to addict children to using the service and then profit off the children’s data.

As U.S. Senator, Moody has introduced and cosponsored bills that directly address AI-generated content and platform design:

NO FAKES Act (Nurture Originals, Foster Art, and Keep Entertainment Safe Act of 2026):

Creates a federal intellectual-property right in an individual’s voice and visual likeness. It makes it unlawful to distribute unauthorized AI digital replicas (deepfakes) and can hold platforms liable if they know the replica is unauthorized. The Senate Judiciary Committee advanced it unanimously in June 2026.

Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA): Requires covered platforms to default to the strongest safety settings for minors, give users and parents the ability to turn off addictive design features and algorithmic recommendations, and provide better parental tools and reporting.

Senator Moody has introduced the SWIPES Act and the STOP Scams Against Seniors Act.

She has also sponsored the James T. Woods Act which passed committee and closes gaps that prosecutors previously faced when threats involved material that is now often AI-generated.

title: Murkowski Advances Three Alaska Energy and Resource Bills Through Committee
text:
Washington, DC—The Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources (ENR) during a business meeting today reported three bills championed by U.S. Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-AK). The measures would strengthen Alaska’s energy security by investing in next-generation geothermal technologies; improving electric grid resilience; and expanding efforts to map critical mineral and other resources. The bills now go to the full Senate for consideration.

Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (Earth MRI): S. 4870 would reauthorize Earth MRI, a U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) program that improves understanding of geologic hazards, critical minerals, geothermal resources, and other subsurface resources across the country. Since its launch in 2019, Earth MRI has accelerated project timelines, reduced exploration risk, and lowered costs by making foundational geologic information publicly available. Current funding for Earth MRI is set to expire at the end of FY26.

The legislation would reauthorize Earth MRI for an additional five years at funding levels similar to those provided under IIJA. The bill would also expand the program to include geologic hydrogen, an emerging domestic energy resource that is attracting growing scientific and commercial interest.

Next-Generation Geothermal Research and Development Act (H.R.8790): S.4406 would establish Research and Development (R&D) Programs at the Department of Energy (DOE). These programs would ensure that existing programs are also available for the testing of these next-generation technologies, enhance the collaboration between DOE and the Department of the Interior (DOI) to locate ideal conditions for next-general geothermal energy production, and expand public-private partnerships by establishing a Next-Generation Geothermal Center of Excellence to advance enhanced geothermal energy technologies, including supercritical geothermal energy production.

Securing Community Upgrades for a Resilient Grid Act (SECURE Grid Act): S. 4166 would empower states to more fully assess risks to their electric grids, from extreme weather to cyber threats and other vulnerabilities.

Each year, states must submit a State Energy Security Plan (SESP) to receive funds from the State Energy Program, which are used to design, develop, and implement renewable energy and energy efficiency programs. The SECURE Grid Act would require future SESPs to account for additional threats and vulnerabilities, including supply chain dynamics, extreme weather, potential physical attacks on the grid, and the impact of growing energy demand.

By assessing these additional factors, states would be better able to recognize and respond to weaknesses in their energy infrastructure. The legislation would also require states to coordinate with suppliers of manufactured components and infrastructure to better understand and prepare for potential disruptions.

To accomplish its goals, the Build American Efficiency Act would encourage the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to share industry-led initiatives to certify products and facilities that comply with BABA requirements. The BABA standards were passed in the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

"I'm committed to using every federal resource available to make building homes in Alaska more streamlined and affordable across the board,” said Senator Murkowski. “This legislation will help identify products that are made in America more easily, cutting through red tape to get more homes built with American-made materials around the country.”

“Despite our country’s desperate need for additional affordable housing options, American homebuilders face steep costs and bureaucratic red tape,” said Senator King. “The Build American Efficiency Act would empower the Department of Housing and Urban Development to share information to help builders, manufacturers, and housing providers navigate complicated compliance requirements and identify verified American-made products. Eliminating this time-consuming and costly additional step for homebuilders will allow them to build more homes faster. It’s a three-page bill that amounts to a common-sense helping hand.”

“Utah’s impressive growth has unfortunately brought with it the strain of rising housing costs—which has already been made worse by unnecessary federal red tape,” said Senator Curtis. “This bipartisan bill is a commonsense fix that makes it easier for builders to identify American-made materials, cut through bureaucracy, and get more affordable homes built faster.”

More specifically, the Build American Efficiency Act would:

Clarify that the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development has the authority to recognize auditable and verifiable systems that document products that comply with Build America, Buy America domestic content requirements

Allow HUD to treat documentation generated under the Make It American Process Standard, or similar standards that provide an auditable and verifiable certification process, as sufficient evidence for domestic content certification

Help manufacturers, builders, and funding recipients more easily determine which products comply with BABA requirements

Reduce time spent navigating waiver requests, duplicative paperwork, and uncertainty over which products have or have not been approved

Preserve flexibility by ensuring the bill does not mandate the use of any one database or prohibit recipients from using other lawful methods to certify compliance.

Nationwide, the bill is supported by ABB, Alliance for American Manufacturing, Associated General Contractors, Eaton, Bipartisan Policy Center Action, Inclusive Abundance Action, Maine Affordable Housing Coalition, National Association of Electrical Distributors, National Association of Manufacturers, National Association of Realtors, National Association of State Housing Agencies, National Electrical Contractors Association, National Electrical Manufacturers Association, Prysmian, Schneider, Siemens, and Southwire.

title: Murphy, Hawley Announce Breakthrough Bipartisan Legislation to Force AI Developers to Prioritize Safety or Face Prison Time
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Senators Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) and Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) announced bipartisan legislation to ensure artificial intelligence (AI) agent operators and developers are held liable for hacking incidents. AI agents are hacking into public websites, networks, and servers. This poses potentially dire consequences to anything connected online—including hospitals, utilities, banks, and other critical infrastructure.

“Hacking is a crime, and when AI agents conduct dangerous cyberattacks, the corporations and executives responsible for those AI agents need to be held accountable,” said Senator Murphy. “Our bipartisan bill forces the heads of big AI companies to develop responsibly or face prison time for the damage done by their products to everyone else.”

“These AI agents are committing cyberattacks. If Big Tech companies are going to design AI agents that wreak havoc, these companies better be on the hook for any damage that is caused," said Senator Hawley. "That’s why I’m introducing legislation to ensure AI agent operators and developers are held liable for hacking incidents. With this liability regime in place, AI companies will have every incentive to keep their products safe.”

The bipartisan AI Agent Accountability Act would:

Hold AI Agent Operators Liable. AI agent operators would be held criminally and civilly liable under the provisions of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA), including for knowing operation of an AI agent that recklessly causes computer hacking damage or loss.

Hold AI Developers Liable. AI agent developers would be held criminally and civilly liable for failure to implement reasonable safeguards against hacking when they knew or had reason to know of the AI agent’s hacking capabilities.

Empower AGs with Power to Enjoin AI Agent Hacking. The Attorney General and state attorneys general are granted power to sue to enjoin AI agent operators and developers when they commit, conspire to commit, or attempt to commit a hacking offense under the CFAA.

Senator Murphy has been a leading voice in the U.S. Senate on the threat unregulated artificial intelligence poses to the cultural and economic health of the United States. In 2025, Murphy was honored in the TIME AI 100 as one of the most influential people shaping the conversation on artificial intelligence. This month, he joined the UN General Assembly to outline the path ahead for Congress to address Americans’ growing concerns around AI, including job loss, competition with China, and humanity losing control over the technology.

title: Murray, Top Appropriators Introduce Bill to Impose Significant Penalties on Trump Admin for Using Taxpayer Dollars to Air Political Propaganda
text:
Penalties for Propaganda Act cuts OMB’s budget by $20 million each instance taxpayer dollars are used for propaganda

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray, Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and top Senate appropriators introduced the Penalties for Propaganda Act, a bill to impose penalties on the Trump administration for breaking federal law and using taxpayer dollars to air government propaganda.

“Not a cent of Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars should ever be used to run political ads glorifying the president. Clearly, this administration couldn’t care less about what the law says or about wasting Americans’ tax dollars on obscene ads. Congress cannot sit on its hands. If the president is going to defy federal law to run propaganda celebrating himself—and his budget director is going to allow it—there must be consequences,” said Senator Patty Murray. “This fair-minded bill hits White House Budget Director Vought’s operating budget each time this administration willfully violates our laws to spend federal funding on North Korea-style propaganda. It is not too much to expect the White House Budget Office to respect the law and the basic principle that tax dollars should not fund political ads. Democrats and Republicans alike have made clear that tax dollars shouldn’t be funding these ads, and I hope every one of my colleagues who agrees will support this bill and work with me to get it signed into law.”

In recent days, the Trump administration has spent at least $2.9 million in taxpayer funds airing several political ads celebrating Trump, according to AdImpact. Federal law prohibits taxpayer funding of political propaganda, including Section 718 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026, which states that: “No part of any appropriation contained in the act or any other Act shall be used directly or indirectly, including through a private contractor, for publicity or propaganda purposes within the United States not heretofore authorized by Congress.”

The Penalties for Propaganda Act imposes a new penalty for violating the anti-propaganda provision contained in federal law. The bill cuts the budget of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), headed by Director Russ Vought, by $20 million each time any part of the administration violates the law.

In addition to Senator Murray, original cosponsors of the legislation include: Senator Jack Reed, Ranking Member of the Financial Services and General Government Subcommittee; Senator Jeanne Shaheen, Ranking Member of the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Subcommittee; Senator Jeff Merkley, Ranking Member of the Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies Subcommittee; Senator Chris Coons, Ranking Member of the Defense Subcommittee; Senator Tammy Baldwin, Ranking Member of the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Subcommittee; Senator Chris Van Hollen, Ranking Member of the Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Subcommittee; Senator Martin Heinrich, Ranking Member of the Legislative Branch Subcommittee; Senator Gary Peters, member of the Committee and Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee; Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, Ranking Member of the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies Subcommittee.

When the government-funded Trump ads first aired, Vice Chair Murray and Ranking Member Reed wrote to White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles demanding the ads come off the air and reminding the White House of federal law. When the Committee became aware the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is bankrolling the ads, Vice Chair Murray and Senator Chris Murphy, Ranking Member of the Homeland Security Subcommittee, wrote to Secretary Markwayne Mullin to demand DHS stop airing the ads and provide the Committee with all relevant information about the spending and contracts. DHS has so far failed to share this information.

title: PASSED: Murray & Daines Floodplain Bill Passes the Senate, Cutting Red Tape, Simplifying Pathway for Ecosystem Restoration
text:
ICYMI: Murray Floodplain Bill Picks Up Dozens of Key Endorsements, Momentum Grows as Commonsense Bipartisan Legislation Is Introduced in the House

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, released the following statement after Senate passage of her Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act—bipartisan legislation Senator Murray introduced with Senator Steve Daines (R-MT) last year. The Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act is a straightforward, commonsense bill that would create a new pathway for ecosystem restoration projects in floodplains that meet specific low-risk criteria—simplifying the approval process for important restoration work while still upholding flood safety standards.

U.S. Representatives Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D, WA-03), Troy Downing (R, MT-02), Janelle Bynum (D, OR-02), and Bryan Steil (R, WI-01), have introduced identical companion legislation in the House of Representatives. The Senate bill now needs to be passed out of the House before it can be signed into law.

“This is great news for Washington state. We are one step closer to making it easier to get ecosystem restoration projects approved. This is a commonsense, zero-cost fix that will cut red tape and allow critical restoration projects in Washington state to move forward,” said Senator Murray. “Government should be making it easier to protect our environment, not harder. And here in Washington state, ensuring our waterways stay healthy is critical for not just our environment, but for our communities and economy as well. I urge my colleagues to waste no time in passing this legislation.”

“This is huge news for Montana. Critical ecosystem restoration projects across our state have been abandoned due to FEMA’s onerous and costly ‘No Rise’ rule. This commonsense, bipartisan bill will reduce unnecessary burdens on important conservation and restoration work, while continuing to keep our communities safe from flooding, and I’m glad to see it pass the Senate. Next step: the U.S. House!” said Senator Daines.

Background on the Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act:

Under current Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) policy, any proposed development in a regulated floodway, whether it’s a shopping mall or salmon habitat, must prove that it will not increase the base flood elevation (BFE) of the area. This requirement is commonly referred to as the “No Rise” rule. While important for protecting communities from increased flood risks, it has had major unintended consequences on important environmental restoration in Washington state and across the country.

In Washington state, many salmon habitat restoration projects involve placing woody debris in rivers and streams to slow water flows and create sheltered areas where juvenile salmon can develop. These projects, and many others, often fail the “No Rise” rule. Currently, the only way to address these impacts is to first update FEMA’s flood maps to account for the projected BFE impacts. This requires extensive and very expensive hydrologic and hydraulic analyses, often performed by a third-party engineer. FEMA then reviews the analyses, replicates them, and approves them internally before giving the okay to move forward, which can take several years to complete. While this process often makes sense in an urbanized, flood-prone community, it is an unnecessary exercise for restoration in rural areas.

Many communities in Washington state have avoided doing restoration work in regulated floodways—which makes up much of the state—to avoid the associated costs. This bill would create a more efficient process for ecosystem restoration in regulated floodways while addressing the “No Rise” issue, which has been a priority concern for Tribal communities and conservation advocates in Washington and across the country.

The following organizations have endorsed Senator Murray and Daines’ Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act: Smarter Safer Coalition; American Rivers; Association of State Floodplain Managers; National Association of Conservation Districts; The Nature Conservancy; Trout Unlimited; Bonneville Environmental Foundation; City of Kenmore; City of Sammamish; City of Seattle; Seattle Public Utilities; Environmental Policy Innovation Center; Environmental Science Center; Island County; King County Department of Natural Resources and Parks; Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe; Montana Trout Unlimited; National Wildlife Federation; Puget Sound Partnership; Puget Sound Salmon Recovery Council; River Alliance of Wisconsin; Southern Environmental Law Center; Upper Deschutes Watershed Council; Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife; Wild Salmon Center; Wisconsin Council of Trout Unlimited; Wisconsin Land and Water Conservation Association; Wisconsin Wetlands Association; WRIA 8 Salmon Recovery Council (Lake Sammamish, Lake Washington, Cedar River Watersheds); City of Shoreline; Mountains to Sound Greenway Trust; Rock River Coalition; and Clean Wisconsin.

“The Puget Sound Partnership is delighted to see the Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act pass the Senate. This legislation is a tremendous step towards accelerating the pace and scale of restoration in Puget Sound and around the country. For too long, critical salmon habitat restoration projects that had no impact on human infrastructure were obligated to complete the same costly hydraulic and hydrologic analyses as subdivisions and strip malls—a process that caused years of delay and millions of dollars of cost increases. Thanks to Senator Murray’s leadership and persistence, this bill will provide local governments with the flexibility they need to get restoration projects done faster and more cheaply. On to the House!” said Mindy Roberts, Executive Director of the Puget Sound Partnership.

“Healthier floodplains are a win-win for people and nature. They can reduce flood risks, improve water quality and provide important habitat for fish and other wildlife,” said Cameron Adams, Policy Advisor for The Nature Conservancy. “The Nature Conservancy applauds the Senate for passing the Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act, which will give communities the flexibility they want and need to scale up science-backed floodplain restoration. We commend Senators Murray and Daines for their attention to this critical issue and strongly support the full passage of FERA into law.”

“In the face of extreme weather and increasing pressures on our nation’s rivers, we need to maximize investments in natural infrastructure and streamline projects that strengthen community resilience, protect public health, and keep our rivers healthy,” said Eileen Shader, Senior Advisor for American Rivers Action Fund. “The Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act is a smart, common-sense step forward to ensuring the regulatory process is efficient and cost-effective. We commend the bipartisan leadership of Senators Murray and Daines advancing this bill and urge the House to take action to pass the bill before the end of the 119th Congress.”

Senator Murray has been a champion for protecting and strengthening critical salmon and fish populations throughout her time in the Senate. Senator Murray secured a historic $2.85 billion investment in salmon and ecosystem restoration programs—including $400 million for a new community-based restoration program focused on removing fish passage barriers in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law—and in the Inflation Reduction Act, Murray secured hundreds of millions for Washington state priorities including $15 million for the Pacific Coastal Salmon Recovery Fund, $3 million to support facilities at the Olympic Coast National Marine Sanctuary, $27 million for Pacific salmon research, and more.

As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Murray has protected critical funding for salmon recovery projects in the Fiscal Year 2026 government spending bills she negotiated and passed into law, including: $75.75 million for the Pacific Salmon account at the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), a $750,000 increase over FY25 funding levels; $27.5 million for Mitchell Act salmon hatcheries, a $4 million increase, to help raise salmon and steelhead for release in the Columbia River Basin for harvest and conservation purposes; $65 million for the Pacific Coastal Salmon Recovery Fund, which the Trump administration proposed eliminating this program altogether in their budget request; $28 million in NOAA construction funds for critical improvements and upgrades at the Northwest Fisheries Science Center in Seattle; $1 million for the Northwest Straits Initiative; $1.5 million for management, intervention, and mitigation of invasive European Green Crab, and more.

title: Senator Murray Reintroduces Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act to Increase Access to Life-Saving Cancer Screenings
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and former chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, reintroduced the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act, legislation that would increase the availability of preventive, life-saving cancer screenings at safety net health care providers like Planned Parenthood. The bill would create new grant and pilot programs to expand access to preventive services and screenings for breast and gynecological cancers—especially for low-income women and women of color—and train health care providers in providing high-quality cancer screening, early detection, and follow-up care.

Jeanette Acosta was a fierce women’s health advocate, a former congressional staffer, and a White House intern in the Obama administration. In 2017, she lost her battle with cervical cancer at the age of 32.

“I’m proud to reintroduce the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act in honor of Jeanette Acosta, a fierce advocate who fought to make sure every woman could get the health care she needs,” said Senator Murray. “Too many women suffer preventable deaths because they didn’t have access to the cancer screenings that would have detected their condition early on. That is an unacceptable tragedy. We know that early detection saves lives—not to mention health care costs—and investing in preventive services to help more women get treatment before it’s too late is just common sense. I’m not going to stop fighting to pass this crucial piece of legislation in Jeanette’s memory.”

“It is an honor that the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act of 2026 is in our daughter’s name. Over eight years ago cervical cancer took the life of our precious and valiant daughter, Jeanette. At the young age of 32, after one year of battling her cancer and suffering incomparable pain and extensive treatment, Jeanette died from her advanced cancer. Jeanette prayed that women be spared from the agony of cervical cancer, and this bill would help to achieve her hope for many women” said Frank X. Acosta, Ph.D., Jeanette Acosta’s father. “This bill will have a lasting and positive national impact in the fight against cancers that afflict women. During her own fight with cancer, Jeanette reached out and provided support and encouragement to other women coping with cancer. She also emphasized the importance of prevention against the onset of cervical cancer. Jeanette, always a warrior for social justice, wanted to shine a light on the disparities to access to prevention and cancer health services for low-income, Latina, and Black women. This bill would brightly illuminate and help to close the gap between cancer prevention and health services and the countless women who have not and may not be able to access these services. Jeanette would adamantly support this bill.”

“Early detection and preventive care saves lives, and everyone deserves access to these critical health services. Planned Parenthood Federation of America is grateful to Sen. Murray for continuing to honor the legacy of former Planned Parenthood patient and health care advocate Jeanette Acosta, who worked to ensure more people can get the care they need,” said Alexis McGill Johnson, president and CEO, Planned Parenthood Federation of America. “The Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act is an important step to increase access to life-saving breast and gynecological cancer screenings, particularly for Black, Indigenous and Latina women who face longstanding barriers to care. We are proud of the over 500 Planned Parenthood health centers providing these essential health services to patients.”

The bill is co-sponsored by: Senators Alsobrooks (D-MD), Baldwin (D-WI), Blumenthal (D-CT), Booker (D-NJ), Duckworth (D-IL), Gallego (D-AZ), Gillibrand (D-NY), Klobuchar (D-MN), Merkley (D-OR), Rosen (D-NV), Schiff (D-CA), Shaheen (D-NH), Van Hollen (D-MD), Whitehouse (D-RI), and Wyden (D-OR).

The bill is endorsed by: American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology, American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Black Women’s Health Imperative, Human Rights Watch, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, National Asian Pacific American Women’s Forum, National Council of Jewish Women, National Family Planning & Reproductive Health Association, National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice, National Partnership for Women & Families, National Women’s Law Center Action Fund, Ovarian Cancer Research Alliance, and Planned Parenthood Federation of America.

title: NEWS: U.S. Senate Passes Sen. Ossoff’s Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen Emergency Alerts; Heads to President’s Desk to Become Law
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff’s bipartisan bill to strengthen emergency alerts during natural disasters has passed the Senate.

Last night, the U.S. Senate passed Sens. Ossoff and John Cornyn (R-TX)’s bipartisan Mystic Alerts Act to improve distribution of wireless emergency alerts (WEA). The Senate unanimously passed H.R. 7022, the House version of their bill.

The bill previously passed the U.S. House of Representatives and now heads to the President’s desk to become law.

In August, Sens. Ossoff and Cornyn introduced the bipartisan bill to enable emergency alerts to be delivered via satellite communications technologies when other systems fail during emergencies, including natural disasters such as hurricanes, wildfires, and floods.

The bipartisan bill comes after last year’s devastating flood in Central Texas that killed over 100 people, where it was later reported residents did not receive emergency alerts after cellular infrastructure was damaged.

“When storms, disasters, or threats to public safety threaten our state, crisis management is key. Our bipartisan bill will help upgrade America’s emergency alert systems to keep Georgia families safe and informed,” Sen. Ossoff said.

“More than 130 people were tragically killed in the July 4th floods that ravaged Central Texas last year, many of whom did not receive emergency alerts due to compromised cellular networks that were knocked out by the storm,” said Sen. Cornyn. “This bill will address this technology shortfall and honor the memory of those lost by ensuring Texans and all Americans can receive wireless emergency alerts on their mobile devices via satellite even when disaster strikes, and I look forward to President Trump signing it into law soon.”

Sen. Ossoff continues working to strengthen public safety.

This year, Sen. Ossoff brought Republicans and Democrats together to deliver $175,000 in Federal funding to help upgrade the Spalding County Sheriff Office’s helicopter rescue infrastructure after the County experienced difficulties in emergency response to Hurricanes Helene and Milton, and Sens. Ossoff and Rev. Warnock brought Republicans and Democrats together to help establish a central law enforcement command center in Norcross.

Also, this year, Sen. Ossoff brought Republicans and Democrats together to deliver $1,031,000 in Federal funding to help the Conyers Police Department strengthen emergency response efforts by purchasing new portable radios and a Mobile Command Vehicle.

In 2023, Sen. Ossoff delivered new resources through the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to construct a new hurricane and tornado safe room on Tybee Island, providing a safe area for emergency personnel who must remain on the Island during hurricanes and other disaster situations.

title: Padilla, Carbajal Introduce Legislation to Investigate Toxic Waste Dump Off California Coast
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) and U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-Calif.-24) introduced the Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act, new legislation aimed at addressing the toxic industrial waste and pesticide pollution dumped off the Southern California coast.

DDT (dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane) is a synthetic pesticide that was widely used in the United States beginning in the 1940s to control agricultural pests and disease-carrying insects. In 1972, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) banned most uses of DDT in the United States because of its adverse environmental effects and potential risks to human health.

For decades, industrial waste — including the pesticide DDT — was disposed of in ocean dump sites off California’s coast, particularly in the San Pedro Basin. The Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act establishes a structured federal study to assess the damage to the local marine ecosystem and develop comprehensive solutions to clean up the waste.

“Our communities deserve to know what’s in the water off of the coast of San Pedro and what it means for our health, our fisheries, and our future. By putting NOAA’s scientists and our leading research institutions to work mapping the contamination, tracking how it moves, and exploring cleanup through bioremediation, we can finally address this problem head-on,” said Senator Padilla.

“The San Pedro Basin has long been the site of an underwater toxic waste dump. This toxic waste – which includes the pesticide DDT – has been very harmful to the health of local marine life and poses a risk to people who live and work near these waters,” said Representative Carbajal. “As the representative of California’s Central Coast, I know firsthand how much our communities depend on a healthy ocean – from our fishermen and maritime workers to our tourism and coastal economies. We have a responsibility to protect these waters. I thank Senator Alex Padilla for joining me in introducing this bill as a first step in fixing this environmental tragedy.”

Recent studies have revealed tens of thousands of barrels of DDT and hazardous waste off Southern California, posing potential risks to marine life, fisheries, and public health. For decades, no federal agency has taken responsibility for assessing these dump sites. The Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act would provide the federal coordination and scientific investment needed to address this issue.

“For decades we used the ocean as a dumping ground for all manner of wastes including deeply-concerning industrial byproducts from DDT manufacturing. This proposed legislation takes an important step to address fundamental issues around the disposition, impacts and remediation options for those wastes. While California may be ground zero for this issue, the legislation provides a needed path to take lessons learned off California’s coast and apply them to waste disposal sites that occur along all our Nation’s coastlines,” said David Valentine, Norris Chair and Distinguished Professor of Earth and Marine Science at UCSB.

Specifically, the bill would:

Direct the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to monitor waste sites in the San Pedro Basin;

Study how toxic chemicals like DDT spread into the ocean food web; and

Build scientific tools to track ocean dumping.

NOAA, in coordination with the EPA and Department of Defense, may award grants to academic and research institutions to study:

Spatial mapping of contamination

Co-contaminants and chemical mixtures

Movement, fate, and breakdown processes

Bioaccumulation and biomagnification in ecosystems

The bill also authorizes $6 million annually from Fiscal Year 2026 through Fiscal Year 2032 to carry out these critical activities.

Padilla has been a strong advocate of protecting California’s coast. Last month, he led House and Senate colleagues in filing an amicus brief challenging the Trump Administration’s efforts to restart the Sable oil pipeline off the Santa Barbara coast. In June, Padilla and U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced legislation to establish strict standards for offshore oil and gas operators and set requirements to hold them responsible for decommissioning and cleanup efforts off the coast. In April, Padilla pressed Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, highlighting that the Trump Administration’s plans to drill off of California’s coast coupled with proposed cuts to funding for environmental programs and enforcement will endanger the coastline, the people who live there, and coastal economies.

title: Padilla Joins Cortez Masto, Wyden, Durbin in Demanding Trump Administration Abandon Proposed Plan to Strip Tax Credits from 700,000 Taxpayers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, joined Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), and Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) in demanding the Trump Administration withdraw a proposed rule that would prevent up to 700,000 Deferred Action on Childhood Arrivals (DACA) and Temporary Protected Status (TPS) recipients and other tax-paying immigrants from claiming tax credits they are eligible for.

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Department of the Treasury are proposing a rule change that would prevent hundreds of thousands of taxpayers from claiming the Adoption Tax Credit, the American Opportunity Tax Credit, the Child Tax Credit, and the Earned Income Tax Credit. DACA and TPS recipients have been lawfully filing their taxes and claiming these credits for decades. In their letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and IRS CEO Frank Bisignano, the Senators expressed concern over the proposed rule.

“According to your own estimates, the proposed rule change could affect up to 700,000 taxpayers,” wrote the Senators. “This would include more than 300,000 individuals living in households with a DACA recipient, two-thirds of whom are U.S. citizens and who have, on average, lived in the United States for over 28 years. The practical effect of these new regulations would be to deny tax credits to immigrants who are legally eligible for them and lawfully present in our country, and to create a byzantine and unworkable system for both tax preparers and taxpayers.”

“The Administration has no legal authority to change congressionally enacted tax law via regulation…” the Senators continued. “Since the passage of PRWORA in 1996, no federal agency has interpreted refundable tax credits as federal public benefits restricted to qualified immigrants. If Congress intended for refundable tax credits to be treated as federal public benefits, it has had over 30 years to clarify the statute.”

“The proposed rule is clear regulatory overreach that would have disastrous impacts for lawfully present immigrants and their families who are legally eligible for refundable tax credits,” concluded the Senators.

In addition to Padilla, Cortez Masto, Wyden, and Durbin, the letter was signed by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), and Patty Murray (D-Wash.)

Last year, during consideration of the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” Padilla filed amendments related to restoring eligibility for the child tax credit to all taxpayers and to removing social security number requirements for various tax credits and benefits discussed in the letter. In July, Padilla and Cortez Masto led their colleagues in filing a bicameral amicus brief urging the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit to uphold a lower court’s order blocking ICE from using — or even viewing — tens of thousands of taxpayers’ addresses found to be illegally obtained from the IRS. Padilla and Durbin also sent a letter to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin urging them to halt improper $1.8 million fines on law-abiding immigrants. In June, Padilla and Durbin led over 50 colleagues in objecting to the Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA)’s recent decision to weaken legal protections for DACA recipients.

Full letter is available here.

title: Padilla, Schiff Press Big Tech CEOs on Social Media Platforms’ Efforts to Combat Election Disinformation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla, Ranking Member of the Senate Rules and Administration Committee, and Adam Schiff (both-D-Calif.), pressed the top executives of the largest social media companies about their plans to combat misinformation and disinformation on their platforms ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

“Today, election mis and disinformation remains a serious danger to American democracy and Americans’ right to vote, even more so because of the Trump Administration’s sustained efforts to diminish the public’s trust in elections across the county, including California,” wrote the Senators. “Nowhere is that more clear than in the Administration’s efforts to influence and deter mail-in voting… As a result, Congress must conduct rigorous oversight over dangerous election mis and disinformation propagated via social media, as we consider investigations and legislation to remedy it and prevent it from happening in current and future elections.”

In their inquiry, the Senators detailed how the Trump Administration’s efforts to sow mistrust in the upcoming elections and advances in artificial intelligence are creating new opportunities for large-scale election mis- and disinformation. The Senators highlighted the need for social media companies to do their part to protect election integrity. They also emphasized that in recent years, the companies have continued to retreat from the responsibility of ensuring that information online is accurate.

“We take our constitutional duty to protect shared democratic principles seriously. Your thorough and prompt responses to these inquiries are required for these efforts, as they will inform our work on legislative solutions to strengthen federal elections and combat large-scale mis and disinformation,” continued the Senators. “Platforms that condone, support, or advance efforts to disenfranchise U.S. voters will be scrutinized and held accountable, including through oversight and potential legislation.”

The Senators demanded answers about the companies’ policies to identify and respond to election mis- and disinformation, what actions they will be taking for the 2026 midterm elections, including the steps they will take to ensure that the Supreme Court’s mail-in ballot ruling is not subject to mis- and disinformation campaigns that undermine the integrity of mail-in voting, and whether they’ve received requests from the Trump Administration relating to election security. They also requested that the companies preserve all records and communications related to their demands on an ongoing basis.

The inquiry was sent to xAI’s CEO Elon Musk, Google’s CEO Sundar Pichai, TikTok’s CEO Adam Presser, Snap, Inc.’s CEO Evan Spiegel, YouTube’s CEO Neal Mohan, Meta Platform’s CEO Mark Zuckerberg, and Head of Instagram Adam Mosseri.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee with oversight over federal elections and California’s former Secretary of State, Padilla has been a vocal leader in protecting our elections amid the Trump Administration’s election interference efforts. Last month, Padilla and Congressman Joe Morelle (D-N.Y.-25), Ranking Member of the House Administration Committee, demanded the Trump Administration immediately restore funding to the Election Infrastructure Information Sharing and Analysis Center (EI-ISAC), which helps state and local election officials protect federal elections from cybersecurity threats and election mis- and disinformation campaigns. In August, Padilla and Senator Mark Warner (D-Va.) called for prediction market companies to take immediate action to protect election integrity and end relationships with paid influencers on their platforms spreading election disinformation.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Mr. Musk, Mr. Presser, Mr. Mohan, Mr. Mosseri, Mr. Pichai, Mr. Spiegel, and Mr. Zuckerberg:

We are writing to seek information regarding your plans to combat misinformation and disinformation on your social media platforms during the 2026 midterm elections. As you know, the Supreme Court recently rejected mail ballot restrictions proposed by the Trump Administration. This is now the law of the land, and it is your responsibility to ensure that widespread mis and disinformation about our electoral system does not take hold on your platforms.

In 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, we led members of Congress in writing to your companies regarding the spread of mis and disinformation on your platforms leading up to the 2024 elections. Despite the ongoing spread of false and misleading content on social media sites, your companies have for years “retreated from some of [your] past commitments to promote election integrity.”

Today, election mis and disinformation remains a serious danger to American democracy and Americans’ right to vote, even more so because of the Trump Administration’s sustained efforts to diminish the public’s trust in elections across the county, including California. Nowhere is that more clear than in the Administration’s efforts to influence and deter mail-in voting. For example, on September 15, 2026, President Trump reacted angrily to the Supreme Court’s 7-2 decision with a false claim that mail-in voting is “totally corrupt and out of control.” President Trump even criticized his own Supreme Court nominees for supposedly “mak[ing] cheating by Radical Left [Democrats], on Mail-In Ballots, a much easier thing to do.”6 As a result, Congress must conduct rigorous oversight over dangerous election mis and disinformation propagated via social media, as we consider investigations and legislation to remedy it and prevent it from happening in current and future elections.

President Trump’s self-serving partisan attacks are not the only new challenge to election integrity. Advances in artificial intelligence and chatbots are creating new opportunities for large-scale election mis and disinformation by both foreign and domestic actors. To be sure, addressing false information about the process of voting is entirely different than censoring a point of view. For example, using social media to tell citizens that Election Day is on Wednesday or that mail-in ballots are illegal is simply election interference. Meanwhile, your companies have continued to retreat from the responsibility of ensuring that information online is accurate. Under the circumstances, Congress has no choice but to carefully scrutinize how social media platforms respond to large-scale election mis and disinformation, both before and after the 2026 midterm elections, which are already underway.

Congress’s Constitutional power to conduct investigations stands on equal footing with its authority to legislate and appropriate. To that end, please provide by October 15, 2026, a detailed written response regarding your company’s current policies to identify and respond to election mis and disinformation and what actions you will be taking for the 2026 midterm elections, along with written answers to the following questions:

What steps are you taking to ensure that the Supreme Court’s clear ruling that state’s mail-in ballot procedures must not be disturbed for the November 2026 midterm elections is not subject to mis and disinformation campaigns that undermine the integrity of mail-in voting? For example, if a campaign alleges that mail-in voting is not permitted in California for the November 2026 midterm elections, how will you ensure that false statement is addressed?

Has your company received any communications from the Trump Administration related to election security or the United States Postal Service’s procedures for mail-in ballots? If so, what instructions or requests did you receive, and how have you engaged with them?

Do you currently have any plans to change your election integrity policies between now and Election Day 2026 (November 3, 2026)? If so, please describe the changes and the reasoning for any particular change.

How will your company address mis and disinformation made by political actors, verified accounts, or synthetic accounts, and how will they be treated differently, if at all, compared to ordinary users?

What are your companies’ plans for keeping Congress fully informed about mis and disinformation campaigns and potential changes in your companies’ election integrity policies?

These records are needed for the U.S. Senate to exercise its essential oversight and legislative functions. We further request that you preserve all records and communications relating to the topics addressed in this letter, from January 1, 2025, to the present and continue preserving such materials on an ongoing basis. This preservation hold applies to all relevant records within your possession and any person or entity representing or purporting to be acting on your behalf. This includes, but is not limited to, records and communications via email, whether official or personal; mobile devices; encrypted or disappearing messaging applications; social media; calendar entries; meeting notes; and voicemail and text messages. To the extent that you use any auto-delete functions, you should immediately suspend auto-delete functions and notify persons with control over potentially relevant records of similar preservation obligations.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We take our constitutional duty to protect shared democratic principles seriously. Your thorough and prompt responses to these inquiries are required for these efforts, as they will inform our work on legislative solutions to strengthen federal elections and combat large-scale mis and disinformation. Platforms that condone, support, or advance efforts to disenfranchise U.S. voters will be scrutinized and held accountable, including through oversight and potential legislation. We look forward to your prompt response, including a written confirmation that you are preserving all records related to this congressional inquiry.

title: Senate Unanimously Passes Bipartisan Padilla, Schiff Bill to Support Over 500 Acres of Tribal Land Management
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — The Senate unanimously passed U.S. Senator Alex Padilla’s (D-Calif.) Pit River Land Transfer Act, a bicameral and bipartisan bill to promote Tribal management of over 500 acres of land in California by transferring federal land to the Pit River Tribe. Padilla introduced the legislation with Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) last year to protect Tribal communities and local environment in surrounding regions.

The Senate passed an amended version of the late Representative Doug LaMalfa’s (R-Calif.-01) companion bill, which now heads back to the House of Representatives for a final vote.

“Senseless conflict and bureaucratic barriers have kept California Tribes from managing their ancestral lands, and it’s past time we take action to help Tribes protect their communities and local environment,” said Senator Padilla. “I am grateful that the Senate unanimously passed this critical bill. We’re another step closer to ensuring the Pit River Tribe can steward the land they have inhabited for countless generations.”

“I am proud to see our legislation to help the Pit River Tribe restore their ancestral homelands and promote Tribal sovereignty pass the Senate,” said Senator Schiff. “This bill will help the Pit River Tribe manage the Four Corners site as their ancestors did.”

The Pit River Tribe consist of 11 autonomous bands traditionally inhabiting the area surrounding the Pit River and its tributaries. They are known for their deep spiritual connection to the land, with a rich cultural heritage centered around fishing, hunting, and seasonal gatherings.

This bill would transfer 557 acres of federal land administered by the United States Forest Service to the Secretary of the Interior to be held in trust for the Pit River Tribe. The Tribe has been actively trying to acquire this land through various governmental processes for over a decade. However, they have experienced a series of delays that have added years to the process.

The proposed land to be transferred is known as the Four Corners Property, located in Shasta County. The Tribe has strong cultural and historical connections to the Four Corners, and they view it as a central landmark of their ancestral lands. In October 1970, members of the Tribe erected a Quonset hut on the Four Corners, staking a peaceful, yet firm claim. That month, over 100 sheriff’s deputies, federal marshals, and forest rangers ordered the occupants to evacuate the property, which eventually resulted in violence and the hospitalization of several Tribal members.

Padilla is a strong advocate for restoring Tribal ownership of ancestral lands. In July, Padilla testified at a Senate Committee on Indian Affairs hearing to advocate for critical water investments for California Tribes. In 2024, the Senate passed Padilla’s Jamul Indian Village Land Transfer Act, which established over 170 acres as trust lands for the benefit of the Jamul Tribe. Under the Biden Administration, a series of Padilla’s bills to restore Tribal stewardship of sacred lands and ensure federal land management laws respected Tribal sovereignty were signed into law. The package included laws to take more than 2,500 acres of land in the San Jacinto Mountains into trust for the Agua Caliente Band of Cahuilla Indians and to place roughly 1,000 acres of federal land located in Humboldt and Siskiyou counties into trust for the Karuk Tribe.

Full text of the Pit River Land Transfer Act is available here.

title: Senate Passes Peters and Cornyn Bipartisan Legislation to Protect Commercial Satellites from Cybersecurity Threats
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Bipartisan legislation led by U.S. Senators Gary Peters (D-MI) and John Cornyn (R-TX) to help commercial satellite owners and operators defend against growing cybersecurity threats has passed in the Senate. Commercial satellites support GPS navigation, weather forecasts, agriculture, scientific research, global communications, and more. The senators’ Satellite Cybersecurity Act of 2025 would help secure these critical satellites against attacks by hackers, foreign adversaries, and cybercriminals that could cause serious disruptions to our economic and national security. The legislation now heads to the House for consideration.

“Commercial satellites are essential to our national security, our economy, and the daily lives of Americans, so we must ensure they are not vulnerable to attacks from cybercriminals and foreign adversaries,” said Senator Peters. “I'm glad that this bipartisan, commonsense legislation has passed the Senate. It’s critically important that the U.S. businesses utilizing commercial satellites receive the support and resources needed to safeguard their satellite systems, especially as cybersecurity threats become more advanced.”

“This legislation would ensure commercial satellite networks are secure against cyber threats and bad actors, and I look forward to it passing the House and heading to the President’s desk soon,” said Senator Cornyn.

The rise of small, affordable satellites has led to a sharp increase in the number of commercial satellites in orbit, but this proliferation has created new risks. Many satellites transmit sensitive data without adequate safeguards, leaving them vulnerable to interception and cyberattacks. Recent studies showed that roughly half of surveyed satellite signals were unencrypted despite the sensitive information or private data they carried.

The Satellite Cybersecurity Act of 2025 requires the Department of Commerce, in coordination with other federal agencies, to develop voluntary cybersecurity recommendations tailored to satellites. It directs the Department of Commerce to create a publicly available online clearinghouse so companies can easily access best practices and information to secure their systems. The legislation also requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to examine efforts to secure commercial satellites from cybersecurity threats, identify any duplication of effort, and assess how satellite systems integrate into critical infrastructure sectors.

The legislation is supported by the Satellite Industry Association and the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI).

Peters continues to lead efforts to ensure our nation is equipped to defend against cyberattacks. Peters’ historic, bipartisan provision to require critical infrastructure owners and operators to report if they experience a substantial cyberattack, or if they make a ransomware payment, was signed into law. Peters’ bipartisan bills to enhance cybersecurity assistance to K-12 educational institutions, bolster cybersecurity for state and local governments, strengthen the federal cybersecurity workforce, and help secure federal information technology supply chains have also been signed into law.
