title: Husted bill to stop human trafficking passes Senate, heads to president’s desk
text:
“Human trafficking is a national tragedy, and we need to do everything we can to stop it.”

View Husted’s remarks here.

WASHINGTON – Sens. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), Chairman of the U.S. House Education and Workforce Committee Tim Walberg (R-Mich.) and Rep. Lucy McBath’s (D-Ga.) bipartisan, bicameral Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act passed the Senate unanimously and is headed to the president’s desk to be signed into law.

This bill directs the Department of Labor (DOL) to train its employees to identify human trafficking and refer suspected trafficking crimes to law enforcement. While DOL employees are on the ground conducting workplace inspections, they will be able to spot human trafficking behavior in real time.

“Human trafficking is a national tragedy, and we need to do everything we can to stop it. This law will help ensure federal workers are equipped to spot the signs of human trafficking and refer suspected crimes to law enforcement. I’m proud this bill will be my fourth bill signed into law since I took office. This is a great example of the bipartisan work we can accomplish for the American people, and I look forward to the lives this law will help save,” said Husted.

“The fight against human trafficking should never be a partisan issue. Survivors and victims in Michigan and across the country are owed justice, accountability, and meaningful action to prevent these crimes from happening in the first place. Our bipartisan bill, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act, provides the Department of Labor with the necessary framework to address these unthinkable crimes head-on. I am proud to have worked alongside my colleagues to get this important legislation passed and look forward to seeing it signed into law,” said Slotkin.

“Human trafficking can hide in plain sight, and this bill will help more people recognize the warning signs. I’m glad the Senate unanimously passed my bill and sent it to President Trump’s desk. By giving Department of Labor employees the right training, we can help identify victims sooner and get potential cases to law enforcement,” said Walberg.

“Human trafficking is a devastating crime that preys on the most vulnerable and robs victims of their freedom and dignity. We have a responsibility to ensure that those on the front lines in our communities and across the federal government have the tools necessary to help combat this crime and provide survivors with a path to safety. Strengthening training for Department of Labor employees is an important step toward recognizing the signs of human trafficking, protecting victims, and connecting them with the resources they need. I thank my colleagues for their support,” said McBath.

The Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act passed the Senate unanimously.

In 2024, law enforcement recorded 334 human trafficking cases involving 509 victims in Ohio.

This bill also requires the DOL to submit a report to Congress detailing its training and referral efforts no later than one year after the DOL implements the program.

Walberg introduced the companion bill to the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking in the House of Representatives. The bill passed the House on March 3, 2026.

title: Husted visits Nationwide Children’s Hospital in Columbus, Kitchen Collective in Portsmouth, and Ohio small businesses
text:
“From supporting healthy pregnancies and child development to investing in our communities and helping small businesses grow, these investments make a real difference for Ohio families and workers.”

COLUMBUS – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) today visited Nationwide Children’s Hospital in Columbus and Kitchen Collective in Portsmouth to highlight how federal investments are supporting Ohio families. He also visited two Ohio small businesses to hear directly about the challenges they are facing.

“Healthy families are the cornerstone of a strong America. From supporting healthy pregnancies and child development to investing in our communities and helping small businesses grow, these investments make a real difference for Ohio families and workers,” said Husted.

At Nationwide Children’s Hospital, Husted joined Rep. Mike Carey (R-Ohio), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Administrator Tom Engels and Deputy Administrator Margaret Bush to highlight how federal investments through the Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting (MIECHV) Programsupport healthier pregnancies and stronger families.

The event highlighted HRSA’s $525 million investment in FY 2026 MIECHV Program awards to support evidence-based home visiting services in all 50 states, which Husted supported in the U.S. Senate.

“Small businesses are the backbone of communities across Ohio, and we need to make it easier for them to grow, invest and create jobs. I’ll continue working to make sure Ohio’s entrepreneurs have the tools and resources they need to succeed,” said Husted.

In Portsmouth, Husted visited Kitchen Collective, a nonprofit shared-use commercial kitchen and event space in downtown Portsmouth, to discuss how federal investments he helped secure will support the renovation of two downtown buildings and address local housing affordability.

Husted also visited Adam’s Flying Pig Coffee House in Wheelersburg and The Shakery: Eats & Treats in Ironton to hear directly from small business owners about the challenges they face and discuss his work in the Senate to support Ohio’s small businesses.

These visits build on Husted’s work to help Ohio workers, manufacturers and small businesses. In the Senate, Husted is supporting:

Made in America Manufacturing Financing Act: This bill would expand access to growth capital for small U.S.-based manufacturers.

Investing in All of America Act: This bill would expand access to capital for small businesses in rural and low-income communities, as well as those in the manufacturing and critical technology sectors.

AI for Mainstreet Act: This bill would provide training, guidance and support to American small businesses looking to implement AI into their businesses.

Repealing Big Brother Overreach Act: This bill would eliminate the requirement for small businesses to report beneficial ownership information to the Treasury Department, which is burdensome and overreaching.

Husted also supported the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, which includes major provisions for small businesses and their workforce:

Cuts taxes on tips and overtime, saving tipped and overtime workers up to $1,750 per year.

Makes the 20% small business tax deduction permanent.

This will deliver $4,600 in average tax relief to 8 million entrepreneurs around the country.

This will create 1.2 million jobs annually for the next 10 years.

Doubles the small business expensing limits for new investments in machinery, equipment and software.

Includes a $7,000 tax cut for 12 million small business owners.

title: Kelly, Gallego Celebrate Committee Passage of Bill to Restore the Grand Canyon’s North Rim
text:
Last week, Arizona Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego celebrated the unanimous passage of the North Rim Restoration Act out of the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources (ENR). The legislation addresses recovery efforts of the North Rim at the Grand Canyon after the devastating Dragon Bravo Fire in 2025.

If enacted, the legislation would streamline the restoration process by granting National Park Service (NPS) emergency contracting authority to bypass standard delays and accelerate renewals. The legislation covers fire-related recovery efforts, including forest management, maintenance, rebuilding, and infrastructure improvements. This would allow the NPS to quickly hire, approve, and oversee contractors for cleanup and reconstruction efforts.

“Rebuilding the North Rim of the Grand Canyon is critical for the communities and small businesses that depend on it,” said Kelly. “We’re one step closer to cutting red tape, restoring the park, and bringing visitors back to the area.”

“The Grand Canyon is not only a marvel to look at—the tourists it attracts act as the economic engine for rural communities in Northern Arizona. These communities have been devastated by the Dragon Bravo fire and need help now,” said Gallego. “I urge the full Senate to take up this bill and provide the resources needed to get these communities back on their feet.”

“We applaud Senators Kelly and Gallego’s support of Representative Crane’s North Rim Restoration Act and its passage through committee. The bill’s passage by unanimous consent represents a critical bipartisan step by Congress to ensure we move as quickly and thoughtfully as possible to rebuild the Grand Canyon’s North Rim. We look forward to working with Senators Gallego and Kelly, Representative Crane, and the full Arizona delegation to ensure Representative Crane’s bill becomes law, and the funding for the rebuild is duly and expeditiously allocated. This will allow federal agencies to quickly begin work and restore the communities hit hardest by the economic hardship,” said Ethan Aumack, Executive Director Grand Canyon Trust.

Background:

In July of 2025, the Dragon Bravo fire initiated following lightning strikes on the North Rim in Grand Canyon National Park, burning thousands of acres of National Park Service land. Over 100 structures were destroyed, including the historic Grand Canyon Lodge, several historic cabins and the North Rim Visitor Center in the Grand Canyon National Park, and a wastewater treatment plant, resulting in a chlorine gas leak.

Since then, Kelly has led efforts to support impacted communities and restore access. In August of 2025, he visited the Grand Canyon to observe the burn scar and meet with local business owners about the economic toll. Alongside Gallego, Kelly also demanded answers on the federal government’s handling of the fire.

title: Kelly, Whitehouse Press EPA, AI Companies on Rollback of Public Input Rules for Data Center Air Permits
text:
U.S. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), members of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works, sent two letters opposing the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) proposal to eliminate the 30-day mandatory public notice period that allows communities to provide input on proposed facilities, like data centers, that may affect the air they breathe.

One letter is addressed to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin urging him to withdraw the proposed rule; the other letter is addressed to nine major data center companies—Anthropic, AWS, Fermi, Google, Joule, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and xAI—calling on them to maintain current public participation standards regardless of the rule’s outcome.

“We agree that permitting should be efficient, predictable, and capable of supporting the infrastructure our country needs. But faster permitting should not come at the expense of transparency or communities’ ability to shape the decisions that affect them,” wrote the senators to Administrator Zeldin.

“Data center companies like yours also have a responsibility not to use weaker requirements to limit public participation or communities’ ability to meaningfully shape decisions that affect them,” wrote the senators to thedata centercompanies. “America can build the infrastructure needed to compete and innovate while keeping communities informed and involved in the decisions that affect them.”

In addition to Kelly and Whitehouse, the letter to the EPA was co-signed by Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Edward Markey (D-MA), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

In addition to Kelly and Whitehouse, the letter to the data companies was co-signed by Ron Wyden (D-OR), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

Read the full letter to the EPA here.

title: King, Colleagues Call on HHS to Prioritize 40-Year Independent Task Record of Prevention Task Force
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — U.S. Senator Angus King (I-ME), alongside Senators Patty Murray (D-WA) and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), is leading a group of his colleagues in criticizing recent actions and calling on the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to prioritize the 40-year independent track record of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF). In their letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., the senators ask him to explain his abrupt overhaul of the USPSTF, appointing eight new members whose qualifications fall short of the traditional standards.

More specifically, the senators explain how a refusal to share information on the decision-making process, and a shift in membership from primary care professionals to specialists, jeopardizes the independence and capabilities of the Task Force. This letter to HHS builds upon Senator King’s defense of USPSTF earlier this year, previously reaching out to Secretary Kennedy to urge the department to prioritize science and data backed preventive medicine, as well as introducing a resolution last year affirming support for the Task Force.

The senators begin their letter, “The Task Force membership historically has been comprised of experts in clinical medicine, scientific research, and public health, who are extensively vetted for conflicts of interest. USPSTF’s process for developing recommendations and its agenda is transparent to the public and based on high-quality and unbiased scientific evidence. Thus, the Task Force’s recommendations can be considered neutral, unbiased, and evidence-based by all stakeholders.”

“Given the background of many of the new members, we have strong concerns about the Task Force’s ability to make independent, evidence-based recommendations. Specialists have always contributed to the Task Force's evidence reviews, and they should. But the Task Force's work is broad and spans the full range of clinical preventive services, for every age group, and it has historically drawn on people trained in primary care, prevention, and evidence-based medicine,” the senators continued. “As five of the eight new members are specialists, we are concerned about the types of recommendations and direction of the Task Force in focusing on patient care and clinical preventive services.

The senators concluded, “We look forward to hearing from you in response to these questions, and urge that the administration prioritize resuming the cost- and life-saving work of the Task Force while adhering to the evidence-based and scientifically informed processes that have ensured the historic credibility of USPSTF.”

Long known as the ‘Prevention Senator,’ King has worked on policy solutions that keep Maine people healthy and lower the costs for patients and providers alike. Last year, he introduced the Preventive Health Savings Act which would instruct the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to fully study the costs and benefits that could be seen with proposed preventive health care legislation. He has previously introduced legislation requiring private insurance plans to cover three annual primary care visits and three annual outpatient mental health or outpatient substance use disorder treatment visits, without charging a copayment, coinsurance, or deductible-related fee. In doing so, this legislation also would catch smaller, or early health symptoms before they become larger threats requiring more extensive and expensive treatments.

Senator King also introduced the ‘Stand Strong’ legislative package, which included the Stand Strong Falls Prevention Act that would require the development of a National Falls Prevention Plan, the Preventive Home Visits Act, which would provide Medicare coverage for qualified care providers to assess the safety of seniors’ homes, and the Wellness and Education for Longer Lives (WELL) for Seniors Act, which would improve Medicare’s Annual Wellness Visit to encourage seniors and their physicians to work together and confront health issues before they become more serious.

In addition to King, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Patty Murray (D-WA), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Jack Reed (D-RI), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Lisa Blunt-Rochester (D-DE), Ed Markey (D-MA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), and Ben Ray Lujan (D-NM).

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

+++

Dear Secretary Kennedy,

We write today to express our alarm and strong concern regarding the status of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (the Task Force or USPSTF). Last week, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) announced the appointment of eight new Task Force members, including five specialists – a major break from the historic makeup of USPSTF membership that is typically comprised of preventionists and primary care practitioners. The Task Force has also not met for a year-and-a-half – the first time it’s not met consistently in at least a decade – delaying critical decisions that directly impact the health of Americans. We write to seek clarity on recent actions, including how they will inform the future work of USPSTF and how the Task Force will continue to adhere to principles of independence and scientific rigor.

The Task Force membership historically has been comprised of experts in clinical medicine, scientific research, and public health, who are extensively vetted for conflicts of interest. USPSTF’s process for developing recommendations and its agenda is transparent to the public and based on high-quality and unbiased scientific evidence. Thus, the Task Force’s recommendations can be considered neutral, unbiased, and evidence-based by all stakeholders.

Going back to at least 2002, HHS under Democrats and Republicans (including under President Trump’s first term) has consistently used either the same format through the Federal Register or the Task Force’s website to announce and solicit requests for nominations. Qualification requirements to be an appointed member of the Task Force was derived from expertise in primary care and prevention medicine.

We were particularly alarmed by the April 23, 2026, Federal Register notice, both for the change in nominee parameters as well as the timeline. AHRQ sought nominations of physician specialists in areas well outside of primary care and preventive medicine, including practitioners in anesthesiology/pain management, cardiology, hematology/oncology, radiology, and surgery, among others. Specialists have always played a role in Task Force operations as consultants, though in part to preclude any conflict of interest that they may have through prescribing an intervention.

The extremely truncated nominations timeline was also incredibly concerning. The process for reviewing nominees historically took a year, with three months to collect nominees. The April 2026 Federal Register Notice gave one month’s notice, for appointments to potentially begin in June 2026. This rushed process not only calls into question the seriousness of this nominations process, but also whether the Members ultimately selected were pre-determined.

In addition to seriously problematic changes to the solicitation notice, the transparency of the selection process was marred from the start. The Chair and leadership of the Task Force historically review and make recommendations to the Secretary for new appointments to USPSTF. On May 19, 2026, the Task Force Chair and Vice Chair were fired because they were supposedly unlawfully appointed per the Braidwood decision. If Braidwood had made such a declaration, the Chair and Vice Chair would have been fired immediately or shortly thereafter the June 2025 decision.

By removing the leadership of the Task Force, this recent appointment process lacked political independence and transparency, expert and historic perspective of Task Force qualifications, and ultimately diminished the integrity of USPSTF. Incredibly, it is unclear how these new members currently adhere (if at all) to the historic rigorous conflict of interest standards of Task Force membership. As of writing today, the Conflict of Interest disclosures page – where individual Members’ disclosures were historically published – is barren and inactive, which gives us serious concern regarding the independence of these new members.

Given the background of many of the new members, we have strong concerns about of the Task Force’s ability to make independent, evidence-based recommendations. Specialists have always contributed to the Task Force's evidence reviews, and they should. But the Task Force's work is broad and spans the full range of clinical preventive services, for every age group, and it has historically drawn on people trained in primary care, prevention, and evidence-based medicine. As five of the eight new members are specialists, we are concerned about the types of recommendations and direction of the Task Force in focusing on patient care and clinical preventive services.

Finally, in addition to the new direction of the Task Force, we have serious concerns about the capability of USPSTF to conduct its incredibly important work given the major cuts that have occurred at its supporting organization, Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ). The Task Force’s evidence reviews are conducted by career staff at AHRQ. Approximately 80 percent of AHRQ staff have been fired or left the Agency without being replaced and there are reportedly less than 2 experts directly working at AHRQ to support the Task Force’s work. We have strong concerns that the Task Force will be able to develop evidence-based and credible recommendations without an adequate support staff.

As you’ll recall, we were joined by a number of our colleagues in writing to you earlier this year, for which we have still not received a response from you. Therefore, given these seriously concerning actions, we request a response to our previous letter and to the following questions by October 15, 2026:

What is the scientific and evidence-based justification for changes to the makeup of Task Force membership to move away from primary care and preventive medical experts to specialists?

Transitioning from a three-month public solicitation plus months-long review process to a two-month-long whole review and selection process is incredibly concerning.

What was the justification for shortening the Task Force member selection review timeline?

Did HHS or AHRQ review candidates prior to the April 2026 Federal Register notice?

What is the legal justification for having removed the Chair and Vice Chair of the Task Force in May 2026?

Where specifically in the Braidwood decision does it discuss that the then-Chair and -Vice Chair were unlawfully appointed?

What is the justification for not publicizing the conflict of interest disclosures of the newly appointed Task Force members?

How is Congress, the medical community, and the public expected to have faith in the independence of the Task Force going forward?

The staff support for the Task Force at AHRQ has been diminished. How does HHS expect the Task Force to develop credible recommendations without adequate support?

We look forward to hearing from you in response to these questions, and urge that the administration prioritize resuming the cost- and life-saving work of the Task Force while adhering to the evidence-based and scientifically informed processes that have ensured the historic credibility of USPSTF.

Sincerely,

###

title: Lankford, Rep. Smith Lead Over 100 Lawmakers in Letter Urging HHS Inspector General to Investigate Planned Parenthood
text:
OKLAHOMA CITY, OK — US Senator James Lankford (R-OK), Chair of the Senate Values Action Team, and Representative Chris Smith (R-NJ-04) recently led 128 Members of Congress in sending a letter to the Inspector General (IG) of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), urging the IG to review and investigate the activities and federal funding streams of Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc. and its affiliates.

“Serious concerns have long been raised regarding the organization’s compliance with applicable federal laws, regulations, and program requirements governing the receipt and use of federal funds,” the Republican lawmakers wrote. “In particular, these concerns relate to whether Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc. and the organization’s affiliates have adhered to applicable requirements governing program integrity, financial accountability, and the proper use of funds provided through HHS-administered programs,” they continued.

The lawmakers argue these concerns warrant a comprehensive review of Planned Parenthood’s use of federal funds and compliance with federal law.

“Congress has taken action to ensure taxpayer dollars are not funding organizations that perform abortions, but our work to protect taxpayers and ensure federal law is followed does not stop there,” said Lankford. “Planned Parenthood and its affiliates have faced serious allegations involving the use of federal funds and compliance with federal law. Those allegations deserve a thorough review. The HHS Inspector General should follow the facts, determine whether federal laws and funding requirements have been violated, and hold accountable anyone who has misused taxpayer dollars.”

“Planned Parenthood should not receive taxpayer dollars. Since 1970, it has killed over ten million unborn babies in its clinics—and today exterminates over 1,000 unborn babies every single day,” said Smith. “Moreover, as the author of our Nation’s first anti-human trafficking law, the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 (TVPA) (PL 106-386), I remain deeply concerned by Live Action’s credible accusations against Planned Parenthood involving its affiliates’ enabling of human sex trafficking. In addition to reports of covering up and perpetuating sexual exploitation and abuse, Planned Parenthood has been haunted by allegations of trafficking fetal tissue, fraudulently using federal funds, and violating health codes. Aided by allies in Congress, the media, and academia, Planned Parenthood has largely escaped scrutiny and accountability, all while fostering a culture of death, denial, disrespect and discrimination against babies. It is long overdue for a comprehensive investigation and review, and I urge the HHS OIG to look closely to determine whether it has violated federal standards for federal funding recipients.”

Background

The letter follows a recent Small Business Administration (SBA) investigation into whether Planned Parenthood affiliates improperly received approximately $88 million in loans through the Paycheck Protection Program during the COVID-19 pandemic. The lawmakers are also raising concerns about additional allegations involving fraud, false statements, potential violations of federal criminal law, and failures to disclose potential violations to the federal government.

The lawmakers are asking the HHS Inspector General to review the federal funds Planned Parenthood and its affiliates have received and determine whether they were used in accordance with federal law. They also urged the Inspector General to coordinate with other federal oversight agencies, including the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), as needed.

Joining Lankford in sending the letter are Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-TN), Katie Britt (R-AL), Ted Budd (R-NC), Kevin Cramer (R-ND), Mike Crapo (R-ID), Ted Cruz (R-TX), Steve Daines (R-MT), Joni Ernst (R-IA), Deb Fischer (R-NE), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS), Jim Justice (R-WV), Mike Lee (R-UT), Cynthia Lummis (R-WY), Roger Marshall (R-KS), Bernie Moreno (R-OH), Pete Ricketts (R-NE), James Risch (R-ID), Mike Rounds (R-SD), Rick Scott (R-FL), and Tommy Tuberville (R-AL). Joining Smith in the House are 105 additional Representatives.

Merkley, Curtis Lead New Bipartisan Bill to Honor Fallen Wildland Firefighters
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley (D-OR) and John Curtis (R-UT) announced the introduction of the Honoring Fallen Wildland Firefighters Act. This groundbreaking legislation would expand death benefits of fallen firefighters to match the up to $100,000 provided to fallen members of the military, a significant change from the maximum death benefit of $10,000 currently available for survivors of federally employed wildland firefighters killed in the line of duty.

“Wildland firefighters put their lives on the fireline to protect our communities, and we must honor these heroes who make the ultimate sacrifice while keeping us safe,” said Merkley. “Our Honoring Fallen Wildland Firefighters Act expands death benefits to the survivors of fallen firefighters, ensuring their families will be taken care of if their loved one is killed in the line of duty. We must do all we can to support our firefighters who risk so much in their service to communities in Oregon and across the nation.”

“Wildland firefighters willingly put themselves in harm’s way to protect our homes, communities, and public lands. When one of these brave men or women makes the ultimate sacrifice, we have an obligation to stand behind the family they leave behind,” said Curtis. “The current death benefit does not reflect the sacrifice of a fallen firefighter or the debt we owe their loved ones. Our bipartisan bill ensures these families receive the same level of support we provide to the families of fallen military servicemembers.”

The bipartisan Honoring Fallen Wildland Firefighters Act would:

Amend the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act to establish a new death benefit for individuals serving as wildland firefighters, on par with that available to members of the military.

Ensure any individual serving as a wildland firefighter is eligible for this death benefit—whether they are a contractor or federal, state, or local employee.

In the Senate, Merkley and Curtis have teamed up to lead a series of bipartisan bills to tackle the worst impacts of wildfires, including the Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act to streamline the use of prescribed burns and the Wildland Firefighter Health and Safety Act to address the long-overdue gaps in health and safety protections that wildland firefighters receive.

The bipartisan Honoring Fallen Wildland Firefighters Act is supported by the National Federation of Federal Employees (NFFE), Wildland Firefighter Foundation, National Association of State Foresters, Grassroots Wildland Firefighters, National Alliance of Forest Owners, National Wildfire Suppression Association, Climate and Wildfire Institute, American Forest Resource Council, United Aerial Firefighters Association, Western Fire Chiefs Association, and Firefighters United for Safety, Ethics, and Ecology (FUSEE).

“Every day, wildland firefighters risk their lives to defend American communities from the wildfire crisis,” said NFFE National President Randy Erwin. “As wildfires become increasingly dangerous and more frequent, the risk of being killed in the line of duty also rises for these brave men and women. It is important that every wildland firefighter has the peace of mind that if they pass away while on the job, their family will be taken care of. Thank you to Senators Merkley and Curtis for your commitment to honoring those who make the ultimate sacrifice.”

“Wildland firefighters put their lives on the line to protect communities and public lands from increasingly dangerous wildfires. When a firefighter does not make it home, their family should not have to face financial uncertainty on top of unimaginable loss. The Honoring Fallen Wildland Firefighters Act recognizes the tremendous risks these firefighters take and provides their families with the support they deserve,” said Timothy Ingalsbee, Executive Director of Firefighters United for Safety, Ethics, and Ecology (FUSEE).

Full text of the Honoring Fallen Wildland Firefighters Act can be found by clicking here.

title: Senator Moody Fights to Protect Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody is fighting to protect an important national military asset in Northwest Florida. Senator Moody has joined Senator Rick Scott in championing the Protecting Florida’s Offshore Military Readiness Act to prohibit drilling oil and gas inside the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range.

“The Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range is a national military asset that can’t be replicated anywhere else in the world, and the work done there directly shapes the lethality of our future military. I’m proud to join Senator Scott on the Protecting Florida’s Offshore Military Readiness Act to keep the range as exactly what it was intended to be—a testing ground. Protecting Eglin is about our national security, and it’s about preserving the Gulf Coast Floridians love,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

“The federal government’s first priority is to keep the American people safe. That means our military needs the irreplaceable value that the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range provides to our warfighters. Protecting the range means protecting America’s military readiness. I am glad to have Sen. Moody’s support on this bill, and I look forward to working with President Trump and his administration to use every tool we have to deliver more abundant, cheap energy while ensuring our military remains the most lethal fighting force on Earth,” said Senator Rick Scott.

BACKGROUND:

The legislation aims to protect the critical Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range from interference that could hamper the U.S. Department of War’s ability to maintain readiness in the Gulf of America.

The EGTTR is a key national security asset that provides the U.S. military with vital air, sea, and joint testing and training capabilities.

Senator Moody is a proud supporter of the U.S. Armed Forces, veterans, and military families.

Senator Moody recently joined the Senate Armed Services Committee.

Last year, Senator Moody recognized 200 years of U.S. Navy presence in Pensacola and discussed the critical importance of the Navy and Coast Guard’s presence in the Florida Panhandle.

Senator Moody has long fought for Florida’s military members. As Florida Attorney General, Moody oversaw the Military and Veterans Assistance Program to assist servicemembers, veterans and their families who encounter scams or fraud.

Senator Moody is proud to be part of a military family.

title: Moreno Blasts Anthropic CEO for Hypocritical Approach to Super Intelligence
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) sent a letter to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calling out the hypocrisy of Anthropic’s plans to IPO, tying millions of Americans’ hard earned dollars to the company’s success, while simultaneously claiming his technology could lead to human extinction. In his letter, Senator Moreno urged Mr. Amodei to follow the White House’s lead and focus on the ways that Super Intelligence (“SI”) can be used to improve the lives of Americans and defend against real, SI-enabled threats.

“These questions are even more consequential as Anthropic prepares to go public and invite millions of Americans to tie their financial futures to the development and success of your company’s technology,” wrote Senator Moreno. “With investors discussing a valuation approaching $2 trillion (about 42 times Anthropic’s revenue and double what the company was worth four months ago), and trading expected as soon as October 2026, Anthropic’s entrance into the public market will be one of the largest in history. While I applaud any company that gives hardworking Americans access to its success, I do not understand how you can ask them to invest their hard-earned savings in Anthropic’s continued development while warning those same Americans that your product could ultimately lead to their extinction.”

Read the full text of the letter HERE or below.

October 5, 2026

Mr. Dario Amodei

Chief Executive Officer

Anthropic PBC

548 Market Street

San Francisco, CA 94104

Dear Mr. Amodei,

Anthropic, PBC (“Anthropic”) maintains a leading presence in the Super Intelligence (“SI”) ecosystem. As Anthropic’s co-founder and a prominent public voice on SI, you, Mr. Amodei, are viewed by the American public and policymakers as one of the technology’s principal stewards. The systems Anthropic is developing could change the American way of life forever. With great power comes great responsibility, and in this case, I am concerned that you are failing to meet the moment.

Anthropic’s recent actions and statements reflect an alarmist approach to SI that places extraordinary emphasis on the technology’s most catastrophic outcomes. As you know, SI researcher Jacob Coxon recently quit his job at Anthropic and accused your company and its business rival, OpenAI, of “gambling with our lives.” Mr. Coxon publicized his exit on Twitter, claiming, “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt. If anything, many executives and senior researchers will couch their phrasing in the press to sound sensible – but I hear the same people express fear privately. No other human activity poses this level of danger.”

That same day, one of Anthropic’s top safety experts, Evan Hubinger, agreed with Mr. Coxon, tweeting, “Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade.” A couple of days after these tweets, you appeared on CNN and said, “It’s funny, I agree with Jacob Coxon on far more than I disagree with him.” You have also been on the record as saying that there’s a twenty-five percent chance that developing SI further will go “really, really badly.” These statements, which include your own words, indicate that your instinct is to wreak havoc on the public SI discourse. Yet your panic-inducing commentary frames SI as an existential threat without providing information to the American people about how SI technology can also be used to combat and defend against the very safety threats you emphasize.

These questions are even more consequential as Anthropic prepares to go public and invite millions of Americans to tie their financial futures to the development and success of your company’s technology. With investors discussing a valuation approaching $2 trillion (about 42 times Anthropic’s revenue and double what the company was worth four months ago), and trading expected as soon as October 2026, Anthropic’s entrance into the public market will be one of the largest in history. While I applaud any company that gives hardworking Americans access to its success, I do not understand how you can ask them to invest their hard-earned savings in Anthropic’s continued development while warning those same Americans that your product could ultimately lead to their extinction.

I am equally concerned that this focus on potential catastrophic outcomes risks crowding out an equally important public debate: how American SI leadership can strengthen U.S. national security, counter SI-powered attacks from our adversaries, and ensure that the United States, not China, shapes the future of this technology. Rather than highlighting how SI could end humanity, public discourse around SI should focus on developing solutions to the real vulnerabilities SI has found in American critical infrastructure and cybersecurity. We should not unnecessarily metastasize SI ‘doomerism,’ but rather recognize that SI, like any cutting-edge technology, presents risks that must be addressed by companies who are able to rise to the occasion. I am sincerely hopeful you and your company will work to develop and propagate such solutions as opposed to publicly pontificating the worst-case scenario. Adding your signature to the White House Accord on Super Intelligence is a notable first step. I applaud President Trump’s unwavering commitment to American dominance in responsible SI development.

Public discourse around SI should center on how American innovators, working where appropriate with the U.S. government, can harness this technology to strengthen U.S. national security, improve the lives of American people, and position the country to respond to our adversaries’ increasingly sophisticated SI-enabled threats. We must address the risks associated with frontier SI. Doing so does not require halting its development or surrendering American technological dominance. It requires confronting those risks with the same ingenuity and creativity that have defined American innovation for generations.

title: Murphy Departs Qatar After Key Diplomatic Meetings, Including With The Emir Of Qatar
text:
DOHA, QATAR – U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) released the following statements after departing Doha, Qatar on a Congressional Delegation (CODEL) trip to the Middle East, where he will also visit Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

“It’s important for members of the Senate to see the damage that has been done to U.S. facilities firsthand… I’m meeting with regional partners, in particular the Qataris and the Saudis, to talk about the impact of the Iran War… and to pull back and think about what our approach should be to the Gulf going forward,” said Sen. In Qatar, Murphy met with His Highness the Emir of the State of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani.

“There are so many things Qatar does to protect U.S. interests. They host our biggest military base in the region. They house 1000 Afghan refugees (that Trump refuses to let into the U.S.). They were key to getting the hostages out of Gaza. And they are mediators right now in the effort to end the war with Iran. I thanked the Emir for all of this. Qatar is and will remain an essential ally of the United States. Of course, I was also candid with him, in particular regarding my deep concerns about the transfer of the luxury plane. title: Padilla, Booker, Blumenthal Urge Mullin to Immediately Recall ICE Officers Hired During Hiring Surge
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, Cory Booker (D-N.J.), and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) called on Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin to immediately remove from field duty all U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers hired during the Department’s 2025 hiring surge. In an oversight letter that comes days after new reports of the agency’s plans to hire 5,000 new officers before year’s end, the Senators demanded DHS complete comprehensive retraining and re-vetting for all officers hired during the 2025 surge period.

“Over the past year, ICE and other DHS personnel have fatally shot and killed multiple people during vehicle stops and enforcement operations, including several instances in which agents opened fire on people inside their own cars,” wrote the Senators. “These killings, combined with the whistleblower’s account of corners cut on both vetting and training, make clear that officers hired during the surge did not receive adequate instruction in de-escalation, use-of-force standards, and vehicle-stop protocols before being sent into communities with the authority to use deadly force.”

Republicans poured $75 billion into ICE through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and then added another $38.5 billion more this summer, allowing ICE to hire thousands of new officers with incentives including a signing bonus of up to $50,000 and up to $60,000 in student-loan repayment. To meet the hiring demand, the agency lowered hiring standards and cut corners on background checks, raising concerns about unqualified and poorly trained armed officers conducting immigration arrests. Several incidents involving death and violence led to increased calls for oversight by Senate Democrats. ICE is now reportedly preparing for a second hiring surge of 5,000 employees, including deportation officers, before the end of the year – roughly a 17% increase in three months – without having completed background investigations for thousands of hires from the first surge.

The letter follows recent New York Times reporting detailing a formal whistleblower complaint to the DHS Office of Inspector General from a 17-year ICE veteran overseeing background investigations. The complaint alleged that job offers were extended to candidates without completion of basic fingerprint, identity, or credit checks and were evaded by political appointees. In another whistleblower disclosure to the Senate, a former ICE Academy instructor and agency attorney disclosed that ICE cut training hours on use of force, firearms safety, and the constitutional rights of the public during this same period. According to another New York Times report, 7,500 active officers with arrest authority hired during last year’s surge are still awaiting the full background investigations required for their positions.

“DHS cannot allow officers whose backgrounds were never properly vetted, and who may never have received adequate use-of-force training, to remain on the streets with arrest authority and firearms,” concluded the Senators.

In the letter, the Senators also urged DHS to:

Immediately suspend field enforcement duties for all ICE officers hired during the 2025 hiring surge, pending completion of full background checks and training.

Provide a full accounting of how many current ICE officers received job offers or field assignments before completing fingerprint, identity, and credit checks, and how many of those officers have discharged a firearm in the course of duty.

Provide ICE’s 2026 hiring plan, including

All documents, memoranda, internal communications, staffing assessments, and analyses of staffing needs;

The vetting and training protocols; and

The name and title of each official who approved the plan.

Provide a copy of the whistleblower’s complaint and any Office of Inspector General findings or corrective action plan arising from it.

Provide a detailed accounting of the use-of-force policy and vehicle-stop protocol changes DHS has made since January 2026.

Including how those changes have been implemented and audited across ICE field offices.

Padilla has been a leader in holding the Trump Administration accountable for its cruel and reckless mass deportation agenda. Last week, Padilla conducted an unannounced oversight visit to the de facto ICE detention facility at the San Francisco International Airport (SFO). Last month, Padilla called out the Trump Administration’s continued abuses of power and inhumane treatment of detained immigrants, after sounding the alarm on the significant increase in deaths among detainees in ICE custody since January 2025. He also demanded DHS immediately halt its reckless plan to equip ICE officers with electric shock gloves. Padilla also condemned Republicans’ partisan bill to provide ICE and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) with an extra $70 billion without necessary reforms and forced a vote on his amendment that would require ICE officers to wear body cameras while on-duty.

Full letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Mullin:

We write to demand that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) immediately remove from field duty all U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers hired and trained during the 2025 hiring surge, and that those officers be required to complete comprehensive retraining and re-vetting before being permitted to return to enforcement operations. Over the past year, public reporting on DHS’s hiring and training requirements, and the conduct of its officers in the field, demonstrates that ICE officers hired during this surge cannot be trusted with a badge and the authority to make arrests. These concerns are heightened now that ICE is preparing a second hiring surge of 5,000 employees before year’s end without having completed background investigations for thousands of hires from the first.

On September 3, 2026, The New York Times reported that a 17-year ICE veteran who oversaw background investigations made a formal whistleblower complaint last year, expressing concern about a systemic breakdown in the vetting of thousands of ICE recruits brought on during the agency’s rapid expansion. According to the complaint, ICE’s human resources division routinely extended final job offers before candidates had completed basic fingerprint, identity, or credit checks, and political appointees were permitted to bypass standard background investigations to obtain national security eligibility. The complaint, filed with the DHS Office of Inspector General, warned that this unprecedented lowering of hiring standards left the agency vulnerable to insider threats, infiltration, and foreign influence, and it called on DHS to immediately suspend the improper practices, hold accountable those responsible, and review recent hires for potential insider threats. A separate whistleblower, a former ICE Academy instructor and agency attorney, separately disclosed that ICE cut training hours on use of force, firearms safety, and the constitutional rights of the public during this same period.

New reporting confirms that the vetting failures the whistleblower described persist today. On September 29, 2026, The New York Times reported that nearly 7,500 individuals hired during last year’s surge are still awaiting the full background investigations required for their positions, and that they may work on a limited basis in the meantime. ICE had already removed hundreds of surge hires by this spring. Before even addressing this problem, ICE now intends to hire 5,000 more employees by year’s end—a workforce expansion of roughly 17 percent in three months—and most will serve as deportation officers with arrest authority. DHS’s assurances that it will apply rigorous standards to this new cohort cannot be taken at face value when it has not yet cleared the officers it already hired.

These vetting and training failures preceded a series of violent and deadly incidents involving ICE officials. Over the past year, ICE and other DHS personnel have fatally shot and killed multiple people during vehicle stops and enforcement operations, including several instances in which agents opened fire on people inside their own cars:

On January 7, 2026, an ICE officer in Minneapolis, Minnesota fatally shot Renée Good, a 37-year-old mother of three, as she attempted to drive away from agents during an enforcement operation. Witnesses reported that federal officers blocked bystanders and medics from rendering aid.

Less than two weeks later, Border Patrol agents fatally shot Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care nurse, during the same wave of Minneapolis enforcement operations.

On July 7, 2026, an ICE officer in Houston, Texas fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old construction worker and father of three, while he was driving a work crew to a job site. Witnesses have disputed DHS’s account that Mr. Salgado Araujo used his vehicle as a weapon.

Six days later, on July 13, 2026, an ICE officer in Biddeford, Maine fatally shot Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a 25-year-old father, in his car after agents rammed his vehicle and fired multiple rounds through it while executing a warrant for someone else. Mr. Durán Guerrero was not the target of the operation and was authorized to work in the United States.

A review of shootings by federal immigration officers during this Administration found that the overwhelming majority—19 of 22 incidents identified as of July 2026—began with a vehicle stop, underscoring that ICE’s current tactics for approaching and stopping vehicles are placing officers and the public in unnecessary danger. These killings, combined with the whistleblower’s account of corners cut on both vetting and training, make clear that officers hired during the surge did not receive adequate instruction in deescalation, use-of-force standards, and vehicle-stop protocols before being sent into communities with the authority to use deadly force.

DHS cannot allow officers whose backgrounds were never properly vetted, and who may never have received adequate use-of-force training, to remain on the streets with arrest authority and firearms. We therefore request that DHS:

Immediately suspend field enforcement duties for all ICE officers hired and deployed during the 2025 hiring surge, pending completion of full background revetting and use of-force retraining.

Provide a full accounting of how many current ICE officers received job offers or field assignments before completing fingerprint, identity, and credit checks, and how many of those officers have discharged a firearm in the course of duty.

Provide ICE’s plan to hire 5,000 employees by the end of 2026, including all documents, memoranda, internal communications, staffing assessments, and analyses of staffing needs related to the plan; the vetting and training protocols that will apply to the new hires; and the name and title of each official who approved the plan.

Provide a copy of the whistleblower’s complaint and any Office of Inspector General findings or corrective action plan arising from it.

Provide a detailed accounting of the use-of-force policy and vehicle-stop protocol changes DHS has made since January 2026, including how those changes have been implemented and audited across ICE field offices.

Finally, we are deeply concerned by indications that DHS and ICE leadership may not be taking whistleblower complaints seriously. ICE’s public response to this most recent whistleblower complaint focused on defending its vetting practices rather than addressing the substance of the allegations. Whistleblowers who come forward in good faith to report waste, fraud, abuse, or threats to public and national security are protected by federal law, and DHS has an obligation to ensure that employees who raise these concerns through proper channels are not retaliated against, sidelined, or pushed out of the agency. We therefore ask that DHS confirm, in writing, the specific steps it is taking to ensure that whistleblower complaints related to ICE hiring, vetting, and training are investigated promptly, that whistleblowers are protected from retaliation consistent with the Whistleblower Protection Act and related authorities, and that findings are shared with the appropriate oversight bodies, including Congress.

We request a written response to this letter, including responses to the items above, no later than October 13, 2026. Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter.

Sincerely,

###

title: Senate Passes Peters and Slotkin Legislation to Extend Federal Funding and Protections for the Great Lakes
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – The Senate unanimously passed legislation championed by U.S. Senators Gary Peters (MI) and Elissa Slotkin (MI) to protect the Great Lakes and vital waterways across Michigan. The legislation would extend the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative (GLRI), authorizing $475 million in annual funding for the program through 2030. The GLRI combines federal and nonfederal efforts to stop the spread of invasive species, restore coastline and habitats connecting our streams and rivers, clean up environmentally damaged Areas of Concern, and prevent future contamination.

“The Great Lakes Restoration Initiative is the most significant investment ever made to restore and protect our Great Lakes from things like invasive species, pollution, and shoreline erosion,” said Senator Peters. “Now more than ever, we need to ensure this vital program has the funding it needs to continue supporting projects that will keep these treasured bodies of water healthy and vibrant for years to come. I’ll keep working in a bipartisan way to get this commonsense bill signed into law.”

“Millions of Michiganders rely on the Great Lakes for their livelihood and protecting it is existential for Michigan,” said Senator Slotkin. “The Great Lakes Restoration Initiative will help protect the lakes, our economy and our way of life – from vital programs that work to mitigate coastal erosion to protecting against harmful invasive species like Asian Carp. I will always fight for our Great Lakes and will continue to work with people in both parties to do just that.”

“The Great Lakes Commission applauds the Senate for advancing bipartisan legislation to reauthorize the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, a proven program that is delivering environmental and economic results for communities across the Great Lakes basin,” said Erika Jensen, Executive Director of the Great Lakes Commission. “Continued federal investment in the GLRI is essential to restoring degraded areas, protecting water quality, combating invasive species, and strengthening communities across the basin. We thank Senators Peters and Slotkin and their colleagues for their leadership and urge the House to move quickly to pass this critically important legislation."

“The GLRI is integral to the health of the Great Lakes and the 30 million people who depend on them for drinking water,” said Laura Rubin, Director of Healing Our Waters-Great Lakes Coalition. “Reauthorizing the GLRI is essential to maintaining the momentum we have built in restoring one of the nation’s most treasured natural resources, and we are grateful for the leadership of the Great Lakes delegation for advancing this legislation, preventing interruption to the GLRI’s vital work.”

Since its inception, the GLRI has spurred tremendous progress in Michigan and throughout the Great Lakes region, including nearly half of a million acres of habitat protected, restored, or enhanced, a five-fold increase in the successful cleanup and delisting of Areas of Concern, a ten-fold increase in the remediation of environmental and public health impairments, and reducing the threat of harmful algal blooms. The GLRI’s efforts have also resulted in economic returns of more than 3 to 1 across the region.

The senators’ legislation is supported by the League of Conservation Voters, National Wildlife Federation, Sierra Club, National Parks Conservation Association, Council of Great Lakes Governors, Great Lakes Fishery Commission, American Great Lakes Ports Association, Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative, American Rivers, American Sportfishing Association, Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership, Ducks Unlimited, Trout Unlimited, Congressional Sportsmen's Foundation, National Audubon Society - Great Lakes, Environmental Law & Policy Center, and other key stakeholders in Great Lakes protection.

Peters and Slotkin have been steadfast supporters of the Great Lakes, including by enacting the single-largest-ever investment in the GLRI through the bipartisan infrastructure law to accelerate the restoration of nine high-priority areas in Michigan whose lakes, rivers and watersheds flow into the Great Lakes.

As Co-Chair of the Senate Great Lakes Task Force, Peters plays a key role in uniting Great Lakes Basin states to coordinate legislative initiatives, funding priorities, and oversight efforts to address the most important issues facing the Great Lakes, such as invasive species, environmental contamination, shoreline erosion, water quality, infrastructure needs, and more.

title: Senator Peters Applauds United States Coast Guard Decision to Restore Full Operations & Staffing at USCG Station Saginaw River
text:
ESSEXVILLE, MI – U.S. Senator Gary Peters (MI) applauded the United States Coast Guard’s (USGC) decision to fully restore staffing and operations at USCG Station Saginaw River in Essexville:

“United States Coast Guard search and rescue units play a vital role in ensuring the safety of Michigan’s Great Lakes communities, and I’m thrilled that full operations are returning to Station Saginaw River in Essexville,” said Senator Peters. “Since operational changes were announced at Coast Guard stations across Michigan, I’ve raised the importance of these resources to communities and called on the Department of Homeland Security to address staffing shortages and restore operations. Thanks in part to this advocacy, Coast Guard recruitment is at record levels, leading to the return of full operations in Saginaw Bay. This announcement will improve the Coast Guard’s ability to respond to crises on the water, keeping Michiganders safe and secure. While this is a positive step forward, the job is not finished until full operations are restored at every impacted Coast Guard station in Michigan, and I’ll keep pushing until that happens.”

“We are very thankful that Senator Peters pushed for the return of staffing at the Saginaw River Station,” said Bay City Fire Chief Kurt Corradi. “The Coast Guard’s operational changes have put a strain on local emergency response teams, so the return to full staffing is welcome news for our partners across the Bay Region.”

Peters led the effort to reverse the previously announced staffing changes at USCG Stations throughout Michigan. In November 2025, he raised these concerns with Admiral Kevin E. Lunday, then-nominee to be Commandant of the USCG. In May of 2025, he called on the Trump Administration to prioritize funding for U.S. Coast Guard recruitment and retention. In a letter to Admiral Lunday, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russell Vought, and U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, Peters also outlined how critical Coast Guard operations have been disrupted as a result of personnel shortages and underscored that further investment is needed to support ongoing recruitment and retention efforts for the Great Lakes region to address these shortages.

title: In Case You Missed It… Sen. Rick Scott, Dr. Rebeccah Heinrichs in The Hill: “If America Wants to Prosper, We Must Lead.”
text:
NAPLES, Fla. – Last week, U.S. Senator Rick Scott and Dr. Rebeccah Heinrichs of the Hudson Institute published a joint op-ed in The Hill that discusses the numerous threats to America’s prosperity — and how to confront them.

In the op-ed, Senator Scott and Dr. Heinrichs argue that America is facing a growing list of threats from an “authoritarian alliance,” as China, Russia, North Korea, Iran and its proxies, and others consolidate power to steer the world away from the U.S.-led global order. The solution, they argue, is to recommit to American strength and leadership on the world stage.

Senator Scott and Dr. Heinrichs wrote, “Lately, a foolish worldview is growing in popularity among elected leaders in Washington. You hear it from voices ranging from Tucker Carlson to Hasan Piker. Some on the left and right have become convinced that solving America’s domestic issues requires our retreat from leadership on the world stage.”

…

“What the Tucker-Piker camp fails to understand is that America still has enemies. Communist China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and Cuba have created an anti-American coalition — an authoritarian alliance — to undercut us as the global superpower and sever the ties between the U.S. and the Western coalition.”

…

“If we retreat and allow this authoritarian alliance to take hold, America will suffer. Communist China and its accomplices will starve us, isolate us, and deprive us of every resource possible until America is weak and dependent. We will have no autonomy, no opportunity, and no freedom. Our financial markets will be powerless to fuel innovation, our business will shutter, and the American Dream will die.”

…

“We cannot sacrifice national and global security to a false dilemma of domestic versus overseas issues. It is not a zero-sum equation. To believe it would destroy a century of American greatness and the American Dream itself. Americans deserve a future that is safe, prosperous and free. For that to happen, America must lead.”

title: Rosen Calls Out Trump Admin for Shortchanging Rural Nevada Families on Home Loans
text:

title: Shaheen Joins Effort to Expand Coverage of Birth Control as Trump Administration Continues Attacks on Contraception and Family Planning
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) helped introduce the bicameral Affordability is Access Act, which would require insurers to fully cover over-the-counter birth control without any fees or out-of-pocket costs, once it is Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved. The introduction comes as the Trump Administration continues its senseless attacks on reproductive care, family planning and contraception, including moves to cancel teen pregnancy prevention grants, attempts to decimate Title X and the U.S. State Department’s extremist decision to falsely label birth control products as abortifacients.

“As the Trump Administration continues its relentless efforts to strip women of our bodily autonomy and limit access to basic reproductive health care, we must do all we can to increase access to contraception and family planning methods,” said Senator Shaheen. “Our legislation would build on successful provisions in the Affordable Care Act that have made birth control more readily available by ensuring over-the-counter options are also available at no cost.”

Under the Affordable Care Act, all private health insurance plans are required to fully cover – without copays or out-of-pocket costs – prescribed FDA-approved, granted or cleared methods of contraception. The Affordability is Access Act would change this to apply to over-the-counter birth control that women can get without a prescription. The Affordability is Access Act would also maintain the FDA’s sole authority to determine the safety and efficacy of drugs and make them available over the counter without a prescription and ensure retailers provide contraception without a prescription. The legislation states that any retailer that stocks contraception that the FDA has approved, granted or cleared without a prescription may not interfere with a consumer’s access to or purchase of such contraception.

The bill text can be read HERE.

Senator Shaheen is an unrelenting advocate for women’s reproductive rights. Shaheen is a longtime cosponsor of the Women’s Health Protection Act which would guarantee a woman’s right to access an abortion free from medically unnecessary restrictions that interfere with a patient’s individual choice or the provider-patient relationship. Shaheen has also joined her Senate colleagues in opposing Senate Republicans’ effort to restrict access to reproductive health care, including their push last year to pass legislation that would have significantly interfered with the doctor-patient relationship and posed unnecessary and harmful obstacles to a woman’s right to make her own decisions about her reproductive health. For years, Shaheen has fought to expand coverage of women’s preventative care, including through her legislation to reduce the cost of contraception for servicewomen and dependents in military families.

title: Senate Passes Tillis, King Resolution Establishing National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day
text:

The Tillis-King resolution encourages the public, veteran service organizations, community partners, and health care providers to raise awareness of veteran suicide prevention and the resources available to veterans in crisis.

“Our veterans have sacrificed everything to defend our freedoms, and we owe them our unwavering commitment to ensure they have access to the care and resources they need during and after their service,” said Senator Tillis. “I thank my colleagues for their overwhelming bipartisan support in establishing National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day. I am proud to have co-led this effort to raise awareness of veteran suicide, connect veterans with lifesaving resources, and ensure those who served our nation know they are never alone.”

“National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day is a solemn reminder of our responsibility to the veterans we have lost, and to the families who carry their memory forward,” said Senator King. “Their experiences demonstrate the critical importance of early support and reliable access to care. We remain committed to strengthening the systems that provide veterans and their loved ones with effective and compassionate services.”

title: Warner Statement on the Appointment of Jay Clayton to Coordinate Federal AI Policy
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sen. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, released the following statement after President Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to serve in an additional role overseeing the administration’s artificial intelligence policy:

“Artificial intelligence is one of the defining national security challenges of our time, and I welcome the administration recognizing that this technology requires serious, sustained attention at the highest levels of government. But creating a new title is not a substitute for having a coherent strategy. So far, the administration has resisted meaningful safeguards without offering a serious alternative for addressing the national security risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems. We still do not know what authority this new role will have, whether it will include developing safety standards or reviewing the most advanced models, or how it fits into the administration’s broader approach to AI. That lack of clarity is especially concerning as leading AI companies themselves are confronting increasingly capable systems that can evade safeguards and exploit cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

“There is real bipartisan interest in Congress in getting this right. I hope this appointment is an opportunity for the administration to move beyond slogans and toward a serious, coordinated national strategy for AI. As I have said repeatedly, that coordination must include the Intelligence Community, where some of our nation’s foremost technical experts on cyber reside. And as Vice Chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, I look forward to working with Director Clayton on ensuring the United States stays ahead of China and other adversaries, strengthening the security and resilience of our most advanced AI systems, and establishing rigorous testing and safeguards so that increasingly powerful systems remain secure, reliable, and under human control. ”

Sen. Warner has been a leading voice in Congress on the national security, economic, and societal implications of artificial intelligence. Earlier this year, he unveiled A Framework for America’s AI Future, a comprehensive legislative agenda focused on AI safety and competition, national security, workforce disruption, and the infrastructure needed to power the technology. Most recently, Warner introduced the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 with Sens. Brian Schatz (D-HI) and Andy Kim (D-NJ), legislation that would establish enforceable safety and security standards for the most advanced AI systems, including pre-deployment testing, stronger cybersecurity requirements, and mandatory reporting of serious AI safety and security incidents. Warner and his colleagues took to the Senate floor this week to seek unanimous consent to pass the legislation.

title: Warnock Statement on Reporting that Trump Admin Let Millions in Rural Housing Development Dollars Expire
text:
According to reporting by POLITICO, the Trump Administration refused to spend around $232 million in federal funding meant to help low-income families in rural communities

The funding officially expired last week

The funding was allocated by Congress to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Single Family Housing Direct Home Loans Program

In Georgia, rural communities received over $14 million less in mortgage assistance compared to the prior years’ average, a 68% decrease

Senator Reverend Warnock: “Time and time again the Trump administration shows its true colors. By denying money to Georgians who need it, the President demonstrates that he doesn’t care about rural and low-income families.”

Washington, D.C. – Today, Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) released the following statement after new reporting by POLITICO found that the Trump administration threw away more than $230 million in federal funding Congress already allocated to help low-income families in rural communities.

“Time and time again, the Trump administration shows its true colors. By denying money to Georgians who need it, the President demonstrates that he doesn’t care about rural and low-income families, rising housing costs, and the affordability crisis plaguing this country,” Senator Reverend Warnock said. “Housing provides dignity and security, particularly in rural communities. When this administration fails to do its job, it is hardworking Georgians in rural communities across our state who pay the price.”

Congress allocated the funding to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Single Family Housing Direct Home Loans Program. As of today, USDA has only used $518 million of the $1 billion in available funding for the program.

About $250 million of the unspent money will carry over to the next fiscal year, but roughly $232 million expired last week with the end of the fiscal year, preventing hundreds of families across Georgia and the country from getting the assistance they need. Each year, the program finances roughly 5,500 mortgages. The $230 million in funding could have helped approximately 850 rural households achieve homeownership across the country.

This fiscal year, Georgians only received $6.9 million in single-family housing direct home loans, a $14 million, or 68%, decrease from prior years’ average, according to data provided by Senator Patty Murray’s (D-WA) office.

title: Rep. Young Kim Introduces Resolution Recognizing National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40) introduced a resolution recognizing October 5th as National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day to raise awareness of these rare genetic disorders and recognize the patients and families impacted by them.

Peroxisomal disorders are estimated to affect roughly 1 in 50,000 births. These rare genetic conditions can affect nearly every system in the body, and severe forms are often terminal in childhood. Patients may experience hearing and vision loss, developmental delays, adrenal insufficiency, neurological complications, and feeding difficulties. There is currently no cure for peroxisomal disorders, and treatment options remain extremely limited.

For families, a diagnosis brings years of specialist visits, complex daily care, and financial and emotional strain, often with few answers along the way. For the Overly family of Lake Forest, this struggle is all too real. Brooke Overly’s daughter Melody was diagnosed with a Peroxisomal Disorder. Melody’s grandfather, Michael Curry, helped spearhead the effort to establish National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day.

“After meeting Melody and her mother Brooke, I saw firsthand the strength it takes for a family to face a rare diagnosis with so few answers,” said Rep. Young Kim. “No parent should have to navigate a devastating diagnosis with so little information available about specialists, treatments, or what comes next. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to raise awareness of peroxisomal disorders, recognize families like the Overlys, and bring greater attention to the need for better understanding, treatments, and ultimately a cure.”

title: Smith, Boyle Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect the Integrity of College Athletics
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Adrian Smith (R-NE-03) and Brendan F. Boyle (D-PA-02), members of House Ways and Means Committee, introduced the Fair Play Enforcement Act, to protect the integrity of college athletics by holding colleges and universities accountable for fielding athletes who violate established standards of fair competition.

“College athletics have a long history of bringing people together, fostering competition, and teaching us what it means to represent something bigger than ourselves. Unfortunately, recent developments continue to put the values and traditions that make college sports unique at risk. I introduced my Fair Play Enforcement Act to ensure that colleges and universities uphold fair competition and preserve the values that have long defined college athletics for generations to come,” said Smith.

“College sports depend on honesty and fair play. Schools should not be fielding players who have bet on games or who have been on professional sports teams. Our commonsense legislation creates a financial consequence for schools that cross that line and helps protect the integrity of college athletics,” said Boyle.

BACKGROUND:

The Fair Play Enforcement Act holds colleges and universities accountable for fielding athletes who violate the standards of collegiate competition. The legislation would impose an excise tax penalty on a school that knowingly or reasonably should have known it was fielding a player in a sanctioned competition who:

Gambled on collegiate sports; or

Signed a contract with and was rostered by a professional sports team in the same sport in which the player subsequently competed at the collegiate level.

Excise Tax Penalty:

If a school is found in violation, the legislation would impose an excise tax based on a percentage of the institution’s total gross athletic revenue, including but not limited to ticket sales, media rights, conference and postseason distributions, sponsorships, licensing and merchandising, athletic donations, concessions, and other revenue attributable to the athletic program.

Safeguards:

Documented determination: Requires a final, documented determination from the appropriate governing body, such as the NCAA, that the player violated the applicable prohibition before a penalty may be imposed.

School knowledge: Applies only when a college or university knew or reasonably should have known that it was fielding a player who violated the applicable standard.

Judicial safe harbor: Provides a safe harbor when a court orders a school to roster or field a player who would otherwise be subject to the prohibition.
