title: Barrett Continues Support for Workers, Small Businesses in Mid-Michigan
text:
Howell, Mich. — Today, Congressman Tom Barrett welcomed Administrator of the U.S. Small Business Administration Kelly Loeffler and Administrator of the U.S. General Services Administration Ed Forst to Howell to highlight their efforts to support small businesses and workers.

Barrett, Loeffler, and Forst met with leadership and staff at Highland Engineering, a family-owned business that designs and builds critical equipment for the U.S. military. The visit showcased the important partnership between small businesses and the federal government, and the officials also discussed their work to lower taxes and foster an economy where workers and small businesses can succeed.

“At Highland Engineering and small businesses across mid-Michigan, people work hard to do their jobs and provide for their families,” said Barrett. “I’ve been leading the charge to build an economy where everyone can succeed, and that starts with lowering costs for families. We delivered no tax on overtime, no tax on tips, and other tax relief that has put more money back in people’s pockets — and there is a lot more to be done. Thank you to Administrator Loeffler and Administrator Forst for coming to Howell to see the good work happening here in our communities.”

“Michigan has long been at the heart of America’s industrial strength, and in visiting Highland Engineering today we saw that legacy in action,” said Loeffler. “New orders are fueling growth and more opportunities for its employees — a powerful example of what the America First economic agenda means for Michigan’s 7th Congressional District. Thanks to President Trump’s commitment to American industry and its workers, and with leadership from congressional leaders like Congressman Barrett, we are bringing vital industries home and restoring the jobs that sustain families and communities across the state.”

“Small businesses like Highland Engineering are the backbone of our economy and critical partners in strengthening our nation's industrial and defense capabilities,” said Forst. “In line with President Trump’s commitment to American manufacturing, GSA is opening doors for domestic innovators like Highland to win the federal contracts and secure opportunities necessary to put the American people and products first.”

Highland Engineering began in 1986 as a fixture and automation design firm serving the automotive industry and now is a leading defense contractor, providing the military with equipment for classified information facilities, water purification, electricity, medical care, cargo transportation, and more.

title: FY26 Community Project Funding Awarded to Oklahoma’s Fifth District
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Stephanie Bice announced that three projects in Oklahoma’s Fifth Congressional District received award notifications for a total of $2,721,813 in Community Project Funding secured by the Congresswoman through the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations process. This funding will modernize Guthrie’s Central Communications Center, which supports emergency communications for 5 police departments and 12 fire departments; improve security at Oklahoma Children’s Hospital, which serves approximately 12,000 inpatients, 35,000 emergency patients, and 250,000 outpatient visits annually; and allow the University of Central Oklahoma’s Forensic Science Institute to acquire new, state of the art technology to support students and the University’s work with law enforcement.

“I am proud to have secured these critical investments for Oklahoma’s Fifth Congressional District,”Congresswoman Bice said.“These projects are great examples of how we can bring taxpayer dollars back home to support the important work already being done in our communities. I am grateful to everyone who helped make these projects possible and look forward to seeing the difference this funding will make.”

“We are constantly looking for ways to improve our infrastructure and our equipment without placing the entire burden on our local taxpayers, and federal grants are a huge part of that,” Guthrie City Manager Eddie Faulkner said.

During the event, Guthrie Police Chief Sweger previously provided a technical overview of the project, detailing how the grant will revitalize the dispatch center. He stated, “The upgrades needed to handle the volume of calls we receive often outweigh our fiscal abilities. These funds will help alleviate some of that weight and ensure the continuance of service to our region.”

“Healthcare workers save lives every day. Ensuring their safety is not merely a workplace issue — it is a public health imperative and a moral obligation,” said Richard P. Lofgren, M.D., MPH, President and CEO of OU Health.“We commend Congresswoman Bice for her continued engagement on this critical matter and call on federal, state, and institutional leaders to invest in the people who make our healthcare system possible.”

title: REP. BOEBERT: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY ORDER KEEPS CRAIG COAL UNIT OPEN
text:
LONE TREE — Rep. Lauren Boebert announced the Department of Energy order keeps Craig Station Unit 1 available and the jobs tied to that unit continue.

"Colorado families and businesses cannot afford to lose baseload power while demand keeps climbing,” Rep. Boebert said. “This order keeps Craig Unit 1 online through the end of the year so the grid has the coal generation it needs, and the jobs tied to the unit that remains open continue.”

Craig Station is a coal-fired power plant in Craig, Colorado, the county seat of Moffat County in the northwest corner of the state. It sits just outside town along the Yampa River. Several hundred jobs are connected to the plant and the mines that supply it.

Secretary Chris Wright issued the order under section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act, finding an emergency in the WECC–Rocky Mountain region from rising demand and a shortage of generation. The order directs Tri-State, the co-owners, and Southwest Power Pool to keep the 446-megawatt coal unit available through December 25, 2026, and to dispatch it only when needed to meet the emergency and limit costs to ratepayers.

Rep. Boebert will continue to work with Secretary Wright on what is best for the 4th District.

title: Buchanan Backs Bipartisan Bills to Help Kids Eat Better and Lead Healthier Lives
text:
Legislation Would Support Florida’s Specialty Crop Growers, Improve Student Nutrition and Tell Families Exactly What Their Children Are Eating

WASHINGTON— Congressman Vern Buchanan, Vice Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee and Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, announced he is cosponsoring two bills to improve the health of students across Florida: the Local Foods for Healthy Schools Act (H.R. 9474), bipartisan legislation introduced by Congressman Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) and Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet (D-Mich.), as well as the Know What’s on the Tray Act (H.R. 9951), introduced by Congressman Tom Barrett (R-Mich.).

“A child who isn’t eating well can’t learn well,” said Congressman Buchanan. “Healthy kids become strong students, and strong students grow into the leaders our country will depend on. Children are 25% of our population, but 100% of our future, and these bills put fresh, local food in our schools and clear information in the hands of parents. That is an investment in the health of our children and grandchildren.”

The Local Foods for Healthy Schools Act would permanently reinstate and modernize USDA’s Local Food for Schools program, which USDA ended in 2025. This program would once again connect local producers and school districts, opening new opportunities for farmers while providing healthy, nutrient-rich meals to students.

The Know What’s on the Tray Act would require schools in the National School Lunch Program and School Breakfast Program to post information about every menu item on their school or district website at least seven days before the meal is served. The information would include its ingredients, the manufacturer or producer, where it was made and whether it was locally sourced or produced on a family farm. The bill would give families more insight into what their children eat and encourage healthier school meals.

Diet-related disease is one of the largest drivers of health care costs in America, and habits formed in childhood often last a lifetime. By connecting schools with nearby farms and giving families clear information about school meals, these bills invest in students’ health and classroom success while supporting local farmers. As Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, Buchanan has made prevention a priority, including bipartisan legislation he introduced to help veterans manage chronic disease through nutrition.

title: Bynum Secures Over One Million for Scio Rural Fire
text:
Today, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum (OR-05) announced that the Scio Rural Fire Protection District has received a $1.19 million federal grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency to support firefighter safety and fire prevention. Congresswoman Bynum advocated for the funding by writing a letter to FEMA in support of Scio Rural Fire’s grant application.

“When you call 911, you shouldn’t have to wonder if there are enough firefighters to answer,” said Rep. Bynum. “This $1.19 million is a big deal for Scio, Jefferson, and the communities they serve. It means more support for the people running toward emergencies and a stronger response when our neighbors need help most. This is exactly what bringing federal dollars home should look like.”

"These grants are a significant opportunity and an important first step in building the capacity our Fire & Life Safety Division needs," said Albany Fire Chief Chris LaBelle. "A community our size, with the growth and unique industries we have, requires a more proactive approach to risk reduction. This position moves us in that direction and supports our mission to Prevent and Protect from Harm."

"Redmond Fire & Rescue would like to thank Senators Merkley and Wyden and Congresswoman Bynum for their support,” said Redmond Fire Chief Ryan Herrera. "With members of our organization having navigated a past cancer diagnosis, and with the recent passing of Firefighter/Paramedic Michael Kienzle from a Line-of-Duty cancer, this funding marks another meaningful step forward in our commitment to carcinogen reduction and improving the long-term health and safety of our firefighters."

"As costs continue to rise faster than available revenue, small fire districts like ours face difficult choices about how to best use limited resources. Recruiting, training, and retaining volunteer firefighters can too often be delayed as we focus on meeting the immediate costs of providing emergency services,” said Scio Fire Chief Kevin White. "This grant is an important investment in the future of our department and our community. It will strengthen our efforts to recruit and retain volunteers, grow our membership, and ensure we have the people and resources needed to provide the high-quality emergency services our community depends on. We are grateful for this support and the opportunity to build a stronger, more sustainable fire department."

FEMA awarded the funding through its Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grant Program, which helps fire departments hire additional firefighters and strengthen recruitment and retention efforts.

FEMA also issued funding under the SAFER Grant Program to the following areas:

More than $2.3 million to Boise Fire Department in Boise, Idaho

More than $1.7 million to South Kitsap Fire and Rescue in Port Orchard, Washington.

More than $1.7 million to Spokane County Fire District 9 in Mead, Washington.

More than $1.1 million to Umatilla Rural Fire Protection District in Umatilla, Oregon.

$1 million to North Whidbey Fire and Rescue in Oak Harbor, Washington.

title: Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, Huffman Lead Colleagues in Urging Removal of Hunt Amendment from Annual Defense Bill
text:
U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA), and House Natural Resources Committee top Democrat Jared Huffman (D-CA-02), led 30 of their colleagues in calling on House and Senate Armed Services Committee leaders to reject the Hunt Amendment’s provision (Section 2835) in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), which would grant unprecedented eminent domain authority to the federal government to benefit Sable Offshore Corporation.

“The NDAA has long served as a bipartisan vehicle to strengthen our national security and support our servicemembers. However, we are deeply concerned by the inclusion of Section 2835, which would grant extraordinary eminent domain authority to the federal government to circumvent established environmental protections for the benefit of a single private company. Given the sweeping implications of this provision, we believe this policy rider does not belong in the NDAA and, therefore, should be removed from the final conference agreement,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers explain how this provision would jeopardize the California coastal economy and do little to strengthen our nation’s energy security.

“California’s coastal economy supports roughly 511,000 jobs and generates over $51.3 billion in GDP from marine-economy activities — largely in tourism and recreation. Another oil spill from a corrosion-prone pipeline that has spilled before would jeopardize the economic security of everyday Americans that rely on our coastal economy for their livelihoods,” the lawmakers continued. “In addition, there is no evidence that this provision would meaningfully advance our nation's energy security. Recent spikes in gasoline prices driven by market uncertainty surrounding the war in Iran underscore that global oil markets—not a single offshore project—continue to dictate prices at the pump.”

The letter goes on to highlight the unprecedented nature of Section 2835, which would grant the federal government extraordinary powers to seize property for the sole benefit of a single private organization.

“The NDAA should not be used to circumvent established permitting processes or create special authorities for individual projects that have failed to secure the approvals required under existing law. The federal government's power of eminent domain is among its most significant authorities and should be exercised only when there is a clear and compelling public purpose—not to resolve private infrastructure disputes or increase the profitability of a single company—at the expense of communities who have to live with the consequences of an oil spill,” said the lawmakers.

The full letter is available HERE.

Joining Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, and Huffman the letter is co-signed by U.S. Representatives Maxine Waters (D-CA-43), Dave Min (D-CA-47), Julia Brownley (D-CA-26), Lou Correa (D-CA-46), Mike Thompson (D-CA-04), Brad Sherman (D-CA-32), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18), Nancy Pelosi (D-CA-11), John Garamendi (D-CA-08), Gil Cisneros (D-CA-31), Ted Lieu (D-CA-36), Derek Tran (D-CA-45), Mike Levin (D-CA-49), Juan Vargas (D-CA-52), Judy Chu (D-CA-28), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), Laura Friedman (D-CA-30), Robert Garcia (D-CA-42), Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12), Kevin Mullin (D-CA-15), Mark Takano (D-CA-39), Ami Bera, M.D. (D-CA-06), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Scott Peters (D-CA-50), Doris Matsui (D-CA-07), Pete Aguilar (D-CA-33), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA-37), George Whitesides (D-CA-27), Luz Rivas (D-CA-29), and Sara Jacobs (D-CA-51).

Background

Sable Offshore acquired the Santa Ynez Unit from ExxonMobil in 2024. The pipeline had been out of service since the 2015 Refugio oil spill. In March 2026, Energy Secretary Chris Wright invoked the Defense Production Act and ordered Sable to restore pipeline operations.

Carbajal has been a leader in opposing the Sable pipeline’s forced restart.

In September 2026, Carbajal led a bicameral group of colleagues in filing an amicus brief in California v. Wright to challenge the Trump Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA) to facilitate the restart of the Sable Offshore oil pipeline system along the California Central Coast. The brief argues that the Administration has failed to identify a legitimate national defense need for Sable’s crude oil and that the DPA order does not satisfy the statutory requirements for invoking this extraordinary authority.

In July 2026, Carbajal spoke on the House floor against the NDAA’s Hunt amendment, which would grant the federal government unprecedented access to California-owned public lands associated with the Santa Ynez Unit and Las Flores Pipeline System.

title: Rep. Carson Seeks Answers on Canceled Naturalization Ceremonies
text:
WASHINGTON, DC—This week, Congressman André Carson (IN-07) led 26 Members of Congress in seeking answers from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) about repeated cancelations of naturalization ceremonies.

In Indianapolis, USCIS canceled at least three naturalization ceremonies since July, citing a “lack of candidates.” But field offices report they have pending naturalization applications that are awaiting action from USCIS.

“Citizenship is a life-changing milestone, and people who have spent years following the law deserve a government that honors its commitments,” said Rep. Carson. “Canceling naturalization ceremonies without a clear explanation leaves families in Indianapolis in limbo and undermines trust in the process. These families deserve more than canceled ceremonies and unanswered questions. USCIS must explain these cancellations and ensure eligible applicants can take their oath without unreasonable delay. I will keep pressing this administration for answers and accountability.”

“We are concerned that lawful permanent residents are experiencing delays in the final stages of their naturalization across the country,” the lawmakers state in the letter. “Applicants who have spent years complying with immigration requirements should not face unexplained or unreasonable delays after becoming eligible for citizenship because of the political or ideological whims of a particular administration. These delays prevent lawful permanent residents from fully exercising the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, including voting, obtaining a U.S. passport, pursuing certain employment opportunities, and petitioning for family members. Congress has made it clear that the fair and timely processing of eligible citizenship applicants is a priority.”

Rep. Carson and his colleagues requested a response from USCIS by October 7, 2026, including the number of pending naturalization applications, how long those applications have been pending, and how many applicants have completed naturalization interviews but are still awaiting final decisions.

The full letter is HERE.

title: Castro Challenges Trump To Visit Dilley Trailer Prison During San Antonio Visit
text:
SAN ANTONIO, TX —Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) renewed his invitation to President Donald Trump to visit the Dilley Trailer Prison during his visit tomorrow in San Antonio, Texas.

“Donald Trump will be in San Antonio tomorrow. I invite him to visit the Dilley Trailer Prison and see for himself the trauma he is inflicting on children and babies, some as young as two months old.”

Castro first challenged the President to see firsthand the conditions facing children at the only family detention center in the country at a march protesting ICE’s proposed detention center in San Antonio. Transcript below:

“President Trump, you're coming to San Antonio. I would invite you to go to Dilley to see what Stephen Miller, who sits with you at the White House, has done to these children. To see the lifelong lasting trauma he's caused to these kids, to see what he's doing in the name of Americans. And I would say, because I would bet that the President has never been into a detention center, that he's certainly not been into a detention center, this trailer prison, where kids are held. Let me say this: the President of the United States is the leader of the country, the leader of the free world. If you can't stand there and go inside and look into the eyes of these kids and tell them that despite the fact they've done nothing wrong, that they belong there just because of where they were born, just because of the color of their skin, just because of the language that they speak, then you don't deserve to be President of the United States.”

“Presidente Trump, vas a venir a San Antonio. Yo te invito a ir a Dilley para ver lo que Stephen Miller, que se sienta contigo en la Casa Blanca, les ha hecho a estos niños. Para ver el trauma duradero que les ha causado a estosniños, para ver lo que está haciendo en nombre de Estados Unidos. Y yo diría esto, porque apostaría a que el presidente nunca ha estado dentro de un centro de detención. Que ciertamente nunca ha estado dentro de un centro de detención, esta prisión de tráileres, donde tienen detenidos a niños. Déjenme decir esto: el Presidente de los Estados Unidos es el líder del país, el líder del mundo libre. Si no puedes estar ahí, entrar y mirar a estos niños a losojos y decirles que, a pesar de que no han hecho nada malo, pertenecen allí simplemente por el lugar donde nacieron, simplemente por el color de su piel, simplemente por el idioma que hablan, entonces no mereces ser Presidente de los Estados Unidos.”

title: Reps. Castro, Cisneros Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — Reps. Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and Gil Cisneros (CA-31) introduced a resolution to honor and celebrate the cultural impacts of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming.

Hispanics and Latinos represent 21% of the total population of the United States but Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming account for less than 7% of on-screen roles and less than 5% of off-screen roles. However, television series and films featuring Hispanic and Latino talent consistently rank among the most watched and financially successful productions.

El Cine, the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, the Latino Film Institute, the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), the National Association of Latino Independent Producers (NALIP), the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), and the National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) signed on as supporting organizations.

“Latino artists have helped shape American film and television for generations, and Latinos are one of the largest and fastest-growing audiences in this country," said Congressman Castro. "Yet we are still underrepresented on screen and in the writing rooms and leadership roles where decisions are made. Latino film festivals across the country are doing important work to support Latino storytellers, and the industry should invest in that talent. I'm proud to join Congressman Cisneros in recognizing these contributions and calling for more Latino representation on and behind the big screen.”

“Latinos and Hispanics represent some of the biggest stars and the most important stories of the century. The time when actors like Rita Hayworth, Anthony Quinn or Martin Sheen had to change their names has given way to mainstream stars like Selma Hayek, Eva Longoria, Diego Luna, and Selena Gomez,” said Congressman Cisneros. “Hispanic and Latino storytellers have enriched our media with diverse stories, artistic excellence, and economic growth and they deserve recognition for their talent. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to celebrate and honor the success of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming and recognize their past, present, and future contributions to the United States.”

“One of the biggest dangers our culture faces is erasure,” said Mariana Da Silva, Founder of El Cine. “We are taught to hide parts of ourselves, our language, our histories, and the stories that make us who we are. At El Cine, we create space for those stories to be seen, heard, and passed on. Latin culture is American culture. We’re proud to support this resolution because recognizing our contributions also means making room for the next generation to tell their stories without having to hide who they are.”

“Fifty-nine percent of Latino adults went to a movie theater last year, more than any other group,” said Juan Proaño, Chief Executive Officer of LULAC. “Latinos are the profit margin of this industry. Yet we hold just 5 percent of the roles on screen, 2.8 percent of the lead roles, and one half of one percent of the writing credits, and 44 percent of top films have no Latino speaking character at all. LULAC is proud to support Congressman Cisneros's resolution, which honors the artists who opened doors and calls on the industry to reflect the audiences who sustain it. When we tell our own stories, the whole country sees itself more clearly.”

“Thirty years ago, Jimmy Smits, Sonia Braga, Esai Morales, Merel Julia and I founded the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), when Latinos were one in ten Americans and almost nowhere on screen," said Felix R. Sánchez, Chair and Co-founder of NHFA. "Today we are one in five, and we hold fewer than three of every hundred lead roles in Hollywood's top films. The country changed, the screen has not.”

“Latino Americans are intertwined in the fabric of the United States – including in film, television, and streaming,” said Brenda Victoria Castillo, President and CEO of National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC). “With the highest per capita consumption in entertainment, representing 24% of film ticket sales, 29% of daily mobile television viewers, and 24% of streaming subscribers, it's no wonder that our stories resonate, inspire, and are central to modern American culture. NHMC thanks Congressmen Cisneros and Castro for recognizing our community and continuing to be allies to increase Latino representation in media.”

“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”

Read the full text of the resolution here.

title: Rep. Chu, Tri-Caucus Leaders Demand HHS Withdraw Harmful English-Only Head Start Proposal
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28), Chair Emerita of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), CAPAC Chair Grace Meng (NY-06), Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC) Chair Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Congressional Black Caucus (CBC) Chair Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Rep. Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), and Rep. Juan Vargas (CA-52) sent a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. opposing HHS’s proposed Head Start rule which would mandate English-only instruction and eliminate longstanding language-access protections for children and families.

Head Start is a critical program that provides high-quality early childhood education and comprehensive support services for low-income children and their families. While the Members urge HHS to withdraw the proposed rule in its entirety, their letter focuses specifically on its harmful changes to language-access protections. Nearly 40 percent of children enrolled in Head Start are dual-language learners, representing almost 290,000 children nationwide, and 30 percent of enrollees come from families whose primary home language is not English.

In the letter, the Members explain that dual-language instruction helps children learn English and prepare for school:

“We share the goal of ensuring that every Head Start child develops strong English-language skills. But requiring English-only instruction is not supported by the evidence and risks undermining that very goal. For many children, Head Start is their first experience in a classroom. Providing an environment in which young children can understand, communicate, and participate supports their ability to learn and successfully transition into school.

The Members also warn that the proposed rule conflicts with Congress’s explicit directives in the Head Start Act:

“Congress directed the Secretary to establish standards ensuring that children with limited English proficiency make progress toward acquiring English while simultaneously making meaningful progress in other developmental domains, including through “culturally and linguistically appropriate instructional services” (42 U.S. Code § 9836a(a)(1)(B)(x)). Congress further directed the Secretary, when revising Head Start standards, to ensure that revisions do not eliminate or reduce the quality, scope, or types of educational, parental-involvement, health, or other services required under longstanding Head Start standards (42 U.S.C. § 9836a(a)(2)(C)). And the Head Start Act explicitly requires agencies to ensure teachers receive literacy training “in methods to promote vocabulary development and phonological awareness (including phonemic awareness) in a developmentally, culturally, and linguistically appropriate manner and support children’s development in their native language” (42 U.S. Code § 9843(d)(2)(B)). Eliminating longstanding language-access protections appears directly at odds with these congressional directives, and the Department has not adequately explained how its proposal can be reconciled with them.”

The Members detail how eliminating bilingual staffing requirements could undermine parents’ ability to participate in their children’s education and jeopardize accurate developmental screenings and assessments:

“Congress recognized that informed and engaged parents are essential to children’s success and required Head Start programs to conduct family needs assessments and communicate with parents, to the extent practicable, in a language they understand (42 U.S. Code § 9836(d)(2)(J)(vii); 42 U.S. Code § 9836(d)(2)(K); 42 U.S. Code § 9836a(f)(2)). Eliminating language-access staffing requirements without providing an adequate alternative could make it more difficult for parents to understand their children’s progress, participate in their education, communicate with teachers and staff, and access the comprehensive services Head Start provides.

We are particularly concerned about the consequences for developmental screenings and assessments. The Head Start Act requires measures used by Head Start programs to be developmentally, linguistically, and culturally appropriate; valid and reliable in the language in which they are administered; administered by appropriately trained staff; and accompanied by appropriate accommodations for children with limited English proficiency (42 U.S. Code § 9836a(b)(2)). These protections are critical. A screening or assessment administered in a language a young child does not sufficiently understand risks mistaking normal second-language development for a developmental delay or, conversely, failing to identify a genuine disability or developmental concern. Either outcome could delay appropriate early intervention at precisely the age when it can make the greatest difference.”

Finally, the Members warn that the proposal would impose significant disruption and costs on Head Start providers while weakening services for hundreds of thousands of children:

“The scale of the disruption caused by the proposed rule’s language-access changes would be substantial. Almost 290,000 dual-language learners nationwide could be affected […] Although the proposal is titled Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs, affected programs could be forced to change curricula, replace classroom materials, and retrain or replace teachers, resulting in an estimated $99 million in costs.”

“HHS should not reverse decades of evidence-based practice, impose new costs on providers, and weaken language-access protections for hundreds of thousands of children without a compelling evidentiary or legal basis for doing so. Accordingly, we strongly urge HHS to withdraw the proposed English-only instruction requirement and retain the longstanding language-access protections that allow Head Start programs to effectively serve dual-language learners and their families. Congress expressly directed Head Start to support English-language acquisition through culturally and linguistically appropriate services, and HHS should uphold, not undermine, that mandate.”

title: García, Colleagues Issue Joint Statement Condemning Israel’s Persecution of Palestinian Healthcare Workers
text:
CHICAGO — Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), along with Congressmembers Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Summer Lee (PA-12), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), and Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) released a joint statement condemning the Israeli government’s systematic persecution of Palestinian healthcare workers, and called for their immediate release from arbitrary detention.

“Over the last three years, the Israeli government has systematically destroyed the health system in Palestine, murdering at least 1,700 Palestinian doctors, nurses, paramedics, and other healthcare workers and destroying dozens of hospitals. It has arrested and arbitrarily detained hundreds of Palestinian healthcare workers, including at least 16 physicians who continue to be held in inhumane conditions. Among them is Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, whom the Israeli government has arbitrarily detained since 2024 and tortured to the point of near-death after previously murdering his son and brutally attacking his hospital,” said the Members.

“Israel’s systematic annihilation of medical facilities and healthcare workers is not an accident or unfortunate consequence of war; it is an intentional policy designed to further occupation, apartheid, and genocide against the Palestinian people. We demand the immediate release of Dr. Abu Safiya and all other arbitrarily detained healthcare workers and Palestinian prisoners. And we demand an end to U.S. arms transfers to Israel, including the Trump Administration’s latest $2.8 billion sale of bombs. Congress must block this sale and pass the Block the Bombs Act to finally end our government’s shameful complicity in Israel’s mass atrocities.”

Congressman García also recently led a letter condemning the violence by Israeli settlers, police and military in the village of al-Mughayyir in the occupied West Bank, and called for the release of Marwan Barghouti who has been detained and tortured in Israeli prison for over 20 years.

title: Ciscomani Highlights $6.3 Million in Federal Investments for Graham County
text:
Tucson, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani toured four Community Project Funding sites in Graham County, highlighting the $6.3 million in preliminary federal funding he has secured to support infrastructure, healthcare, roads, and teacher housing across Thatcher, Safford, and the greater Graham County area.

"These $6.3 million in preliminary investments across four projects will deliver lasting improvements for communities across Graham County," said Representative Ciscomani. "From improving essential roads and modernizing the courthouse to expanding access to healthcare and supporting teacher housing, these projects address real needs identified by local leaders. As Arizona’s sole appropriator, I am committed to bringing federal resources home, moving these projects forward, and delivering results that matter for Graham County families."

The funding was awarded through the highly competitive Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations process. Graham County’s four projects stood out among more than 70 applications submitted to Ciscomani’s office and will support key priorities across the community:

$3 million will support the reconstruction and widening of 1st Avenue Road in Thatcher, improving a critical local roadway and making travel safer and more efficient for residents, businesses, and the surrounding community.

$2 million will support modernization and improvements to the Graham County Courthouse in Safford, helping upgrade a critical public facility and ensure it can continue meeting the needs of Graham County residents.

$650,000 will help Mt. Graham Regional Medical Center purchase a new mammography unit, bringing advanced breast cancer screening and diagnostic services closer to home and reducing the need for local patients to travel outside the community for care.

$650,000 will support teacher housing at Fort Thomas Unified School District, helping provide more affordable housing options for educators and strengthening the district’s ability to recruit and retain teachers in the community.

Thatcher Mayor Jenny Howard praised Ciscomani’s advocacy and commitment to the community.

"He gets rural," said Thatcher Mayor Jenny Howard. "He gets the state, he gets this district, but he gets rural; he knows we struggle."

​Howard continued:

"The Town of Thatcher is incredibly grateful for Representative Ciscomani’s leadership and advocacy as he works to secure this $3 million investment for our community. We were proud to host him yesterday and show him firsthand why this project is so important to Thatcher and the surrounding region. This investment would be a game changer for our community and will truly have a lasting impact. We appreciate Representative Ciscomani’s commitment to seeing this project through and bringing this critical investment home to Southern Arizona. This is the kind of investment that will make a real difference for our community for years to come."

These investments build on more than $60 million in Community Project Funding Ciscomani has delivered for Arizona in Fiscal Years 2024 and 2026, including $5.5 million for Graham County.

Previous Graham County projects include:

$2 million for a new Pima Fire Station

$1.3 million for the Graham County Gila River Linear Park

$1.2 million for new waterlines at the Graham County Fairgrounds

$1 million for a new road to Pima High School

This $6.3 million investment for Graham County is a testament to Representative Ciscomani’s commitment to delivering for rural Arizona. This year, he has preliminarily secured funding for 20 projects totaling $42.7 million, bringing critical resources back home to Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District. As Arizona’s sole member of the House Appropriations Committee, Ciscomani’s efforts ensure stronger communities, better infrastructure, and a brighter future for families across the region.

Hispanics and Latinos represent 21% of the total population of the United States but Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming account for less than 7% of on-screen roles and less than 5% of off-screen roles. However, television series and films featuring Hispanic and Latino talent consistently rank among the most-watched and financially successful productions.

El Cine, the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, the Latino Film Institute, the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), the National Association of Latino Independent Producers (NALIP), the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), and the National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) signed on as supporting organizations.

“Latinos and Hispanics represent some of the biggest stars and the most important stories of the century. The time when actors like Rita Hayworth, Anthony Quinn or Martin Sheen had to change their names has given way to mainstream stars like Selma Hayek, Eva Longoria, Diego Luna, and Selena Gomez,” said Congressman Cisneros. “Hispanic and Latino storytellers have enriched our media with diverse stories, artistic excellence, and economic growth and they deserve recognition for their talent. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to celebrate and honor the success of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming and recognize their past, present, and future contributions to the United States.”

“Latino artists have helped shape American film and television for generations, and Latinos are one of the largest and fastest-growing audiences in this country,” said Congressman Castro. “Yet we are still underrepresented on screen and in the writing rooms and leadership roles where decisions are made. Latino film festivals across the country are doing important work to support Latino storytellers, and the industry should invest in that talent. I'm proud to join Congressman Cisneros in recognizing these contributions and calling for more Latino representation on and behind the big screen.”

“One of the biggest dangers our culture faces is erasure,” said Mariana Da Silva, Founder of El Cine. “We are taught to hide parts of ourselves, our language, our histories, and the stories that make us who we are. At El Cine, we create space for those stories to be seen, heard, and passed on. Latin culture is American culture. We’re proud to support this resolution because recognizing our contributions also means making room for the next generation to tell their stories without having to hide who they are.”

“Fifty-nine percent of Latino adults went to a movie theater last year, more than any other group,” said Juan Proaño, Chief Executive Officer of LULAC. “Latinos are the profit margin of this industry. Yet we hold just 5 percent of the roles on screen, 2.8 percent of the lead roles, and one half of one percent of the writing credits, and 44 percent of top films have no Latino speaking character at all. LULAC is proud to support Congressman Cisneros's resolution, which honors the artists who opened doors and calls on the industry to reflect the audiences who sustain it. When we tell our own stories, the whole country sees itself more clearly.”

“Thirty years ago, Jimmy Smits, Sonia Braga, Esai Morales, Merel Julia and I founded the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), when Latinos were one in ten Americans and almost nowhere on screen,” said Felix R. Sánchez, Chair and Co-founder of NHFA. “Today we are one in five, and we hold fewer than three of every hundred lead roles in Hollywood's top films. The country changed, the screen has not.”

“Latino Americans are intertwined in the fabric of the United States – including in film, television, and streaming,” said Brenda Victoria Castillo, President and CEO of National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC). “With the highest per capita consumption in entertainment, representing 24% of film ticket sales, 29% of daily mobile television viewers, and 24% of streaming subscribers, it's no wonder that our stories resonate, inspire, and are central to modern American culture. NHMC thanks Congressmen Cisneros and Castro for recognizing our community and continuing to be allies to increase Latino representation in media.”

“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”

Read the full text of the resolution here

Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.

title: Reps. Crane and Davids Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Housing Access for Tribal Veterans
text:
This afternoon, Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) and Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS) introduced the bipartisan Tribal Veterans Voucher Flexibility Act to improve how unused housing vouchers are managed and distributed through the Tribal HUD-VASH program. The legislation would allow Tribes to voluntarily give back vouchers they do not plan to use, so the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) can redirect assistance to Tribal communities facing a shortage.

Native American veterans experience some of the highest rates of homelessness in the United States. To address this, Congress created the Tribal HUD-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (Tribal HUD-VASH) demonstration program, which provides rental assistance and supportive services to Native veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.

Although the program has helped many veterans secure stable housing, it lacks a clear process for Tribes to return vouchers they cannot use or to request additional ones. As a result, valuable housing support sits idle while veterans in other Tribal communities wait for help.

The Tribal Veterans Voucher Flexibility Act directly addresses this gap by requiring HUD to establish a voluntary program for reallocating unused Tribal HUD-VASH vouchers. Under the bill, Tribes and Tribally Designated Housing Entities (TDHEs) can notify HUD if they have vouchers they do not expect to need in the following fiscal year. Importantly, releasing vouchers will not affect a Tribe’s or TDHE’s consideration for future allocations.

Likewise, Tribes and TDHEs that require additional vouchers can request them, and HUD may then reassign available assistance to those communities. This approach directs limited resources to the veterans who need them most.

To reduce administrative barriers, the bill ensures Tribes and TDHEs can report unused vouchers through digital, phone, or mail correspondence. It also requires HUD to launch the program within 180 days of enactment and to deliver a report to the relevant congressional committees within the same timeframe. The report must include:

The number of vouchers each Tribe or TDHE left unused

Each Tribe or TDHE that received reallocated vouchers

The number of Tribes and TDHEs without enough vouchers

Recommendations for better distributing surplus vouchers to Tribes and TDHEs seeking more

An assessment of whether the overall number of Tribal HUD-VASH vouchers should be increased

By creating a streamlined reallocation process, this bill strengthens the Tribal HUD-VASH program and expands Native veterans’ access to the housing assistance they have earned.

This is not the first time Reps. Crane and Davids have partnered on legislation to assist Tribal communities. In both the 118th and 119th Congresses, Rep. Davids introduced the Native American Entrepreneurial Opportunity Act, which would bolster U.S. Small Business Administration outreach to Tribal entrepreneurs navigating the unique complexities of running a business on a reservation. Rep. Crane co-led the measure, and it has twice passed the House with strong bipartisan support.

Rep. Crane also joined Rep. Greg Stanton (D-AZ) in leading an amendment to redirect $5 million from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) General Administration account to the VA Office of Rural Health. The House unanimously adopted the amendment, which would fund mobile clinics and targeted clinical staffing to improve access to care for Tribal veterans. Today’s introduction builds on Rep. Crane’s ongoing efforts to close gaps in the care and services available to Native veterans.

“The Tribal HUD-VASH program helps house Tribal veterans in need, but the current system is not as efficient as it should be. Some Tribes have leftover vouchers they cannot use while others lack the resources to take care of our veterans. Our legislation aims to resolve this longstanding issue by getting unused vouchers into the hands of Tribes that can put them to use. This is a sensible approach that makes better use of existing support without expanding the size and scope of the federal government. As the representative for more than half of the Tribes in Arizona, I’m honored to advocate for these heroes by reforming and modernizing this process. I appreciate Rep. Davids’ willingness to work across the aisle. We’ve made real progress together before, and I look forward to building on that success with this bill,” said Rep. Eli Crane.

title: Rep. Crockett Investigates Police Use of Force Against Students in Texas Schools
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett (TX-30) sent a letter to Governor Greg Abbott, Attorney General Ken Paxton, and Education Commissioner Mike Morath demanding answers and accountability over the use of excessive force against children in Texas public schools.

“Texas is failing our kids. Our children deserve to go to school in an environment that fosters learning and growth, not environments where ordinary student behavior can end with a child in handcuffs, hogtied, shocked with a Taser, or pepper-sprayed.”

Crockett expressed concern regarding the expansive presence of police in school, putting Texas students in unnecessary contact with the criminal system, further opening the door to the school-to-prison pipeline.

In her letter, Crockett highlights how officers using excessive force to respond to student behavior could ordinarily be addressed through school discipline. The letter cites a New York Times investigation documenting more than 2,600 school-based use-of-force incidents across Texas from January 2022 through December 2025.

Crockett is demanding answers regarding police involvement in routine student discipline, incident reporting, accountability for police misconduct, and potential changes to state law training.

“The number of “incidents” is alarming. Our kiddos should not be treated like criminals. They are the future of this country, and we owe it to them to protect them from cruel and abusive behavior. I am urging our Texas leaders to exercise immediate oversight and ensure accountability for these horrific reported actions. This is unacceptable, and it has to stop.”

title: Davids Helps Launch Bipartisan Agenda to Cut Red Tape, Boost Local Economies, Lower Everyday Costs for Kansas Families
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids, a member of the Build America Caucus, helped announce the Build More Agenda — a major bipartisan policy platform designed to fix federal gridlock, strengthen local economies, create jobs, and lower everyday prices for hardworking families. By streamlining approval processes for energy, housing, and infrastructure, the roadmap directly targets the bureaucratic delays that slow down construction, drive up utility and housing costs, and prevent critical projects from getting built.

“Kansans don’t want D.C. talking points — they want lower utility bills, homes they can actually afford, and roads that aren't falling apart,” said Davids. “The problem isn't a lack of good ideas; it's the bureaucratic red tape slowing projects down for years. I’m supporting the bipartisan Build America Caucus’ new agenda because it would help cut through government gridlock and start building these projects now, not a decade from now.”

The bipartisan Build America Caucus was established to give pro-growth, pragmatic policymaking a permanent foothold in Congress. Over the past year, the Caucus helped negotiate and pass major bipartisan housing reform legislation and led bipartisan efforts to deliver permitting certainty for energy and infrastructure projects. Spanning seven core policy areas and over 60 legislative proposals, the Build More Agenda builds on those successes, establishing a comprehensive framework to spur domestic production, bring manufacturing home, create good-paying jobs, and lower the cost of living for Kansans.

“Not enough homes or energy, shortages of doctors and daycares, cures that take too long to reach patients, and infrastructure projects that drag on for decades. That’s what life in America looks like today because we’ve lost the ability to build the things we need,” said CaucusCo-Chairs Harder and Maloy. “We used to believe that America was the only place in the world where the boldest dreams could be realized, and we need a new politics of action to restore that national ambition and trust in government. The Build America Caucus was founded a little over a year ago with that goal in mind, and the Build More Agenda is our bipartisan roadmap to make growth and prosperity the cornerstone of American life once again.”

The solution to systemic dysfunction is to build our way to prosperity:

Lowering Housing Costs: With the nation facing a shortage of five million homes, the agenda reduces regulatory delays, unlocks new project financing, and fully implements the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to expand homeownership options and bring housing prices back within reach for young families and working Kansans.

Cutting Healthcare Costs & Red Tape: We spend more on healthcare than any other nation, but that care is unaffordable, inaccessible, and archaic. It reallocates physician training investments and slashes mountain-high administrative paperwork, so doctors spend time on patient outcomes rather than bureaucracy — cutting health system waste and lowering out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.

Cheaper, Reliable Energy: Electricity rates have jumped more than 30 percent in recent years. The platform fixes broken permitting rules, so grid upgrades and energy projects don't take longer to approve than to actually construct, bringing down monthly electricity bills for households and small businesses.

Building Infrastructure Faster: It establishes dedicated fast-track approvals and smarter federal funding models to ensure roads, bridges, and water systems are completed on schedule and under budget — ending costly construction delays that waste taxpayer dollars.

Accelerating Medical Cures: America is losing its scientific edge because our scientists spend half their time on paperwork and research dollars aren’t geared toward modern discovery. It saves American medical researchers over one million hours a year spent on bureaucratic paperwork, redirecting resources toward breakthrough science and AI technology to accelerate cures for cancer, Alzheimer's, and chronic conditions.

Expanding Childcare & Workforce Pipelines: It strengthens workforce development programs that directly match workers to high-paying local jobs, while expanding accessible childcare options so parents can stay in the workforce without breaking their household budgets.

Modernizing Government to Save Taxpayer Dollars: It cuts redundant D.C. red tape, updates archaic federal technology systems, and builds a skill-focused public workforce that manages taxpayer funds efficiently.

Read the full agenda here. Read a section-by-section here.

“America knows how to build, we just have to get out of our own way and start doing it,” said Rep. Janelle Bynum (D-OR-05). “More homes, better roads and bridges, new technology, and good jobs – this agenda is about turning big ideas into things people can actually see and feel in their communities. I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and help get it done.”

“Americans are tired of Washington making it harder and more expensive to build, innovate, and grow,” said Rep. Buddy Carter (R-GA-01). “The Build More Agenda brings Republicans and Democrats together around commonsense solutions to cut red tape, lower costs, strengthen American energy, improve access to healthcare, and get critical projects built. I’m proud to work with the Build America Caucus to turn good ideas into real results for the American people.”

“The Build More Agenda reflects what we can accomplish when we work across the aisle to tackle challenges facing American families and businesses,” said Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12). “I’m proud to join my colleagues in the bipartisan Build America Caucus to advance practical solutions that cut unnecessary red tape, lower costs, and help America build faster and smarter. By modernizing infrastructure and creating opportunities for American workers and manufacturers, we can strengthen our economy, make taxpayer dollars go further, and deliver lasting results for our communities.”

“America used to pride itself on accomplishing big things — winning world wars, sending man to the moon, or discovering the next medical breakthrough,” said Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA-50). “Today, our challenges have not gone away, but our capacity to achieve great things has. Our constituents are counting on us to put politics aside and invest in our country’s future to make their lives better. The bipartisan Build More Agenda includes ways to do exactly that: lower costs, create good-paying jobs, strengthen communities, and restore America as a global leader in progress and innovation.”

“Folks in Western and Southern Colorado know how to build things, create jobs, and get things done,” said Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-03). “Too often, Washington just gets in the way. The Build More Agenda is about cutting unnecessary red tape so we can produce more American energy, build the housing and infrastructure our communities need, and bring down costs for working families. Republicans and Democrats aren’t going to agree on everything, but we ought to be able to agree that it shouldn’t take years of paperwork and bureaucracy to build something in this country.”

“A housing shortage is a tax on working people, and they pay it every month in rent,” said Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15). “For decades, we have piled on rules and caps that make it slower and costlier to build homes, and few places have paid a higher price than the Bronx. The surest way to bring down the cost of housing is to bring up the supply of housing. The Build More Agenda is built on that principle, because a pro-growth agenda is a pro–working class agenda. Progress should be measured not by how many projects we regulate but by how many we deliver.”

“Congress passed a housing abundance bill this term,” said Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA-04). “It's seriously debating a bipartisan energy abundance bill. Build America has momentum in its mission to lower prices by building more, faster & better – next up are unlocks to lower prices in medicine, transportation, and childcare.”

“As a senior member of the Housing, Transportation, and Urban Development Subcommittee, I’m proud to be a member of the bipartisan Build America Caucus. My constituents tell me every day they want to see their representatives in Washington take actions that will make their lives better – lower the cost of housing, healthcare, and energy,” said Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL-05). “At a time of deep political division, we have the unique opportunity to come together as Democrats and Republicans to lower costs and solve the housing crisis.”

“Whether it’s rebuilding a bridge over I-95 in record time or passing landmark housing legislation, we know that government can still get things done, if rarely,” said Rep. Jim Himes (D-CT-04). “I’m in the Build America Caucus because this group of lawmakers fundamentally believes government needs to get things done — not as the exception, but as the rule. Our agenda reflects that belief, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to turn our group’s governing principle into law.”

What they’re saying about the Build More Agenda:

“For too long, we’ve treated a four-year college degree as the default path to a good career. The Build America Caucus’s push to get more apprenticeships and higher-quality workforce training programs off the ground is a critical step forward. If we want to build more in America, we need to make it easier for more Americans to learn how to do the building,” said Zach Boren, Senior Vice President, Apprenticeships for America.

“Getting lawmakers from both parties to agree on what's holding the country back is no easy feat, and we applaud the Build America Caucus for assembling a genuinely bipartisan coalition around these questions. BPC Action has long argued that the problems on this list — the cost of building housing, the time it takes to approve energy projects, and a broken childcare system — are solvable ones. We look forward to working with the caucus and its members as they move from agenda to legislation,” said Michele Stockwell, President, BPC Action.

“Through their work with the Build America Caucus, Reps. Harder and Maloy have asked how we can build more of what Americans actually need and answered it across housing, childcare, energy, and more. We applaud this effort and its goal to build 5 million homes, add millions more new childcare slots, modernize the energy grid, and get infrastructure built faster. This comprehensive plan demonstrates that pragmatic, actionable solutions can still be ambitious. This Agenda, written by a Democrat from California and a Republican from Utah, also shows the strength of abundance solutions in building coalitions. I urge Congress to take action on these solutions,” said Derek Kaufman, President, Inclusive Abundance Action.

“The Build More Agenda is an innovative, bipartisan framework for creating a more abundant future in America. The priorities laid out in this agenda have the potential to make a massive difference in areas from science and innovation to housing, transportation, and energy. For example, we were thrilled to see X-Labs and metascience units highlighted as vehicles to accelerate scientific discovery and increase the return on investment for R&D. Similarly, the Agenda’s focus on reducing land use regulations, building transit at lower cost, and achieving energy abundance is crucial for letting America build again and innovate in the world of atoms,” said Alec Stapp, CEO, Institute for Progress.

“For the past year, the Build America Caucus has worked across the aisle to notch key policy wins, making it easier, cheaper, and faster to build in America. The Build More Agenda strengthens that foundation, with over sixty policy proposals covering seven different policy areas. NAIA looks forward to working with the Caucus to back the builders,” said the New America Industrial Alliance.

“Finding childcare that's both affordable and meets their family’s specific needs is nearly impossible for far too many American parents. This agenda from the Build America Caucus offers an innovative menu of reforms to identify and remove the barriers to a more abundant supply of childcare options that fit family preferences without sacrificing quality or safety,” said Josh McCabe, Director of Social Policy, Niskanen Center.

“The housing affordability crisis is the result of many different factors, and solving it requires an all-hands-on-deck approach. The Build America Caucus agenda delivers this, with solutions that make it easier and less expensive to build housing. Critically, it does the same for transportation infrastructure and buses, because abundant housing and effective transportation options work together to connect people to economic opportunity,” said Kimberly Burnett, Deputy Director of Housing and Transportation, Niskanen Center.

“America's healthcare affordability crisis is fueled by a scarce and consolidated supply side of the market. This agenda from the Build America Caucus rightly targets solutions that increase care availability and cut out the incentives that drive consolidation,” said Lawson Mansell, Senior Health Policy Analyst, Niskanen Center.

“We applaud the Build America Caucus for its energy agenda focused on more power and lower bills. Getting transmission right and having neighboring regions connected is how you build a grid Americans can afford,” said Sarah Iskander, Government Affairs Manager, Niskanen Center.

“Whether it's housing, transportation, energy, or infrastructure, the federal government needs the tools and capacity to deliver for the American people. Meeting those demands requires a government whose systems and processes make delivery possible, and right now ours is not built to keep pace with changes in the workforce, technology, and the public's needs. The Build America Caucus's policy agenda takes this challenge head-on, rightly recognizing state capacity as essential to unlocking a prosperous future for our country,” said Max Stier, President and CEO, Partnership for Public Service.

title: Deluzio Kicks Off October Town Hall Tour in Penn Hills, PA
text:
PENN HILLS, PA – Yesterday, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) kicked off his October Town Hall Tour with an event open to the public and the press in Penn Hills, Pennsylvania. A large group of Western Pennsylvanians joined him for the first stop of the Town Hall Tour in Pennsylvania’s 17th District.

The event covered a wide range of topics, including corruption, AI, and the cost of living. Constituents had an opportunity to speak directly with their elected representative in Congress, share their opinions, and ask questions. Congressman Deluzio also provided updates from his work down in Washington.

“A lot has happened down in Washington this year, and it is good to be home to hear from the people that Congress’s work impacts the most,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Folks in Penn Hills want to know how we can fight the cost-of-living crisis, end the President’s reckless war in Iran, and restore the American Dream right here in Western Pennsylvania. I’m excited to keep the conversation going and hear from the good people of Carnegie and Beaver Falls next."

Congressman Deluzio has attended more than twenty similar open Q&A events during the 119th Congress (2025-2026). Deluzio’s Town Hall Tour will stop next in Carnegie on Tuesday, October 13th at 5:30pm and in Beaver Falls on Saturday, October 17th at 2:00pm.

title: Rep. Foushee Demands Answers From Secretary Kennedy Regarding Cancellation of Teen Pregnancy Prevention Grants
text:
WASHINGTON, DC (October 6, 2026) — Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Kennedy Jr. regarding the Teen Pregnancy Prevention (TPP) grants that were canceled by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

“I am concerned that HHS is still holding funding for these important grants that support locally delivered, evidence-based programs that reach young people where they live, often in communities with limited access to health education and services, including rural areas,” the Congresswoman wrote.

“HHS must have a plan to ensure that this vital program continues (...) HHS must immediately reinstate funding for TPP Program grantees that your department cut off earlier this year,” Congresswoman Foushee continued.

“I request that you immediately share HHS's plan to allocate funding for the TPP program with funds obligated by Congress and ensure that grantees, including North Carolina, will continue to offer important evidence-based education and not see their funding and program implementation further interrupted,” the Congresswoman concluded.

Duke University, located in North Carolina’s Fourth Congressional District, was a recipient of a Teen Pregnancy Prevention grant in 2023.

In July, 79 members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus (DWC) and the Democratic Caucus, sent a letter to the Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, demanding the reversal of the Trump Administration’s cancellation of 53 active Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program (TPP) grants that the Department claimed were no longer aligned with the agency’s priorities.

Recent decisions by the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia blocked HHS from establishing new grants with new funding conditions. 92 members of Congress, including Rep. Foushee, recently stated in a letter to HHS, that this funding must be reinstated for TPP grantees that were cut off earlier this year.

title: RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Leads Los Angeles Delegation and Entertainment Unions in Push for National Film Tax Credit
text:
Levels international playing field against 65 countries that offer incentives America does not match

Above: Friedman and entertainment union members rally for the national film tax credit.

GLENDALE, CA – Today, October 6, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) led Members of the Los Angeles congressional delegation, and the major unions representing film and television workers at the Alex Theatre in a new push for the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. This bipartisan legislation creates a national film tax credit on qualified labor expenses to bring production jobs back home.

A recording of the rally can be found here and here.

For decades, the United States has offered no national filming incentive, leaving American crews to compete against roughly 65 countries that do. The result has been hundreds of thousands of lost jobs for the drivers, grips, electricians, carpenters, caterers, and crew members.

WHAT THE BILL DOES:

A 20% credit on American labor expenses. Feature films, television pilots, and television seasons that cost more than $1 million qualify if at least 75% of their principal photography days happen in the United States.

Bonus credits that reward hiring where it is needed most. Productions can earn an additional 5% each, up to a 30% total credit, for shooting at least 30% of their days in a rural opportunity zone or a federally declared disaster area, for independent productions, for spending at least $10 million in qualified wages across 10 or more states, and for increasing domestic production relative to what a company shoots abroad.

Includes post-production and visual effects work. Domestic post-production and VFX qualify as long as at least 75% of those costs are incurred in the United States, with the same 5% bonuses available.

Usable by independent producers, not just major studios. The credit is transferable, meaning a producer who doesn't owe enough in federal taxes to use it can sell it to a company that does and get the cash up front.

Takes effect quickly. The credit applies to productions that begin in taxable years starting after December 31, 2026.

A one-pager with more details can be found here.

“When a production leaves this country, the stars still work. The crew is who gets left behind,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “65 countries offer incentives we don’t match, and no single state can outbid a foreign government on its own. Our bipartisan bill is built on labor costs, which means it only pays off when American workers get hired. These are good paying union jobs with benefits and pensions, and I won’t stop fighting until they come home.”

“You won’t see the carpenters, electricians and camera crews on screen, but they are the backbone of the film industry,” said Congresswoman Linda T. Sánchez (CA-38). “Many live in my district and have watched their jobs move overseas as other countries use incentives to lure production away. Our bipartisan bill will level the playing field to bring good-paying union jobs back to Southern California and keep them here.”

"Southern California has been the heart of America’s film and television industry, but today, too many productions are leaving the United States for countries offering better incentives," said Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28). "That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, which would provide a long-overdue federal tax credit to incentivize production here in the United States. Our creative workforce is the backbone of this industry. It's time we must invest in them and bring American film and television production back home.”

“Movie magic is central to the California story, and we need to keep it that way,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33). “Our state is losing good-paying, union jobs because filming in this country has become far too expensive. The bipartisan Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act will bring jobs back to America, boost wages for workers and keep productions at home.”

“California is the heart of film and television production, in large part because of the workers and technicians who bring the magic to life,” said Representative Tran (CA-45). “Yet the U.S. is rapidly losing jobs in this industry to competitors overseas. When productions relocate outside the U.S., it’s the American-based crews that suffer the most. California’s workforce deserves better. This bill incentivizes American-based productions, strengthens California’s production workforce, and brings jobs back to the U.S.—where they belong.”

“Southern California is the birthplace of the modern film and television industry. From the movies and television shows that have entertained audiences around the world to the hardworking people behind them, this industry is a vital part of our community and economy,” said Congressman Lieu (CA-36). “We can’t let the United States’ film industry lose ground to foreign competitors. I am pleased to be an original co-sponsor of the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. It’s time to strengthen our domestic film industry and protect American jobs.”

“American performers and entertainment workers should not have to leave the country to find work in an industry that was built here. Film and television are more than entertainment — they are a major American industry that supports hundreds of thousands of good-paying union jobs and generates significant economic activity in communities across the country. For decades, foreign governments have recognized the economic value of production and successfully used incentives to attract these jobs overseas. States across the country have shown what targeted incentives can do to attract and retain production, and a federal incentive would build on those efforts and give the United States a stronger tool to compete. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act is an investment in American workers, American industry and American communities. SAG-AFTRA is proud to stand with Congresswoman Friedman and our labor partners in support of this important legislation,” said SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland.

“The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will benefit entertainment industry workers, as well as the supporting businesses and local economies that rely on a robust domestic entertainment industry. Lawmakers have an opportunity to invest in an important American industry and preserve middle-class jobs, by passing the first-ever federal film and television tax incentive program,” said WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta.

"Let’s not overthink this. The world is a complicated place, but this legislation is a no-brainer. It's going to get people back to work, and everyone just wants an opportunity to work in the industry they love in this country. Everyone will benefit from this – Republicans, Democrats, workers, audiences -- because our industry touches everyone," said Mike Farah, an Emmy-winning producer and a President of the Producers Guild of America.

“I’ve worked aggressively with labor and entertainment industry leaders, and together we've already expanded state-level tax incentives and reduced filming fees locally. A federal tax credit is critical so our local incentives remain competitive with countries that offer larger benefits and have drawn productions out of the United States,” said Mayor Bass. “I want to thank the bipartisan leadership of Representatives Laura Friedman, Brian Jack, Linda Sánchez, and Nathaniel Moran and Senators Adam Schiff and Tim Scott for understanding the importance of investing in an industry that is so critical to Los Angeles and the country. As a former Member of Congress, I'll continue leveraging my relationships in Washington to ensure this bill is passed into law.”

U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (CA-30) was joined by Senator Adam Schiff (CA), U.S. Representatives Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Maxine Waters (CA-43), Judy Chu (CA-28), Pete Aguilar (CA-33), Ted Lieu (CA-36), David Min (CA-47), and Derek Tran (CA-45), Glendale Mayor Ardy Kassakhian, IATSE International Vice President and Director of the Motion Picture and Television Department Mike Miller, SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta, DGA Associate National Executive Director and Western Executive Director Rebecca Rhine, Teamsters At-Large Vice President and Motion Picture Division Director Lindsay Dougherty, LiUNA Business Manager Alex Aguilar, Jr., and producer and three-time Emmy winner Mike Farah.
