title: Rep. Gillen Announces More Than $500,000 in New Federal Funding for Nassau County Fire Departments
text:
GARDEN CITY, NY — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) announced that four fire departments in New York’s Fourth Congressional District have been awarded more than $500,000 total in federal funding for improved equipment, training and recruitment. Three departments were awarded Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG), including the Inwood Fire Department for emergency vehicle acquisition as well as the Bellerose Terrace Fire Department and the Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department for operations and safety. Stewart Manor Village received funding through the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant to help recruit and retain more volunteer firefighters.

“Firefighters across Long Island put their lives on the line every day to protect our families and communities. They should have the resources of a modern firefighting force,” said Rep. Gillen. “I’m proud to help secure more than $500,000 in federal funding for Nassau County fire departments to support critical equipment, vehicle and recruitment needs. I will continue working with our local fire departments to deliver federal dollars and ensure they have the tools and support they need to keep our communities safe.”

“The chiefs, officers and members of the Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department thank Congresswoman Gillen very much,” said Chief Joseph McHugh, Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department. “This will help keep our members safe and take a big financial burden off of us.”

The Inwood Fire Department received $220,476 through the AFG program to assist with the purchase of new vehicles for the department.

The Stewart Manor Village Fire Department received $119,500 through the SAFER program to help recruit and retain trained volunteer firefighters.

The Bellerose Terrace Fire District received $96,666 through the AFG program to help support the operations and safety of their department.

Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department received $72,857 through the AFG program to help support the operations and safety of their department.

During the FY25 grant application process, Rep. Gillen urged all departments in New York’s Fourth Congressional District to apply for funding through the AFG and SAFER programs and wrote letters of support. As a member of the bipartisan Congressional Fire Services Caucus, Rep. Gillen has also pushed for increased funding for the AFG and SAFER Programs to help ensure Long Island fire departments have the federal resources to improve emergency response and support their firefighters.

The AFG program, administered by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), provides funding to local fire departments to help obtain needed equipment, protective gear, vehicles and training. The SAFER grant is a federal program administered by FEMA that provides direct funding to local fire departments and volunteer firefighter organizations to help increase or maintain the number of trained firefighters.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Flydubai Flight 1073 Heroes
text:
Condemns Attempted Terrorist Attack

Resolution Honors Captain, Crew, Passengers Who Saved All Lives

Calls for a Full Investigation

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10), and Congressman Don Bacon (NE-2) introduced a bipartisan resolution honoring Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073, and condemning the attempted terrorist attack on the flight.

“Captain Machchhar is a hero. While gravely wounded, he fought off a terrorist attack and saved every soul on that plane, including 27 children and four Americans,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Congress must honor his extraordinary courage, and we must be clear that this was an act of terrorism and an attack on the safety of international air travel. I’m proud to lead this resolution with Congressman McCaul and Congressman Bacon, and we wish Captain Machchhar and everyone injured a full recovery.”

“I’m proud to co-lead this resolution, which condemns the attempted terrorist attack, calls for a full investigation, and honors the brave crew and passengers. The world owes a debt of gratitude to these heroes — especially Captain Smit Machchhar, who sustained injuries fighting the attacker and still managed to unlock the cockpit door and allow others to land the plane,” said Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10). “Were it not for his extraordinary courage, this story could have ended in horrific tragedy. I wish Captain Machchhar, the crew, and all the passengers healing and strength as we await a comprehensive investigation into this harrowing incident.”

On September 30, Flight 1073 departed Dubai for Tel Aviv carrying approximately 174 passengers and six crew, including 4 U.S. citizens and 27 children. Midway through the flight, the first officer attacked the captain with the aircraft’s emergency crash axe and tried to seize the controls, sending the plane plunging more than 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds. Despite grave injuries, Captain Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack and unlocked the cockpit door so off-duty pilots could enter and land the plane, and so crew and passengers could restrain the first officer. The aircraft landed safely in Saudi Arabia with everyone accounted for. On October 3, the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates announced that the investigation had determined the first officer attempted to carry out a terrorist act.

The resolution:

Honors Captain Machchhar for extraordinary courage in protecting every soul aboard his aircraft;

Commends the off-duty pilots, cabin crew, and passengers who secured the flight deck and brought the aircraft safely down;

Wishes Captain Machchhar and all who were injured a full recovery;

Condemns the attack as an act of terrorism and an attack on the safety of international civil aviation;

Calls for a full and expeditious investigation by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and for the United States and Israel to be kept fully informed.

title: Moore, Bonamici, Frost, Grijalva, and Pocan Blast Regulations Paving the Way for National Voucher Scheme
text:
The Treasury Department recently released regulations on their national voucher scheme, which was established through the Republicans’ Big Ugly Bil (HR 1). That law allowed Americans to receive a tax credit, up to $1,700, for donations to eligible scholarship-granting organizations, including religious schools. These regulations will double the credit amount for married couples. Representatives Gwen Moore (WI-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), and Mark Pocan (WI-02) have introduced HR 9289, the Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act, which would repeal the H.R .1 voucher scheme.

In states across the country, taxpayer supported voucher programs operate with little oversight and fund private schools who lack civil rights and other protections for students. In Wisconsin, the current voucher program at the state level will cost state taxpayers more than $700 million this year alone. Nearly all the students receiving a voucher in Wisconsin attend private, religious schools.

Republicans are working to enact and expand this flawed system at the national level. So far, six states have resisted, including Wisconsin.

“Despite what Republicans claim, these regulations make it clear this voucher scheme is designed to prop up private schools– at the expense of our public schools. Public schools serve every student who walks through its doors. Our tax dollars should not be funneled to schools that can discriminate against students who try to enroll. That is why I am proud to spearhead legislation to reverse this voucher scheme,” said Representative Gwen Moore (WI-04).

"The Treasury Department's school voucher regulations clearly demonstrate that the Trump administration has no interest in supporting public schools or the students they serve," said Representative Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01). "Diverting public resources into private schools - including religious schools - that can pick and choose which students they enroll is unjust and irresponsible. Alarmingly, the regulations actually prohibit states from implementing additional oversight, reporting, accountability, or civil rights protections. The vast majority of students in this country attend public schools. We should be strengthening public education, not destroying it."

“This voucher scheme sends public money to private schools with less accountability for how that money is spent," said Representative Maxwell Frost (FL-10)."We’ve already seen the consequences in Florida, where the state struggled to track hundreds of millions of dollars in voucher funds and cases of fraud surfaced. Now the Treasury Department and Trump administration want to take that same model nationwide. We shouldn’t be making it easier to lose track of taxpayer dollars; we should be making sure every dollar is accountable to the public.”

“Arizona’s fraud-ridden school voucher program should serve as a warning to the rest of the country. Instead, the Trump Administration is moving full steam ahead with a national voucher scheme while failing to include even basic safeguards to prevent taxpayer dollars from being wasted or abused. Arizona has already seen where this road leads. That’s why Congress must act to ensure federal taxpayer dollars strengthen the public schools that serve the overwhelming majority of America’s children, not subsidize privatization schemes rife with fraud,” said Representative Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07).

title: Comisionado Residente entrega más de $1 millón para ampliar educación STEM en San Juan
text:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández visitó Vimenti, en el Residencial Ernesto Ramos Antonini en San Juan, donde presentó $1,031,000 en fondos federales que aseguró para desarrollar el Next Generation STEM Learning Lab Accelerator. La iniciativa ampliará las oportunidades de educación STEM para estudiantes de Vimenti School y otras tres escuelas del programa de Escuelas Comunitarias de Servicio Completo.

El Comisionado Residente aseguró los fondos mediante una solicitud de Financiamiento para Proyectos Comunitarios (Community Project Funding) presentada ante el Comité de Asignaciones de la Cámara de Representantes. Los recursos serán canalizados a través de la Oficina de STEM Engagement de la NASA.

“Llevo semanas diciendo que tenemos que priorizar lo básico, y la educación es básica. Nuestros niños fracasan en las materias básicas de español, inglés, ciencias y matemáticas. Este tipo de asignación ayuda a resolver ese problema.”, dijo el Comisionado Residente.

“Agradecemos al comisionado residente, Pablo José Hernández Rivera, y a su equipo, por la confianza depositada en este proyecto. Este logro reafirma nuestro compromiso de seguir identificando y allegando recursos que permitan que más escuelas públicas de Puerto Rico cuenten con espacios, herramientas y oportunidades educativas de excelencia para sus estudiantes, maestros y familias”, expresó Bárbara Rivera Batista, directora ejecutiva de Vimenti.

“Esta subvención confirma lo que puede lograr el modelo de Escuela Comunitaria de Servicio Completo cuando se le brinda el respaldo necesario. Nuestro compromiso es que estos recursos y espacios STEM se queden en cada escuela, sostenidos por sus propios equipos, mucho después de que termine el financiamiento”, indicó Lola Yglesias Quiñones, directora de Expansión de Vimenti.

A través del proyecto, las escuelas podrán desarrollar nuevos espacios educativos con herramientas de robótica y programación, astronomía y ciencias espaciales, ciencias de la Tierra, análisis de datos e inteligencia artificial. La iniciativa también contempla capacitación y acompañamiento para maestros, con el objetivo de fortalecer la capacidad de las escuelas para mantener y ampliar estos programas a largo plazo.

Durante su visita, el Comisionado Residente también sostuvo un conversatorio con estudiantes, familias y maestros sobre el modelo de Vimenti, los resultados que ha alcanzado la organización y la importancia de ampliar el acceso a oportunidades educativas en áreas STEM.

Según datos provistos por Vimenti, durante el año escolar 2023-2024 sus estudiantes alcanzaron un 54% de dominio en matemáticas, frente a un 11% a nivel de Puerto Rico. Entre los estudiantes con discapacidades, el dominio en matemáticas alcanzó un 63%, comparado con tasas de entre 10% y 18% a nivel estatal.

Vimenti atiende a estudiantes y familias mediante un modelo de dos generaciones que integra educación, salud y bienestar, desarrollo laboral, capacidad financiera, emprendimiento y mentoría. De acuerdo con su estudio de impacto de siete años, la organización ha generado cerca de $59 millones en impacto económico mediante sus operaciones y proyecta otros $97 millones asociados a iniciativas futuras.

title: Social Security Administration Refuses to Provide Services for Foster Care Youth, Horsford and Cortez Masto Demand Answers
text:
For Immediate Release

October 6, 2026

Social Security Administration Refuses to Provide Services for Foster Care Youth, Horsford and Cortez Masto Demand Answers

NORTH LAS VEGAS – Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) and Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) sent a joint letter to the Social Security Administration, calling on the agency to process pending applications submitted by Clark County Family Services (CCFS) to obtain Social Security Cards for youth in foster care. The letter comes after months of unanswered attempts by CCFS, County Commissioners, and both Rep. Horsford’s and Sen. Cortez Masto’s offices to work with SSA to rectify the issue.

In December 2025, SSA notified CCFS that Social Security number applications required certain accompanying documentation to be physically certified by the custodian of record. For children in foster care, the custodian of record is the State of Nevada, which has operated digitally since 2010 when the Eighth Judicial District Court of Nevada mandated electronic filing for civil and family cases. This discrepancy between state law and federal agency policy makes it nearly impossible for CCFS to comply with SSA’s rule.

“Once again, the people are caught up in bureaucracy,” said Rep. Horsford. “Our priority is ensuring people have access to the services they are entitled to and can live their lives to the fullest. Our foster youth are among the most vulnerable in our community and SSA’s unwillingness to acknowledge our local laws shows this Administration’s regard for Nevadans.”

Over 1,300 foster youth in Clark County are currently unable to receive their Social Security Cards, severely restricting their livelihoods and quality of life.

“Without Social Security numbers, these youth can’t receive federal healthcare coverage, secure permanent placement in loving families, or even get their first job,” said Sen. Cortez Masto. “The Trump Administration must immediately process outstanding Social Security number applications and work with Clark County to remedy these documentation issues, so Nevada’s foster children don’t have to proceed any longer with their lives on pause.”

Since the initial notice in December, CCFS has provided documentation from the State of Nevada to SSA consistent with the state’s mandated electronic records and has offered to obtain any necessary information from the state to authenticate these records that may be used in other states. To date, there has been no response from SSA to this request.

“Clark County is grateful to the leadership of Senator Cortez Masto and Congressman Horsford as they work on our behalf to address this pressing issue which is impacting over 1,300 children in our care,” said Kevin Schiller, Clark County Manager. “Our most sacred responsibility is ensuring our most vulnerable children are cared for and we are being inhibited from doing this in the current state with the Social Security Administration.”

title: Hoyer, Comptroller Lierman Visit Nonprofit Organizations Across Maryland's Fifth Congressional District
text:

"Maryland's Fifth Congressional District is home to a multitude of nonprofit organizations that deliver critical resources and create opportunities for the region. From Westbrook Horse Farm to LifeStyles of Maryland, each advocate and organization we met with has an invaluable role in shaping the lives of Marylanders. I thank each organization for welcoming us, and I will continue to support their efforts during the remainder of my term in Congress," said Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05).

Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with board members of the

The group discussed strategy and ongoing investments to connect residents and local businesses with opportunities to support defense activities and boost the economy. Congressman Hoyer and the Comptroller continue working to maintain an effective relationship between military facilities, elected officials, and the greater Southern Maryland community.

Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with LifeStyles CEO Sandy Washington and

Support Staff at the LifeStyles Headquarters in LaPlata, Maryland.

Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman spent the rest of their afternoon at the LifeStyles Inc. headquarters in LaPlata, Maryland to receive an update on the around-the-clock support services provided at this location. During their tour, LifeStyles CEO Sandy Washington highlighted their work to deliver food, clothing, and housing assistance and workforce training for nearly 3 decades. LifeStyles of Maryland has 8 offices and distribution centers across the state to help meet the needs of underserved communities in the region.

title: SHNS: Birth center expects first delivery after ‘leadership transition’
text:
Elected leaders who hailed the reopening of the state’s second freestanding birth center earlier this year may have celebrated prematurely.

The Cambridge Health Alliance Birth Center, which closed in March 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic, was scheduled to reopen on July 6 with the aim of welcoming 100 babies in the first year. CHA said the center would serve all patients but have a “special focus on vulnerable and underserved populations who will benefit most from midwifery care and a birth center experience.”

But no deliveries happened this summer, even as supporters of the 2024 maternal health law tried to create new urgency around bolstering access to care and removing healthcare disparities for people of color.

“The Birth Center has been open for prenatal and outpatient visits,” CHA spokesperson David Cecere told the News Service Thursday. “We are anticipating our first delivery this week — they had been on hold as we worked through a leadership transition.”

Cecere said that “unexpected turnover” prompted the center to “hold deliveries until we established a plan to ensure high quality care and an exceptional patient experience.”

A spokesperson for the Department of Public Health, asked whether it was aware of any paused operations or staffing issues, said DPH had called the birth center and was told it was “taking clients.”

CHA has said the reopening would not have been possible without $1 million in state funding, which Cambridge Rep. Marjorie Decker helped secure in the fiscal 2024 budget. The center also received a grant from Beth Israel Lahey Health to help cover training, equipment, and community education and outreach.

The birth center, situated in a Victorian home with three renovated birthing rooms, held an open house on June 17 with more than 200 attendees, according to CHA. Speakers included Decker, U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark, Sen. Sal DiDomenico, Cambridge Mayor Sumbul Siddiqui and Public Health Commissioner Robbie Goldstein.

“Too often we are talking about the closure of maternity services, but today we get to celebrate a spectacular rebirth – and one that I hope will be followed by many more,” Goldstein said in a statement at the time. “Expanding access to community-based, relationship-centered care is key in advancing health equity. The reopening of the CHA Birth Center supports families who deserve more options for culturally responsive maternity care.”

Clark said the reopening was a “signal to women everywhere that we can and will keep making progress on maternal health.”

“We’re going to keep fighting for a healthcare system worthy of every mother in this community and a future worthy of the children who will begin their lives at CHA,” she said.

Michele Helgeson, a member of the Community Coalition for the Cambridge Birth Center, said everything had seemed “very positive” and “very, very upbeat” surrounding the open house. The coalition has met with CHA leaders to advocate for community interests and promote a midwifery model of care.

“There was no indication that there was any reason to stop or pause at that point,” said Helgeson, who added she wants to see CHA conduct community outreach and assure patients about available services at the birth center.

Birth centers are seen as alternatives to hospital deliveries, particularly in low-risk pregnancies. The facilities offer a home-like environment and are staffed by midwives who can provide more personalized care.

The 2024 law removed regulatory barriers to opening freestanding birth centers and created a pathway for certified professional midwives to become licensed. The state started accepting applications for temporary CPM licensure last month, as DPH expects to issue regulations for “standard” licensure in early 2027.

Until the CHA Birth Center returned to the maternal health landscape, Massachusetts was home to only one such freestanding facility in Northampton. But Seven Sisters Midwifery and Community Birth Center faces intense financial pressure due to low reimbursement rates compared to services provided in hospitals, according to owner and clinical director Ginny Miller.

Legislation (S 784) to ensure that certified nurse midwives, certified professional midwives and licensed freestanding birth centers are not paid less than physicians and hospitals delivering the same services has been lodged in the Senate Ways and Means Committee since April.

Kimberly Amsley-Camp was the CHA’s director of midwifery from August 2025 through September 2026, and she managed a staff of 20 certified nurse midwives and nurse practitioners, according to her LinkedIn profile. Working with a “multi-disciplinary” team, Amsley-Camp wrote she “planned and developed reopening of a hospital owned freestanding birth center.”

Amsley-Camp did not respond to a News Service request for comment.

Cecere said consultant and certified nurse midwife Erin Stein is now overseeing “daily operations” of the CHA Birth Center. She’s working alongside Dr. Tara Singh, chief of obstetrics and gynecology, and Allisyn Brady, senior director of OB/GYN.

Helgeson said the coalition wants to meet with CHA leaders and get an update on birth center operations, though she expects that won’t happen until November due to scheduling logistics.

“There is definitely support for the sustainability of the birth center, and that’s really what we’re hoping to achieve in the long run,” Helgeson said. “The opening is important, but we really want it to succeed in the long-term as well.”

title: Kean Secures $1.25 Million for Water Infrastructure in Sparta
text:
(October 6, 2026) SPARTA, NJ – Yesterday, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ‑07) presented $400,000 to Sparta Township to support critical upgrades at the White Deer Plaza Pump Station, improving both surface and groundwater quality. Furthermore, Congressman Kean is advocating for an additional $850,000 to help the township replace aging lead service lines and strengthen its drinking water infrastructure. Together, these investments will enhance public health, modernize essential systems, and ensure long‑term reliability for Sparta residents.

“Strong water infrastructure is essential to keep our communities running,” said Congressman Kean. “That is why I fought to secure these federal funds to support both the pump station upgrades and the lead service line replacements to protect the health and safety of Sparta Township residents by ensuring high-quality water infrastructure for decades to come.”

title: Kelly Backs Bipartisan STORMWATER Act to Strengthen Water Infrastructure and Protect Great Lakes Communities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- This week, U.S. Representative Mike Kelly (R-PA) co-sponsored the bipartisan Stormwater Treatment, Optimization, Resilience, and Management with Academic Technological Expertise and Research (STORMWATER) Act, legislation which aims to strengthen communities’ ability to manage stormwater, reduce flooding, and protect local waterways from pollution.

Kelly is a member of the House Great Lakes Task Force. This legislation is endorsed by the Great Lakes Commission.

The legislation, introduced by Rep. Tim Kennedy (D-NY) in August, would reauthorize federal grant programs that support stormwater innovation, technical assistance, and flood mitigation.

"20 percent of the world's surface freshwater supply is in the Great Lakes, including Lake Erie. We must do everything we can to preserve and protect this national treasure for generations to come. This legislation takes an important step toward doing just that," said Rep. Kelly.

“Every Western New Yorker deserves to know that when the next major storm comes, our communities have the infrastructure and expertise to withstand it,” said Congressman Kennedy. “The STORMWATER Act is about making that investment now – strengthening our water infrastructure, protecting our neighborhoods and businesses, and putting Great Lakes communities at the forefront of the technologies we need to safeguard the critical waters we all call home.”

"The Great Lakes Commission commends Rep. Kennedy for introducing the STORMWATER Act, which will ensure the Stormwater Centers of Excellence program continues nationwide while recognizing the Great Lakes as a unique resource increasingly threatened by stormwater impacts,” said Tim Bruno, Chair of the Great Lakes Commission. “Communities across the Great Lakes region are confronting more frequent flooding that threatens public health and water quality, carrying nutrients, debris, chemicals and other pollutants into our waterways. This bill will provide crucial resources to help communities prepare for and address these growing challenges."

Specifically, the STORMWATER Act would:

Establish a fifth Center of Excellence focused on the Great Lakes region, ensuring the region’s unique stormwater and water-quality challenges receive dedicated expertise;

Reauthorize $5 million annually from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to support and maintain five Centers of Excellence;

Reauthorize $10 million annually from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for competitive Stormwater Control Infrastructure Project grants to support communities’ stormwater infrastructure needs.

BACKGROUND

Stormwater runoff occurs when rain or melted snow cannot absorb into the ground and instead flows over hard surfaces like roads, rooftops, and parking lots. As that water moves rapidly into drainage systems and waterways, it can overwhelm infrastructure, contribute to flooding, and carry oil, debris, fertilizers, chemicals, and other pollutants into local streams and lakes.

For Pennsylvania communities surrounded by the Great Lakes, these challenges are both environmental and economic. Stronger stormwater infrastructure can help protect homes and businesses from flooding, reduce pollution entering local waterways, and preserve the health and economic vitality of the Great Lakes for generations to come.

The existing grant programs were set to expire in September 2026. The legislation would extend them through fiscal year 2031, providing communities with the resources and continuity needed to plan and implement long-term infrastructure improvements.

title: Krishnamoorthi and Vindman Introduce LESSONS from Ukraine Act to Apply Ukraine’s Battlefield Innovations to U.S. Military
text:
WASHINGTON — On Monday, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07), a 25-year Army veteran, introduced the Learning Effective Strategies and Systems Optimization for National Security (LESSONS) from Ukraine Act, legislation requiring the Pentagon to study and apply lessons from Ukraine’s battlefield innovations to U.S. military doctrine and training.

“During my visit to Ukraine, I saw firsthand how the Ukrainians are rapidly adapting to a battlefield where drones and electronic warfare are changing how wars are fought,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. “The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will make sure our military learns from what Ukraine has discovered through years of defending itself against Putin’s invasion, from countering drone swarms and operating through electronic warfare to sustaining weapons production under attack. We need to put those lessons to work to strengthen our own military, protect our servicemembers, and ensure we are prepared to deter aggression across the world.”

“Ukraine’s defense against Russia has shown just how rapidly modern warfare is evolving. I saw that firsthand during my trip to Ukraine last month, where drones, electronic warfare, cyber operations, and defense manufacturing are reshaping the battlefield in real time,” said Vindman. "As a 25-year Army veteran, I know our military must constantly learn, adapt, and innovate to maintain our strategic advantage and protect our service members. The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will ensure the Department of Defense learns from Ukraine’s hard-earned experience and applies those lessons to our doctrine, training, and capabilities so our military is prepared for the threats of tomorrow.”

The LESSONS from Ukraine Act would require the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress within 120 days on lessons the U.S. military can draw from the Russia-Ukraine War, including the use of drones and other unmanned systems, electronic and cyber warfare, air defense, operations without GPS or satellite communications, battlefield medicine, and Ukraine’s efforts to expand and decentralize weapons production. The Pentagon would also be required to develop a plan and timetable for incorporating those lessons into U.S. military doctrine and training. Congressman Krishnamoorthi first announced the legislation following an August official visit to Ukraine, where he visited a Ukrainian drone production facility and met with officials about the battlefield and Ukraine’s rapidly evolving defense innovations.

title: Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers on FDA Move to Rewrite Vaping Approval Rules, Blasts Weakening of Scientific Standards
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Caucus to End Youth Vaping, today demanded answers from Food and Drug Administration Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas over FDA’s September 28 announcement that it is considering new rulemaking to replace the 2021 regulations governing approval of new tobacco products, pressing the agency over whether the move could weaken the scientific standards manufacturers must meet.

Krishnamoorthi is also demanding to know whether FDA discussed potential changes with tobacco manufacturers, industry associations, or parties challenging the current rules before announcing its review, and is seeking communications between agency officials and Altria, Reynolds American, their subsidiaries and representatives, and other parties challenging the framework.

FDA announced its review less than four weeks after Altria subsidiaries NJOY and Helix Innovations sued the agency over the current Premarket Tobacco Product Application framework. FDA itself cited recent litigation challenging the framework, along with the widespread illicit tobacco market, in explaining its decision to consider replacing the rule.

“The widespread sale of illegal products is an enforcement problem,” Krishnamoorthi wrote. “It should not become a justification for lowering the evidentiary requirements manufacturers must satisfy before FDA authorizes their products.”

Krishnamoorthi also raised concerns about the review in light of FDA’s recent authorization of flavored e-cigarette products. In May, the agency authorized Glas products in mango and blueberry flavors despite FDA data indicating that fruit-flavored e-cigarettes are the most popular flavor among youth. The letter notes that the FDA Center for Tobacco Products did not require the manufacturer to demonstrate that the flavors provided an added benefit to adults attempting to transition from combustible products, and that former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary reportedly resigned in part amid political interference surrounding the authorization.

FDA then authorized additional JUUL products on August 28, including a JUUL2 menthol product.

“FDA acknowledged that the menthol product carries risks ‘including youth appeal,’ but concluded that its benefits to adults who smoke outweighed those risks,” Krishnamoorthi wrote. “Exactly one month later, FDA announced that it may replace the broader framework governing applications for new tobacco products.”

Krishnamoorthi concluded:

“The FDA’s job is to protect public health, not make it easier for tobacco companies to evade rigorous scientific review. The agency should crack down on companies selling illegal products, not use their lawbreaking as a rationale for weakening safeguards governing products seeking FDA authorization.”

Krishnamoorthi requested written responses by October 20, 2026, to the following questions:

Which specific provisions of the 2021 PMTA rule is FDA considering changing or eliminating, and what evidence supports each potential change?

Will FDA commit that any replacement framework will not lower the scientific evidentiary bar manufacturers must meet to demonstrate that marketing their products is appropriate for the protection of public health? If not, why not?

Did FDA discuss potential changes to the 2021 PMTA rule with any tobacco product manufacturer, industry association, or party challenging the 2021 PMTA rule before announcing its review? Please identify each such entity and provide all communications since January 20, 2025, between FDA officials and those entities. Please also provide all communications since January 20, 2025, between FDA officials and Altria, Reynolds American, their subsidiaries or representatives, and any other party challenging the rule concerning the PMTA framework or potential changes to it.

How does the existence of a widespread illicit market justify changes to the regulatory requirements governing products seeking lawful authorization? What connection has FDA identified between illegal sales and the scientific evidence manufacturers should be required to provide before receiving authorization?

What additional enforcement actions will FDA take, in coordination with the Department of Justice and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, to remove unauthorized e-cigarettes from the U.S. market?

The full letter is available here.

title: Connecticut Congressional Delegation and Governor Lamont Announce Disaster Declaration from U.S. Small Business Administration for Homeowners, Renters, and Businesses Impacted by September Flooding
text:
Hartford, CT – Today, members of the Connecticut Congressional delegation joined Governor Ned Lamont to announce a disaster declaration from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) for Fairfield County and the contiguous counties of New Haven County and Litchfield County in response to the flash flooding event that impacted the region on September 13, 2026. The approved declaration means that homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits in the impacted counties can apply for low-interest loans from the SBA to aid in their recovery.

“This declaration makes low-interest loans available to homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits so they can recover and rebound from these flash floods,” Governor Lamont said. “I am glad that we’ve been able to secure this funding and encourage anyone who was impacted by this storm to look into this assistance and determine whether it can help you in the recovery process.”

“As communities continue to recover from severe flooding that hit our state last month, I am glad that the Small Business Administration granted our request for a disaster declaration," said Congressman John B. Larson. "This declaration is a crucial step forward, so small businesses, local organizations, and homeowners can get the help they need to repair and rebuild after incurring damage—including in Litchfield County. Our delegation will keep working with the governor and state leaders to ensure the federal government is responsive to the towns and cities that were impacted by this storm.”

“This disaster declaration is a strong step toward bringing federal aid to Connecticut following severe floods last month. This step allows Connecticut state agencies to work with federal partners like the SBA to continue recovery efforts and potentially unlock more federal assistance to rebuild local businesses. I am grateful to the SBA for their swift response to Governor Lamont and our delegation’s request,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal.

“Connecticut communities were hit hard on September 13 by sudden and intense flooding. I encourage all small business owners in the counties covered by this disaster declaration to take advantage of the available assistance from the Small Business Administration,” said Congressman Joe Courtney.

“Extreme weather events like flash flooding are damaging our communities more often and more unexpectedly. I am glad that federal support is on its way through this SBA disaster declaration for the businesses, residents, and communities that were impacted by devastating flash floods last month. I will continue to fight for federal resources so that Connecticut has the support necessary rebuild after disasters like this one,” said Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro.

“I’m glad the federal government is stepping up to assist Connecticut residents and businesses, especially those in Fairfield County, in recovering from last month’s flooding. I encourage anyone whose residence or business was impacted by the severe weather to look into these resources. I will continue fighting alongside the rest of Connecticut’s Congressional delegation to bring home the federal support our constituents need to rebound,” said Congressman Jim Himes.

“Extreme weather continues to impact our state. I am pleased to see the U.S. Small Business Administration approve federal assistance for parts of the Fifth District and our state. These federal resources will help alleviate the financial losses of business leaders and homeowners from the recent flooding,” said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes.

The following groups may be eligible for low-interest SBA disaster loans:

Homeowners: Up to $500,000 to repair their primary residence.

Homeowners and renters: Up to $100,000 to repair or replace damaged or destroyed personal property.

Business owners: Up to $2,000,000 for the replacement of real property, inventories, machinery, equipment, and other physical losses.

Businesses and nonprofits: Economic Injury Disaster Loans of up to $2,000,000 to provide necessary working capital until normal operations resume after a disaster.

“We know there are people with uninsured losses. These low-interest SBA loans are a means for people to rebuild and recover from the flooding. Additionally, our Volunteer Organizations Active in Disaster—independent faith-based and nonprofit groups—remain engaged in helping people needing cleanup,” saidConnecticut Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection Commissioner Ronnell A. Higgins.

How to apply for low-interest SBA disaster loans

Under this declaration, the application deadline for physical damage loans is December 1, 2026, and the application deadline for economic injury loans is July 2, 2027.

Applications may be submitted to the SBA through the following methods:

In-person: A temporary, in-person SBA Disaster Loan Outreach Center will open at the Margaret E. Morton Government Center at 999 Broad Street in Bridgeport beginning October 7, 2026.

It will operate Mondays through Fridays from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Saturdays from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.; and it will be closed on Sundays.

Due to prior engagements, it will have adjusted hours of 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on October 9, 2026; and 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on October 20 and 21, 2026.

It will be closed on October 12, 2026, due to the Columbus Day holiday.

It is expected to permanently close at 4:00 p.m. on October 21, 2026.

Online: The MySBA Loan Portal at https://lending.sba.gov provides applicants with the ability submit applications online, view loan details, check balances, make payments, and access statements.

title: Letlow Legislation Helps Women Better Understand their Breast Cancer Risk
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – As Breast Cancer Awareness Month kicks off, Congresswoman Julia Letlow has filed legislation aimed at strengthening risk assessment services for women vulnerable to a breast cancer diagnosis.

Letlow’s Know Your Risk Act would require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to advance a single, universal breast cancer risk assessment tool, while expanding access to risk evaluation services under the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program.

“1 in 8 women will develop breast cancer in their lifetime, and early interventions are proven to increase treatment quality as well as the odds of survival. A risk assessment tool was crucial for determining my own risk, and I want all at-risk women to have the same opportunity,” said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.

Risk assessments generally evaluate an individual’s likelihood of developing cancer based on family history, genetic factors, reproductive history, and lifestyle factors. A universal tool would give women better access to information about their individual breast cancer risk, while helping physicians detect cases earlier and thus provide more effective treatments.

A proliferation of risk evaluation tools and the lack of a clear, go-to assessment prevents many women from properly determining their risk.

“We have to close gaps that prevent many women from evaluating their risk in the first place,” added Letlow. “Like many women and families, I’ve had personal experiences with this awful disease and continue to see the need to ensure that women are not left in the dark when it comes to knowing their risk.”

Specifically, the legislation:

Requires HHS to advance plans for a single, publicly accessible risk-assessment tool.

Requires the agency to study existing breast-cancer risk tools and report to Congress on inaccuracies in existing risk-assessment tools, gaps in their use among different populations, and what causes those inaccuracies and gaps.s

Expands access to breast cancer risk assessment tools under CDC grants available to states under the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program.

title: REP LIEU JOINS REP. FRIEDMAN, LOS ANGELES DELEGATION, AND ENTERTAINMENT UNIONS IN PUSH FOR NATIONAL FILM & TV TAX CREDIT
text:
Takes effect quickly. The credit applies to productions that begin in taxable years starting after December 31, 2026.

title: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna Delivers $953,390 for Marine Research at Eckerd College
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13) presented a $953,390 check in federal funding to Eckerd College to advance environmental monitoring and marine research focused on generating critical data needed to protect and preserve coastal resources of Tampa Bay and the West Florida Shelf.

The funding, secured by Rep. Luna, will support a one-year Eckerd College Marine Science Program project monitoring major environmental pressures across Tampa Bay. Faculty and students will gather critical data on water quality, marine ecosystems, and changing conditions to inform conservation efforts and protect coastal resources vital to the region’s economy and communities.

“Florida’s way of life depends on healthy waters,” said Rep. Luna. “This funding gives Eckerd scientists and students the tools to better understand Tampa Bay and preserve it for generations to come.”

Tampa Bay’s coastal resources are also a major economic driver for the region, with tourism, commercial fishing, shipping, recreation, and other industries relying heavily on local waters. An estimated one in ten jobs across the Tampa Bay region is tied to local waters, making reliable environmental monitoring essential not only to protecting marine ecosystems but also to preserving the economic activity they sustain.

“Our faculty and students are protecting and preserving these resources across our region through critical monitoring initiatives,” says Eckerd College President James J. Annarelli, Ph.D. “From microplastic pollution and red tide blooms to invasive invertebrate species and stone crab fisheries, the four monitoring initiatives to be supported by this Community Project Funding will make a lasting impact on ecosystem health and economic vitality in our region.”

For decades, Eckerd College has paired undergraduate marine science education with hands-on faculty research, helping students earn 115 NOAA Hollings Scholarships and numerous Goldwater, Fulbright, and NSF Graduate Fellowships. The new funding will expand those opportunities for students to contribute directly to research protecting Tampa Bay and the West Florida Shelf.

The research will build on years of work by Eckerd faculty studying changes across the local marine ecosystem, from harmful algal blooms and emerging contaminants to wildlife, biodiversity, and economically important fisheries. Their findings will help scientists and resource managers better understand changing conditions to guide future conservation efforts and protection of the region.

Rep. Luna presented the check at Eckerd College alongside College President Dr. James J. Annarelli

title: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna Re-Presents Legion of Merit to Captain Stanley Beach
text:
Washington, D.C. — On Monday, Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13) formally re-presented the Legion of Merit to retired U.S. Navy Captain Stanley Beach after helping correct his military record to officially reflect the award he received upon his retirement from the Navy in 1987.

Captain Beach served 30 years in the Navy, including 27 years in the Chaplain Corps and service alongside Marines in Vietnam. His distinguished career earned him recognition as a “living legend” within the Chaplain Corps. Decades after his retirement, he discovered that the Legion of Merit had never been recorded on his DD-214. Rep. Luna worked with the Department of the Navy to correct his record and secure a DD-215 formally adding the award.

“Captain Beach spent nearly three decades serving our country, and his military record should reflect every honor he earned,” said Rep. Luna. “Correcting this decades-old omission is the least our nation owes him for his service and sacrifice, and I am grateful my office could help make it happen.”

Captain Beach’s son, Police Chief Randall Beach, hosted the ceremony and credited Rep. Luna and her office with helping resolve the issue on his father’s behalf. “What really made this happen was the leadership of Representative Anna Paulina Luna and her staff,” said Beach. “You cannot do this without Congress. It matters!”

A DD-214 is the primary separation document issued to service members and records key details of their military service, including decorations and awards. A DD-215, formally known as a Correction to DD Form 214, is issued when information on that original separation record must later be corrected or added. Unlike the DD-214, it is not routinely issued to veterans, making it a comparatively uncommon document that reflects a formal amendment to an existing military record.

Captain Beach enlisted as a Sailor in 1953 and entered the Chaplain Corps in 1960. After volunteering to serve with Marines in Vietnam, he joined the 3rd Marine Division and later served with 3rd Battalion, 4th Marines at Phu Bai and during intense fighting at Mutter’s Ridge. While under enemy fire, Beach ministered to wounded Marines and carried them to aid stations before sustaining severe injuries to his leg and stomach that required his own evacuation.

For his actions in Vietnam, Beach received the Bronze Star with Valor, the Purple Heart, and the Navy Commendation Medal with Combat “V.” He later served as Director of the Navy Chaplains School and received the David E. White Leadership Award in 2007. In 2012, and the Naval Chaplaincy School and Center named its building Stanley J. Beach Hall in recognition of his heroic service with 3rd Battalion, 4th Marines during the Vietnam War.

Rep. Luna re-presented the Legion of Merit to Captain Beach at Freedom Square in Seminole alongside local officials and members of the community.

title: Chairman Meuser Releases Staff Report on Public Housing Agency Failures
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Congressman Dan Meuser (PA-09), Chairman of the House Financial Services Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, and Congressman French Hill (AR-02), Chairman of the House Financial Services Committee, released a staff report examining Public Housing Agencies (PHAs) nationwide.

This report is the culmination of a year-long Subcommittee-led investigation into serious mismanagement of PHAs across the country. On February 9, 2026, Chairman Meuser, Chairman Hill, and Congressman Mike Flood (NE-01), Chairman of the Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance, sent letters to 32 PHAs designated by HUD as “troubled,” seeking information on living conditions, management, and financial oversight. This was followed by an Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee hearing examining management failures at PHAs and ways to improve conditions for residents. During the hearing, witnesses outlined severe shortcomings at PHAs due to mismanagement from previous administrations and discussed best practices for reversing the trend.

On March 13, 2026, Chairman Meuser held a Subcommittee field hearing in Little Rock, Arkansas, focused on failures at the city’s PHA—the Metropolitan Housing Alliance (MHA)—and its impact on residents. Committee leadership also sent a letter to the U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas urging an investigation into MHA.

Federal law requires PHAs to provide housing that is decent, safe, and sanitary. However, the Subcommittee’s investigation found that many troubled PHAs failed to meet these requirements due to management issues and oversight problems, resulting in significant waste of taxpayer resources and poor living conditions.

The Housing Authority of Champaign County is a good example of a PHA that has implemented commonsense Trump Administration policies, such as Moving to Work (MTW) requirements and voluntary time limits, that strengthen public housing standards and promote solutions that improve financial management.

“For years, the Biden Administration allowed PHAs to fail without proper support or oversight. Mismanagement and a lack of accountability in PHAs have wasted taxpayer dollars meant to support our most vulnerable citizens and led to unacceptable living conditions,” said Subcommittee Chairman Meuser. “This report shows that taxpayers and residents pay the price when leadership at PHAs falls short. Democrat administrations allowed this problem to fester for far too long. I appreciate Chairman Hill’s leadership, as well as President Trump and HUD Secretary Turner for their efforts to enhance federal support for public housing and demand greater accountability. This report supports and builds on that work to ensure that taxpayer-funded resources are well managed, and that Americans in need can benefit from decent, safe, and sanitary housing. I look forward to implementing our report’s recommendations and providing these crucial reforms to America’s most vulnerable citizens.”

“Americans living in federally supported housing deserve access to housing that is safe, clean, and livable,” said Chairman Hill. “PHAs exist to deliver on that promise. Unfortunately, as we've seen firsthand in my hometown of Little Rock, too many PHAs are failing the tenants who rely on them and the taxpayers who are footing the bill. I thank Subcommittee Chairman Meuser for his work holding PHAs accountable, protecting tenants, and for advocating for responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars.”

“PHA accountability and addressing waste, fraud, and abuse are key priorities for President Trump, Secretary Turner, and myself. At HUD, we are committed to restoring compliance and operational integrity. Our residents need it, and taxpayers expect it. HUD will continue working with Chairman Hill and Congress to ensure America’s public housing authorities are providing quality housing to America’s most vulnerable,” said HUD Assistant Secretary for Public and Indian Housing Ben Hobbs.

Key Findings:

PHA Leadership: Frequently, PHA Boards lack sufficient understanding of housing programs to effectively manage the PHA.

HUD’s Assessment Systems Disincentivize Rent Collection: HUD’s assessment system awards up to 16 points for occupancy but only 6 for rent collection, so a PHA that collects no rent can still pass HUD’s operations assessment.

Between 15 and 30 percent of residents at struggling PHAs pay only the minimum rent. The COVID-era eviction moratoriums caused unpaid rent to rise sharply.

Data and Due Diligence Issues: Troubled PHAs have insufficient data retention and due diligence standards across their operations, but particularly as it relates to their contracting and procurement standards.

PHAs struggle to find staff: PHAs struggle to find staff with sufficient experience and understanding of their roles and responsibilities. PHAs have particularly struggled to hire and retain maintenance staff, who can often find higher pay and more flexibility as independent contractors.

What HUD is Doing:

Proposed rule allowing work requirements and time limits: PHAs could opt in to work requirements of up to 40 hours a week and time limits of two years or more for work-capable adults. The comment period has closed, but the rule isn't final yet.

Reformed NSPIRE Inspections: HUD retrained inspectors, issued more guidance, improved its online inspection systems, and reorganized how inspectors are assigned to cut costs. It set February 1, 2027, for full implementation of these new standards.

More Inspections: HUD did 25 percent more inspections in 2025 than in 2024, and PHAs say inspections have become more consistent.

Took steps on safety: HUD launched a national public housing crime hotline, required stricter background checks for applicants, and rescinded guidance that had allowed people with criminal records to live in Section 9 housing.

Key Report Recommendations:

PHAs should develop systems and policies to enhance oversight of employees and contractors.

PHAs should conduct self-inspections at least quarterly and require before-and-after photos of maintenance work. They should also digitize their records, strengthen oversight of staff and contractors, and better enforce rent collection.

HUD and Congress should set baseline qualifications for PHA board members and executives and give HUD the authority to remove poor leaders.

Congress should consider legislation that permanently allows for and encourages PHAs to implement time limits and work requirements on public housing assistance for able-bodied adult residents.

title: Dr. Miller-Meeks Joins Iowa Delegation in Push for More Rural Health Care Funding
text:
IOWA – Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks, M.D. (IA-01) joined the Iowa congressional delegation in urging Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet Oz to support Iowa’s latest funding request through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), known as Healthy Hometowns. The program, created through the Working Families Tax Cuts law, has already delivered $209 million to strengthen rural health care across Iowa in its first year.

“Iowa’s rural communities deserve access to high-quality health care close to home, and we are already seeing these investments make a difference,” said Dr. Miller-Meeks. “As a doctor and a representative of rural Iowa, I will continue fighting to bring more resources home, strengthen our rural health care workforce, and make sure Iowans can get the care they need without having to travel hours from home.”

In addition to Miller-Meeks, the letter was signed by U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA), U.S. Sen. Joni Ernst (R-IA) and U.S. Reps. Ashley Hinson (IA-02), Zach Nunn (IA-03) and Randy Feenstra (IA-04).

“In January, Iowa became the first state in the nation to award Rural Health Transformation Program funding as part of its Healthy Hometowns initiative, and it has ensured resources are going directly to rural communities, not bureaucrats. In year one of the program, Iowa’s $209 million federal investment is improving cancer prevention and treatment, workforce recruitment and retention, chronic disease care, and maternal and child health,” the members wrote.

“As we each travel throughout Iowa, visiting hospitals, health centers, clinics, and more, we witness firsthand how these investments are making a difference toward the health, well-being, and quality of life in rural communities. During your visit to the University of Iowa in May, you learned how our state is using telehealth and a hub-and-spoke model to increase access to care and improve health outcomes in our rural communities,” the members continued.

The members noted how communities across Iowa are already benefiting from these federal investments, including through the following six projects:

Mahaska Health in Oskaloosa is purchasing a new PET/CT system with cardiac imaging capability and recruiting an OB/GYN and a general surgeon physician assistant.

Washington County Hospital in Washington is purchasing a new CT scanner that is improving diagnostic capabilities and patient outcomes.

Lucas County HealthCenter in Chariton is purchasing its first-ever MRI machine to bring early detection cancer screenings to residents.

North Iowa Medical Center in Mason City is purchasing a new robotic bronchoscopy system that detects lung cancer earlier than previously possible.

Sioux Center Health in Sioux Center is expanding prenatal care through a new regional maternal health coordinator.

Wayne County Hospital in Corydon is standing up a radiation oncology center and will be serving as a combat cancer health hub.

Background

Dr. Miller-Meeks has been a strong advocate for expanding access to health care in rural Iowa. She has held three roundtables focused on the Rural Health Transformation Program, bringing together Iowa health care providers and stakeholders to discuss how the program can strengthen rural health care and expand access.

Miller-Meeks also raised the need for additional rural health resources directly with CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz during his visit to Iowa. Iowa’s timely and proactive implementation of its Rural Health Transformation Program could position the state to receive additional funding if other states do not utilize their available resources.

title: ICYMI: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Urges HUD to Implement Whole Home Repairs Law
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) joined U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) and U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) in a letter to U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Secretary Scott Turner urging an establishment of a Whole Home Repairs program through the Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes.

The Members wrote:

“Almost 7 million Americans live in homes that are in need of significant repair, with deficiencies including leaky roofs, faulty wiring, and mold. This is an issue that disproportionately affects America’s seniors, many of whom would like to downsize but do not want to sell the home at a steep discount due to the updates required. As we saw in Commonwealth of Pennsylvania’s successful Whole Home Repairs program, providing grants for repairs allowed seniors to sell larger homes to growing families.”

The Whole-Home Repairs Act was signed into law with the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. The Whole Home Repairs pilot program will provide renovation and repair grants to homeowners and small landlords. This will help ensure America’s aging homes do not fall out of the housing supply.

The Members continued:

“The language in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act authorizes you to operate a Whole Home Repairs program through 2031. We want to show the nation that repairing America’s crumbling homes is not a red or blue issue. Creating greater access to housing is an American issue. Any delays will mean millions of American families may never realize the benefit of this program. We were proud to help the Whole Home Repairs bill become law, and we stand ready to support you in making it a reality for Americans.”

title: Nunn, Iowa Delegation Push for Continued Rural Health Care Investment
text:
DES MOINES, IA — Representative Zach Nunn (IA-03) joined Iowa’s congressional delegation in urging the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to fully consider Iowa’s request for a second year of Rural Health Transformation Funding. This new phase of funding would build on the initial $209 million awarded in 2026 to strengthen rural healthcare statewide.

“Where you live shouldn’t determine whether you can get the health care you need,” said Rep. Nunn. “That’s why we fought to bring $209 million back to Iowa to strengthen rural health care. In Wayne County, that means a patient fighting cancer can get treatment close to home instead of spending hours on the road — near the family and neighbors helping them through it. That’s the difference these investments can make. Rural hospitals have been asking for this support for years, and now they’re putting it to work for their patients. I’m urging CMS to keep that progress going for Iowa’s rural communities next year.”

The Rural Health Transformation Program was established through the Working Families Tax Cuts, which invested a historic $50 billion over five years to strengthen rural health care nationwide. This year, Iowa led the nation as the first state to roll out these funds, delivering grants to 58 awardees for rural healthcare worker recruitment, 42 awardees for new medical equipment, and five for new Combat Cancer Health Hubs, along with investments in chronic disease prevention and maternal and child health.

Four of Iowa’s five Combat Cancer Health Hubs are located in the Third District: Wayne County Hospital in Corydon, Ottumwa Regional Health Center, Greater Regional Medical Center, and Shenandoah Medical Center. These hubs will build regional cancer care networks to expand treatment access in rural communities. Together with other investments through the Rural Health Transformation Program, these funds will help rural health care providers expand services through new medical equipment, workforce recruitment, telehealth, and partnerships with other providers.

The delegation’s letter highlights the immense progress already underway across Iowa’s healthcare system and urges CMS to give the state’s fiscal year 2027 Rural Health Transformation Program funding request full and fair consideration to continue this historic investment.

A copy of the letter can be found here.

title: Nunn, Secretary Rollins Tour Animal Rescue League, Highlight Puppy Mills CrackDown
text:
“Man’s best friend deserves better than a lifetime of cruelty at the hands of puppy mill operators chasing a profit,” said Rep. Nunn. “I secured a bipartisan crackdown on puppy mills in the House-passed Farm Bill, and I’m grateful to work alongside Secretary Rollins to turn that authority into action: enforce the law, stop the abuse, and protect dogs before shelters have to rescue them.”

“Animal cruelty has no place in this country, and breeders who break the law must be held accountable,” said Secretary Rollins. “USDA is strengthening inspections and enforcement to protect dogs from abuse before rescue becomes their only hope. I’m grateful to Congressman Nunn for his leadership and to the Animal Rescue League of Iowa for its tireless work giving these animals the care and the second chance they deserve.”

Iowa remains one of the largest puppy mill states in the nation. In 2024 alone, the Animal Rescue League of Iowa and partner organizations rescued more than 400 animals from puppy mills, hoarding, and other inhumane conditions across the state. Rep. Nunn secured a bipartisan amendment in the House-passed Farm Bill reinforcing USDA’s authority to crack down on abusive breeders.

In September, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) deployed a new Animal Protection Bureau to identify unlicensed breeders, strengthen inspections, and coordinate enforcement against illegal operations. So far in 2026, USDA has conducted more than 2,000 inspections of dog breeder and broker facilities, suspended six licenses, and revoked five more from chronic violators.

title: Pappas Meets with NH CAP Leaders on Rising Energy Costs and LIHEAP
text:
Yesterday Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) hosted a roundtable with leaders of New Hampshire Community Action Partnership agencies for a discussion on the impact of rising energy costs on Granite Staters and the importance of the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).

New Hampshire households could pay $2,300 for home heating oil this winter because of President Trump’s war with Iran, a 31% increase. The cost of groceries rose 2.9 percent overall this year, and families paid $310 more for food during President Trump's first year in office compared to 2024. In total, American families have spent over $3,800 more on goods and services since President Trump took office.

“Electricity prices are up, natural gas and home heating oil prices are up, and diesel fuel is hitting record highs. Granite Staters don’t need federal data to tell them this: they are feeling it with every electric and gas bill. As we enter the colder months, tackling the rising cost of energy could not be more urgent,” said Congressman Pappas. “My new legislation would lower energy costs by increasing federal support for heating assistance, expanding eligibility to more families, and lowering gas and diesel costs. I will continue fighting to lower costs for families and put more money back in their pockets.”

Pappas recently introduced three new bills to lower energy costs.

The LIHEAP Act would expand the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), one of the most successful programs aimed at reducing energy costs for working families.

The American Homes First Act would increase funding for LIHEAP by redirecting $1 billion from President Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ slush fund.

The Consumer Fuel Prices Relief Act would provide federal fuel tax relief until the end of September 2027 by pausing the gas tax, the diesel tax, and the aviation fuel tax, while ensuring the benefit is immediately passed on to consumers in full. The legislation builds on his bicameral Gas Prices Relief Act of 2026, introduced in March, which would have suspended the federal gas tax through October 1, 2026. The legislation safeguards and maintains funding for roads, bridges, and gas spill remediation, and holds corporations accountable if they fail to pass along savings to individual consumers.

Background:

LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 30,000 households in New Hampshire, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff and President Trump’s repeated efforts to fully defund the program have put this assistance at risk.

In September 2026, Pappas led 116 of his Congressional colleagues across the aisle in urging for LIHEAP funds to be delivered to states as soon as possible, and no later than November 1st. He previously led 89 of his Congressional colleagues in calling for the protection of LIHEAP and the rehiring of all HHS staff who manage the LIHEAP program that were fired in April 2025, and has repeatedly led bipartisan calls for the Trump administration to distribute LIHEAP funds in a timely manner.

title: Pou Statement On Release of Martin Soto from ICE Detention
text:
PATERSON, NJ – Tonight, U.S. Representative Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) celebrated the release of Martin Soto, a resident of the Ninth Congressional District who was held in ICE custody for several months.

“I am so overjoyed that Martin Soto is finally freed from ICE custody,” stated Rep. Nellie Pou, a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security. “Martin was undeniably targeted and mistreated, being moved from Delaney Hall to the Elizabeth Detention Center and held in solitary confinement. For months my office has been pushing ICE to release Martin and tonight justice is finally being done. It should have happened months ago. ICE remains out of control in our state and we must continue to oppose its rampant abuses. But tonight we can be grateful the hard work from so many paid off and Martin is being reunited with his family.”

Initially detained in Newark, Martin Soto was moved to the Elizabeth Detention Center in retaliation for his role in the hunger and labor strike to highlight the deplorable conditions at Delaney Hall. There, Martin experienced harsh retribution including isolation.

Rep. Pou and her staff have been working with the Soto family, advocates, and other elected officials to obtain his release for months.

“I am so happy Martin is finally being released from ICE custody,” said Gabby Soto, wife of Martin Soto. “I want to thank Congresswoman Nellie Pou for all of her work on his case. Her efforts were critical to us finally reaching this moment.”

title: WATCH: Pressley, Wu, Breadon Condemn USPS Service Cuts and Proposed Closure of Allston Post Office
text:
Transcript: Rep. Pressley Condemns USPS Plan to Close Allston Branch

October 5, 2026

Allston, MA

In serving on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, I was conducting a lot of oversight in the fight to send Postmaster DeJoy on his way. And I thought when we did that that we might be getting on a path to what the people deserve, and certainly the dedicated postal workers deserve. Instead, we find ourselves here.

But the reason why, in the midst of this, I still have hope, is because I believe in the power of pressure.

I believe in the power of organizing. I believe in the power of solidarity.

I was looking at Representative Honan and remembering the fight to save our branch libraries when we all came together and understood that they are a public good, a lifeline to and for the community, and so this is that same kind of fight. This is about livelihoods. This is about lives. This is about commerce. This is about connectivity. So that’s what brings us all here today.

I’m so grateful for the leadership of everyone who has been named and who has not been named, I’m so grateful to our mayor for convening us, and certainly grateful to our Council President, President Breadon, who has been indefatigable, and that is what we need to be in this fight.

Folks were shuddering a little bit. Maybe it’s a little chilly. It’s hot one second, cold the next. Yeah, welcome to perimenopause.

But the point is, the point is, you might be a little uncomfortable, but deal with it, so that we are never complacent in our advocacy.

I grew up in a family of proud letter carriers, postal workers, nurses, first responders. That was how we built the middle class. These good union jobs. They take pride in that work, no matter the weather, no matter the season, no matter the ingratitude, so that’s what brings us here today.

So I thank you all for showing up, for giving a damn, to show your support for reopening your neighborhood’s post office, which has been closed since 2019.

It is a shame, and the reason why we have to agitate, resist, and give our feedback, we see this is a very slippery slope because they’re trying to bring the same pain to Dorchester, which is why solidarity is so essential in this moment.

But everyone here, your advocacy, your love of community is inspiring. Now, while this injustice has gone on for too long, you refuse, you accept it as an inevitability, and let it be quietly swept under the rug.

So again, I say thank you to everyone, and especially to Scott Hoffman and all of our brothers and sisters at the American Postal Workers Union, who stand up every day for their members, as well as service and reliability for our neighbors.

For the past seven years, Allston residents have gone without retail post office services and had to travel to Brighton, to Brookline, or Cambridge to do their daily business. In that time, USPS has made commitments to my office, my colleagues’ offices, and the folks living in this community that they were searching for a new location and would indeed reopen.

There have been ups and downs, but finally, finally, it appeared we were close to having the branch reopen. A lease had been agreed to, construction plans were in place with the developer. Now we are told that this plan is to keep this branch permanently closed.

This is unconscionable. This is unacceptable.

With last week’s announcement of the quote-unquote “temporary” closure of the Fields Corner Post Office, I find it hard to believe that this is just a coincidence. And to be clear, these efforts to close our local branches are all part of a coordinated campaign.

Y’all are tired of me saying it as the co-founder of the Stop Project 2025 Task Force, but it was all laid out. It was not a blueprint. It was a playbook. They want to privatize the USPS. They want to privatize these essential services that our constituents need every single day.

The USPS has been serving our communities for 250 years, delivering our mail, our checks, our prescriptions, and our ballots.

The dedicated carriers who are out on our sidewalks six days per week are members of our community. They know our neighbors, and they are the way folks most often interact with the federal government.

These services are not nice to haves—they are must haves. And you, along with every other community, has come to depend upon them and rightly deserve them.

These efforts to degrade and undermine the postal service are intended to exhaust you and your neighbors, so that you’ll give up and do your business somewhere else. Hell no, we won’t go. But the services provided by USPS are a public good and should not be left to billionaires and for-profit private corporations to play games with.

Today, I’m proud to stand with Allston and everyone here, calling for the Postal Service to keep their word to this community.

They must reverse the decision, work to reopen the Austin branch, and restore daily service.

If they intend to follow through with this closure plan, they must give the community a way to have their voice heard, not simply hold a midday Zoom meeting when folks are at work or at school.

The 87,000 Allston-Brighton residents, our neighbors in Fields Corner, folks in Somerville, Grove Hall, and Mission Hill all need and should have an accessible and conveniently located post office to do their business.

So we will not stop advocating for what you deserve.

Again, I believe in the power of pressure, of organizing, and of solidarity.

We will not stop fighting the Republican campaign, because they are the architects of this, to privatize the postal service, and we will not stop fighting until Allston has a post office again.

And now, as someone who comes from a long line of letter carriers, it is my privilege to introduce a man who fights for better service for our friends and neighbors every single day, national business agent for the American Postal Workers Union, Scott Hoffman.

—
