title: Rep. Sara Jacobs Responds to Trump’s Dangerous Comments on San Diego
text:
Following President Trump’s comments suggesting that hypothetical Iranian attacks on San Diego or Los Angeles would be a “small price to pay,” Rep. Sara Jacobs released the following statement:

“The President sent San Diegans into a panic with his dangerous comments last night. I’ve received a flood of texts, calls, and emails from my constituents wondering if we’re safe, if there’ve been credible threats, and if we’re under attack. I’ve personally spoken with the local FBI field office and military leaders today, and they relayed to me that there are currently no increased threats to San Diego.

“It’s unbelievably distressing that President Trump is the cause of this stress when he’s supposed to protect and reassure our country. His comments are inexcusable. They don’t need more context, and we don’t need a thicker skin to understand them. San Diego and Los Angeles aren’t expendable, and neither are the service members who’ve already been killed in President Trump’s war with Iran. We need to end this war now before President Trump decides that all Americans can be collateral damage.”

title: Smucker Makes Case for Bipartisan Fiscal Commission on 584 Vetoes Podcast
text:
WASHINGTON — Rep. Lloyd Smucker (PA-11), Vice Chairman of the House Budget Committee and a senior member of the House Ways and Means Committee, joined the 584 Vetoes podcast to discuss the nation’s $40 trillion national debt and the need for bipartisan action to put the country on a more sustainable fiscal path. The podcast was hosted by Brian Miller, MD, MBA, MPH, FACPM, a practicing hospitalist, Associate Professor of Medicine at the Johns Hopkins University, and a Visiting Fellow at the Hoover Institution.

Listen here on Spotify | Listen here on YouTube | Listen Here on Apple Podcasts |

Read more and listen here on Substack

During the conversation with host Brian Miller, Smucker made the case for establishing a bipartisan fiscal commission that would bring lawmakers, experts, and the American people into a national conversation about the country’s fiscal future.

“The commission would be a vehicle to discuss the options that we have available, and perhaps even more important, it would be a discussion with the American public,” Smucker said. “That, I think, is the value of a commission.”

Smucker said he envisions a commission holding hearings across the country to engage Americans directly in understanding the nation’s fiscal challenges and the consequences of failing to address them.

“People get that and people want to see us solve this,” Smucker said. “The commission would engage the public and then bring the experts in and provide the recommendations that would lead to that legislation.”

Smucker also discussed the impact of the federal government spending more than $1 trillion annually on interest on the debt, the need to strengthen Social Security and Medicare for future generations, and the combination of stronger economic growth and responsible spending reforms necessary to improve the nation’s fiscal outlook.

Smucker said the House Budget Committee has an important role to play in driving that conversation, describing the committee as the “conscience of the conference and of Congress” and saying it should hold Congress accountable while providing “the road map and the path to better fiscal policy.”

The full episode of 584 Vetoes, “It’s Time for a Fiscal Commission to Fix the Debt with Congressman Lloyd Smucker,” is available here.

title: Soto Announces $1 Million U.S. Department of Justice Grant for the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office’s Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force

OSCEOLA COUNTY, FL — Today, Rep. Darren Soto (FL-09) announced that the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office received $1 million from the U.S. Department of Justice to purchase sophisticated software, equipment, and technology for the Central Florida Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force.

“I am proud to announce that the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office’s Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force is receiving $1 million from the U.S. Department of Justice as a result of our FY26 Community Project Funding request. This funding is critical to ensuring the task force has the resources to protect Central Florida children from predatory behavior online,” said Rep. Soto. “Over the years, we have worked closely with local law enforcement on securing COPS grants and bringing down federal dollars to help keep our communities safe.”

“The Osceola County Sheriff’s Office appreciates everything that Rep. Darren Soto has done to protect children, including his support of the ICAC Task Force,” said the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office.

The funds awarded through the Byrne Discretionary Community Project Grants/Byrne Discretionary Grants Program result from a FY26 Community Project Funding request made by Rep. Soto. title: Rep. Subramanyam Announced $1.5 Million Federal Funding for Oak Hill
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) announced an award of $1.5 million in federal grants for the mansion and outbuildings of the fifth President of the United States, James Monroe. Oak Hill, located in Loudoun County, has been preserved for hundreds of years and provides the local community and visitors access to American history and educational programming. Earlier this year, the Virginia General Assembly approved Governor Spanberger’s budget amendment to designated Oak Hill as a State Park. That amendment was championed by Senator Russet Perry and Delegate John McAuliff.

“Oak Hill is an important part of our history and has survived hundreds of years. This funding will ensure it can continue to live on for generations. I am proud that federal funding will help maintain and preserve this historical landmark. I look forward to seeing people of all ages in our community and across the world visit Oak Hill for many years to come,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanayam.

“For more than two years, we fought in Richmond to make Oak Hill a state park and protect more than 1,200 acres of Loudoun County and President Monroe’s historic home. We got it done, and now the work is making sure Oak Hill has what it needs to thrive for the long term. This $1.5 million in federal funding will help us do that, and I’m grateful to Congressman Subramanyam for securing these resources and being a partner in Oak Hill’s future. I’m looking forward to continuing this work and getting Oak Hill State Park open to the public,” said Senator Russet Perry.

"Oak Hill will be an enormous investment in the quality of life and conservation of Western Loudoun by opening up over 1,200 acres of farm and forestland for recreational use. The new funding secured by Congressman Subramanyam and State budget language provided by Gov. Spanberger ensures this land and history will be treasured by generations to come," said Delegate John McAuliff.

“Oak Hill stands as a powerful reminder of our nation’s founding story, and these grants ensure that story will be preserved for generations to come. We’re grateful to Rep. Subramanyam and our federal partners at the National Park Service for recognizing what this site means – not just to Loudoun County, but to the story of our nation as we mark 250 years of independence,” said Heather Richards, Mid-Atlantic Vice President, The Conservation Fund.

Of the $1.5 million in grants for preservation and restoration, $750k from Save America’s Treasures and $750k from Semiquincentennial grants. View the NPS announcements of funding here and here.

title: Congresswoman Lee Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect High-Risk Faith-Based and Community Organizations
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and María Elvira Salazar (R-FL) introduced the bipartisan Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act, which would make it easier for nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist attack to access federal grant funding for target hardening and physical security enhancements.

“We can all agree that our children should be able to go to school and that families should be able to worship without fear. As hate crimes rise throughout the country, nonprofit organizations, churches, synagogues, mosques, and religious schools are diverting their scarce resources away from serving their communities to pay for security cameras, guards, and emergency trainings,” said Congresswoman Lee. “No organization should be forced to choose between keeping their members safe or their financial stability. This commonsense, bipartisan bill will help nonprofit organizations fund security improvements and overall preparedness, so they can keep those they serve safe amid increased violence and harassment.”

“Every American should be able to worship without fear. When a church, synagogue, or other place of worship is approved for a federal security grant, it should be able to spend the money to improve security immediately. The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act gets security dollars out the door faster and helps protect our communities,” said Congresswoman Salazar.

Congress created the Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) in 2004 to help nonprofit organizations prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from terrorist or extremist attacks. The program funds target hardening, physical security improvements, and related preparedness activities for nonprofits at high risk of terrorism or hate-motivated violence.

Under current law, nonprofit organizations selected to receive an NSGP grant through a competitive application process must pay out of pocket for approved critical security upgrades and then wait months—or even years—to be reimbursed. This places these organizations in an impossible situation: cut into their limited budgets to ensure the safety of those they serve without any idea of when they might see that money or forgo critical security upgrades to ensure they can continue their work unabated.

The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act would amend the current law to require that NSGP awards be issued to approved nonprofits in advance, rather than as a reimbursement for costs already incurred. By allowing advance payments, FEMA could better support approved nonprofits that lack upfront capital, speed implementation of needed security measures, and strengthen protection for vulnerable communities.

“Synagogues and nonprofit are paying out of pocket for essential security, then waiting months or years to get their money back,” said Jonathan Greenblatt, ADL CEO and National Director. “Providing funding upfront to institutions already approved for security grants would help ease that financial burden and allow them to make critical security improvements sooner. We thank Representatives Susie Lee and María Elvira Salazar for advancing this commonsense solution to get security dollars where they’re needed, when they’re needed.”

“According to American Jewish Committee’s (AJC) State of Antisemitism in America 2025 Report, 28% of American Jews say that at least one Jewish institution they are affiliated with has been a target of antisemitic incidents in the last five years. As threats against Jewish institutions continue to rise, we applaud Representatives Susie Lee and María Elvira Salazar for introducing the Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act,” said Julie Rayman, AJC’s Senior Vice President of Policy and Political Affairs. “By removing a financial barrier that can delay or prevent needed security upgrades, this legislation will help at-risk institutions better protect the communities they serve.”

“Counties are on the front lines of keeping communities safe, but too often they are left filling the gap when nonprofits can’t afford to pay upfront for critical security upgrades,” said National Association of Counties Executive Director Matthew Chase. “The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act would allow approved nonprofits to receive funding upfront, helping them strengthen security sooner rather than delaying upgrades due to lack of capital. That means safer facilities, stronger coordination with local law enforcement and more resilient communities. Counties urge Congress to advance this bipartisan legislation quickly.”

“The Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) is an important resource for houses of worship to better secure themselves against acts of hate and prepare for all kinds of emergencies, but the logistical burdens of the process can pose barriers to applicants. This important proposal to disburse funds up front rather than requiring a reimbursement-based model removes one such major hurdle. With these kinds of improvements, as well as timely and apolitical execution by the Department of Homeland Security, NSGP can continue to serve more of our nation's most vulnerable communities in a time of increased threats.” – Mannirmal Kaur, Senior Federal Policy Manager, The Sikh Coalition.

The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act is endorsed by Jewish Nevada, American Jewish Committee (AJC), Anti-Defamation League (ADL), Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), National Association of Counties (NACO), Secure Community Network, and The Sikh Coalition.

title: Congressman Taylor Joins Ohio Trucking Leaders in Roundtable Discussion
text:
CHILLICOTHE, OH – Congressman Dave Taylor (OH-02) today joined the Ohio Trucking Association and local trucking industry leaders in a roundtable discussion at Kenworth on the critical role trucking plays in Ohio’s economy and the challenges trucking companies are facing across the state. Representatives from local companies shared their perspective and discussed ways Congress could best support the industry and promote safety on Ohio’s roads.

“America’s trucking industry moves 11 billion tons of goods more than 300 billion miles each year, and serves as the backbone of our economy,” said Congressman Taylor. “I was grateful to hear directly from Ohio’s trucking professionals today about the challenges they’re facing on the road and how I can best support them in Congress. As the founder of the Congressional Trucking Caucus, I will continue fighting to support Ohio’s hardworking truck drivers, uphold strong CDL safety standards, and ensure commercial trucks and families can safely share the road.”

Congressman Taylor is a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and is the founding member of the bipartisan Congressional Trucking Caucus, where he works to advance policies that support America’s trucking industry, strengthen highway safety, and keep goods moving across the country.

title: Thompson, Keating Highlight German-American Partnership
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) and Bill Keating (D-Mass.), co-chairs of the bipartisan German-American Caucus, introduced a resolution reaffirming German-American Friendship and supporting continued cooperation between the United States and Germany.

More than 36 years after the fall of the Berlin Wall, this resolution reaffirms the importance of the alliance between the United States and Germany and underscores our shared commitment to democracy. It also supports the “Wunderbar Together” initiative, which aims to celebrate German-American art, culture, science, friendship, and more.

“Pennsylvania has one of the largest populations of Americans with German heritage, and this resolution is an opportunity to acknowledge the strong alliance between the United States and Germany. I look forward to continuing to foster this partnership for years to come, and celebrating our two countries shared interests,” Rep. Thompson said.

“Germany and the United States share a relationship based on values, traditions, and friendship between peoples. This resolution recognizes the profound contributions of Germans to the United States and Congress’ unwavering support for the US-German relationship. As Co-Chair of the Congressional German-American Caucus, I look forward to strengthening our relationship in the years to come," Rep. Keating said.

“The transatlantic partnership between Germany and the United States remains a cornerstone of our economic ties and is grounded in shared values and interests. At a time of significant global economic and geopolitical challenges, strong transatlantic cooperation is more important than ever. The Representative of German Industry and Trade (RGIT) is pleased to reaffirm its support for Representative Thompson’s and Representative Keating's resolution and for continued cooperation between Germany and the United States.”– Representative of German Industry and Trade

Representative of German Industry and Trade (RGIT) is the liaison office of the Federation of German Industries (BDI) and the German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DIHK) in Washington, D.C.

Read the full resolution here.

title: Trahan, Warren, Lynch, Lead Demands to Trump Administration to Provide Relief for Skyrocketing Winter Heating Bills Amid Iran War
text:
LOWELL, MA – Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and Congressman Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08) led 24 of their colleagues from Northeastern states in pressing the Department of Energy (DOE) to take immediate action to address the rapidly rising cost of heating oil, which has surged around 60 percent since the start of President Trump’s war in Iran. In their letter, the lawmakers urged the DOE to support an immediate end to the war and prioritize lowering energy costs for the winter, warning that rising prices will force families to choose between heating their homes and paying for basic necessities.

“Heating oil costs for the upcoming winter are projected to reach record levels, and families throughout the northeastern United States will likely bear the brunt of these costs,” wrote the lawmakers.

The President’s war in Iran has played a large part in driving up the price of heating oil. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed crude oil from $72 to over $100 a barrel, causing a massive increase in heating oil costs in the United States. American families that rely on heating oil are projected to pay about $600 more to keep their homes warm this winter than last year.

In addition to increasing the cost of heating oil, the Trump administration has made or attempted to make heating costs for the upcoming winter even higher by:

Attempting to eliminate the $4 billion Low-Income Heating Assistance Program (LIHEAP) that supports families with high energy bills.

Effectively increasing taxes on solutions to the heating cost crisis by eliminating four tax credits and deductions that supported residential and commercial building energy efficiency upgrades.

Cutting more than $20 billion in clean energy and grid modernization funding for hundreds of energy projects across the country that would have decreased costs for families.

“As Americans face immense difficulty with keeping the heat on, the administration appears to be cutting off all avenues for meaningful relief, handing out tax cuts to billionaires, spending tens of billions of dollars on an unnecessary foreign war, and jacking up costs for struggling families,” the lawmakers continued.

“To address these costs for American families, we urge you to reverse course on the senseless war in Iran, undo the administration’s cuts to clean energy and grid modernization programs, work with Congress to repeal the tax increases imposed on energy efficiency upgrades and other ways to lower heating costs, and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP,” the lawmakers concluded.

The lawmakers were joined by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.); and Representatives Gabe Amo (D-R.I.), Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.), Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), Maggie Goodlander (D-N.H.), Bill Keating (D-Mass.), Seth Magaziner (D-R.I.), John Mannion (D-N.Y.), Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), Grace Meng (D-N.Y.), Seth Moulton (D-Mass.), Richard Neal (D-Mass.), Chris Pappas (D-N.H.), Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), and Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.).

A copy of the letter sent today can be accessed HERE.

title: Dân Biểu Derek Trần giới thiệu dự luật giảm chi phí nhà ở cho các gia đình Nam California
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) giới thiệu Dự Luật Hỗ Trợ Chi Phí Sinh Hoạt Nhà Ở cho Người Thuê Nhà (COST) Act, để hỗ trợ cư dân tại Nam California đang phải đối mặt với chi phí nhà ở ngày càng tăng. Dự luật thiết lập các khoản tín dụng thuế dành cho người thuê nhà, tiếp nối nỗ lực của Dân Biểu Derek nhằm giúp người dân có thêm cơ hội tiếp cận nhà ở với chi phí hợp lý.

“Chi phí nhà ở trên cả nước, đặc biệt tại Nam California, đã tăng đến mức báo động. Nhiều gia đình phải chật vật mới đủ tiền trả tiền thuê nhà, chưa nói đến việc tiết kiệm cho tương lai,” Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. “Dự luật này sẽ mang lại sự hỗ trợ thiết thực và kịp thời cho những người thuê nhà đang gặp khó khăn, giúp họ trang trải tiền thuê nhà, có thêm ngân sách cho các chi phí sinh hoạt hằng ngày, hoặc thậm chí dành dụm để mua nhà. Tôi tự hào dẫn đầu nỗ lực này vì các gia đình khắp nước Mỹ.”

Các gia đình tại Nam California phải đối mặt với mức chi phí nhà ở thuộc hàng cao nhất cả nước. Tại Orange County, tiền thuê nhà trung bình hiện vượt $3,200 mỗi tháng, tăng gần 40% kể từ năm 2017.

Dự luật đề nghị một khoản tín dụng thuế hoàn lại ở mức căn bản 8% dành cho các gia đình có tổng thu nhập từ $150,000 trở xuống, với mức hỗ trợ tối đa $333 mỗi tháng cho mỗi gia đình, tương đương $4,000 mỗi năm. Riêng tại Địa Hạt 45 của California, hơn 75,000 gia đình có thể được hưởng lợi từ chính sách này.

Trong khi những giải pháp khác nhằm giảm chi phí nhà ở có thể cần nhiều thời gian để thực hiện, dự luật này sẽ trực tiếp giúp người thuê nhà có thêm tiền để trang trải thực phẩm, thuốc men, chi phí chăm sóc trẻ em, và các nhu cầu thiết yếu khác.

Nỗ lực lập pháp này tiếp nối những hoạt động của Dân Biểu Derek Trần nhằm giải quyết vấn đề nhà ở trong khu vực:

Dân Biểu Derek Trần đã vận động thành công $250,000 ngân sách liên bang để hỗ trợ xây dựng 2,700 căn nhà ở giá phải chăng lâu dài khắp Orange County.

Dân Biểu Derek đồng bảo trợ Dự Luật Saving the American Dream Act, nhằm thành lập một lực lượng đặc nhiệm liên cơ quan để giải quyết cuộc khủng hoảng nhà ở, và Dự Luật Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act, hỗ trợ tài chính cho việc xây dựng thêm các khu nhà ở nhiều căn.

Ngoài ra, Dân Biểu Derek đã bỏ phiếu ủng hộ Dự Luật 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, được ký thành luật vào Tháng Bảy, 2026, đẩy nhanh tiến độ xây dựng nhà ở và giảm bớt các thủ tục hành chính không cần thiết.

Toàn văn dự luật có thể được xem TẠI ĐÂY.

title: Congressman Van Drew Calls on FERC to Determine Refunds and Rate Relief for South Jersey
text:
Washington, DC - Today, Congressman Van Drew sent a letter to Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Chairman Laura Swett calling on the Commission to independently review how much Atlantic City Electric (ACE) customers were overcharged after a federal audit found the company overbilled transmission customers from 2021 to 2025.

"Atlantic City Electric cannot be allowed to decide for itself how much it overcharged people and then tell everyone the answer is less than two cents a month," said Congressman Van Drew. "First, we were told there was nothing wrong. Then we were told that residential customers were not impacted. Once the federal audit proved there was overbilling, suddenly the answer became that people were owed almost nothing. Meanwhile, they have continued asking for rate increases while bringing in record profits. Anyone opening an electric bill in South Jersey knows why people are not buying that.

"The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities should have gotten to the bottom of this, but they have not. With the state refusing to act, I am asking FERC to use the authority available to it to independently determine what customers are owed from these transmission overcharges and what relief should follow. We need independent numbers and full refunds with interest to bring relief for South Jersey families."

title: Rep. Vasquez Urges Administration to Halt Rule Change Expanding Vehicle Access and Increasing Risks on Public Lands
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 6, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Under Secretary Michael Boren and U.S. Forest Service (USFS) Chief Tom Schultz strongly opposing the Administration’s proposed rule expanding vehicle access to public lands and trails that are already facing maintenance backlogs. Vasquez was joined by 28 of his House and Senate colleagues in his call to keep the 2005 Travel Management Rule in place.

“New Mexicans deserve public lands that are safe and well-managed. Ending the long-established Travel Management Rule would put public safety at risk and open the door to damage that will take generations to undo,” said Vasquez. “Hikers, hunters, and ranchers alike shouldn’t have to worry about more folks driving through the spaces they use for recreation and grazing. Instead of opening more of our public lands to vehicle access in places where access already exists, the Forest Service should focus on maintaining existing trails and roads. This broad reversal is unnecessary."

The USFS and the Bureau of Land Management have separate but similar rules requiring our public land agencies to provide clear, consistent guidance for how public lands are used, including where motorized vehicles, including cars and ATVs, can travel. For those who enjoy our public lands, whether on foot or on wheels, these rules help keep trails open, accessible, and responsibly managed. They also require public input before designating routes, produce Motor Vehicle Use Maps that show visitors where they can go, give rangers clear standards to enforce, and allow exceptions for emergency, military, and law enforcement vehicles.

Changing the 2005 rule, as proposed by USDA, could endanger public safety, reduce quality access to our public lands, and degrade the quality of trails, lands and waters that support our nation’s wildlife and outdoor recreation economy.

The letter demands that any revisions to the 2005 Travel Management Rule preserve the following core principles:

Maintain the current default of keeping routes and areas closed to motorized use unless expressly designated as open.

Carry forward criteria that guide local land management decisions and protect critical public land values, including soil, watersheds, vegetation, and wildlife habitat, as well as reduce conflicts between public land uses such as camping, hiking, hunting, and grazing.

Travel management decisions should continue to be informed by robust public engagement and local input.

The agencies must retain the ability to protect fish and wildlife habitat, riparian areas, water quality, and cultural resources.

The agencies should continue to clearly identify where motorized travel is permitted.

The agencies should consider the long-term cost of properly maintaining, staffing, and administering their transportation system before adding new routes or expanding access.

“This is yet another egregious attack in the systematic dismantling of public lands management of our national forests,” said Paul Sanford, director for equitable access policy advocacy at The Wilderness Society. “Travel management provides the basic guardrails that let hikers, hunters, anglers, and riders share the same forest without chaos; removing those guardrails threatens the freedom of all public lands users to safely enjoy our national forests the way they choose. Paired with the proposed repeal of the Roadless Rule, this destructive agenda sells out future generations’ enjoyment of our forests in order to hand them over for corporate profits.”

“We’re grateful to see Congressional Leaders pushing back on federal agency proposals to gut travel management regulations and prioritize off-road vehicles at the expense of wildlife, cultural sites, desert waterways and other recreationists, proposals that will make visiting Utah’s canyon country worse for everyone,” said Laura Peterson, Senior Attorney at the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance (SUWA). “The Trump Administration’s vision for public lands is not about balance or reasonable access, it is about blanketing landscapes with off-road vehicle routes, transforming quiet, wild places into motorized playgrounds.”

"We stand with Rep. Vasquez and his urgent request to keep the Travel Management Rule intact,” said Taylor Rush, government relations representative at Defenders of Wildlife. "For more than two decades, this rule has protected our cherished wildlife, outdoor recreationists, clean water supply and local communities from the harmful impacts of unmanaged motorized vehicle use. Weakening the framework used to reduce habitat damage and social conflict would result in dangerous degradation of our wild places and wildlife."

title: Vindman Stands Up for Roadless Rule to Protect Virginia’s Natural Resources, Local Economies
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) — the only Virginian on the U.S. House Agriculture Committee — joined Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04) in sending a letter to Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins opposing the Trump Administration’s proposal to rescind the Roadless Area Conservation Rule, commonly referred to as the “Roadless Rule.”

Since its implementation in 2001, the Roadless Rule has protected 45 million acres of forest lands across the country, including nearly 394,000 acres in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Under the Trump Administration, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Forest Service filed a proposal in August of this year to repeal the Roadless Rule, which could have devastating impacts on water quality, biodiversity, economic development and more for these regions.

The letter was also signed by U.S. Senators Mark Warner (D-Va.) and Tim Kaine (D-Va.), and U.S. Representatives Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) and James Walkinshaw (Va.-11).

“This proposal would strip protections from approximately 84% of Virginia’s roadless areas, opening these lands to road construction, logging, and other industrial activities. The consequences for Virginia’s environment, economy, and public health would be severe, falling squarely on the families and communities we represent,” wrote the lawmakers. “With more roadless acres than any other state east of the Mississippi River, Virginia has an outsized stake in decisions regarding the Roadless Rule. Once lost, these ecosystems and the countless benefits they provide to clean air, clean water, and climate resilience cannot be easily restored, if at all.”

The letter outlines the risks this rescission would pose to Virginia by jeopardizing Virginia’s drinking water and ecosystems, threatening economic activity driven by recreation and tourism activities, increasing wildfire risk and straining public resources.

“For 25 years, the Roadless Rule has demonstrated that protecting America’s national forest lands is both effective and widely supported. Rescinding the Roadless Rule would ignore this overwhelming public consensus while undermining Virginia’s drinking water, biodiversity, local economies, and public safety,” the lawmakers concluded. “We urge the Department to withdraw this dangerous proposal and maintain the Roadless Area Conservation Rule of 2001 in its entirety.”

title: Walberg Welcomes EPA Regional Administrator to Berrien County
text:
Today, Congressman Tim Walberg (MI-05) welcomed Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 5 Administrator Anne Vogel to southwestern Michigan for a visit to a local brownfield site and a stakeholder roundtable focused on Great Lakes priorities.

Congressman Walberg and Administrator Vogel visited the former Anstey Foundry brownfield site in Stevensville. The site was awarded a $733,250 grant in June 2026, as part of the EPA's Brownfields Program to support cleanup, restoration, and community engagement efforts.

They then traveled to the Village of Michiana for a roundtable discussion with local leaders on Great Lakes Restoration Initiative successes, current basin challenges, and the EPA’s ongoing priorities.

"It was an honor to host Regional Administrator Vogel to highlight our shared commitment to protecting the Great Lakes and discuss the importance of strategic investments to create healthier, revitalized communities," said Rep. Walberg. "Strong partnership with the EPA is essential to meeting the challenges facing the Great Lakes basin, accelerating cleanup efforts, and ensuring Michigan communities remain resilient and thriving for generations to come.”

"Today’s visit underscored how collaboration across all levels of government can move cleanup efforts forward and deliver lasting benefits for the people of Berrien County," said EPA Region 5 Administrator Anne Vogel. "By partnering with local leaders and leveraging federal tools like the Brownfields Program and the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, we are helping communities address legacy contamination, support economic revitalization, and protect one of our nation’s most important water resources."

title: Blumenthal, Tonko, & Foushee Demand FanDuel Fess Up About Celebrity Promo Videos After VIP Message was Used to Target Gambling Addict
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and U.S. Representatives Paul Tonko (D-NY) and Valerie Foushee (D-NC) today demanded FanDuel provide full videos and information about whether personalized celebrity messages were used to exploit vulnerable consumers and entice addicts to further gamble. Blumenthal, Tonko, and Foushee previously wrote to FanDuel after reports that the sportsbook used a personal video message from Philadelphia Phillies first baseman Bryce Harper to target an individual suffering from gambling addiction.

In response to the lawmakers’ previous letter, FanDuel acknowledged it had sent “approximately 30 such videos of athletes and entertainers over the last two years” as a “token of appreciation for a customer’s loyalty.”

In a letter sent today to FanDuel CEO Christian Genetski, the lawmakers demanded the sportsbook provide copies of each personalized video as well as information about whether the videos were sent to problem gamblers, writing, “While FanDuel claimed it ‘has not used personalized videos or messages to induce customers to continue gambling,’ that statement is clearly contradicted by the fact that the video of Mr. Harper that gave rise to these concerns was sent to an individual that had lost $1.5 million on bets on your platform.”

Blumenthal, Tonko, and Foushee continued, “In addition, FanDuel claims to monitor a range of behaviors through ‘automated and manual proactive reviews to identify players who may be experiencing gambling harm,’ yet does not provide a full picture of how it uses this information, including whether that same data is used to target bettors with such predatory promotions.”

The full text of the lawmakers’ letter to Genetski is available here and below. FanDuel’s September 24 response to the lawmakers is available here.

Dear Mr. Genetski,

We write to demand that FanDuel provide the full videos and information regarding the dozens of personalized celebrity messages sent to VIP bettors, as revealed in its September 24th response to our Congressional inquiry. Despite FanDuel’s claims that these videos were not sent to entice destructive gambling, we remain concerned that FanDuel’s VIP program and its perks are used to exploit vulnerable bettors, especially those suffering from a gambling addiction.

On September 3, 2026, we wrote to you regarding FanDuel’s failure to adequately respond to our questions about disturbing reports that your VIP program repeatedly targeted problem gamblers with predatory perks, including with a personal message from Philadelphia Phillies first baseman, Bryce Harper. In your response, FanDuel acknowledged “approximately 30 such videos of athletes and entertainers over the last two years” as a “token of appreciation for a customer’s loyalty.” While FanDuel claimed it “has not used personalized videos or messages to induce customers to continue gambling,” that statement is clearly contradicted by the fact that the video of Mr. Harper that gave rise to these concerns was sent to an individual that had lost $1.5 million on bets on your platform. In addition, FanDuel claims to monitor a range of behaviors through “automated and manual proactive reviews to identify players who may be experiencing gambling harm,” yet does not provide a full picture of how it uses this information, including whether that same data is used to target bettors with such predatory promotions.

Given FanDuel’s repeated failures to protect bettors and previous deficient responses, we request that you provide the following information no later than October 20, 2026.

Please provide copies of each personalized video FanDuel has sent to its VIP bettors.

For each video, please describe the circumstances in which these were sent including:

the total amount each recipient had wagered beforehand and the amount that they had won or lost;

whether the recipient had ever requested to suspend their account, pause notifications, or take action to limit their gambling on the platform;

the reason that the VIP host decided to target that bettor;

what steps the VIP host took to ensure that the bettor was not vulnerable to problematic gambling or showed signs of significant losses or economic hardship; and

what service was used to obtain the video.

For each video, please describe the extent to which the athlete or celebrity was aware of the video’s promotion of gambling or connection to FanDuel.

Please describe the data and behaviors monitored in FanDuel’s screening process for problem gambling, and whether that same information is used to target bettors with personalized videos, push notifications, promotion, retention bonuses, and any other perks.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Coons submit ethics complaint against Third Circuit Judge Jennifer Mascott
text:
U.S. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester and Chris Coons, a senior member of the Senate Judiciary Committee (both D-Del.), submitted a complaint against Judge Jennifer Mascott of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit with Circuit Executive Margaret Wiegand, calling for a review of Mascott’s conduct in light of recent reporting by Politico indicating that Mascott continued to run her late husband’s public affairs firm after her confirmation to the federal bench.

“In our view, the ethical implications of Judge Mascott’s decision to lead this firm while simultaneously serving on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit deserve review,” the senators wrote. “Although ownership of an independent public affairs firm does not necessarily constitute judicial misconduct, ongoing and active engagement in managing that firm can be.”

In August, Politico broke the news that Mascott was “deeply involved in daily operations” at Adfero, a Washington public affairs firm she inherited from her late husband, for at least six months after her confirmation to the Third Circuit. While serving as a judge, Mascott worked out of Adfero’s Washington offices, oversaw staffing and business development operations, and made key “operational and strategic” decisions. Mascott also pushed the previously non-partisan firm in a conservative direction, bringing on consultants and clients “with strong MAGA credentials.”

“If she is logging time [at Adfero] and it has the potential to interfere with her judicial duties, that is a no-go,” Charles Geyh, a law professor at the Indiana University Maurer School of Law who studies judicial ethics, told Politico.

“Under a basic reading of the Code of Conduct for United States Judges,” the senators continued in their complaint, judges “may not maintain a second profession that could take time and focus away from their Senate-confirmed job. We are concerned that by dedicating extensive time and attention to her role in Adfero, Judge Mascott may have engaged in misconduct.”

The two senators also posed questions about whether Mascott’s work with Adfero has detracted from her work on the Court of Appeals, noting that since joining the bench, Judge Mascott “has issued only three written opinions in precedential cases, two of which are only about a page long.” Other Third Circuit judges have written significantly more in that time.

title: U.S. Senators Katie Britt, Raphael Warnock Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Level the Playing Field for Atlanta Braves, Other Publicly Traded Sports Teams
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Katie Britt (R-Ala.) and Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.) introduced bipartisan legislation to address disparities in the tax treatment of publicly traded and privately owned sports teams. The legislation would update the tax code to ensure publicly traded professional sports teams receive the same tax treatment as privately owned teams when accounting for compensation paid to players, coaches, and team managers.

“Beginning next year, a tax law signed in 2021 will expand to include a public company’s five highest-paid employees beyond its senior executives. For publicly traded professional sports organizations like the Atlanta Braves, this means players and other on-field personnel will be swept into a tax rule designed around executive compensation,” said Senator Britt. “Our bipartisan bill makes a targeted correction by excluding athletic personnel from that additional five-employee category while leaving the existing executive-compensation rules in place. I appreciate Senator Warnock’s partnership on this commonsense fix to ensure the Atlanta Braves are not unfairly penalized for being a public company.”

“The Atlanta Braves are a historic franchise that has showcased Atlanta and Georgia to the world,” said Senator Warnock. “I am proud to have worked across the aisle to help the Atlanta Braves and other publicly owned teams continue to thrive and win on the playing field. This legislation will ensure fair tax treatment between professional sports teams.”

The legislation is supported by the Atlanta Braves. A companion bill is being led in the U.S. House of Representatives by Representatives Nicole Malliotakis (R-N.Y.), Tom Suozzi (D-N.Y.), Brian Jack (R-Ga.), and Lucy McBath (D-Ga.).

“We applaud the bipartisan work of Senators Warnock and Britt and Representatives Malliotakis, Suozzi, Jack, and McBath to correct an unintended competitive disadvantage harming publicly traded professional sports teams,” the Atlanta Braves said in a statement. “Unlike C-suite executives, professional athletes work within league rules and do not receive equity or make business decisions for their teams. Yet, the tax code does not recognize the distinction. These members agree that this was an unintended consequence, and we appreciate their willingness to clarify the original intent of the law.”

title: Senators Coons, Blunt Rochester submit ethics complaint against Third Circuit Judge Jennifer Mascott
text:
Court of Appeals judge ran right-wing lobbying firm while serving on the federal bench in potential violation of ethical requirements

WILMINGTON, Del. – U.S. Senators Chris Coons, a senior member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, and Lisa Blunt Rochester (both D-Del.) submitted a complaint against Judge Jennifer Mascott of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit with Circuit Executive Margaret Wiegand, calling for a review of Mascott’s conduct in light of recent reporting by Politico indicating that Mascott continued to run her late husband’s public affairs firm after her confirmation to the federal bench.

“In our view, the ethical implications of Judge Mascott’s decision to lead this firm while simultaneously serving on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit deserve review,” the senators wrote. “Although ownership of an independent public affairs firm does not necessarily constitute judicial misconduct, ongoing and active engagement in managing that firm can be.”

In August, Politico broke the news that Mascott was “deeply involved in daily operations” at Adfero, a Washington public affairs firm she inherited from her late husband, for at least six months after her confirmation to the Third Circuit. While serving as a judge, Mascott worked out of Adfero’s Washington offices, oversaw staffing and business development operations, and made key “operational and strategic” decisions. Mascott also pushed the previously non-partisan firm in a conservative direction, bringing on consultants and clients “with strong MAGA credentials.”

“If she is logging time [at Adfero] and it has the potential to interfere with her judicial duties, that is a no-go,” Charles Geyh, a law professor at the Indiana University Mauer School of Law who studies judicial ethics, told Politico.

“Under a basic reading of the Code of Conduct for United States Judges,” the senators continued in their complaint, judges “may not maintain a second profession that could take time and focus away from their Senate-confirmed job. We are concerned that by dedicating extensive time and attention to her role in Adfero, Judge Mascott may have engaged in misconduct.”

The two senators also posed questions about whether Mascott’s work with Adfero has detracted from her work on the Court of Appeals, noting that since joining the bench, Judge Mascott “has issued only three written opinions in precedential cases, two of which are only about a page long.” Other Third Circuit judges have written significantly more in that time.

“As representatives for the people of Delaware in the United States Senate, we want to ensure that the judges serving our state on the Third Circuit are fully committed to doing their best work, free from undue distraction or unethical conduct,” the senators concluded. “We look forward to your review of this complaint and thank you for your attention to this matter.”

title: Senators Coons, Sheehy introduce bipartisan STRATA Act to strengthen critical minerals supply chains
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Chris Coons (D-Del.) and Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.) introduced the Strategic Technology and Resilient Alliances (STRATA) Act, bipartisan legislation to strengthen U.S. and allied critical minerals supply chains by accelerating innovation and developing new technologies at every stage of mining and refining critical minerals. Representatives Young Kim (R-Calif.) and Ami Bera (D-Calif.) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

“China’s critical mineral dominance poses a challenge the U.S. cannot address through traditional mining and processing alone,” said Senator Coons. “The STRATA Act would use America’s advantages in innovation and our strong ties with partners and allies around the world to secure our critical mineral infrastructure. By working with our allies to advance new technologies, build technical capacity, and strengthen supply chains, we can expand access to critical minerals and protect our national security.”

“America is a nation of innovation. As we race to counter China’s dominance of critical minerals and secure our supply chain, we must maintain our competitive edge with new technological advances that can expedite the delivery of new critical mineral sources, reduce our dependency on foreign adversaries, and protect our national security,” said Senator Sheehy.“The STRATA Act will accelerate breakthroughs in extraction, processing, recycling, recovery, and advanced materials, working with our allies to build resilient supply chains and keep America at the forefront of critical-minerals innovation.”

“The Chinese Communist Party has spent decades cornering the market on critical minerals and using supply chains as a tool of economic coercion,” said Rep. Kim. “We cannot wait another moment to address this challenge. The STRATA Act plays to America’s greatest strengths: innovation and our strong alliances. By launching a Critical Mineral Innovation Initiative at the State Department, sharing technology with allies, and expanding domestic recycling, we will build a secure supply chain faster and smarter. I’m proud to partner with Senator Coons in the Senate to get this bill signed into law, because economic security is national security, and the STRATA Act delivers both.”

Critical minerals are essential to advanced technologies, energy infrastructure, semiconductors, and defense systems, but critical minerals supply chains remain heavily concentrated in China. The United States has made significant investments in expanding domestic mining and processing, including recent federal investments in new mining technologies, mineral recovery, and processing capacity.

The STRATA Act would complement those efforts by making innovation and international collaboration a central part of the U.S. critical minerals strategy. The legislation would establish formal partnerships with trusted allies to accelerate the development and deployment of advanced extraction and processing technologies, mineral substitution, recycling, recovery from waste streams, and new materials.

The STRATA Act would:

Establish a Critical Minerals Innovation Partnership Program at the State Department to coordinate U.S. and allied strategies, develop joint research and innovation initiatives, and support partnerships with universities, national laboratories, nonprofits, and industry

Create International Centers of Excellence at academic institutions to advance research, technical assistance, workforce development, and long-term partnerships across the critical minerals supply chain

Launch a public digital platform serving as a centralized clearinghouse for funding opportunities, solicitations, and collaborative research, while creating pathways for startups and emerging companies to participate

Connect innovation to commercialization and national security by coordinating with federal agencies, financing institutions, the National Science and Technology Council, and the National Defense Technology and Industrial Base Council to help move promising technologies from research and development ultimately into deployment

Strengthen supply chain safeguards and transparency by establishing standards for data security, sensitive technologies, supply chain transparency, monitoring, and verification, while limiting participation by countries and entities of concern

Build long-term allied capacity through technical assistance, joint research, shared infrastructure, and cooperation on environmental, labor, and human rights standards

The STRATA Act would authorize these partnerships for 10 years and require congressional notification before establishing new partnerships. The legislation would also prohibit partnerships with countries of concern and entities of concern.

“The STRATA Act represents forward-thinking policy that the United States needs to maintain its technological edge and its leadership on science diplomacy,” said Daniel Correa, Chief Executive Officer of the Federation of American Scientists. “Structured partnerships with our allies on critical minerals innovation can ensure that the best science and the best talent are working together towards shared security and economic prosperity.”

“Engaging earlier and in-depth on critical technologies that will shape our collective futures is a statecraft imperative for liberal democracies globally. I’m delighted to see this Committee and the Legislative Branch recognizing and acting to drive a leadership role for the US and the DoS. Now is absolutely the time!” said Dawn Meyerriecks, former director of the Directorate of Science and Technology at the Central Intelligence Agency.

“Increasing the legibility of existing investments, agreements, and supplies of critical minerals can surface information for policymakers and private investors focused on securing supply chains,” said Joshua Levine, director, Technology & Statecraft, Foundation for American Innovation (*affiliation for identification only). “STRATA works to do this, within a defined timeline, and should be seen as a positive step toward loosening chokepoints for inputs critical to American innovation and next-generation technologies.”

“STRATA is a well-timed and strongly bipartisan effort to tackle one of the most important national security challenges of the day — how to ensure that the growing demand for critical minerals to power our defense systems, energy transition and the infrastructure to support America’s lead in the AI revolution does not strengthen China’s already strong position in these supply chains,” said Geoff Pyatt, Ambassador (ret.), senior managing director of Energy and Critical Minerals at McLarty Associates. “The State Department — and the energy security team that I was honored to lead — has worked closely with the Congressional foreign affairs leadership to make sure that America’s national security toolkit is fit for purpose on these issues. And China has already demonstrated in repeated instances its willingness to weaponize its market dominance in these sectors for strategic advantage. I applaud Senator Coons and his Senate colleagues for focusing SFRC attention on this critical line of effort.”

“America and our allies have the ingenuity and industrial base to lead the world in critical minerals mining and processing,” said ClearPath Action CEO Jeremy Harrell. “The STRATA Act puts these advantages to work and funds the joint research needed to surpass China and secure the supply chain that next-generation energy technologies rely on.”

“The STRATA Act takes a smart, forward-looking approach to securing the critical minerals our economy depends on, investing in the researchers and entrepreneurs developing new ways to produce, recycle, and replace these materials. NAIA supports this bill and thanks Senators Coons and Sheehy for their leadership,” said a representative from the New American Industrial Alliance.

Read the full text of the STRATA Act here.

title: Daines Urges ITC to Level the Playing Field, Defend American Sheep Producers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Steve Daines and Representative Celeste Maloy (R-Utah) today led a letter to the U.S. International Trade Commission Chairman urging strong support for U.S. sheep producers and relief from damages resulting from sheep imports to ensure U.S. producers are able to compete on a level playing field.

“As Members of Congress who proudly represent growers and processors in the American sheep industry, we write regarding the U.S. International Trade Commission’s (Commission) global safeguard investigation of lamb meat imports pursuant to Sections 201-204 of the Trade Act of 1974. During this investigation, we urge the Commission to carefully consider the data and testimony before it regarding the significant challenges faced by American sheep producers. And should the Commission make an affirmative determination in accordance with the statute, we urge the Commission to recommend a remedy that provides prompt and meaningful relief to the domestic industry.

The families behind America’s sheep farms and ranches have faced mounting pressures, including from rapidly increasing imports, which negatively impact our rural communities and domestic food production. The U.S. Trade Representative’s (USTR) July 13, 2026, letter directing the Commission to initiate the Section 201 investigation states that “import statistics indicate that lamb meat imports…have increased in recent years” and “[a]vailable information suggests that these imports have resulted in domestic industry lost sales, revenues, and market share as imported lamb meat significantly undersold the domestic like product.” USTR’s letter further states that “firms have exited the domestic industry entirely, and there have been domestic industry job losses, decreased capacity utilization rates, and struggles to maintain profitability,” they wrote in the letter.

title: Durbin Receives Federal Bar Association Chicago Chapter’s Inaugural Lifetime Achievement Award
text:
Durbin receives award in honor of his decades-long work on the Senate Judiciary Committee

CHICAGO – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today was presented the Federal Bar Association Chicago Chapter’s inaugural Lifetime Achievement Award in recognition of his longstanding efforts to support the federal judiciary and his decades-long work on the Senate Judiciary Committee.

As Chair of the Senate Judiciary Committee during the Biden Administration, Durbin led the effort in the Senate to confirm 235 lifetime federal judges—the largest number of confirmations in a single term since the Carter Administration. These 235 judges represent more than a quarter of the federal bench. The 235 judicial confirmations include: 187 district court nominees; 45 circuit court nominees; one Supreme Court nominee; and two Court of International Trade nominees. During Durbin’s tenure in the U.S. Senate, 58 federal judges have been confirmed in Illinois—52 district judges and six Seventh Circuit Illinois seats.

Photos of Durbin at today’s event can be found here.

Key Quotes as prepared for delivery:

“Judge Harjani, thank you for that warm introduction and congratulations on the conclusion of your term as president of the Federal Bar Association’s Chicago Chapter.”

“I would also like to thank the Chicago Chapter for this award and all of you for being here today—it is a pleasure to be surrounded by so many familiar faces.”

“In listening to that introduction, I was reminded of something that District of Minnesota Judge Patrick Schiltz said earlier in September. He remarked that, ‘The rule of law to democracy is like oxygen to a human body. It is something that you absolutely need to survive.’ I think that sentiment encapsulates the mission we have as lawyers, judges, and members of Congress.”

“In our positions, we serve as the lungs of democracy—the decisions we make, in the courtroom and on the Senate Floor, affect how Americans experience justice.”

“I kept that sentiment top of mind when I chaired the Senate Judiciary Committee and led the effort to confirm 235 judges under President Biden—the largest number of confirmations in a single term since the Carter Administration. Every single one of these judges received at least a ‘Qualified’ rating from the American Bar Association. But these nominees were more than just qualified. They were a group of people that reflected the rich demographic and professional diversity of our nation and legal profession.”

“These nominees came from all walks of life—they were labor lawyers, civil rights lawyers, and public defenders. And those 235 judges include more women and women of color confirmed to the bench than any other presidential administration in history. That of course includes Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, the first Black woman and first former public defender on the Supreme Court.”

“For nearly 30 years as a Senator, I took the responsibility of recommending judicial nominees to the President—along with the Senators I have served alongside with—very seriously. Over the course of my Senate career, 58 federal judges have been confirmed to lifetime appointments in Illinois, including 37 confirmed to the Northern District and six to Seventh Circuit Illinois seats—many of whom are here today.”

“These jurists, like the Federal Bar Association, represent the best of the bar in Illinois—former prosecutors, public defenders, private practitioners, and civil rights lawyers. And that is true, from Judge Rebecca Pallmeyer—the first judge confirmed to the bench when I became a Senator—to Judge April Perry—the most recent judge confirmed.”

“Unfortunately, these judges are serving at a time when our judiciary faces unprecedented challenges. While judicial rulings have always been subject to public criticism, today that criticism has devolved into threats, harassment, and acts of intimidation targeting judges who are simply doing their jobs. Members of Congress have repeatedly filed articles of impeachment against judges not because they have engaged in misconduct but because of political disagreements with their decisions.”

“Amid these challenges, judges have performed their duties capably and courageously. I have implored executive branch officials and my colleagues in Congress to support our judges in the face of these attacks. But I also implore you all, as judges and lawyers, to continue to uphold and advance the rule of law.”

“It is a true honor to receive the inaugural Lifetime Achievement Award from the FBA Chapter here in Chicago.”

title: Ernst Names Small Business of the Week, Doe a Deer

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues Reintroduce Legislation To Increase Access To Life-Saving Breast And Gynecological Cancer Screenings
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) joined Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) in reintroducing the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act, legislation that would increase the availability of life-saving cancer screenings at safety net healthcare providers like Planned Parenthood. The bill would create new grant and pilot programs to expand access to preventive services and screenings for breast and gynecological cancers—especially for low-income women and women of color—and train healthcare providers in providing high-quality cancer screening, early detection, and follow-up care.

The legislation is named for Jeanette Acosta, who was a fierce women’s health advocate, former congressional staffer, and White House intern in the Obama administration. In 2017, she lost her battle with cervical cancer at the age of 32.

“Millions of women in the U.S. do not have access to preventative screenings that could catch deadly illnesses early and save their lives. That is a national tragedy that demands action,” said Senator Gillibrand. “The Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act is a commonsense piece of legislation to increase access to life-saving breast and gynecological cancer screenings for women who may otherwise slip through the cracks. I am doing everything I can to get this bill across the finish line.”

“It is an honor that the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act of 2026 is in our daughter’s name. Over eight years ago cervical cancer took the life of our precious and valiant daughter, Jeanette. At the young age of 32, after one year of battling her cancer and suffering incomparable pain and extensive treatment, Jeanette died from her advanced cancer. Jeanette prayed that women be spared from the agony of cervical cancer, and this bill would help to achieve her hope for many women,” said Frank X. Acosta, Ph.D., Jeanette Acosta’s father. “This bill will have a lasting and positive national impact in the fight against cancers that afflict women. During her own fight with cancer, Jeanette reached out and provided support and encouragement to other women coping with cancer. She also emphasized the importance of prevention against the onset of cervical cancer. Jeanette, always a warrior for social justice, wanted to shine a light on the disparities to access to prevention and cancer health services for low-income, Latina, and Black women. This bill would brightly illuminate and help to close the gap between cancer prevention and health services and the countless women who have not and may not be able to access these services. Jeanette would adamantly support this bill.”

“I’m proud to reintroduce the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act in honor of Jeanette Acosta, a fierce advocate who fought to make sure every woman could get the health care she needs,” said Senator Murray. “Too many women suffer preventable deaths because they didn’t have access to the cancer screenings that would have detected their condition early on. That is an unacceptable tragedy. We know that early detection saves lives—not to mention health care costs—and investing in preventive services to help more women get treatment before it’s too late is just common sense. I’m not going to stop fighting to pass this crucial piece of legislation in Jeanette’s memory.”

In addition to Senators Gillibrand and Murray, the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act is cosponsored by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

The bill is endorsed by: American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology, American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Black Women’s Health Imperative, Human Rights Watch, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, National Asian Pacific American Women’s Forum, National Council of Jewish Women, National Family Planning & Reproductive Health Association, National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice, National Partnership for Women & Families, National Women’s Law Center Action Fund, Ovarian Cancer Research Alliance, and Planned Parenthood Federation of America.

Senator Gillibrand has long been a champion for women’s health. Last month, she held the first ever congressional hearing on menopause, shedding light on the need for additional federal support for menopause research, training, and care. Gillibrand also leads the Moms Matter Act—part of the Momnibus Act that was reintroduced earlier this year—which would increase investments in maternal mental health programs and expand this vital workforce to better support moms and pregnant women. She also leads the Healthy Maternity and Obstetric Medicine (MOM) Act, legislation designed to expand healthcare access for pregnant women and ensure they receive coverage that meets their needs.

The full text of the Jeanette Acosta Invest in Women’s Health Act can be found here.

title: Grassley, Iowa Congressional Delegation Advocate for More Rural Healthcare Funding to Iowa
text:
Republicans’ Working Families Tax Cuts law has already invested $209 million to strengthen rural healthcare across Iowa

Click HERE for audio.

BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) led the entire Iowa congressional delegation in a letter urging Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet Oz to support Iowa’s latest funding request for the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), known as Healthy Hometowns. The RHTP was created in Republicans’ Working Families Tax Cuts law and, in just its first year, has already invested $209 million in rural communities across Iowa to strengthen access to care.

In addition to Grassley, the letter was signed by U.S. Sen. Joni Ernst (R-Iowa) and U.S. Reps. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa), Zach Nunn (R-Iowa) and Randy Feenstra (R-Iowa).

“In January, Iowa became the first state in the nation to award Rural Health Transformation Program funding as part of its Healthy Hometowns initiative, and it has ensured resources are going directly to rural communities, not bureaucrats. In year one of the program, Iowa’s $209 million federal investment is improving cancer prevention and treatment, workforce recruitment and retention, chronic disease care, and maternal and child health,” the members wrote.

“As we each travel throughout Iowa, visiting hospitals, health centers, clinics, and more, we witness firsthand how these investments are making a difference toward the health, well-being, and quality of life in rural communities. During your visit to the University of Iowa in May, you learned how our state is using telehealth and a hub-and-spoke model to increase access to care and improve health outcomes in our rural communities,” the members continued.

The members noted how communities across Iowa are already benefiting from these federal investments, including through the following six projects:

Lucas County Health Center in Chariton is purchasing its first-ever MRI machine to bring early detection cancer screenings to residents.

Mahaska Health in Oskaloosa is purchasing a new PET/CT system with cardiac imaging capability and recruiting an OB/GYN and a general surgeon physician assistant.

North Iowa Medical Center in Mason City is purchasing a new robotic bronchoscopy system that detects lung cancer earlier than previously possible.

Sioux Center Health in Sioux Center is expanding prenatal care through a new regional maternal health coordinator.

Washington County Hospital in Washington is purchasing a new CT scanner that is improving diagnostic capabilities and patient outcomes.

Wayne County Hospital in Corydon is standing up a radiation oncology center and will be serving as a combat cancer health hub.

Click HERE for audio of Grassley discussing the letter.

Click HERE to read the letter.

Background:

The Rural Health Transformation Program is the largest investment in rural healthcare in American history, focused on increasing access to care, driving innovation and expanding the healthcare workforce. Over a period of five years, Iowa will receive, at a minimum, $100 million annually from this fund.

title: PASSED THE SENATE: Hassan, Scott Bill to Protect Innocent Spouses from Unfair Tax Liability Passes Senate
text:
WASHINGTON – Bipartisan legislation led by U.S. Senators Maggie Hassan (D-NH) and Tim Scott (R-SC) to help ensure that taxpayers are not unfairly held responsible for tax debts caused by a spouse’s hidden income, mistakes, or misconduct unanimously passed the Senate. The Tax Relief for Innocent Spouses Act, which was included as part of the Taxpayer Assistance and Service (TAS) Act, now heads to the House for consideration.

“When married couples file taxes jointly, one spouse can sometimes be left facing serious financial consequences because of mistakes that they had no knowledge of or control over,”said Senator Hassan. “This bipartisan bill helps ensure that innocent spouses, including those who may have experienced abuse or lacked access to their finances, will have a fair opportunity to present their case and receive the relief that they deserve. I’m glad to see it pass the Senate, and I’ll keep working across the aisle to get it passed into law.”

“One spouse should not bear the responsibility for another spouse’s hidden income or mistakes, and the Tax Relief for Innocent Spouses Act gives the Tax Court greater authority to review the full scope of evidence in appeal cases,” said Senator Tim Scott. “For spouses who face domestic abuse or who lack access to financial information, this legislation would be life changing. By ensuring innocent Americans are treated fairly under our tax laws, we could provide much-needed relief and opportunities to move forward.”

When married couples file taxes jointly, both spouses are liable for any misstatement of income or underpayment, even if one spouse had no knowledge of the violation. This can be a particularly common issue in abusive relationships when one spouse takes control of the finances or hides additional income. The “innocent spouse” who is unaware of the tax violations may qualify for tax relief and be protected from liability for tax violations they did not know about.

Under current law, courts reviewing innocent spouse claims can only consider evidence that was newly discovered, not evidence that was previously submitted during the IRS administrative review process. This can make it harder for innocent spouses to obtain relief, particularly if they experienced abuse, lacked access to financial information, or did not understand the process.

The Tax Relief for Innocent Spouses Act would allow courts to consider all relevant evidence when reviewing innocent spouse claims, helping give taxpayers a fair opportunity to receive relief from tax liabilities they did not cause.

title: PASSED THE SENATE: Senator Hassan’s Legislation to Strengthen Cybersecurity
text:
WASHINGTON – Legislation led by U.S. Senators Maggie Hassan, Bill Cassidy (R-LA), John Cornyn (R-TX), and Mark Warner (D-VA) to protect Americans’ health data by strengthening cybersecurity recently passed the U.S. Senate by unanimous consent. The Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act is a product of the senators’ bipartisan health care cybersecurity working group launched in 2023.

"Cyberattacks have exposed patients’ private medical information and disrupted critical patient care in New Hampshire and across the country,” said Senator Hassan. “This bipartisan legislation will help hospitals and health care providers, particularly those in rural communities with fewer resources, strengthen their cybersecurity and respond faster to attacks. I’m pleased to see that the Senate came together to pass this bill, and I’ll keep working across the aisle to protect patients and strengthen our health care system.”

“Cyberattacks can shut down hospitals and expose patients' private medical records,” said Senator Cassidy. “At a time when hostile actors are increasingly using sophisticated tactics to breach health care systems, the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resilience Act will help health care providers strengthen their defenses against cyber threats and protect patients’ health data.”

“Patients deserve absolute confidence that their sensitive medical data stored online is protected and shielded from cybersecurity breaches or ransomware attacks,” said Senator Cornyn. “This legislation would strengthen interagency coordination and improve security practices for rural providers, ensuring Texans’ health care is not delayed or compromised by cyberattacks.”

“Cyberattacks on our health care systems can have life-or-death consequences for patients and put the sensitive information of millions of Americans at risk,” said Senator Warner. “I’m proud to have helped pass this critical legislation through the Senate, and I urge the House to act quickly. This bill will strengthen our cybersecurity, better protect patients and their information, and give rural health care providers in Virginia and across the country additional tools to defend against cyber threats.”

The Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act:

Provides a variety of resources for the health care sector to improve cyberattack prevention and response

Provides training to health care entities on cybersecurity best practices.

Supports rural communities by providing best practices to rural health clinics and other providers on cybersecurity breach prevention, resilience, and coordination with federal agencies.

Improves coordination between the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to better respond to cyberattacks in the health care sector.

Modernizes current regulations so entities covered under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) use the best cybersecurity practices.

Requires the HHS Secretary to develop and implement a cybersecurity incident response plan.
