title: Heinrich, Kim Introduce Legislation to Ensure Military Families Have Access to Healthy Meals
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), a member of the U.S. Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies, and U.S. Senator Andy Kim (D-N.J.) led the introduction of their Nutrition Continuity for Military Families Act, legislation that will ensure military families have access to healthy meals and critical nutrition programs. This builds on their introduction of the Military Dependents School Meal Eligibility Act, which they introduced last month.

The Nutrition Continuity for Military Families Act of 2026 will ensure military families are notified of their potential eligibility and do not lose access to crucial supplemental nutritional benefits through the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) program when conducting a mandated Permanent Change of Station (PCS).

The Military Dependents School Meal Eligibility Act will help combat hunger among military families by ensuring military children are no longer excluded from school meal assistance programs.

“Military families already sacrifice so much to serve our country — they shouldn’t also have to worry about whether their children have enough to eat or can access the meals they need at school,” said Heinrich.“Our legislation will cut through unnecessary barriers and make sure military families in New Mexico and across the country can access healthy school meals and critical nutrition programs. We have a responsibility to take care of the families who sacrifice so much to take care of all of us.”

“As military families move place to place as a part of their service to our country, they shouldn’t have to worry about losing access to benefits along the way. We know hunger and access to care is a real issue in our military communities – let’s make this fix so essential services never get interrupted for those who need it most,” said Kim.

The Nutrition Continuity for Military Families Act of 2026

Military service members make tremendous sacrifices to serve our country. Unfortunately, many military families, especially young, enlisted service members and their families, face food insecurity. And critical nutrition assistance remains significantly underutilized. Research highlighted by the American Academy of Pediatrics found that 70% of WIC-eligible active-duty military families were not enrolled in the program. Frequent military moves can disrupt access to these benefits and force families to repeatedly navigate new state and local systems. Ensuring service members and their families receive timely notification of potential eligibility and uninterrupted access to WIC benefits throughout a military move is critical to protecting military families from food insecurity during already challenging transitions.

The Nutrition Continuity for Military Families Act helps ensure military families have uninterrupted access to critical nutrition benefits by requiring the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) to:

Notify families who may be eligible for WIC when they receive PCS orders;

Issue a Verification of Certification card to covered service members at the time of WIC certification or recertification;

Ensure WIC benefits remain certified throughout the PCS process; and

Ensure each military installation has knowledgeable personnel available at least three days per week to provide WIC assistance to service members.

A one-pager of the bill is here.

The full text of the bill is here.

The Military Dependents School Meal Eligibility Act

School meals help children build healthy eating habits that can last a lifetime. Research shows that students who participate in school meal programs have better overall diet quality than nonparticipants. Yet military families can face unnecessary barriers to accessing free and reduced-price school meals because their Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH) is counted as income when determining eligibility.

The Military Dependents School Meal Eligibility Act ensures military families are not unfairly excluded from school meal programs by:

Excluding BAH from income calculation for military families’ eligibility in free and reduced-price meals provided under the National School Breakfast Program and National School Lunch Program; and

Requiring the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and DoD to submit a report to Congress on the feasibility and cost of creating a program to directly certify military children for free and reduced-price school meal programs, including breakfast and lunch.

The full text of the bill is here.

Last month, Heinrich and Kim also introduced the Healthy Meals Help Kids Learn Act, legislation to address the rising cost of school meals and help end childhood hunger in America.

title: Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee Advances Heinrich’s WIPP Economic Assistance Assurance Act
text:
During the Committee hearing, Heinrich denounced legislation picking winners and losers in the energy sector, criticized a Republican bill that raises electricity prices, and spoke out against policies that harm public lands

WASHINGTON — Last week, during a U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee business meeting to consider pending legislation, the Committee passed U.S. Senator and Committee Ranking Member Martin Heinrich’s (D-N.M.) bipartisan Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (WIPP) Economic Assistance Assurance Act, legislation to ensure long-term funding for community infrastructure projects in New Mexico surrounding WIPP.

WIPP is the nation’s only deep geologic repository for the disposal of transuranic waste generated by the country's nuclear weapons program, playing a critical role in supporting national defense by managing legacy nuclear materials and national security-related cleanup efforts across the Department of Energy (DOE). The WIPP Economic Assistance Assurance Act, introduced by Heinrich in April 2026, would amend the WIPP Land Withdrawal Act to maintain vital infrastructure projects for the duration of WIPP’s operation, ensuring sustained and inflation-adjusted funding goes toward New Mexico communities.

VIDEO: U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, delivers opening remarks during a Committee hearing to consider pending legislation, September 30, 2026.

During the hearing, Heinrich also expressed concern over the Committee’s lack of willingness to pass bipartisan weatherization legislation that would lower costs for American families, and criticized legislation that harms public lands. He also denounced U.S. Senator John Hoeven’s (R-N.D.) GRID Power Act, which would allow fossil fuels to receive favorable treatment and connect to our grid faster than clean energy projects, ultimately raising costs for consumers.

Heinrich began his opening remarks by criticizing efforts by U.S. Senator Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the Committee, to prioritize his legislation, S.1568, the Liberating Incandescent Technology (LIT) Act, over bipartisan weatherization legislation that would actually improve home efficiency upgrades and save Americans money on utilities.

“At a time of rising electric bills and increasing new demands on the electric grid, this Committee should focus on lowering costs and increasing reliability. We have a chance to extend and improve a program that has served more than 7.2 million families, saving households an average of $372 per year and supporting 8,500 good jobs. Unfortunately, the Chairman has declined to bring weatherization bills up for a vote,” said Heinrich. “Instead, we are spending our time and attention ‘liberating’ light bulbs that industry doesn’t even make, and most of us haven’t even thought about in a decade.”

“According to analysis of DOE and EIA data by consumer groups, LED lightbulbs save the average household $370 a year on their electric bills,” Heinrich continued.

Heinrich submitted a letter of opposition to S. 1568 from consumer advocacy groups.

Heinrich then raised concerns over Lee’s OHVs in Capitol Reef National Park Act, which would authorize the use of off-highway vehicles (OHVs) inside the park, “All 12 roads defined in the bill are accessible to conventional vehicles, so the idea that this bill increases access to park land is dubious. If passed, the bill would strain local emergency medical services, wear down backcountry roads faster, and push noise levels past National Park Service standards.”

On S. 3785, the North Rim and Kaibab National Forest Restoration Act, Heinrich spoke to his proposed amendment that would ensure transparency and oversight of the non-competitive contracts authorized by the bill, so that taxpayer money is properly used for restoration purposes.

“We have seen what happens when this administration doesn’t have to go through regular competitive contracting processes. We get shoddy work, like the Reflecting Pool, with taxpayer money funneled to the president’s donors,” said Heinrich. “The last thing the communities of northern Arizona need is for no-bid contracts to be awarded to fly-by-night companies that cannot get the job done at the end of the day.”

In the markup portion of the Committee, Heinrich spoke out against S. 465, U.S. Senator John Hoeven’s (R-N.D.) GRID Power Act, which would allow transmission providers to submit proposals to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) that would favor fossil fuel companies to connect to the grid faster than clean energy companies. Heinrich noted that favoring one form of generation over others is not a smart, cost-saving path forward.

“While issues remain with generator interconnection backlogs, favoring fossil-fueled generators over others is not a smart, cost-saving path forward,” said Heinrich. “My amendment would remove the word ‘dispatchable’ from S. 465. The amendment would still allow transmission providers to speed up their generator interconnection queues, but in a generation-neutral manner.”

A video of Heinrich’s remarks is here.

Heinrich’s full opening remarks as delivered are below:

Thank you, Mr. Chairman.

I look forward to advancing a number of the bills on this agenda, including important legislation that I have offered with Senator Risch to restore economic support for much-needed road and infrastructure improvements near the Department of Energy’s Waste Isolation Pilot Plant.

I’m also pleased we will consider bipartisan legislation related to cybersecurity and the electric grid, and advancing geothermal research.

At a time of rising electric bills and increasing new demands on the grid, this Committee should focus on lowering costs and increasing reliability.

That’s why I’ve asked to have bipartisan weatherization legislation included on the agenda. For 50 years, the popular weatherization program has helped add insulation, repair furnaces, and make other home efficiency upgrades to households who need it most.

We have a chance to extend and improve a program that has served more than 7 million families, saving households an average of $372 per year and supporting 8,500 good jobs.

Unfortunately, the Chairman has declined to bring weatherization bills up for a vote today.

Instead, we are spending our time and attention “liberating” light bulbs that industry doesn’t even make and most of us haven’t even thought about in a decade.

According to analysis of DOE and EIA data by consumer groups, LED lightbulbs save the average household $370 a year on their electric bills.

Earlier this month, I submitted a letter of opposition for the record to S. 1568, the “Liberating Incandescent Technology Act” or the LIT Act, from industry.

The National Electrical Manufacturers Association and the American Lighting Association warned of Chinese products flooding the market if this bill becomes law.

I would now ask for unanimous consent to submit a letter of opposition to S. 1568 from consumer groups.

Consumer Reports, the Consumer Federation of America, and the National Consumer Law Center, urge members to vote no on S. 1568, and protect Americans from skyrocketing energy costs.

I’m also concerned about S. 465, the Grid Power Act.

The bill would codify “queue jumping,” allowing natural gas power plants to connect to the grid faster than clean energy sources.

This is not necessary as FERC approved a one-time process to allow some power plants to skip to the front of the line while remaining technologically neutral.

Changing this now, especially as this administration illegally props up uneconomic coal plants, could be harmful to families’ and small businesses’ bottom lines.

So I have an amendment that would keep the requirement for FERC to modify its generator interconnection procedures but would allow transmission providers to simply prioritize “new power projects that will improve grid reliability and resource adequacy.”

Any project—not just those favored by this administration—that improves our grid’s reliability could be expedited under this language.

Additionally, I would like to voice my concern over S. 2970, the OHVs in Capitol Reef National Park Act, which would authorize the use of off-highway vehicles inside the park.

All 12 roads defined in the bill are accessible to conventional vehicles, so the idea that this bill increases access to park land is dubious.

If passed, the bill would strain local emergency medical services, wear down backcountry roads faster, and push noise levels past National Park Service standards.

Lastly, on the North Rim and Kaibab National Forest Restoration Act, I have filed an amendment to ensure transparency and oversight of the non-competitive contracts authorized by the bill.

We have seen what happens when this administration doesn’t have to go through regular competitive contracting processes.

We get shoddy work, like the Reflecting Pool, with taxpayer money funneled to the president’s donors.

The last thing the communities of northern Arizona need is for no-bid contracts to be awarded to fly-by-night companies that cannot get the job done at the end of the day.

I know how important this restoration work is, particularly to the members from Arizona, so I am not going to vote against this bill today, but I hope we can put some necessary guardrails into this legislation to ensure the work actually gets done and taxpayer dollars aren’t diverted to this administration’s vanity projects.

Thank you, Mr. Chairman.

Heinrich’s remarks on his proposed amendment to S. 465, the GRID Power Act:

Mr. Chairman, I'd like to offer an amendment to S. 465.

S. 465, the GRID Power Act, would allow transmission providers to submit proposals to FERC that would allow fossil-fueled generators to jump those queue lines.

Generator interconnection queues have faced backlogs for years. And to FERC’s credit, the Commission has taken action in recent years to speed up these queues, including issuing Order No. 2023.

While issues remain with generator interconnection backlogs, favoring one form of generation over others is not a smart, cost-saving path forward.

My amendment would simply remove the word “dispatchable” from S. 465. It would still allow transmission providers to speed up their generator interconnection queues, but in a generation-neutral manner.

There’s no debate that there is room for improvement in our generator interconnection queues. And I think, actually, that our bipartisan permitting package, once released, will show how Chairman Lee and I agree on some common solutions to improve these queues.

But FERC has never been in the business of picking winners and losers—and they shouldn’t start today.

I ask for a roll call vote on the amendment.

Thank you.

title: Hoeven: North Dakota Ag Producers to Receive an Estimated $721 Million This Month Under Enhanced ARC, PLC Reference Prices
text:
FARGO, N.D. – Senator John Hoeven today held a roundtable with Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman John Boozman (R-Ark.) at North Dakota State University (NDSU) with producers, commodity groups and agriculture researchers. Hoeven invited Boozman to the state to hear directly from North Dakota farmers, ranchers, researchers and agri-businesses as the senators continue their efforts to:

Advance the implementation of the farm safety net enhancements passed as part of the Working Families Tax Cut Act (WFTCA), also known as the One Big Beautiful Bill (OB3), which go into full effect this month.

Under this legislation, reference prices for the Agriculture Risk Coverage (ARC) and Price Loss Coverage (PLC) programs were increased by 10 to 20 percent.

As a result, North Dakota will receive an estimated $721 million this month in payments for the 2025 crop year under ARC and PLC, according to the Senate Agriculture Committee.

The updated reference prices resulted in an estimated increase of $456 million for North Dakota producers in the 2025 crop year, up from the $265 million producers would have received without the WFTCA’s passage.

This comes in addition to the improvements to crop insurance affordability from Hoeven’s FARMER Act provisions, which were included in WFTCA.

This will provide more than $91 million in additional premium support for North Dakota producers in 2026, according to projections from the NDSU Agricultural Risk Policy Center.

Pass the Farm Bill into law and ensure the final legislation includes key wins for agriculture producers from the Senate’s version of the bill. Hoeven and Boozman worked to ensure the Senate’s Farm Bill 2.0:

Builds on and further strengthens the WFTCA farm safety net improvements.

Supports the development of greater market opportunities for agriculture producers.

Authorizes the year-round sale of E15.

Working with U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) Ambassador Jamieson Greer to protect domestic sugar producers and push back on foreign nations dumping into the U.S. sugar market.

Hoeven led a bipartisan, bicameral letter with 112 members of Congress calling for USTR to take action in support of the American sugarbeet and sugarcane industry and has been working with Ambassador Greer to move the investigation forward.

“We made significant enhancements to the farm safety net in the Working Families Tax Cut Act, improving the affordability of crop insurance, strengthening livestock disaster programs and updating the counter-cyclical safety net so it reflects the actual cost of production. This month, those policies come into full effect and deliver meaningful assistance to North Dakota producers, who are set to receive an estimated $721 million from ARC and PLC for the 2025 crop year. In times of market uncertainty and increased input costs, those funds will make a real difference for our farmers,” said Senator Hoeven. “The Senate’s Farm Bill 2.0 builds on that good work and includes more than 100 bipartisan bills to support the long-term success of our farmers and ranchers. We will continue working to move this critical legislation forward and get it passed into law.”

“North Dakota farm families helped shape the Working Families Tax Cuts, and because we listened to their priorities, we made sure the law included enhancements to the farm safety net. Farmers will begin receiving those benefits this month, with North Dakota producers expected to receive $721 million in ARC and PLC payments––more than double what they would have received without this law. I’m pleased to continue working with Senator Hoeven to strengthen the future of American agriculture. Together, we’ve developed policies to support our farmers, and we’re not done. We’re committed to advancing Farm Bill 2.0 and securing additional farm assistance before the end of the year,” said Senator Boozman.

Additionally, the Senate farm bill includes the following Hoeven-authored provisions:

The PACE Act – Increases Farm Service Agency direct and guaranteed loan limits.

The BINS Act – Adds fertilizer storage and handling infrastructure as eligible facilities under the Farm Storage Facility Loan Program.

The SCALE Act – Provides matching grants to support state-led soil health and wildlife habitat programs, like Governor Armstrong’s Legacy Soil Health and Habitat Program.

Prairie Dog Management – Provides greater certainty for grazing permittees by preventing prairie dog colonies from expanding beyond reasonable levels.

MCOOL – Includes an amendment based on Hoeven-cosponsored legislation that requires mandatory country-of-origin labeling (MCOOL) for beef.

Joint Chiefs Program – Reauthorizes the program, which has provided more than $3.2 million for partnerships with private landowners to help improve and restore grasslands in North Dakota.

Farm Ownership and Improvement Act – Establishes a pilot program for pre-approval and pre-qualification of FSA Direct Farm Ownership loans.

Dry Edible Beans Study – Authorizes USDA to study the potential inclusion of dry edible beans as a Title I commodity.

Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP) – Clarifies non-adult cattle weight categories by establishing in statute, payment categories for calves weighing less than 400 pounds and 400 pounds or more.

Fargo-Moorhead Crop Insurance Fix – Protects producers impacted by operation of the Fargo-Moorhead Diversion Project by excluding affected years from Actual Production History (APH) calculations.

title: Husted introduces bill to modernize H-1B wage threshold and protect American workers
text:
“American workers should always come first, and this bill closes an outdated loophole that lets companies bypass them.”

WASHINGTON – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) introduced the Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act, a bill that would update the outdated salary threshold used to determine when H-1B dependent employers must prioritize hiring American workers.

“For decades, companies have been able to sidestep hiring American workers because of a salary threshold that hasn’t budged since 1998. That’s not modernization, that’s a loophole. This bill simply asks that when a company is heavily reliant on these visas and wants to bring in more H-1B workers, they shouldn’t be relying on an outdated law to get around offering these jobs to qualified American workers first,” said Husted.

Under current law, H-1B dependent employers, companies whose H-1B share of their workforce exceeds a particular threshold, must attest that they have first tried to hire American workers before sponsoring additional H-1B visas. However, employers are exempted if they pay the H-1B worker at least $60,000 per year, or if the worker holds a master’s degree or higher.

The $60,000 threshold was set in 1998 and was intended to be twice the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) National Average Wage Index at the time. It has never been adjusted for inflation. Today, the SSA National Average Wage Index is nearly $70,000, meaning the original threshold, adjusted for inflation, would be nearly $140,000.

The Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act would replace the fixed $60,000 threshold with a dynamic standard equal to two times the national average wage index, as calculated by the Social Security Administration. This would ensure the threshold keeps pace with wage growth going forward, rather than remaining frozen in place.

title: Klobuchar, Boozman Lead Senate Recognition of 4-H
text:
Senate Adopts Resolution Designating October 4-10 National 4-H Week

WASHINGTON?–?U.S. Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry Ranking Member Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Chairman John Boozman (R-AR), co-chairs of the Senate 4-H Caucus, are celebrating National 4-H Week by leading a resolution recognizing the importance of the program on youth development. The Senate passed the resolution designating October 4-10, 2026 as National 4-H Week.

“Minnesota 4-H is preparing over 50,000 young Minnesotans to lead in their communities,” said Klobuchar. “I’m glad to partner with Senator Boozman to recognize the work of 4-H by celebrating this week as National 4-H Week. As co-chair of the 4-H Caucus, I’ll continue working with my colleagues to support exciting opportunities for youth engaged in agriculture.”

“4-H has made a lasting impact on countless Arkansans, including my three daughters, who benefited from their participation in this program. I’m proud to support 4-H as it continues developing future generations of leaders and equips young people with the skills and values they need to succeed,” Boozman said.

4-H is a youth development program of the Cooperative Extension System of land-grant universities, and it is the largest youth development organization in the country. It provides experiences for nearly six million young people through hands-on projects in health, science, agriculture and civic engagement annually including 50,000 in Minnesota and 130,000 in Arkansas.

title: Luján, Heinrich, Vasquez Urge USPS to Reconsider Permanent Closure of Mule Creek Post Office
text:
Santa Fe, N.M. – Today, U.S. Senators Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) and Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), and U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.) wrote to Postmaster General David Steiner demanding that the United States Postal Service (USPS) reconsider the proposed permanent closure of the Mule Creek Post Office in Grant County, New Mexico, and to keep postal service in the community it has served for more than 100 years.

The Mule Creek Post Office opened on January 16, 1916, and has served ranchers, veterans, seniors, families, and small businesses for generations. In 2024, the facility was damaged, and repairs were never made. The U.S. Postal Service set up a mobile unit as a temporary fix, but more than two years later, residents still have no permanent post office. Now, instead of restoring service, USPS has proposed permanently closing the Mule Creek Post Office.

“We are deeply concerned about the impact this proposed permanent closure would have on the residents of Mule Creek and the surrounding rural service area. We strongly urge that the United States Postal Service (USPS) reconsider the proposed closure and maintain postal service in Mule Creek,” the lawmakers wrote.

“The Mule Creek Post Office has served the community since 1916. It’s more than one hundred years of service reflects its longstanding role in the life of the community. We request that USPS reconsider the proposed closure and undertake a comprehensive, community-specific review before proceeding with any final decision,” the lawmakers concluded.

Read the full letter here and below:

Dear Postmaster General Steiner,

We write as a delegation regarding the proposed permanent closure of the Mule Creek Post Office in Grant County, New Mexico. We are deeply concerned about the impact this proposed permanent closure would have on the residents of Mule Creek and the surrounding rural service area. We strongly urge that the United States Postal Service (USPS) reconsider the proposed closure and maintain postal service in Mule Creek.

The Mule Creek Post Office has served the community since January 16th, 1916—more than 110 years. For generations, it has provided essential postal services to residents, ranchers, veterans, senior citizens, families, and small businesses. In 2024, the Mule Creek postal facility was damaged, and the landlord subsequently declined to make the necessary repairs. As a result, USPS was required to locate a new property from which to continue permanent operations. While USPS quickly established a mobile postal unit to provide interim service, what was intended to be a temporary solution has now become a two-year challenge.

Mule Creek residents continue to lack a permanent post office and must rely on a mobile unit that provides reduced hours and services. Currently, residents can access the mobile unit only from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. on weekdays. These limited hours create significant accessibility challenges for residents and further underscore the importance of finding a permanent solution rather than allowing temporary arrangements to become the basis for permanent closure. It has now been more than two years since the original facility was damaged, and residents continue to wait for USPS to establish a permanent postal facility in Mule Creek. The prolonged absence of a permanent facility, combined with reduced hours and services, has created uncertainty for the community and raised serious concerns about the future of the post office. The consequences of this closure are particularly devastating because Mule Creek residents do not have universal residential mail delivery. Many residents would have to travel substantially far to retrieve letters, packages, prescriptions, government correspondence and other essential items.

We understand that USPS has identified Buckhorn as a potential alternative location. Buckhorn is approximately 18 miles from the current Mule Creek Post Office, requiring a resident traveling between the two locations to make an approximately thirty-six-mile round trip. For residents living in the more remote service area, the total round-trip distance to an alternative post office can range from approximately forty-five to seventy-five miles. These distances could create a significant burden for residents who rely on local postal services.

We are concerned about the effect of closure on senior citizens, veterans, individuals with disabilities, residents with medical needs and individuals without reliable transportation. The potential consequences extend to the timely receipt and shipment of prescription medications, medical correspondence, government documents, business materials, packages, and other time sensitive items. Requiring residents to travel substantially greater distances for routine postal needs would impose recurring costs in fuel, vehicle maintenance, mileage, and travel time.

We respectfully request that USPS consider the importance of the Mule Creek Post Office to the residents and community of Mule Creek. This local post office serves a purpose that extends beyond the processing and delivery of mail. It provides an important point of contact for residents who may otherwise have limited opportunities to interact with neighbors, exchange information and maintain essential community relationships.

After more than a century of continuous service, the Mule Creek Post Office has become an established and valued institution within the community. We recognize USPS’s responsibility to operate efficiently and to evaluate its facilities and services. At the same time, decisions concerning rural postal facilities should account for the unique circumstances of communities where geographic isolation and the absence of universal residential delivery can make access to an alternative facility substantially more difficult.

To that end, we respectfully request that the Postal Service undertake a comprehensive review of the proposed closure and specifically:

Suspend and reconsider the proposed closure of the Mule Creek Post Office pending further review;

Conduct a thorough assessment of the actual distances, driving times, and transportation requirements residents would face in accessing alternative postal facilities;

Consider the absence of universal residential mail delivery within the Mule Creek servicearea and the resulting importance of local access to postal services;

Evaluate the specific effects of closure on senior citizens, veterans, individuals with disabilities, residents with medical needs, and those without reliable transportation;

Assess the economic consequences for ranchers, home-based businesses, agricultural operations, and other local enterprises that rely on dependable postal services;

Consider the cumulative fuel, vehicle, and transportation costs that would be imposed upon residents required to travel greater distances;

Evaluate the potential consequences for the timely receipt and shipment of prescription medications, medical correspondence, business materials, and other time-sensitive items;

Engage directly with the Mule Creek community and local stakeholders to explore alternatives that would preserve meaningful, reliable, and accessible postal service.

The Mule Creek Post Office has served the community since 1916. It’s more than one hundred years of service reflects its longstanding role in the life of the community. We request that USPS reconsider the proposed closure and undertake a comprehensive, community-specific review before proceeding with any final decision.

We appreciate your attention to this critical issue affecting our constituents and urge USPS to provide a timely and detailed response outlining the steps it will take to fulfill its obligations to the residents of Mule Creek.

title: Markey Joins Kelly, Whitehouse to Press EPA on Rollback of Public Input Rules for Data Center Air Permits
text:
Washington (October 6, 2026) - Senators Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), members of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works, this week sent a letter opposing the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) proposal to eliminate the 30-day mandatory public notice period that allows communities to provide input on proposed facilities, like data centers, that may affect the air they breathe.

“We agree that permitting should be efficient, predictable, and capable of supporting the infrastructure our country needs. But faster permitting should not come at the expense of transparency or communities’ ability to shape the decisions that affect them,” wrote the senators to Administrator Zeldin.

The letter to the EPA was co-signed by Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.).

Read the full letter to the EPA here.

The proposed rollback is included in the Senator’s recent report, The EPA’s Data Center Disaster: How the Trump Administration is Destroying Environmental Protections and Selling Out Communities for Big Tech, which details the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)’s campaign of reckless deregulation to dilute environmental and public health guardrails in direct service of Big Tech’s race to build data centers.

Senator Markey has been a leading voice against irresponsible and unregulated data center buildout at the expense of public health and the environment.

In July, Senator Markey released a discussion draft of his Protecting Communities Against Data Center Impacts proposal, a bill that would create a national framework to prevent increased energy costs, pollution, and adverse health harms related to the rapid buildout of data centers and associated fossil fuel infrastructure.

In June, Senator Markey wrote to EPA Administrator Zeldin to demand the withdrawal of a proposed rule that underminesClean Air Act permitting standards to facilitate the buildout of data centers and associated fossil fuel infrastructure.

In June, Senator Markey reintroduced his Artificial Intelligence (AI) Environmental Impacts Act, legislation that would require data center operators to report the full range of their facilities’ environmental impacts.

In November 2025, Senator Markey wrote to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) urging the agency to ensure that increased and projected energy demand from data centers does not result in unjust or unreasonable rate hikes for American households.

In September 2025, Senator Markey wrote to the EPA in opposition to the agency’s initial announcement of plans to roll back the NSR program for data center buildout.

In July 2025, Senator Markey hosted a roundtable discussion titled The Data Center Next Door: Hidden Costs and Harms of Artificial Intelligence and Cryptomining to highlight the adverse environmental, health, climate, and energy cost impacts of data center proliferation in communities across the United States, and to condemn the deregulatory actions set forth in President Trump’s AI Action Plan. On the day of the roundtable, Senator Markey also released a storybook to spotlight the experiences of American families living with data centers in their backyard.

title: Merkley, McGovern Unveil New Legislation to Protect Hong Kong Residents in America from Being Forced to Return to PRC
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley and U.S. Representative James P. McGovern (MA-02)—Ranking Members of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China (CECC)—announced the Hong Konger Promise of Refuge Act, new legislation to provide protections for Hong Kong residents who have fled persecution and are living in the United States.

Since 2021, Hong Kong residents have been protected from deportation under the Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) program; however, the program is set to expire in early 2027. Merkley and McGovern’s bill would allow certain Hong Kong residents in America to apply for U.S. lawful permanent resident status and ultimately U.S. citizenship, rather than be forced to return to the People’s Republic of China (PRC).

“As the PRC and Hong Kong authorities continue to undermine the fundamental rights and freedoms of Hong Kongers, the United States must protect Hong Kong residents who have sought refuge in America,” said Merkley. “The PRC’s erosion of autonomy, rule of law, and civil liberties in Hong Kong and the political persecution of those who were brave enough to speak out in dissent mean that America cannot just abandon Hong Kongers who sought refuge here. Congress must take action and enact our legislation to ensure Hong Kongers residing in the U.S. do not have to fear deportation.”

“Hong Kongers have found safe harbor in the United States under DED, and we should continue to protect them from being deported back to danger in Hong Kong,” said McGovern. “I urge President Trump to extend DED, but if he does not, Congress should pass our bill. Providing refuge to Hong Kongers used to have bipartisan support, including from then-Senator Marco Rubio. Now, the Trump-Rubio Administration is working to send people back to persecution under the Chinese Communist Party they once said they opposed. We should not be complicit in such human rights violations. The U.S. must extend DED now.”

Merkley and McGovern have led the charge to stand up for the rights of Hong Kongers and protect Hong Kong residents living in America from deportation. They have also highlighted the case of Jimmy Lai and other pro-democracy advocates who have been the targets of the Chinese and Hong Kong governments’ coordinated repression of free speech and democracy.

The Hong Konger Promise of Refuge Act is supported by Hong Kong Watch, Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong (CFHK) Foundation, and Hong Kong Democracy Council.

“Hongkongers living in the United States were given protection because of a crackdown this country has condemned for seven years, and they are now being arrested despite that protection. Deferred Enforced Departure was never meant to be permanent, and a memorandum that expires in February is no safeguard against a government that puts bounties on pro-democracy activists abroad. We welcome this legislation, which follows the precedent Congress set after Tiananmen: a closed group, a one-year window to apply, and a real path to permanent status. Congress should pass it without delay,”said Ray Wong, Policy and Strategy Advisor for Hong Kong Watch.

“Members of Congress from both parties have long been the bedrock of support for freedom and human rights in China and Hong Kong. Now, Hongkongers who have built lives in the United States face the prospect of being sent back to a place where they could face political persecution. Deferred Enforced Departure, which was granted by a Democratic administration and implemented by a Republican one, is set to expire on February 5, 2027, and there is no guarantee it will be renewed. If it lapses, thousands of people will lose their protection from removal and their ability to work. It is time for Congress to stand up for freedom and human rights and pass this legislation in 2026 so that Hongkongers are not forced back into the hands of an authoritarian regime. Time is short, and action is necessary,” said Jonathan Stivers, U.S. Director, Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong (CFHK) Foundation.

“Since August 2021, thousands of Hong Kongers have lived, worked, and contributed to American life while lawfully present under Deferred Enforced Departure. Many face immediate danger if forced to return home due to their record of pro-democracy activism. They cherish freedom and human rights because they have seen the Chinese Communist Party chipping away at the values they hold dear firsthand. The program that now protects them was twice expanded and extended, but it was always meant as a stopgap executive measure until legislation establishing viable, permanent humanitarian pathways. While previous efforts have faltered, the Hong Konger Promise of Refuge Act is an important step in the right direction that can eliminate uncertainties clouding the future of a community already in the United States,” said the Hong Kong Democracy Council.

Full text of the bill can be found by clicking here.

title: New Analysis Shows Federal Government to Save Nearly $2 for Every $1 Invested in Flood Prevention
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, at the request of U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Ranking Member of the Senate Budget Committee, the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office (CBO) released a report detailing that every $1 the federal government invests in flood adaptations can save taxpayers nearly $2 in disaster spending, as well as reduce National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) claims.

“Every year, billions of taxpayer dollars are spent cleaning up and restoring the damage caused by flood waters. From coastal towns to rural communities, climate change related events are exasperating federal resources that are allocated to help families rebuild from these costly disasters,” said Merkley. “Today, CBO confirms that a simple way for the federal government to be a better steward of taxpayer money, is to invest in flood adaptation methods—such as repairing local dams and levees or working to elevate high-risk properties. We owe it to the American people to make investments that will not only protect their property and surrounding community but also save lives.”

In his June letter, Merkley specifically asked CBO to estimate the amount of potential future savings that could accrue to the federal government for every dollar it spends on flood adaptation and mitigation. A previous CBO report published in September 2024 detailed how spending for adaptations can reduce flood damage.

CBO breaks down the 30-year savings as for every $1 billion spent in prevention in present-value terms:

Future flood damage costs will decrease by $3 to $4 billion,

Taxpayers will save $1.8 billion in disaster spending, and

NFIP claims reduced by $300 million, mostly benefiting ratepayers through lower premiums.

CBO’s full report is HERE.

title: VIDEO: During National Fire Prevention Week, Senator Moody Announces More Than $44 Million in Grant Awards for Fire Departments Across Florida
text:
LEHIGH ACRES, Fla.—As Florida’s dry season begins, Senator Ashley Moody today announced the award of more than $44 million in federal grants going to fire departments statewide. Senator Moody’s announcement comes during National Fire Prevention Week surrounded by firefighters at the Lehigh Acres Fire Control and Rescue District—which will be receiving $4.2 million from FEMA’s SAFER Grant Program. Through the SAFER Grant Program, fire departments across the state are receiving funds to help hire more firefighters and better protect Florida communities.

“During National Fire Prevention Week, we’re recognizing the brave firefighters who work to protect Florida families and communities when emergencies arise. I’m in Lehigh Acres today to announce more than $44 million in recent federal funding for fire departments across our state to help ensure our first responders have the resources and equipment they need to answer the call and keep Floridians safe,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

Over the past year, Florida has faced several wildfire threats, including the massive wildfire outside of Miami earlier in the summer. Last year, there were 2,913 wildfires across Florida, burning more than 228,000 acres. Since January of this year, there have been approximately 2,975 wildfires in the state, burning more than 280,000 acres.

BACKGROUND:

Since Senator Moody has been in office, the total amount of firefighter grant awards provided to Florida fire entities is more than $89 million. This includes 71 individual awards made to Florida applicants across three different FEMA grant programs.

The Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant award announced today will allow the Lehigh Acres Fire Control and Rescue District to hire 21 new firefighters.

It is National Fire Prevention Week. Florida is the lightning capital of the U.S., and nearly half of the state is covered in forests—land that is both fire-dependent and fire-prone.

The following are tips to help prevent fires at home in addition to wildfires:

Install smoke alarms on every level of a residence, inside bedrooms and outside sleeping areas, and test alarms every month;

Institute a family fire escape plan, and practice the plan twice a year;

Practice safe yard waste burning—never burn on windy days, refrain from burning during dry weather and during periods of high fire danger;

Prepare yards for potential wildfires—remove all dead vegetation from yards, roofs, rain gutters, windows and decks; trim trees regularly; create a separation between trees, shrubs and items that could catch fire;

Harden the home and outbuildings against fire—keep working fire extinguishers on hand, make sure eaves are made with fire resistant materials, clean vents regularly; and

Have an emergency supply kit ready in the event of needing to evacuate quickly—it should include a seven-day supply of prescriptions or other medications, cell phone with chargers; cash, copies of important documents like birth certificates and passports, and an inventory of home contents.

title: Padilla Announces Troubling New FBI Whistleblower Disclosure: White House Allegedly Directed Kash Patel to Investigate LA Protesters Exercising 1st Amendment Rights
text:
Whistleblower reveals White House, DOJ leadership, and FBI leadership pressured FBI employees to illegally investigate protesters of this Administration’s cruel mass deportation agenda

FBI leadership allegedly acknowledged unconstitutionality of the investigations and nonetheless instructed employees to proceed

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, announced the receipt of a new whistleblower disclosure that alleges the White House instructed Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel to have the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office open an investigation into protesters solely for their First Amendment activity. The whistleblower also alleges that in a separate incident, then Acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove instructed the LA Field Office to open an investigation into any anti-Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) protesters demonstrating at federal buildings in Los Angeles without identifying any federal criminal activity, actual or potential national security threats, or vulnerability to such threats.

“Free speech and assembly are protected by the First Amendment because they are foundational to our democracy. This whistleblower disclosure is deeply alarming. It points to a President and political appointees who continue to weaponize the justice system against perceived enemies, and it alleges that FBI leadership believed these directives were unconstitutional yet carried them out anyway. Investigations like this undermine the Constitution, divert resources from real crimes, put careers at risk, and send a chilling message to anyone who might oppose this Administration: you could be next,” said Senator Padilla. “I thank the whistleblower, and any who may come forward in the future, for speaking truth to power. Our democracy is bigger than one man, and each of us has a responsibility to shine a light on abuses of power and hold leadership accountable.”

The disclosure received by Senator Padilla claims that:

Trump allegedly directed the FBI to investigate protestors exercising their First Amendment right to free speech.

Trump allegedly saw video footage of a protest in Alhambra, California depicting “community members in a residential neighborhood using megaphones and other alerts to warn residents about the presence of immigration enforcement officers, while advising neighbors of their legal rights and encouraging them not to open their doors without a signed judicial warrant.” Trump was “angry about the incident” and “wanted those protesters investigated and arrested,” despite FBI agents concluding that the protests “never crossed the line into impeding arrest or being a threat.” “The President wants this investigation,” and “the directive had to be followed,” the disclosure says.

On a separate occasion, despite no apparent evidence of a threat, FBI employees were directed to open investigations into anti-ICE and CBP protesters at federal buildings in Los Angeles—again solely based on their First Amendment activity.

The whistleblower – in their capacity as a Supervisory Intelligence Analyst at the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office– was informed by Field Office leadership that Bove instructed FBI personnel to open an investigation into any anti-ICE and CBP protesters demonstrating at federal buildings in Los Angeles. This directive was issued despite the absence of any information indicating that the protesters posed a national security threat, had engaged in criminal activity, or were vulnerable to such threats.

Field Office leadership followed the White House, DOJ, and FBI’s directives due to political pressure, despite acknowledgement that it was unconstitutional.

Alarmingly, when the whistleblower raised objections to opening an investigation into the protesters, leadership asserted that even though they knew the act was unconstitutional, “a criminal investigation was being pursued because the President wanted protestors investigated and arrested even after a finding… that the protestors’ actions were constitutionally protected.”

Field Office leadership subsequently told the whistleblower their job was at risk for their refusal to participate in the unlawful investigation. The whistleblower alleges that they were retaliated against for their disagreement, including by being removed from their supervisory position. Ultimately, the whistleblower resigned from the FBI before they could be fired.

The whistleblower’s supervisor also expressed “fear of challenging leadership directives, even when they believed those directives were unlawful or unconstitutional,” underscoring the chilling effect that the Trump Administration’s weaponization of the justice system has had in silencing dissent.

Resources were diverted from legitimate public safety missions to satisfy the White House’s unconstitutional directive.

Additionally, the whistleblower outlines that significant law enforcement resources were diverted from core public-safety missions to satisfy the Trump Administration’s push to silence its detractors. FBI intelligence analysts and investigative personnel were reassigned and resources were diverted from ongoing matters involving drug trafficking, violent crime, and transnational organized crime to support protest-related inquiries without evidence of actual or potential national security threats, criminal activity, or vulnerability to such threats that would have justified such a diversion of resources. This diversion impaired the Los Angeles Field Office’s ability to focus on critical public-safety and national-security priorities.

In response to the compelling allegations in the disclosure, Padilla demanded Patel and Attorney General Todd Blanche provide answers on the nature of these investigations, transparency into any subsequent investigations into protestors, and documents related to these investigations.

“Throughout your appearances before the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, you promised that cases would be based only on the facts and the law, free from political interference. But the Disclosure paints a starkly different picture and raises serious questions about whether other similar investigations have been initiated under your tenures. The Disclosure depicts an FBI and DOJ willing to surveil individuals solely for First Amendment activity criticizing the Administration—at the behest of the White House and Trump loyalists, over the objection of senior staff, and in contravention of agency policy and the Constitution. Such allegations raise grave concerns about the rule of law under your leadership, and the diversion of resources from ongoing criminal investigations, and the testimony that you provided under oath to Congress,” wrote Senator Padilla.

The whistleblower is a former FBI employee and a licensed attorney represented by the Government Accountability Project and David Laufman.

The whistleblower’s disclosure follows a chilling pattern in which the Administration has pursued Trump’s baseless claims at the expense of Americans’ safety. A separate, recent whistleblower disclosure alleges DHS and USCIS leadership abruptly diverted USCIS Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate immigration officers from their national security-related duties and directed them instead to use illegal procedures and questionable data to identify purported “unlawful voters,” and create federal law enforcement records against them, including naturalized U.S. citizens. The Administration also redirected Homeland Security Investigations analysts from their typical work on criminal matters and to a so-called “tiger team” for the sole purpose of investigating, surveilling, and detaining students and other individuals based solely on their political opinions.

title: NEW REPORT: Rosen, Cortez Masto Release Joint Report Detailing How Trump’s Economy Is Hurting Nevada Latino Families
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – During the final week of Hispanic Heritage Month, U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) released a new report detailing the harm that Donald Trump’s policies are causing Latino families in Nevada. Because of Trump’s tariffs, war in Iran, and his “One Big Beautiful Bill,” Latino families are paying more for everyday essentials and seeing fewer opportunities to get ahead.

“Donald Trump’s economy is a disaster for Latinos in Nevada. Anyone who’s willing to work hard should have a fair shot at getting ahead, but that’s become almost impossible under Trump’s leadership,” said Senator Rosen. “Families are paying more for gas, groceries, health care, and housing, all while our tourism industry declines as a result of Trump’s policies. I’m committed to helping every Nevadan live the American Dream, and I’ll keep working to bring down costs and expand opportunities for Nevada families.”

“This report confirms what Nevada families have known for months: under the Trump economy, it’s getting harder to put food on the table and a roof over your head,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “From his blanket tariffs to his reckless war in Iran, everything this President is doing has driven up costs for Latinos in Nevada. Every family deserves the chance to get ahead, and I’m going to keep doing everything I can to reverse President Trump’s disastrous policies.”

Below is a breakdown of how Trump and Washington Republicans’ policies are hurting Latino families in Nevada.

Gas and Groceries

Trump’s war in Iran has cost Latinos in Nevada about $230 million extra at the gas pump since the war began, which breaks down to an additional $659 per family.

Latinos account for more than a quarter of Nevada SNAP participants, including over 48,000 Latino children.

As a result of Donald Trump’s cuts to SNAP in the “One Big Beautiful Bill,” 38,000 Latino Nevadans have lost their SNAP benefits, including as many as 16,000 children.

Trump’s first year in office cost Latinos in Nevada an additional $108 million on groceries, which is $310 per family.

Trump’s mass deportation agenda is taking immigrant workers off the job, and as a result, prices are rising in sectors like agriculture that depend on immigrant labor.

More than 60% of farm laborers nationwide are Latino, and the vast majority are immigrants. Targeting of this workforce has led to a 32.1% increase in lettuce prices, a 7.1% increase in apple prices, a 6.3% increase in fresh citrus prices, and a 7.9% increase in canned fruit prices.

Economic Opportunity

The tax provisions in Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” disproportionately benefit the top one percent of earners and leave the working class behind.

title: Senators Rosen, Lankford Honored for Bipartisan Leadership Against Antisemitism
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Yesterday, the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the leading anti-hate organization in the world, honored U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and James Lankford (R-OK) with the Levenson Family Defender of Democracy Award in recognition of their bipartisan leadership to protect Jewish communities and combat antisemitism.

Senators Rosen and Lankford have worked together across the aisle to protect Jewish communities across the country and strengthen federal efforts to fight antisemitism. Their leadership on the bipartisan Jewish American Security Act will protect Jewish communities, students, and institutions from antisemitic hate, violence, discrimination, and intimidation across sectors.

“When Senator Lankford and I founded the first-ever Senate Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, we made it our goal to bring the fight against antisemitism and Holocaust denial to the forefront of the national agenda. Through introducing and passing legislation, engaging with Administrations of both parties, and organizing active discussions with high-ranking officials both at home and abroad, we’ve managed to reach across the aisle and push for real change and protections for Jewish communities at home and abroad,” said Senator Rosen. “It is truly an honor to receive the Levenson Defender of Democracy award with my good friend and colleague Senator James Lankford. We promise to continue fighting to ensure that Jewish communities everywhere can practice their religion and participate in society without fear.”

As just the third Jewish woman to ever serve in the U.S. Senate and the first former synagogue president, Senator Rosen has been leading the fight against antisemitism. She and Senator Lankford helped elevate the U.S. Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism to the rank of Ambassador. Senator Rosen also successfully led the bipartisan push last Congress to reauthorize the bipartisan Never Again Education Act, which she was also instrumental in helping to pass in 2020. She and Senator Lankford also introduced the Holocaust Education and Antisemitism Lessons (HEAL) Act, which would direct the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to study and report on state efforts to educate students on the Holocaust.

title: Senate Passes Peters and Slotkin Legislation to Extend Federal Funding and Protections for the Great Lakes
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — The Senate unanimously passed legislation championed by U.S. Senators Gary Peters (D-MI) and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) to protect the Great Lakes and vital waterways across Michigan.

The legislation would extend the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative (GLRI), authorizing $475 million in annual funding for the program through 2030. The GLRI combines federal and nonfederal efforts to stop the spread of invasive species, restore coastline and habitats connecting our streams and rivers, clean up environmentally damaged Areas of Concern, and prevent future contamination.

“Millions of Michiganders rely on the Great Lakes for their livelihood and protecting it is existential for Michigan,” said Senator Slotkin. “The Great Lakes Restoration Initiative will help protect the lakes, our economy and our way of life – from vital programs that work to mitigate coastal erosion to protecting against harmful invasive species like Asian Carp. I will always fight for our Great Lakes and will continue to work with people in both parties to do just that.”

“The Great Lakes Restoration Initiative is the most significant investment ever made to restore and protect our Great Lakes from things like invasive species, pollution, and shoreline erosion,” said Senator Peters. “Now more than ever, we need to ensure this vital program has the funding it needs to continue supporting projects that will keep these treasured bodies of water healthy and vibrant for years to come. I’ll keep working in a bipartisan way to get this commonsense bill signed into law.”

“The Great Lakes Commission applauds the Senate for advancing bipartisan legislation to reauthorize the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, a proven program that is delivering environmental and economic results for communities across the Great Lakes basin,” said Erika Jensen, Executive Director of the Great Lakes Commission. “Continued federal investment in the GLRI is essential to restoring degraded areas, protecting water quality, combating invasive species, and strengthening communities across the basin. We thank Senators Peters and Slotkin and their colleagues for their leadership and urge the House to move quickly to pass this critically important legislation.”

“The GLRI is integral to the health of the Great Lakes and the 30 million people who depend on them for drinking water,” said Laura Rubin, Director of Healing Our Waters-Great Lakes Coalition. “Reauthorizing the GLRI is essential to maintaining the momentum we have built in restoring one of the nation’s most treasured natural resources, and we are grateful for the leadership of the Great Lakes delegation for advancing this legislation, preventing interruption to the GLRI’s vital work.”

Since its inception, the GLRI has spurred tremendous progress in Michigan and throughout the Great Lakes region, including nearly half of a million acres of habitat protected, restored, or enhanced, a five-fold increase in the successful cleanup and delisting of Areas of Concern, a ten-fold increase in the remediation of environmental and public health impairments, and reducing the threat of harmful algal blooms. The GLRI’s efforts have also resulted in economic returns of more than 3 to 1 across the region.

The senators’ legislation is supported by the League of Conservation Voters, National Wildlife Federation, Sierra Club, National Parks Conservation Association, Council of Great Lakes Governors, Great Lakes Fishery Commission, American Great Lakes Ports Association, Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative, American Rivers, American Sportfishing Association, Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership, Ducks Unlimited, Trout Unlimited, Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation, National Audubon Society – Great Lakes, Environmental Law & Policy Center, and other key stakeholders in Great Lakes protection.

Peters and Slotkin have been steadfast supporters of the Great Lakes, including by enacting the single-largest-ever investment in the GLRI through the bipartisan infrastructure law to accelerate the restoration of nine high-priority areas in Michigan whose lakes, rivers and watersheds flow into the Great Lakes.

title: Tuberville Honors Christopher Carlile of Enterprise as October “Veteran of the Month”
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) released a video honoring U.S. Army Colonel Christopher Carlile as the October “Veteran of the Month.”

Excerpts of Sen. Tuberville’s remarks can be found below, and complete remarks can be found here.

“Transitioning from military to civilian life can be difficult for many of our veterans. For U.S. Army Colonel Chris Carlile of Enterprise, he’s combined many of his passions and experiences to make this transition easier for Alabama’s heroes. Chris is a 6th-generation Army veteran who spent more than 36 years protecting our country across the globe.

[…]

After retiring from the military, Chris and his wife Sandra returned to the Wiregrass where they first met when he was a young pilot in training. He became involved in the Wiregrass veterans community and now helps veterans apply for their benefits as a Veterans’ Service Officer with Disabled American Vets, Post 9. Chris also serves as the Chairman of the Executive Committee of the Army Aviation Museum Foundation where he helps tell the story of Fort Rucker’s role in army aviation to more than 100,000 visitors every year. His passion for army aviation also shines through his involvement with the Friends of Army Aviation where he has coordinated public nationwide air shows, funeral honor flights, displays for community service, and helicopter ride events with their Huey choppers. They made Alabama proud with their flights during the Army’s 250th Birthday parade in Washington, D.C. Chris is also a Harvard-educated cattleman and is part of the Coffee County Cattlemen’s Association where he mentors other veterans who are wanting to transition from the military to the ag industry.

We have a lot to thank Chris for when it comes to our military security and our national food security. It’s my honor to recognize him as the October ‘Veteran of the Month.’”

Constituents can nominate an Alabama veteran and submit their information to Sen. Tuberville’s office for consideration in the 2026 “Veteran of the Month” series by emailing press_office@tuberville.senate.gov.

Senator Tommy Tuberville represents Alabama in the United States Senate and is a member of the Senate Armed Services, Agriculture, Veterans’ Affairs, HELP and Aging Committees.

title: Van Hollen, Booker, Colleagues File Amicus Brief in Lawsuit Against Trump’s Department of Housing and Urban Development for Attacking Fair Housing Program
text:
Today, U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) and Cory Booker (D-N.J.) led more than 15 of their colleagues in submitting an amicus brief supporting a federal judge’s ruling that the Trump Administration’s Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) unlawfully restricted funding to groups that investigate and enforce laws against housing discrimination. The amicus filed argues that HUD’s unprecedented attempt to direct $46 million away from fair housing organizations – while diverting an additional $10 million to government agencies with separate appropriations – has no lawful justification and would harm the nation’s fair housing enforcement infrastructure. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Cory Booker submitted the brief to the United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit in the case of Massachusetts Fair Housing Center; National Fair Housing Alliance v. Department of Housing and Urban Development and were joined in submitting it by Senators Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Mark Warner (D-Va.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Edward Markey (D-Mass.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), and Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.).

The Senators begin the brief, “Congress intended FHIP to foster a nationwide network of private organizations, like Plaintiffs, that can aid the federal government in uncovering and eliminating housing discrimination. Since Congress piloted FHIP in 1988 and codified it in 1992, FHIP has consistently sustained private fair housing organizations through three grant streams: the Private Enforcement Initiative (‘PEI’) to support investigative and enforcement activities; the Education and Outreach Initiative (‘EOI’); and the Fair Housing Organization Initiative (‘FHOI’) to build organizational capacity. With this funding, private organizations handle most housing discrimination complaints and enforcement nationwide.”

“HUD’s July 2, 2026 Notices of Funding Opportunity (‘NOFOs’) endanger fair housing organizations and their vital work. The NOFOs deviate from FHIP’s authorizing statute, decades of FHIP practice, and Congress’s intent. For the first time since FHIP’s codification in 1992, the FY2025 NOFOs provide no new awards for PEI or EOI—the lifeblood of fair housing organizations—nor do they fulfill existing multi-year PEI awards. Instead, HUD attempts to direct $46 million—the vast majority of funds—away from existing qualified organizations in favor of organizations with no experience in fair housing enforcement, while diverting the remaining $10 million to governmental agencies for which Congress separately appropriated. These unprecedented actions have no lawful justification and would seriously harm the nation’s fair housing enforcement infrastructure. The district court rightly vacated HUD’s unlawful notices and directed funding to flow under the prior framework. HUD’s request to stay that well-founded order should be denied,” they argue.

The Senators conclude, “The Doles Memo’s stated aims are misleading and contrary to FHIP’s purposes as well. It claims the FY2025 NOFOs will ‘expand geographic coverage,’ ‘broaden’ expertise, and ‘strengthen the long-term resilience of the national fair housing infrastructure.’ HUD’s NOFOs do the opposite—losing geographic coverage, expertise, and organizational resilience by concentrating FHIP funding in a handful of grants that existing organizations cannot receive. Worse, the Doles Memo treats fair housing organizations like maligned welfare recipients—charging them with ‘perpetual dependence’ on federal funding. FHIP’s goal always has been to sustain these organizations as a vital organ of the fair housing enforcement system, particularly in areas underserved without federal resources. HUD’s NOFOs, if unaddressed, would set fair housing enforcement back decades. Defendants’ Motion for Stay should be denied.”

title: Warnock Calls on Georgia Department of Community Health to Preserve and Expand Health Coverage for Hardworking Georgians
text:
In a letter to the Georgia Department of Community Health, Senator Reverend Warnock pressed the state to preserve and expand access to health care coverage for low-income Georgians

Senator Warnock slammed the Kemp administration’s threat to eliminate Georgia Pathways unless the state receives a 90 percent federal match

Senator Warnock is a leading proponent of Medicaid expansion and has long championed efforts to expand Georgians’ access to affordable health care

Senator Reverend Warnock: “I urge the State to do everything in its power to keep as many people enrolled in affordable coverage”

Atlanta, GA – Last month, Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) pressed the Georgia Department of Community Health over the state’s threat to shut down its health care coverage program for low-income Georgians, which would strip some of the state’s lowest-income residents of their health care coverage. Under Governor Brian Kemp’s direction, the state is demanding a 90 percent federal match to bankroll Georgia Pathways, Governor Kemp’s own deeply flawed health care coverage program, or threatening to suspend coverage for all enrollees.

“I urge the State to do everything in its power to keep as many people enrolled in affordable coverage,” wrote Senator Warnock in a letter to the Georgia Department of Community Health. “If it does not, make no mistake: it is the State’s mismanagement of funds and poor construction of its ‘innovative program’ that will continue to doom the lowest-income Georgians to a life without health care.”

Georgia has so far declined to fully expand Medicaid, rejecting federal incentives that at one point estimated to be nearly $2 billion in funding to support program expansion. Instead, Governor Kemp pursued Georgia Pathways to Coverage, a state-run program rife with bureaucratic red tape and arbitrary coverage restrictions. Despite hailing Pathways as a success after its launch, the Kemp administration now claims it cannot afford to provide health care coverage to the nearly 100,000 hardworking Georgians estimated to gain eligibility in 2027.

Senator Warnock is a leading proponent of Medicaid expansion and has long championed efforts to expand Georgians’ access to affordable health care. Last year, he released a report titled “Healthy People, Healthy Economy,” which found that investing in Medicaid stimulates economic growth and promotes access to employment. In the report, Senator Warnock warned that if other states adopt Georgia’s flawed Pathways to Coverage model, millions of Americans could lose access to health care, government bureaucracy could grow, hospitals could close, jobs could be lost, and the economy could slow. Since then, Congressional Republicans have used Georgia’s Pathways to Coverage program as a model for the health care cuts and changes included in their July 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill, set to take effect in 2027.

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and text is below:

“Ms. Hicks,

“I respectfully submit my written comments regarding Georgia’s Department of Community Health’s (DCH) proposed State Plan Amendment (SPA) implementing the Medicaid community engagement requirement under H.R. 1 and the CMS Interim Final Rule (CMS-2454-IFC).

“While I have concerns with the deeply flawed Georgia Pathways to Coverage (“Pathways”) program, I am alarmed by insinuations that the State of Georgia (“the State”) will simply end the program without a 90 percent federal match. Such an abrupt termination would pull the rug out from the few Georgians currently covered by the program and cause even more Georgians to lose access to health care. I take issue with the State’s embrace of work reporting requirements, which have been shown to wrongfully prevent working adults from accessing care. However, it has always been my core belief that we must expand health coverage to as many Georgians as possible until we fully expand Medicaid and close the coverage gap. That is why the State must do whatever it can to protect and expand Medicaid coverage for Georgians.

“When the State launched Pathways in 2023, it limited coverage to individuals who reported completing 80 hours of work, job training, education, or community service each month. At the time of its initial launch, Georgia was the only state in the country with active work reporting requirements in its Medicaid program. The State estimated that as many as 100,000 people would sign up and that up to 345,000 people could be eligible.

“In January 2025, the State modestly increased eligibility and exempted parents and guardians of children up to age 6 from the work reporting requirements. Even with this change, the most recent estimate of enrollment in Pathways was just over 19,000 people — well short of the 100,000 enrollees predicted.

“In July 2025, Congressional Republicans passed H.R. 1 to implement new federal work reporting requirements for the Medicaid expansion population starting after December 31, 2026, pointing to the ‘success’ of Georgia’s Pathways.4 The new federal reporting requirements, however, are more generous than Georgia’s current program. According to the SPA, the State is now being ‘forced to expand the program to 100,000 new individuals in order to maintain the coverage of approximately 20,000 hard- working Georgians.’ ‘Forced’ to provide healthcare to Georgians. That is quite the sentiment, especially when these new individuals are veterans, parents of school-aged children, children formerly in foster care, and other individuals classified as medicinally frail. These are the people the State does not want to be ‘forced’ to cover.

“In 2022, the State initially predicted its program could cover as many as 100,000 people. Now, the State claims it cannot possibly cover this amount—at least, not without a substantially more generous federal match of 90 percent. Had the State simply expanded Medicaid in 2022, they would have received an automatic 90 percent federal match for over a decade. Congressional Democrats even enacted an additional federal incentive for states that newly adopted expansion, which was at one point was estimated to bring in nearly $2 billion in additional federal funding for Georgia.

“Instead, the State spent tens of millions of dollars to launch a bureaucratic program that covered a fraction of the expected population. A report based on Pathways data through June 2025 found that Georgia spent about $13,597 per active enrollee on program costs.6 A U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) report from September 2025 found that the State spent over $54 million on administrative costs for the program. And now, the State is claiming it cannot afford to provide health coverage to as many as 100,000 working Georgia families, despite touting its ability to do just that 4 years ago.

“I urge the State to do everything in its power to keep as many people enrolled in affordable coverage. If it does not, make no mistake: it is the State’s mismanagement of funds and poor construction of its ‘innovative program’ that will continue to doom the lowest-income Georgians to a life without health care.

Sincerely,”

###

title: Welch Brings Common Grounds Listening Session to Windham County
text:

“The pressures on Vermont are the same as those facing every red and blue state across the country—these are shared challenges. But my colleagues across the aisle haven’t embraced the idea that whether you’re from Indiana, or Idaho, or Vermont, the people we represent need an affordable health care system.
