title: ICYMI: Rep. Grijalva Joins Local Community Members to Raise Alarm Over Marana Detention Facility
text:
Marana, Arizona — Yesterday, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva joined local community members in Marana for a press conference addressing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s new contract with Management and Training Corporation (MTC) to open an immigration detention facility in Marana within the next 60 days.

The press conference brought together community members and local voices to raise concerns about the proposed facility and the record of MTC, the company contracted to operate it. MTC has previously operated correctional facilities in Arizona that faced allegations and documented concerns involving conditions including sexual abuse, inadequate food, extreme heat, and prison riots. The State of Arizona has terminated previous contracts with MTC under both Democratic and Republican governors.

Earlier this year, Rep. Grijalva wrote a letter demanding transparency on the proposed facility to then-Secretary Noem. This comes after Rep. Grijalva wrote a letter demanding transparency on the proposed facility to then-Secretary Noem and joined community members earlier in the year at a press conference alongside Reps. Stanton and Ansari.

A copy of her remarks are below:

“Buenas tardes. Thank you to PRICE for organizing this press conference.

We’re here today because DHS is once again rushing to open another private detention facility in Arizona.

Eso no está bien. Nuestra comunidad merece respuestas.

This is happening as deaths in ICE custody reach record levels – and as the agency fails to provide even the most basic care for the people already in its custody.

Just today, I learned about another disease outbreak - this time at a facility in Eloy.

Yet instead of addressing these conditions, this Administration is marching full steam ahead to fuel its cruel mass-deportation agenda.

And there is another reason we should be deeply concerned about this particular facility: Management & Training Corporation, or MTC, has a long and documented history of serious problems at facilities it has operated.

Here in Arizona, that history includes allegations of sexual abuse that were not properly reported, chronic understaffing and inadequate training, major security failures, and destructive prison riots.

In 2010, three inmates escaped from an MTC-operated prison in Kingman due to serious security failures.

While on the run, two of the escapees brutally murdered an elderly couple in New Mexico, leading to a large wrongful death settlement between the state of Arizona and the victims’ family.

Five years later, after riots at the same prison, an investigation found a “culture of disorganization, disengagement, and disregard.”

Those aren’t my words. Those are the findings that led Republican Governor Doug Ducey to terminate the state’s contract with MTC.

In 2017, at an MTC-operated ICE Processing Center in New Mexico, the DHS Office of the Inspector General raised concerns about the treatment and care of detainees.

Two people detained there died after pleading for medical help from facility staff.

This is the company the federal government is entrusting with the lives of hundreds of people here in Marana.

And they are moving fast. MTC says it plans to have this facility up and running within 60 days of signing its contract with ICE.

Sixty days.

That should alarm every person in this community, especially when there are still so many unanswered questions.

First and foremost: How many people are actually going to be held here?

A document earlier this year suggested more than 1,300, but the contract MTC signed says up to 775. Both of these numbers are significantly above the 513-bed capacity the state prison previously operated under.

Regardless of what the final number is, one thing is abundantly clear: local residents do not want this facility.

La gente de Marana merece tener voz.

Since President Trump returned to office, at least 56 people have died in ICE custody, including four in Arizona.

And now the federal government has awarded MTC a contract with a potential value of more than $355 million to operate this facility.

That is a drop in the bucket of the nearly $261 BILLION Congress has approved for immigration enforcement under Trump.

Our communities are tired of our taxpayer dollars being wasted on these private detention centers to meet arbitrary deportation quotas.

We are tired of seeing private companies profit off Trump’s cruel and inhumane immigration agenda.

No queremos más dinero para compañías privadas

While the federal government operates in secrecy, local residents and their elected officials across the country are pushing back against these facilities, using zoning, public nuisance laws, and other means.

MTC’s history of poorly-run facilities, combined with the track-record of abuses at DHS, underscore the concerns of Marana residents.

Unfortunately, the responsibility of oversight has fallen on local governments because the federal government is willfully asleep at the wheel.

We will continue asking questions.

We will continue demanding accountability.

And we will continue fighting to ensure that the people of Marana have a voice in what happens in their own community.

Vamos a seguir luchando por nuestra comunidad.

Thank you. Muchas gracias.”

###

title: Grothman Announces $17.9 Million in FEMA Aid for Storm and Tornado Recovery
text:
Congressman Glenn Grothman (R-WI) welcomed President Donald Trump’s announcement of $17.9 million in federal disaster relief for Wisconsin communities affected by the July 27, 2026, storms in Forest, Outagamie, Vilas, and Winnebago counties.

“Thank you to President Trump for supporting Wisconsin’s recovery,” said Grothman. “I was proud to lead our bipartisan congressional delegation in urging federal support following the devastating July storms and tornado. Local officials, first responders, and community members have worked hard to help their communities recover, and federal assistance can help build on those efforts. I especially want to thank the volunteers who have given their time to help neighbors clean up and begin rebuilding. Their generosity reflects the best of Wisconsin.”

Residents with questions about federal disaster assistance or who need help working with FEMA or another federal agency are encouraged to contact Congressman Grothman’s Fond du Lac office at (920) 907-0624.

Background Information

The July 27, 2026, storms caused extensive damage across Forest, Outagamie, Vilas, and Winnebago counties. An EF3 tornado tore through the Fox Valley, causing widespread destruction in communities including Appleton and Menasha. It remained on the ground for more than 20 minutes, traveled approximately 12 miles, reached nearly one mile in width, and produced estimated winds of 136 to 165 miles per hour. More than 30,000 homes and businesses lost power.

Damage assessments conducted by FEMA and Wisconsin Emergency Management identified 2,346 residential structures affected, including 84 destroyed and 412 with major damage, with estimated losses exceeding $8.2 million. Public-sector damage exceeded $13.8 million, surpassing Wisconsin’s per-capita threshold by more than $2.4 million.

Congressman Grothman led two letters signed by every member of Wisconsin’s congressional delegation seeking federal support:

August 12: The delegation urged FEMA to work with Wisconsin Emergency Management on a Joint Preliminary Damage Assessment, an essential step toward determining eligibility for federal disaster assistance.

August 27: Following completion of those assessments, the delegation urged President Trump to approve a Major Disaster Declaration and make Individual Assistance, Public Assistance, and Hazard Mitigation assistance available.

title: Georgia's Congressional Democrats Push Back on State Board’s 'Unsubstantiated Claims' in DOJ Letter
text:
ATLANTA, GA — Today, four of the five members of the Georgia U.S. House of Representatives Democrat delegation and Rep. Joe Morelle of New York, the Ranking Member of the Committee on House Administration that oversees federal elections, sent a letter to the Georgia State Election Board pushing back on its Sept. 30 letter to the Department of Justice seeking their intervention in the state’s voting machines ahead of the November midterms elections, which are now in just 27 days.

“We are greatly alarmed by the mischaracterizations, and clear partisan motivations, that underlie the “Formal Request” letter you submitted to the U.S. Department of Justice on September 30, 2026. This letter, which plainly misstates the requirements of federal law — and which requests the Attorney General take action exceeding the power of the Department of Justice — is a clear attempt to sow public mistrust in the security of American elections. We demand that the Georgia State Election Board (“SEB”) clarify to the voters of Georgia that the tested and certified voting systems in use in the state, which have been used for three federal elections, are legal, secure, and safe.”

Read the full letter HERE and below.

Georgia State Election Board

2 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive SE

Floyd West Tower

Suite 324

Atlanta, Georgia 30334

Dear Mr. Mills:

We are greatly alarmed by the mischaracterizations, and clear partisan motivations, that underlie the “Formal Request” letter you submitted to the U.S. Department of Justice on September 30, 2026. This letter, which plainly misstates the requirements of federal law—and which requests the Attorney General take action exceeding the power of the Department of Justice—is a clear attempt to sow public mistrust in the security of American elections. We demand that the Georgia State Election Board (“SEB”) clarify to the voters of Georgia that the tested and certified voting systems in use in the state, which have been used for three federal elections, are legal, secure, and safe.

There is absolutely no ambiguity on this point: The voting system used by Georgia voters complies with state and federal law. Your unsubstantiated claim that Georgia’s voting system is “inconsistent” with the requirements of the Help America Vote Act (“HAVA”) is deeply troubling; one would expect that someone in your position would have some basic understanding of applicable federal election law. HAVA mandates that the United States Election Assistance Commission (“EAC”) “provide certification, decertification, and recertification of voting systems, as well as the accreditation of voting system testing laboratories.” The EAC also issues Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (“VVSG”), which cover “pre-voting, voting, and post-voting operations consistent with the definition of a voting system in HAVA Section 301(a).” And, as you should know, a state’s voting devices and software “must meet [VVSG specifications] in order to receive certification from the EAC.” Of course, Georgia’s voting system has undergone the EAC’s thorough testing process, as evidenced by the fact that the EAC has certified Georgia’s voting system, as required by Georgia’s statutory and regulatory regime.

The intent of your letter is clear—to serve as a pretext for undermining public confidence in Georgia’s election results this November. Americans should know that the State Election Board does not administer Georgia’s elections. That responsibility rests with the Secretary of State and the Secretary of State’s Elections Division. The SEB has important statutory oversight and rulemaking responsibilities, but those responsibilities should not be conflated with the actual administration and certification of Georgia elections. Nor should any erroneous SEB communication to the Department of Justice concerning Georgia’s elections be understood as anything more than partisan political actors’ attempt to justify future attempts to overturn a free and fair American election—an extraordinarily serious, and cynical, misuse of official communication.

Public confidence in elections depends in substantial part upon public officials communicating accurately, responsibly, and within the scope of their statutory authority—and without incompetently, or intentionally, mischaracterizing the law. Georgians have used the state’s voting system for three straight federal elections—elections won by both Republicans and Democrats. And Georgia has one of the most rigorous, robust post-election audit regimes in the country—this is how we know that Georgia’s elections are free, fair, and secure. You should therefore promptly clarify the record, correct any inaccurate characterization of HAVA or Georgia’s voting-system requirements, and make clear that Georgia’s elections are administered by the Secretary of State and conducted using voting systems that have satisfied the certification requirements established by state and federal law.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Reps. Joe Morelle (NY-25), Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Nikema Williams (GA-05), Everton Blair (GA-13).

###

title: Comisionado Residente solicita nuevas respuestas tras revisar documentos sobre contrato de generación temporera
text:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, solicitó nueva información y documentación sobre el proceso de adquisición y contratación de generación temporera adjudicado al consorcio encabezado por Power Expectations, LLC, tras identificar interrogantes en los documentos producidos al Congreso sobre la investigación y el manejo de alegaciones surgidas durante el proceso competitivo.

En una carta dirigida al Zar de Energía, Josué Colón Ortiz, y al presidente del Third Party Procurement Office (3PPO), Osvaldo Carlo Linares, el Comisionado Residente solicita información para esclarecer qué se investigó sobre la alegada firma no autorizada de Enchanted Rock, quién realizó esa revisión, con qué autoridad, y por qué transcurrieron casi más de siete semanas antes de referir el asunto a las autoridades competentes.

La gestión da seguimiento a una carta enviada por el Comisionado Residente el 3 de septiembre. Tras examinar los informes, referidos y comunicaciones producidos al Congreso, su oficina identificó que un informe de 3PPO del 8 de agosto describió una “revisión exhaustiva” de las alegaciones, mientras que una comunicación enviada al día siguiente indicó que la revisión se había limitado a evaluar la suficiencia de la documentación sometida durante el proceso competitivo.

“Desde nuestra primera solicitud hemos estado revisando cuidadosamente los documentos y siguiendo los hechos. La información que recibimos nos permitió avanzar, pero también levantó preguntas adicionales que ahora corresponde aclarar”, expresó el Comisionado Residente. “Queremos entender con precisión qué se revisó, qué se determinó y cómo se tomaron las decisiones durante este proceso.”

A partir de esa revisión, el Comisionado Residente identificó varias áreas que aún requieren aclaración y, en esta carta, busca precisar:

El propósito y alcance de la revisión realizada por 3PPO y qué asuntos permanecían sin resolver.

La cronología de las gestiones realizadas entre el 17 de junio y el 10 de agosto.

Qué información y hallazgos existían cuando el asunto fue referido al Departamento de Justicia de Puerto Rico y a las autoridades federales.

Cuándo fueron informadas la AEE y la Junta de Supervisión Fiscal, y cómo se tomaron las decisiones de informarles.

Las comunicaciones y documentos internos relacionados con la revisión y el manejo de las alegaciones.

La información deberá ser entregada no más tarde del 15 de octubre de 2026.

“Estamos dando seguimiento a lo que surge de los propios documentos y vamos a continuar procurando las respuestas que aún están pendientes”, concluyó el Comisionado Residente.

title: REP. HOYLE STATEMENT ON THIRD ANNIVERSARY OF OCTOBER 7TH
text:
Eugene, OR – Today, U.S. Representative Val Hoyle released the following statement on the third anniversary of the October 7th attack:

“It’s been 3 years since Hamas’ brutal terrorist attack on October 7. We cannot forget the 1,200 innocent people who were brutally murdered that day and the more than 250 hostages taken from their families. As the world grapples with these actions, we must continue speaking out against this horrific atrocity and call out the hate that has stemmed from it. Over 70,000 Palestinians have senselessly lost their lives—including a heartbreaking 20,000 children— and countless others have been displaced and left without access to food, water and medical care. How many more have to die before we have peace?

I continue to call on the Netanyahu government to end the violence in Gaza and the West Bank, for the Trump administration to bring the needless, immoral war in Iran to an end, and for our partners in the Gulf region to bring their considerable negotiating powers to the table to achieve freedom, security and self-determination for Israelis and Palestinians alike.”

title: LEADER JEFFRIES STATEMENT MARKING THREE YEARS SINCE THE TERRORIST ATTACK OF OCTOBER 7
text:
Today, to mark three years since Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, 2023, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries released the following statement:

Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists intent on destroying Israel launched an unthinkable massacre, murdering, kidnapping and sexually assaulting innocent Israeli civilians, as well as American citizens. We continue to mourn with the loved ones of those who were killed on that tragic day and stand with all still healing, including former hostages recovering from unimaginable horror.

As we solemnly commemorate October 7 and antisemitic attacks around the world surge, we are reminded of the painful reality that the Jewish people are in a constant struggle for survival, as has been the case for thousands of years. America must remain committed to Israel’s right to exist as a Jewish and democratic state, living in safety and security with its neighbors. We must permanently remove Hamas from power, eradicate terror and strive for a just and lasting peace in the region.

Throughout the past three years, considerable suffering has plagued the Middle East. The horrific death of Palestinian civilians, destruction of civil society and devastation in Gaza is reprehensible and can never be allowed to happen again.

In order to end the vicious cycle of bloodshed, for the good of the Israeli and Palestinian people, American policy in the region must change dramatically. We must commit to the creation of an independent Palestinian state to provide dignity, respect and self-determination for the Palestinian people. We must also support a new generation of Palestinian leaders and put an end to the egregious settler violence in the West Bank. Nothing short of a future that involves Israel and a Palestinian state living side by side in peace and prosperity is acceptable.

title: Brownley and Houchin Introduce National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month Resolution
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (D-CA) and Congresswoman Erin Houchin (R-IN) announced the introduction of a resolution recognizing October 2026 as National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month. Observed annually in October, National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month raises public awareness of learning disabilities, promotes early and accurate diagnoses, and highlights the importance of ensuring individuals have access to the resources, tools, and support they need to succeed in school, the workplace, and their communities.

“Having a learning disability should never stand in the way of a person’s ability to pursue their goals and achieve success,” said Congresswoman Brownley. “I began my career in public service to ensure that individuals like my daughter, who has dyslexia, have access to the resources and tools that empower them to learn and grow with confidence. I am grateful for Congresswoman Houchin’s partnership in recognizing National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month as we work to foster positive and supportive learning environments and improve learning outcomes and lived experiences for people with learning disabilities.”

“Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed, and that starts with the early identification of learning disabilities,” said Congresswoman Houchin. “Students who struggle quickly fall through the cracks of our education system. That’s why I am proud to recognize National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month alongside Congresswoman Brownley. We can, and should, do more to screen children as early as possible for learning challenges, like dyslexia, and this resolution brings awareness to the issue.”

This resolution is endorsed by the National Center for Learning Disabilities, a leading non-profit organization focused on building community, sharing resources, and shaping policy to help individuals with learning and attention issues.

The full text of the resolution can be found here.

title: Kamlager-Dove, Meeks Push State Department for Answers on Brazil
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Reps. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Co-Chair of the Congressional Brazil Caucus, and Gregory W. Meeks (NY-05), Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, led 10 Members of Congress in demanding answers from the State Department about its decision to revoke Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti’s diplomatic visa.

In their letter, the lawmakers condemned the decision as an unnecessary escalation that threatens U.S.-Brazil relations and undermines American interests in the Western Hemisphere. They emphasized Brazil’s importance as a major democracy and regional security and trading partner.

“This unnecessary escalation is the latest of a series of actions that has driven a rupture in our relationship with the largest democracy and economy in South America. At a time when the Trump Administration claims to be prioritizing the Western Hemisphere, this misguided decision further damages America’s reputation in the region and pushes Brazil closer to the hands of our adversaries,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers also criticized what they described as the Trump Administration’s sustained effort to influence Brazil’s 2026 elections. They cited State Department officials’ meetings with former President Bolsonaro, sanctions against Supreme Court Justice de Moraes, and statements questioning the integrity of Brazil’s elections as actions threatening the country’s democratic institutions and electoral processes.

“Congress therefore has an obligation to understand why the Department of State departed from established practices and took the extraordinary step to revoke the Brazilian Ambassador’s visa,” concluded the lawmakers.

The letter can be viewed in full here.

In addition to Reps. Kamlager-Dove and Ranking Member Meeks, the letter was signed by James P. McGovern, Pramila Jayapal, Nydia M. Velázquez, Jonathan L. Jackson, Sylvia R. Garcia, Dina Titus, Yvette D. Clarke, Mike Quigley, Jasmine Crockett, and Madeleine Dean.

title: Whip Clark, Markey, Warren, Massachusetts Delegation Members Statement on Massachusetts Nurses Negotiations
text:

Markey (D-Mass.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Representatives Richard Neal (MA-01), Jim McGovern (MA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), and Bill Keating (MA-09) released the following statement urging Mass General Brigham (MGB) and the Massachusetts Nurses Association (MNA) to continue their negotiations to avert a strike at Brigham and Women’s Hospital.

title: Kean Delivers $560,000 in Federal Funds to Mount Arlington for Memorial Pond Stormwater Dredging
text:
(October 7, 2026) MOUNT ARLINGTON, NJ – On Monday, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) presented $560,000 to Mount Arlington Borough to address stormwater drainage in the local community.

Mount Arlington’s Memorial Pond manages stormwater and acts as a basin before it enters Lake Hopatcong. Over time, the pond has filled up with sediment, and this federal funding will support a necessary dredging project.

“I am pleased to deliver this federal funding in order to protect the health and water quality of both Memorial Pond and Lake Hopatcong,” said Congressman Kean. “This $560,000 will fund a dredging project in Memorial Pond that will help ensure that Lake Hopatcong can continue being used by New Jerseyans for recreational activities.”

“Thanks to a $560,000 federal investment secured by Congressman Tom Kean, Jr., Mount Arlington can move forward with the engineering, environmental analysis and dredging needed to restore Memorial Pond, improve stormwater management and help protect the water quality of Lake Hopatcong,” said Mount Arlington Mayor Michael Stanzilis. “This funding will support the work necessary to restore the pond’s beauty and environmental health while strengthening the protection of this important regional natural resource.”

Mayor Stanzilis continued, “As Mayor, protecting our environment, and particularly Lake Hopatcong, has always been a priority. Memorial Pond is a beautiful and special part of our community, and I look forward to seeing it restored for future generations. I thank Congressman Kean for recognizing the importance of this project and for his continued partnership with Mount Arlington.”

“With this money, Memorial Pond can be cleaned for the use and benefit of all residents,” said State Senator Anthony Bucco. “When this pond is cleaned and dredged, it will have a direct impact on making sure that Lake Hopatcong continues to have the quality of water that this area needs for recreation and the economy. The residents of Mount Arlington are winners today as a result of the work of Congressman Kean.”

“Congressman Kean reminds us that no project or town is too small,” said Assemblywoman Aura Dunn. “This was needed funding for a project that could not have otherwise happened. We thank Congressman Kean for his leadership down in Washington and for making sure they all remember how important Mount Arlington is.”

“Congressman Kean’s work to secure this grant for a small town like Mount Arlington will not only impact this park, but also everything downstream,” said Morris County Commissioner Tayfun Selen. “Morris County and Sussex County share Lake Hopatcong, and what is being done to improve a tiny pond and the environment of this small community, will flow downstream to improve the quality of life for an entire region.”

“What enters Memorial Pond doesn't stay in Memorial Pond, eventually it all flows straight into Lake Hopatcong,” said Kyle Richter, Executive Director of the Lake Hopatcong Foundation. “Removing years of built-up sediment means fewer nutrients feeding harmful algal blooms, cleaner water at our beaches, and a healthier future for New Jersey's largest lake. We're grateful to Congressman Kean Jr. for securing the funding for this critical project and helping to protect and improve Lake Hopatcong.”

Since taking office, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. has secured more than $14.5 million for water infrastructure in New Jersey’s Seventh Congressional District through the Community Project Funding process.

All 15 projects that Congressman Kean won for NJ-07 through the FY2026 Community Project Funding process are now law. View the full list of projects HERE.

title: National Archives Issues Dismissive Response to Lawmakers & Community Concerns
text:
SAN BRUNO, CA –Despite bipartisan and bicameral support for preserving America’s national archives, the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) gave a dismissive response to federal lawmakers who are working to protect local public access to historic records.

Before providing any justification or opportunities for the public to weigh in, NARA recently announced it would be closing its San Bruno and Chicago facilities, which are two of just 13 regional archives across America. Over one hundred community advocates, researchers, genealogists, and local families gathered at a rally and press conference Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15) hosted in August to emphasize the importance of retaining culturally and historically significant records in the Bay Area.

U.S. Reps. Mullin and Judy Chu (CA-28) led a bipartisan coalition of 37 federal lawmakers in writing to NARA in August to urge it to reconsider the San Bruno closure, and requesting more information about its plans and rationale. In its response letter, NARA failed to fully acknowledge concerns about the public losing physical access to local archival records, or a 2009 agreement to keep regionally-sensitive immigration files in San Bruno. NARA also did not explain how it made decisions about where to transfer non-immigration related files, and provided no insight into how the fragile 100+ year-old records would be cared for while moved across the country.

NARA didn’t definitively answer questions about the future of its local workforce, many of whom are experts in their field. While it cited an estimated $4.7 million in annual savings by shuttering the building, it didn’t justify the need to find such savings – which is less than the taxpayer funding President Trump wants to spend on renovating his living quarters at the White House this fiscal year alone.

The national archives in San Bruno house records from not only California but also Nevada, Hawaii, Pacific Island territories, and Tribes. These records hold deep value to the local community including Angel Island immigration files, Chinese Exclusion Act and Japanese Internment records, Native American and indigenous history documents, and even the notable Wong Kim Ark files, on which the recent birthright citizenship case at the Supreme Court hinged. NARA said it plans to move the immigration files to Kansas City – suggesting it expects Bay Area community members who deeply care about their ancestors’ records to travel over 1,500 miles if they want see them in person.

In August, Rep. Mullin also introduced the National Archives Protection Act, which is co-authored by Reps. Chu; Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), whose district includes the Seattle archives; and Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), whose district includes the Chicago archives. The bill would prevent NARA from closing any of its facilities including archives, records centers, and research rooms, without Congressional approval. Following the House bill, a Senate companion version was introduced on Sept. 30 by Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), along with U.S. Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Alex Padilla (D-CA), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

After facing community pushback – and months after quietly notifying congressional offices of its plans – NARA announced it would host two virtual listening sessions for Tribal Nations on Oct. 13 and 15. Reps. Mullin and Chu encourage all Tribal members interested in joining to visit NARA’s website for instructions on signing up for a listening session at www.archives.gov/research/news. Reps. Mullin and Chu are urging NARA to conduct more public input sessions and engage with additional stakeholders who have an interest in maintaining the physical archives within the communities they represent.

“NARA’s response to federal lawmakers is extremely disappointing and dismissive toward the sincere concerns from the public about losing direct access to irreplaceable community and family records. These archives aren’t just boxes of paper — they hold the stories, memories, and history of generations of Americans. Families whose ancestors immigrated through Angel Island can track their lineage, those whose loved ones served in the Navy and were stationed in the Pacific can learn about their legacy, and Native Americans whose history is documented over generations are all able to learn more by visiting this national archive,” said Rep. Mullin. “NARA has a responsibility to ensure these tangible records are carefully preserved and accessible to the people they represent. I will continue to fight against these closures and encourage everyone – from federal lawmakers and Tribal leaders, to community advocates and researchers – to keep up the pressure and consider all legal means to protect these historic resources.”

“NARA’s response falls far short of addressing the real concerns of the communities who rely on these archives,” said Rep. Judy Chu. “For all Californians, and particularly the AANHPI community, these records are more than files and boxes. They tell the stories of families who endured the Chinese Exclusion Act and the incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II, and they are where descendants go to learn what their loved ones lived through. Moving these records across the country would force families to travel thousands of miles and spend significant time and money simply to access their own American history. NARA has offered no convincing reason to put that history out of reach, and it has a responsibility to protect these records and keep them accessible to the communities they belong to. We will keep fighting the closures of the San Francisco and San Bruno facilities, and we will not let up until these irreplaceable pieces of AANHPI history are kept with the communities whose stories they tell.”

The letter regarding the San Bruno archives was signed by U.S. Reps. Mark Amodei (NV-02), Ami Bera (CA-06), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Ed Case (HI-01), Judy Chu (CA-28), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), , Laura Friedman (CA-30), John Garamendi (CA-08), Jesús García (IL-04), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Steven Horsford (NV-04), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Susie Lee (NV-03), Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Doris Matsui (CA-17), Grace Meng (NY-06), Dave Min (CA-47), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Brad Sherman (CA-32), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-29), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Dina Titus (NV-01), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Norma Torres (CA-35), Maxine Waters (CA-43); and Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam B. Schiff (D-CA), Jacklyn Rosen (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL).

title: LaHood Urges President Trump to Issue Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for Continued Recovery Efforts from August Storms
text:
Washington, D.C. – Yesterday, Congressman Darin LaHood (IL-16) sent a letter to President Donald Trump encouraging him to issue a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for McLean, Tazewell, Ford, Champaign, Cook, Fulton, Vermilion, and Will Counties following severe storms that caused significant wind damage and flooding in August.

In the letter, LaHood writes:

"I am writing in support of the State of Illinois’ request for a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for Champaign, Cook, Ford, Fulton, McLean, Tazewell, Vermilion, and Will Counties following severe storms that impacted Illinois from August 11-16, 2026. The storms caused widespread damage across Central and Northern Illinois, and I urge your Administration to provide these communities with the federal assistance they need to recover and rebuild.

Beginning on August 11, a multi-day severe weather event brought multiple rounds of severe storms, tornadoes, powerful winds, and flooding to the affected counties. In McLean County, which I represent, the impact has been substantial. Severe winds and storms left behind fallen trees and power lines, flooding, and significant property damage. The Normal Fire Department responded to a record number of calls during a 24-hour shift, stretching emergency services across the area to their limits. In Bloomington alone, crews have hauled away more than 2,300 loads of brush and 500 tons of bulk waste in the weeks since the storm. Across McLean County, local officials have reported approximately $42.5 million in damage.

A Major Disaster Declaration would give these communities the federal resources needed to recover, repair damaged infrastructure, and rebuild. I support the State’s request for FEMA assistance, including Individual Assistance, Public Assistance, and Hazard Mitigation, as well as the request for an SBA disaster declaration to help eligible residents, small businesses, and nonprofits recover from the damage and disruption caused by these storms.

I have been impressed by the response of local leaders, first responders, and residents who stepped up to help their communities in the aftermath of these storms. However, the scale of the damage and the continued demands of recovery demonstrate that local and state resources alone are not enough. These communities have done their part, and now we need to make sure the federal government lends a hand.

Disaster recovery requires cooperation at every level of government. I respectfully urge you to approve the State of Illinois’ request and ensure that the people of McLean County and the other affected Illinois communities have access to the federal resources they need to recover. I appreciate your consideration of this important request and stand ready to work with your Administration to support the communities impacted by these devastating storms."

The full letter can be read here.

This follows up on a letter sent by the entire Illinois delegation sent in September.

title: Larsen: New B.C. Oil Pipeline is “Not Ready for Prime Time”
text:
Last Friday, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) commented on the news that Canada is fast-tracking a new oil pipeline project that would increase oil tanker traffic in Larsen’s district:

“This project is not ready for prime time, and speeding up the review process will only make that worse,” said Rep. Larsen in the Washington State Standard. “Canada’s plan to fast track this new oil pipeline project puts sensitive marine habitats at risk and raises the chance of a devastating spill occurring before the U.S. and Canada can put updated plans in place.”

On July 2, the Government of Alberta announced a proposed new oil pipeline from Alberta to the Pacific Ocean that would transport 1 million barrels per day to an export terminal at Roberts Banks in British Columbia. Last Thursday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney designated the pipeline, now known as the Pacific Link, as a project of national interest, enabling a speedier regulatory review that could see pipeline design and construction underway by next fall. The new pipeline will increase tanker traffic in Haro Strait and Boundary Bay in the Salish Sea, and with it the risks for catastrophic oil spills impacting sensitive marine environments.

“The people I represent have serious concerns about this new pipeline and how it could harm the Salish Sea,” continued Rep. Larsen. “They deserve answers to their questions and updated spill response plans that account for more oil tanker traffic, and I will keep fighting to get them both."

Last month, Rep. Larsen’s staff observed a joint exercise between the U.S. Coast Guard and the Canadian Coast Guard designed to simulate response efforts and coordination between the two countries in the event of an oil spill in shared waters.

“This type of collaboration across the border between the U.S. and Canada is even more critical because of Canada’s plans to ship more oil in the Salish Sea with the proposed new Alberta to B.C. pipeline,” said Rep. Larsen. “I have concerns about the potential impacts of this proposed pipeline, including on tanker traffic in the Salish Sea, and I am glad that my staff could observe the exercise to ensure that there are relationships and procedures in place that benefit both countries in the event of a disastrous spill.”

Rep. Larsen is the top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, which has oversight authority over the U.S. Coast Guard. In July, Rep. Larsen sent a letter to Admiral Kevin E. Lunday, Commandant of the Coast Guard, to insist that the Coast Guard review and update its oil spill preparedness plans in light of the new proposed pipeline. Larsen also pressed Coast Guard officials on their awareness of the new Canadian pipeline and how it would implicate existing oil spill prevention plans at a committee hearing. A video clip from that hearing can be found here, and the recording of the entire roundtable can be found here.

The Washington State Standard article is available here and below.

A proposed Canadian oil pipeline to a supertanker terminal at the Port of Vancouver in British Columbia is raising hackles among Washington state’s political leaders.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday designated the West Coast Oil Pipeline, now known as the Pacific Link, as a project of national interest. That enables a speedier regulatory review that could see pipeline design and construction under way by next fall.

In response, Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson on Friday sounded alarms about increased oil spill risk to the Salish Sea in his first public comments on the massive project.

The Carney announcement wasn’t a surprise. In July, the prime minister and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith talked of fast-tracking the proposed 775-mile pipeline capable of carrying one million barrels of crude oil a day.

It would run from the Edmonton region to a new export terminal capable of handling supertankers proposed for Port of Vancouver’s Roberts Bank in British Columbia just north of the U.S. border. Oil could flow through by the early 2030s.

Once operating, many more oil-filled vessels traveling from the port would pass by the San Juan Islands and Olympic Peninsula on their way to Asia. Project critics fear a spill could easily reach north Puget Sound, the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Washington’s outer coast, threatening sensitive ecosystems and killer whale habitat.

Ferguson said Friday that he was “disappointed” at the decision because resources needed to respond to a major spill are insufficient today.

“If a project of this scale is going to proceed, it needs to come with a corresponding commitment to also increase our region’s capacity to prevent and respond to a catastrophic spill,” he said in a joint statement with Casey Sixkiller, director of the state Department of Ecology.

Ferguson said the size of the oil supertankers envisioned for the route are unprecedented, and have been barred from Washington ports since the 1970s. Their capacity of 92 million gallons of oil is eight times the volume of oil spilled by the Exxon Valdez, he noted.

“If this project proceeds, it is critical that the Canadian government make detailed commitments to safeguard our shared marine waters and fill these gaps in our response capabilities,” he and Sixkiller said in the statement.

San Juan County council members, northern Washington tribal representatives and others have been pushing Ferguson since July to speak out and engage with the Canadian provincial and federal governments about the crude pipeline and tanker traffic.

On Tuesday, Ferguson met with Mark Wiseman, Canada’s ambassador to the U.S. in Seattle. It is not known if the two discussed the pipeline and Ferguson’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the meeting.

Sixkiller dispatched a lengthy letter to Canadian Intergovernmental Affairs Minister Dominic LeBlanc in mid-September in a vain bid to forestall the fast-tracking of the Alberta pipeline permitting.

U.S. Rep. Rick Larsen of Everett, whose 2nd Congressional District includes the state waters through which the supertankers would travel, was equally vexed. Many questions about the project and oil spill response need answers, he said.

“This project is not ready for prime time, and speeding up the review process will only make that worse,” he said in an email. “Canada’s plan to fast track this new oil pipeline project puts sensitive marine habitats at risk and raises the chance of a devastating spill occurring before the U.S. and Canada can put updated plans in place.”

The project comes as Canada looks to strengthen its economic ties beyond the U.S. and as Carney has said the nation is seeking to become an “energy superpower.”

Smith has said the province chose a southern pipeline route that ends on the shores of the Salish Sea because it can take advantage of the existing Trans Mountain Pipeline corridor as well as established relationships with First Nations.

“It would be reasonable to expect that a project with the potential to shape the environmental, economic, and social future of a region for decades to come would face an especially rigorous level of scrutiny. Instead, this project is being fast-tracked without any concern for its long-term impacts on ecosystems, communities and the people who depend on them,” she wrote in an update to supporters Friday.

title: Chairman Lawler Remembers October 7 Attacks, Reaffirms Commitment to Jewish Security and Israel
text:
Pearl River, N.Y. – 10/7/26… Today, Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17), Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa, released the following statement marking the anniversary of the October 7, 2023 terrorist attacks against Israel:

“Three years ago today, the world witnessed the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust. Hamas terrorists murdered more than 1,000 people, committed horrific acts of sexual violence, and took hundreds hostage, including American citizens. I will never forget what I saw when I traveled to Israel shortly after the attack. I met with families whose loved ones had been murdered or taken hostage, spoke with Israeli officials, and saw firsthand the brutality Hamas unleashed on innocent civilians. The barbarity of October 7 must never be forgotten, minimized, or justified,” said Congressman Lawler.

“The rise in antisemitism we have witnessed in the United States since that day has made clear that Jewish Americans are under threat. No one should have to fear going to synagogue, sending their children to school, or openly practicing their faith. Three years later, our commitment must remain unwavering. We must fully disarm and dismantle Hamas. We must stand with Israel. And we must ensure that never again is not simply a slogan, but a commitment we live by every single day,” concluded Congressman Lawler.

Since October 7, Lawler has made combating antisemitism, strengthening Jewish security, and supporting Israel a central focus of his work in Congress. This agenda has included:

Leading the bipartisan Antisemitism Awareness Act: Lawler was the lead House sponsor of the bipartisan legislation with Rep. Calling for the release of all hostages: Lawler has consistently demanded that Hamas release every remaining hostage and has made clear that lasting peace requires Hamas to surrender and no longer pose a threat to Israel.

Calling out antisemitism across the political spectrum: Lawler has repeatedly said antisemitism must be confronted regardless of where it comes from, including publicly criticizing prominent voices on both the political right and left.

Fighting for Jewish Americans’ right to live without fear: Lawler has warned that Jewish Americans are under attack and has emphasized that no American should be afraid to attend synagogue or openly practice their faith.

As Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa, Lawler has continued to make Israel’s security, the defeat of Hamas, the release of hostages, and the fight against antisemitism central priorities of his work in Congress.

title: Rep. Mike Levin Pushes Administration to Adopt Critical Reforms to Improve Access to SNAP Benefits for Veterans
text:
Washington, D.C.—Today, Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) applauded a new Government Accountability Office (GAO) report outlining recommendations to improve veterans’ access to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). In January 2024, Rep. Levin served as the Ranking Member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity with Chair Derrick Van Orden (WI-03) and requested GAO to examine how states with reported high and low rates of food insecurity have targeted veterans in the state annual outreach plans. On October 1, 2026, GAO published the report, “Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Federal Actions Needed to Help Veterans Access Benefits,” which highlights the importance of conducting veteran-specific SNAP outreach to increase awareness and use of food resources.

According to a 2023 RAND report, more than one million veterans faced food insecurity each year from 2015 to 2020. Eligible veterans can use SNAP benefits to access healthy foods, but they’re less likely to participate than non-veterans. In the report, GAO reviewed states’ efforts to target SNAP outreach to veterans and work with veterans’ organizations to help connect veterans to the program. GAO also examined state and federal efforts to improve the type of SNAP outreach conducted to veterans. The report makes four recommendations for the Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to more effectively tackle veteran food insecurity.

“More than one million veterans face food insecurity in this country. That is one million too many. That is why, when I served as Ranking Member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity, I asked GAO to investigate how states and the federal government can better help veterans get the support they need. I am encouraged by the report’s findings on successful state outreach efforts, but I am deeply troubled that USDA has still not updated its website to inform veterans about new requirements that could result in them losing their benefits,” said Rep. Levin. “One of the many reasons I opposed H.R. 1 was because it eliminated the work requirement exemption for veterans and created additional barriers to accessing food assistance. I am also concerned that, following staffing cuts in 2025, USDA has failed to fill critical positions that support coordination with the Department of Veterans Affairs on veteran hunger. That is unacceptable. USDA must take these findings seriously and act quickly to address the gaps identified by GAO. I plan to work with my colleagues to hold the Administration accountable for implementing GAO’s recommendations as quickly as possible and ensuring veterans can access the support they have earned.”

GAO made three recommendations to USDA and one to VA, including:

The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure Food and Nutrition Administration’s (FNA) SNAP eligibility website includes up-to-date information about exceptions to the SNAP time limit.

The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure FNA develops and disseminates additional SNAP outreach materials tailored to veterans, in collaboration with Veterans Health Administration (VHA).

The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure a formal mechanism is in place to collaborate with VA on efforts to address veteran food insecurity. This could include reviewing the memorandum of agreement (MOA) and updating the agreement as needed.

The Secretary of Veterans Affairs should ensure a formal mechanism is in place to collaborate with VA on efforts to address veteran food insecurity. This could include reviewing the MOA and updating the agreement as needed.

Rep. Levin will continue working with the relevant federal agencies to ensure they implement GAO’s recommendations and address reducing barriers for veterans seeking access to SNAP.

title: Maryland Delegation Members Push for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives April McClain Delaney, Steny Hoyer, Sarah Elfreth, Kweisi Mfume, Jamie Raskin, Glenn Ivey, and Johnny Olszewski were joined by Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) in requesting $11 million for U.S. Cyber Command as Congress works to complete the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense appropriations. In the letter to Appropriations Committee leadership, the lawmakers stressed the importance of the health and wellbeing of the service members and civilian employees of U.S. Cyber Command, as well as the importance of their work to our national security. The $11 million program increase would fund U.S. Cyber Command’s high-performance team training, an operation aimed at improving care for service members, including helping commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, care, and resilience practices.

The lawmakers begin, “We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training under Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations, as Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act. Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent military operations missions.”

“As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear,” they continue.

On the need for funding for High Performance Team Training at Cyber Command, the lawmakers note, “The requested $11 million would help U.S. Cyber Command close this gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Embedded support would improve access to care for service members inside secure facilities, give providers a better understanding of the mission and its operational tempo, identify concerns earlier, and help commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, and resilience practices. Models used in other high-demand military communities, including special operations and remotely piloted aircraft units, and dedicated intelligence commands demonstrate the value of treating psychological health and human performance as readiness requirements. Cyber Command noted that without this funding, burnout and force degradation will increase.”

“Preserving this funding would demonstrate Congress’s commitment to the health and readiness of the cyber workforce at Fort Meade, Maryland, and across the Nation. It would also help ensure that the Department establishes an enduring system of prevention, care, and operational resilience rather than relying solely on short-term interventions following a tragedy. One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again. We appreciate your continued leadership and support of Maryland’s servicemembers, federal employees, and families,” the lawmakers conclude.

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Chairman Cole, Ranking Member DeLauro, Chair Collins, and Vice Chair Murray:

We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training under Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations, as Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act. Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions.

As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear.

Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many are effectively “deployed in place” for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unit-level reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments. Because much of their work is classified, they may be unable to discuss the sources of their stress with family members or medical professionals who lack the clearances or access to secure facilities necessary for a complete conversation. These conditions can isolate personnel, delay appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness.

These challenges are particularly relevant at Fort Meade, where U.S. Cyber Command, the National Security Agency, military cyber components, and other national security organizations operate within a highly secure and interconnected environment. Although Maryland has a significant network of military, federal, and civilian health resources, traditional centralized-care models do not always give cyber personnel timely access to appropriately cleared professionals in the facilities where they work.

Congress and the Department have already recognized this gap. Congress previously directed a review of the psychological and occupational demands placed on cyber operators, and the Department subsequently acknowledged that existing resources did not fully meet the needs of the U.S. Cyber Command. The Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) also expanded mental health services intended to address the U.S. Cyber Command’s unique requirements by integrating behavioral health professionals with security clearances within cyber units. Nevertheless, dedicated support teams and embedded care have not been implemented consistently across the force.

The requested $11 million would help U.S. Cyber Command close this gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Embedded support would improve access to care for service members inside secure facilities, give providers a better understanding of the mission and its operational tempo, identify concerns earlier, and help commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, and resilience practices. Models used in other high-demand military communities, including special operations and remotely piloted aircraft units, and dedicated intelligence commands demonstrate the value of treating psychological health and human performance as readiness requirements. Cyber Command noted that without this funding, burnout and force degradation will increase.

This represents a modest investment compared with U.S. Cyber Command’s broader annual budget and the strategic value of its highly trained workforce. Recruiting, clearing, and developing cyber operators takes years. Losing experienced personnel harms Maryland families, disrupts operational teams, increases replacement and training costs, and reduces the Nation’s ability to defend critical systems and conduct cyber missions.

Accordingly, we respectfully request that the final Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act retain the following program increase:

12D CYBERSPACE OPERATIONS

High Performance Team Training ........................................ $11,000,000

Preserving this funding would demonstrate Congress’s commitment to the health and readiness of the cyber workforce at Fort Meade, Maryland, and across the Nation. It would also help ensure that the Department establishes an enduring system of prevention, care, and operational resilience rather than relying solely on short-term interventions following a tragedy. One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again.

We appreciate your continued leadership and support of Maryland’s servicemembers, federal employees, and families.

title: STATEMENT: Rep. Dave Min on the Three-Year Anniversary of October 7th Attack
text:
Rep. Dave Min issued the following statement, marking the three-year anniversary of the Oct 7th attack:

"Three years ago today, Israel suffered the worst terrorist attack in its history. The barbaric and horrific murder of 1200 Israelis with hundreds more taken into captivity shocked decent people across the world.

My thoughts continue to remain with the families and loved ones of those victims and also with those who are experiencing antisemitism here at home. I also mourn the Palestinian civilians who have been killed in Gaza, including tens of thousands of children.

I pray for peace and a stop to the violence in the Middle East, and as a member of Congress, I will continue to do all I can to try to achieve that goal."

title: “DON’T MESS WITH NEW YORK”: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND NEW YORK DELEGATION INTRODUCE BICAMERAL LEGISLATION TO REVERSE TRUMP’S DEVASTATING CUTS TO HEALTHCARE AND RESTORE COVERAGE FOR 450,000 NEW YORKERS
text:
Congressman Pat Ryan and the entire New York Democratic Delegation introduced legislation to reverse the Republican cuts to health care and restore coverage for 450,000 New Yorkers.

In NY-18, 15,656 Essential Plan enrollees were impacted by cuts to health care funding in Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, Congressman Pat Ryan joined the entire New York Democratic delegation in introducing the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act, legislation to restore health coverage to the nearly 450,000 New Yorkers who were kicked off of the Essential Plan under the Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act. In NY-18, 15,656 Essential Plan enrollees were impacted.

Specifically, the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act would repeal the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s premium tax credit eligibility restrictions, fully restoring funding for the Essential Plan. In addition to restoring the program, the legislation would provide all states with the option to expand health coverage through the Affordable Care Act’s Basic Health Plan.

“For over a year now, we’ve felt the devastating consequences of Trump and Republicans’ health care cuts right here in the Hudson Valley. Trump and spineless rubber-stamp Republicans in Congress cut $1 trillion from your health care and food assistance to fund a tax cut for billionaires – and they specifically targeted New York’s Essential Plan, ripping healthcare from more than 15,000 people in our district,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “It’s cruel, un-American, and the exact opposite of everything our community stands for. On behalf of the 450,000 New Yorkers kicked off their insurance, we’re fighting back. I’m incredibly proud to join our entire state Democratic delegation in introducing this legislation to reverse the cuts, restore your coverage, and send a clear message to Trump: Don’t mess with New York.”

Congressman Ryan was an early, strong critic of President Trump domestic spending agenda – calling it a “Big, Ugly Betrayal” of the American people. Trump’s agenda rips health care coverage away from more than 17 million Americans, has caused a massive hike in insurance premiums for millions, and has already closed, significantly reduced services, or forced mass layoffs at countless hospitals nationwide. 77% of respondents to Ryan’s survey on ACA premiums said they’d already received notice their bills would increase.

This legislation is cosponsored by the entire New York Democratic delegation including: Senators Schumer (D-NY) and Gillibrand (D-NY), Leader Jeffries (NY-08), and Representatives Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Clarke (NY-09), Espaillat (NY-13), Gillen (NY-04), Goldman (NY-10), Kennedy (NY-26), Latimer (NY-16), Mannion (NY-22), Meeks (NY-5), Meng (NY-6), Morelle (NY-25), Nadler (NY-12), Riley (NY-19), Ryan (NY-18), Suozzi (NY-3), Tonko (NY-20), Torres (NY-15), and Velázquez (NY-07).

title: ICYMI: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN HOSTS HUDSON VALLEY RESTAURANT OWNERS FOR DISCUSSION ON RISING COSTS & IMPACTS OF PROPOSED SYSCO-RESTAURANT DEPOT MERGER
text:
Mid Hudson News: Ryan and restaurant owners dish on Sysco at diner

Ryan hosted Hudson Valley restaurant owners, caterers, and small food distributors to discuss how corporate consolidation is raising prices and making it harder to run their small businesses

The discussion comes after Ryan called on FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson to block the proposed $29.1 billion merger between Sysco and Restaurant Depot, arguing the merger would reduce competition, drive up operating costs for restaurants, and make dining out more expensive

NEWBURGH, NY – Yesterday, Congressman Pat Ryan – co-chair of the Congressional Monopoly Busters Caucus – hosted a roundtable conversation at Alexis Diner with Hudson Valley restaurant owners, caterers, and small food distributors to discuss how corporate consolidation is raising prices and making it harder to run their small businesses.

Participants discussed how the proposed merger between Sysco and Restaurant Depot – two of the largest suppliers Hudson Valley independent restaurants rely on – would bring a dramatic, negative impact to their businesses.

The conversation followed a letter Ryan sent to Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Chairman Andrew Ferguson last week, demanding the FTC block the proposed $29.1 billion merger and raising the alarm on how it would reduce competition, drive up operating costs for restaurants, and make dining out in the Hudson Valley more expensive.

“When the largest food distributor in the country seeks to acquire one of its biggest competitors, it’s all of us – our small restaurant and diner owners, food truck operators, caterers, and customers – who will be forced to pay the higher price,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “Hudson Valley restaurants are part of what makes our community so special. We should be making it easier, not harder, for them to succeed. Keeping prices competitive is essential to the success of these restaurants, which is why we’re going to fight with everything we’ve got to make sure the FTC blocks this harmful deal and protects the independent businesses that keep our Hudson Valley communities thriving.”

“We're grateful that Congressman Ryan is standing with independent restaurants and bars by urging the FTC to fully investigate the proposed merger between Sysco and Restaurant Depot,” said Erika Polmar, Executive Director of the Independent Restaurant Coalition. “Restaurants already operate on margins of just 3 to 5 percent, and when one company controls more of the food supply chain, owners lose bargaining power and are left with higher prices, fewer options and lousy terms, costs that either land on the menu or eat into already meager margins. Restaurants are New York's second-largest private employer, and letting Sysco absorb the supplier independents rely on most would threaten the neighborhood businesses that anchor communities across the state.”

Read more:

Mid Hudson News: Ryan and restaurant owners dish on Sysco at diner

By Jeanine Agnolet

TOWN OF NEWBURGH – A handful of small, independent restaurant owners, food educators, chefs and a farmer sat around a table at the Alexis Diner in Newburgh on Monday to express their concerns to Congressman Pat Ryan (D, NY -18) about the proposed merger of the food industry giant Sysco Corporation and Restaurant Depot.

Above the frenetic sounds of a hectic lunch crowd with plenty of hot coffee, they candidly described what they said was the disaster that will strike if Sysco is successful in acquiring Restaurant Depot, which has a warehouse in the Town of Newburgh.

“The merger will drive the food prices up, and it will drive small restaurants right out of business,” said Tom Costa, chef and owner of North Plank Road Tavern in the Town of Newburgh and an active member of the Independent Restaurant Coalition. “Right now, I can run out to Restaurant Depot, and I can get three pounds of Faroe Island salmon, but if I have to order a case of it from Sysco, I risk losing some of it before I actually sell it. Restaurant Depot is a godsend for the small, independent restaurant, which is a dying breed.”

Congressman Ryan held the roundtable discussion to get feedback from local restaurant owners and food service providers.

Last Friday, Ryan, who co-chairs the Congressional Monopoly Busters Caucus, sent a letter to Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, urging him to block the proposed $29.1 billion merger.

Ryan says the appeal to prevent the acquisition has bipartisan support.

“I cannot overstate how big of a deal this is as one of the biggest mergers in this country in the past decade,” said Ryan. “At a time when costs are already exorbitantly high, this is incredibly problematic.”

Ryan said there are nearly 2,000 food service and accommodation businesses in his district, most of them with less than 20 employees.

“There are over 30 thousand food workers in these three counties—a huge source of employment across our communities, so this affects everyone,” said Ryan.

Sysco is the single biggest distributor of food in the nation, serving over 700,000 customers globally, including schools, hospital systems and other organizations that have high volume.

Earlier this year, it announced plans to purchase Restaurant Depot, one of the nation’s largest food wholesale cash-and-carry warehouse companies, that sells to independent restaurant owners, caterers and non-profits.

Restaurant owners contend the proposed merger would reduce competition, drive up operating costs and make dining out more expensive.

Rei Peraza, director of Operations and Executive Chef for Rossi & Sons, prides himself on the fact that he has never utilized Sysco.

“Sysco has an algorithmic pricing system. The more you buy, the better your pricing is, and that’s why it doesn’t work for a lot of small, mom and pop operations. I don’t think Sysco and the way they do business has ever been good for small businesses,” said Peraza.

With Sysco, the identities of restaurants get lost. You’re using the same chicken fingers and the same toilet paper as everyone else. As a whole, they have very little to offer in quality products outside of convenience.”

In 2013, Sysco attempted to acquire US Foods, but the Federal Trade Commission sued to block the merger and won.

Assemblyman Jonathan Jacobsen says he intends draft a letter to State Attorney General Letitia James, urging her to take action and enforce the current laws that prohibit monopolistic practices.

“It’s wrong in the insurance, healthcare and pharmaceutical industries, and it’s wrong here,” said Jacobsen.

“With this merger, we’ll be out priced, and this will be catastrophic,” said Gaby Pereyra, owner of Yara Farm in Middletown, New York and director of Operations for the Chester Agricultural Center. “It would be impossible for small farmers to be able to sell to small restaurants or suppliers.”

Ryan says he is hopeful that the merger can still be stopped, despite the fact that negotiations are in the final stages.

“Sysco has a pricing structure based on volume,” said Tom Costa. “It may be smart but it’s going to kill the little guy.”

Ryan’s letter to FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson is included in full below, and can be viewed here.

Dear Chairman Ferguson,

I am writing to urge the Federal Trade Commission to conduct a rigorous review of Sysco Corporation's proposed acquisition of Restaurant Depot, and to formally oppose the merger unless substantial evidence is shown that the merger will not lessen competition in the markets on which independent restaurants and small food service operators rely. This issue is of personal interest as many of my constituents rely on the Restaurant Depot Warehouse located in my district in Newburgh, New York. In addition, as independent restaurants are forced to raise prices, those high prices are either absorbed, decreasing profits, or passed along to consumers. My constituents are already drowning in skyrocketing prices, and this acquisition will only make it more difficult both for small businesses working hard to make a living and for customers trying to afford the basics, like a warm meal from a local restaurant.

Restaurant Depot exerts indirect but consequential competitive pressure on Sysco by serving as an outside option for independent, price-sensitive operators who want to avoid rising delivery fees. Independent restaurant operators, including the 30,000 restaurant workers in my district, depend on low-cost product sourcing to operate. While Sysco has defended the acquisition, characterizing the two companies as possessing “minimal overlap” in customers, the truth is that this acquisition would establish Sysco’s total control over two unique channels of distribution that independent restaurants have historically used as substitutes for each other.

This acquisition would make Sysco the largest player in the cash-and-carry market, on top of its existing leadership in the broadline distribution market. This consolidation of market power will have severe and devastating consequences for independent restaurants, food service operators, and other small businesses who rely on competitive markets to keep prices low for their customers. With folks feeling intense financial pressure across the board right now, we should be working together to bring down costs, instead of fueling high prices. I’ll continue to stay in close contact with local businesses negatively impacted by rising prices and help them fight for fair practices.

As you look into the details of the merger, I urge the Federal Trade Commission to closely review the potential impact on the food service industry, including the small businesses and consumers who patronize our beloved independent restaurants.

On behalf of the hardworking independent restaurants and constituents who would be impacted by this merger in my district and around the nation, I urge the Commission to investigate this matter and take decisive action to protect competition, consumers, and small businesses.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
