title: What They’re Saying: Bipartisan Permitting Reform Will Deliver Cheaper Energy, More Jobs, Responsible Growth
text:
Labor, energy producers, and nonprofits voice strong support for Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Since four Senators from across the political spectrum introduced their Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act last week, a broad coalition of labor leaders, energy producers, and nonprofits has voiced support for the permitting reform plan, noting that it will deliver cheaper energy, more jobs, and responsible growth. The legislation was drafted by U.S. Senators Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee; Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources (ENR) Committee; Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member of the EPW Committee; and Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the ENR Committee.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act delivers cheaper energy, more well-paying jobs, and responsible growth by accelerating the permitting and construction of critical energy and infrastructure projects while maintaining key environmental and historic preservation safeguards. The legislation provides greater certainty for projects that have already been permitted and financed, including by preventing future administrations from arbitrarily blocking entire classes of energy projects, while establishing clear timelines for environmental reviews and legal challenges. It also includes targeted reforms to expand and modernize the electric grid, speed the development of geothermal and other energy projects, and ensure that rapidly growing data centers pay the full cost of their associated transmission needs rather than passing those costs on to families and small businesses. The legislation reflects input from members of Congress on both sides of the aisle and a diverse group of stakeholders.

The bill text is available here.

Labor

“For LIUNA, the key consideration is whether a permitting package will translate to good union jobs, with prevailing wages and robust apprenticeship opportunities. S.5653 exceeds those standards while maintaining proper regulations and safeguards that protect both our members on the job as well as the local communities in which projects take place. Moreover, it will lower energy costs for all Americans at a time when prices of everyday living expenses are at an all-time high,” said LIUNA General President Brent Booker. “For more than a decade LIUNA has testified before Congress, submitted comments, participated in roundtables, and endorsed numerous iterations of permitting bills only to see every effort and attempt fail in final hours of the congressional calendar. Congress has another opportunity to get this done. We urge lawmakers in both parties to seize this moment, pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, and finally deliver meaningful permitting reform. It is time to stop making permitting reform the Groundhog Day of Congress.”

“In our industry, uncertainty means one thing: unemployment. It is long past time that Congress enacts meaningful permitting reform to put UA members to work faster delivering reliable and affordable energy to American communities. Today’s announcement is the culmination of a long process to reach a bipartisan deal and take a critical step towards a long-overdue modernization of our country’s permitting process. This bipartisan legislation, led by Chairs Lee and Capito and Ranking Members Heinrich and Whitehouse, will increase project certainty, streamline federal review timelines, and create thousands of good-paying jobs – all while maintaining reasonable environmental safeguards and opportunities for public input. The UA looks forward to continuing our work with members of both parties in the Senate to advance this critical legislation and with all members in the House to ultimately pass it into law,” said United Association of Union Plumbers and Pipefitters (UA) General President Mark McManus.

“We have seen too many projects unnecessarily delayed for years through litigation, and other projects abandoned by contractors or terminated by the federal government because of our nation’s antiquated permitting process. As a result, thousands of good-paying union jobs have been lost, and taxpayers have been deprived of safer infrastructure and more affordable energy,” said John L. Downey, General President of the International Union of Operating Engineers. “Passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will result in building energy transmission capacity faster, delivering more energy to the grid, creating greater certainty for projects permitted and financed across administrations, and setting clear deadlines for environmental reviews. These reforms will put thousands of Operating Engineers to work, along with other highly skilled crafts people, while making energy more affordable and reliable for American families.”

Nonprofits

“If America is going to meaningfully reduce our emissions and truly address climate change, we need to connect much more clean energy to the grid,” said Citizens Climate Lobby’s Executive Director Ricky Bradley. “This bill will make remarkable, rapid progress toward that goal. We’re proud to endorse it, and we’re excited to mobilize our grassroots volunteers in full support.”

“For decades, the Club for Growth has championed deregulation and permitting reform. We commend President Trump and Senate leaders for moving this agreement forward with legislative text. These reforms are critical to expanding American energy production and lowering energy costs for families and businesses. Excessive regulation has constrained production and contributed to higher costs for American consumers. We urge the Senate andHouse to act swiftly and pass these important permitting reforms,” said David McIntosh, President, Club for Growth.

“The Climate Leadership Council is encouraged by progress on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. Council analysis projects U.S. electricity demand to grow nearly 60% by 2050, and meeting that demand will require building energy infrastructure faster than our current system allows. Permitting reform is essential to keep pace with the demands of a modern economy, and the energy infrastructure it unlocks is what drives clean energy deployment and innovation. CLC looks forward to continued engagement with stakeholders and policymakers as the bill moves forward,” said Erin Alejandre, Director of Policy at the Climate Leadership Council.

“On behalf of grassroots activists across the country, we strongly applaud theintroduction of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). Your work over much of this Congress to negotiate the details and make a bipartisan package a reality is a major step forward for the American people and for our energy, technological, and national future,” said Brent Gardner, Chief Government Affairs Officer, Americans for Prosperity.

“After years of working toward this goal, lawmakers from both parties have reached a deal to fix the broken system that keeps America from building the power plants and power lines that would bring costs down. This is a huge bipartisan win at a moment when our politics has made wins like this rare,”said Inclusive Abundance Action President Derek Kaufman. “Families are paying too much for electricity because new energy projects wait years on government reviews, then years more in court, and even once they clear, partisan politics can still take them out. That scarcity is a choice. Today, Congress is choosing differently.”

“The need for reform is one of the few things Republicans and Democrats agree on, and these Senate leaders have translated that consensus into a comprehensive, bipartisan bill. Permitting reform cannot wait, and the time to act is now,”said Michele Stockwell, president of Bipartisan Policy Center Action. “BPC Action has long argued that durable permitting reform must be bipartisan, technology-neutral, and maintain strong environmental standards. We urge swift action and look forward to working with members of both parties to get this bill to the president’s desk this Congress.”

“Pacific Legal Foundation strongly supports the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026,” said John Nagle, federal policy manager at Pacific Legal Foundation. “Americans should not have to navigate years of costly and unpredictable government processes simply to build a home, develop new energy resources, or create the infrastructure our communities need. Reforming our permitting system is essential to removing unnecessary government barriers that delay projects, drive up costs, and discourage investment. We encourage Congress to move quickly to pass this bill to lower costs for Americans, protect property rights, and restore America’s ability to build.”

“Today, one of America’s most important supply lines is its electric grid, and we are not building it fast enough to meet the moment. Our military installations depend on the same civilian grid as every American household. When a transmission line takes a decade or more to approve, that is not just an economic problem. It is a strategic vulnerability, and our adversaries are not waiting years to build. This bill addresses that vulnerability. It sets firm deadlines on environmental reviews, speeds approvals for the transmission lines and power projects the country needs, and gives the federal government tools to move interstate power lines forward when they stall. Just as important, it ensures that once a project is permitted, no administration can revoke it for political reasons. At the same time, it preserves the government's ability to act in the face of a genuine safety or national security threat, and it keeps reasonable environmental safeguards and opportunities for public input in place. That kind of certainty matters for every form of American energy, including the clean energy that will power our future,” said Major General Paul D. Eaton, U.S. Army (Ret.), Senior Advisor at VoteVets.

“[The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act] is better than I could have expected. Sens. Capito (R-WV), Heinrich (D-NM), Lee (R-UT), and Whitehouse (D-RI) negotiated a compromise bill where each side got real, meaningful wins. This bill would fix our permitting processes so that we can review and build efficiently, reducing costs, improving quality of life, growing our economy, and improving economic outcomes. It’s truly a win-win. I’m optimistic that this incredible bill can be signed into law this year,” said Xan Fishman, Vice President, Energy, Bipartisan Policy Center.

“Permitting reform has stalled for years because Democrats feared losing environmental protections and Republicans feared a deal that would only help renewables. Sens. Heinrich, Lee, Capito and Whitehouse have shown there is a bargain that works for both sides,” said Colin Mortimer, Senior Director of Partnerships at the Progressive Policy Institute. “This bill would get power lines, clean energy and critical infrastructure built faster and lower costs for families while keeping strong safeguards in place.”

“If you care about decarbonizing the economy or reshoring American manufacturing, or cutting bills for ratepayers, then you should support this bill. No agreement is perfect, but there’s something in this permitting reform agreement that will, on net, benefit everybody. And there isn’t a better deal out there,” said Jane Flegal and Pavan Venkatakrishnan of the Searchlight Institute.

Bill Owens, Chairman of the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB) said, “NAHB applauds Senators Lee, Capito, Heinrich and Whitehouse and for their leadership and bipartisan approach to crafting the most meaningful reforms in decades to several key federal environmental permitting programs. The housing sector stands to benefit from many of these federal permitting reforms, including an increase in acreage thresholds under the Clean Water Act’s (CWA) Nationwide Permit program along with extending the statutory timeframe from five to 10 years for the CWA permit programs. These provisions provide the industry with needed clarity and consistency during the federal permitting process.”

Energy Companies and Associations

“The American Clean Power Association greatly appreciates the leadership of Senators Capito, Whitehouse, Lee and Heinrich in developing strong, technology neutral permitting reform legislation that includes an Administration commitment to approve wind projects. All energy industries must be able to confidently rely on the durability of federal permitting decisions. The transmission provisions will also enhance grid reliability and enable economic growth. If adopted, the legislation will substantially increase the deployment of clean resources. Passage before the end of the year is essential to enable the construction of critical energy infrastructure and lower consumer prices,” said Jason Grumet, CEO of American Clean Power Association.

“Washington has a generational opportunity to fundamentally transform a broken permitting system and help address the affordability challenges facing American consumers,” API President and CEO Mike Sommers said. “President Trump and Senators Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich deserve credit for working across party lines to bring durable reform within reach. The bipartisan package would modernize NEPA, reduce duplicative reviews and unnecessary litigation, and provide greater certainty for critical projects. Congress should seize this moment and finish the job—making it easier to build the infrastructure America needs and helping keep costs down for consumers.”

“We support this bipartisan effort and applaud Senators Capito, Heinrich, Lee, and Whitehouse for advancing meaningful reforms to help meet America’s growing energy needs. As one of the nation’s largest electric utilities and the operator of the country’s largest transmission network, AEP understands firsthand the critical need for diverse generation and transmission infrastructure to serve our customers and help meet the unprecedented demand for electricity. The process to permit, site and construct energy infrastructure can take years due to unnecessary hurdles that delay projects needed to support reliability, affordability and economic growth. This legislation will help accelerate the process to bring critical infrastructure projects online, supporting the investments required to enhance reliability for our customers, reduce costs, and create new economic opportunities in the states we serve. Congress should pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 now,” said American Electric Power (AEP) Chairman, President and CEO Bill Fehrman.

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 represents an historic opportunity to modernize the grid and meet customers’ electricity demand with reliable, affordable power. If enacted into law, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 would safeguard critical environmental standards while providing greater process certainty for environmental reviews and ensure that the customers we serve benefit from our nation’s diverse energy resources. It will also unlock trillions of dollars in private sector investment and job creation to expedite the construction of critically needed energy infrastructure,” said Mark Hewett, President and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway Energy.

“Independent oil and natural gas producers are ready to build, produce, and create jobs, and permitting delays and uncertainty can turn attractive projects into missed opportunities—especially for small producers. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 gives Congress an opportunity to deliver bipartisan permitting reform with clear and enforceable timelines, greater levels of certainty, and fewer unnecessary delays—without compromising the environmental and safety standards that protect our communities and natural resources. Republicans and Democrats should seize that opportunity and move swiftly. American energy shouldn’t have to wait in line for Washington’s bureaucracy. American energy shouldn’t be held back by a permitting system that doesn’t keep pace with energy demand. This is an opportunity to celebrate what bipartisan cooperation can accomplish, providing real solutions to the complex problems that surround America’s broken permitting system,” said Edith Naegele, President and CEO of the Independent Petroleum Association of America (IPAA).

“This is the kind of bipartisan action America needs to meet growing energy demand, put downward pressure on energy prices, and deploy more affordable, exactly reliable solar and storage for American families and businesses,” said Tim Pawlenty, CEO of the Solar Energy Industries Association.

“Affordable advanced energy resources, including solar, wind, storage, and transmission are delivering for America, but opaque, politicized, and endless red tape is getting in our industry’s way of building as much as is needed. That’s why we welcome technology-neutral permitting reform from Congress. This bill text demonstrates bipartisan support for building more advanced energy, faster. With fair competition, better planning, and less red tape, we can move more electrons and tamp down energy costs. Thank you to Sen. Capito, Sen. Mike Lee, Sen. Whitehouse, and Sen. Heinrich on their leadership. We encourage Congress to build on this progress and to prioritize these critical reforms,”said Heather O’Neill, President and CEO of Advanced Energy United.

“Constraining abundant, domestic clean energy could cost the U.S. at least $121 billion in additional energy expenses in the coming years,” CEBA CEO Rich Powell said. “This bipartisan package is a generational opportunity to unleash American energy through faster infrastructure permitting and improved transmission planning. Thank you to Chairs Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee, Ranking Members Sheldon Whitehouse and Martin Heinrich, and President Donald Trump for your leadership on this critical issue. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act presents an incredible opportunity for clean energy, and we look forward to seeing it cross the finish line.”

“This bipartisan breakthrough goes big to durably reform a broken permitting system that needlessly drives up energy costs and puts America’s energy security at risk. These comprehensive reforms would unlock generational investments to make energy more affordable and position America to win the global energy race that will define our future. We urge the Senate to act with the urgency this moment in history demands by passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act,” said Anne Bradbury, the American Exploration & Production Council (AXPC) CEO.

“American economic growth requires an energy permitting system built on predictable, durable, bipartisan principles that will outlast two- and four-year election cycles,” said ACORE President and CEO Ray Long. “Clean energy builders and financers have made it clear they intend to keep investing in clean energy. The bipartisan legislation released today represents momentum toward providing the policy certainty the market needs to unleash capital and build the energy infrastructure we need.”

“Failing to pass permitting reforms would have real consequences for all of us,”said Zach Zimmerman, Director of Research and Policy for Grid Strategies.“Every year that major transmission projects are delayed means higher system costs and less ability to move power where it is needed during extreme weather. Without reform, we will continue to pay more for the grid.”

“Pass the frickin’ bill so we can start building things again,” said the U.S. Oil & Gas Association.

Business and Manufacturing Groups

“Manufacturers are all in on this game-changing agreement and getting it across the finish line. Our nation’s permitting system is outdated and burdensome, delaying projects across industries and contributing to rising costs across the economy. Costly, duplicative permitting delays are costing manufacturers $8 billion annually, limiting manufacturers’ ability to hire new workers, build and expand their operations. Removing these barriers would unlock greater investment and growth. Manufacturers are ready to build, and modernized permitting will help us race to the future,” said National Association of Manufacturers President and CEO Jay Timmons.

“BCSE commends the continued bipartisan work in Congress to modernize the nation’s permitting system and the further development of a comprehensive legislative permitting reform package. Building on the important progress made by the House of Representatives, Congress now has an opportunity to advance comprehensive, durable permitting reform that can provide greater certainty for investment and accelerate the deployment of critical energy infrastructure,” said Lisa Jacobson, President of the Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE).

“We appreciate all the work that made this strong package possible. Any bipartisan compromise will have trade-offs, but the permit certainty, transmission, and grid modernization components of this deal are strong, and now is the time to deliver reforms that allow us to build the clean energy infrastructure we need to reduce costs for American businesses and consumers,” said Zach Friedman, Senior Director of Federal Policy at Ceres. “We look forward to continuing to work with companies, partners, and key lawmakers to meet the moment and advance this package to drive down costs by accelerating deployment of affordable, homegrown clean energy infrastructure.”

“Business Roundtable strongly supports the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026. This vital legislation would create a faster, more durable permitting process that gives businesses the certainty they need to invest, build and grow,” said Business Roundtable CEO Joshua Bolten. “Advancing wide-ranging permitting reform is one of the most consequential steps Congress can take to unlock America’s economic potential. By accelerating approvals for critical infrastructure projects, this bill would help lower costs, create good-paying jobs and strengthen America’s long-term competitiveness.”

“For too long, America’s broken permitting system has turned the ability to receive a permit into a barrier to job creation and economic growth. This bipartisan agreement represents a major step toward changing that. By establishing more reliable timelines, creating greater certainty and breaking down longstanding barriers to building, Congress can help ensure that projects across the economy move from the drawing board to the job site,” said Steel Manufacturers Association Executive Vice President Brandon Farris.

“The legislation would modernize federal environmental review and permitting processes for infrastructure projects, provide greater certainty for federal permits and authorizations, and help enable the all-of-the-above energy resources needed to meet America's growing energy and manufacturing demands,” said the American Chemistry Council. “America cannot build, power, and compete without modern infrastructure. Whether it’s expanding energy production, strengthening manufacturing, building next-generation infrastructure, projects cannot move forward if permitting delays and regulatory uncertainty stand in the way. This bipartisan legislation is an important step toward creating a permitting system that is more predictable, transparent, and effective.”

“We are undeniably in the age of demand – from energy to semiconductors, drones to transmission lines – and securing robust supplies of the mined materials that allow us to build, manufacture and power almost everything is key to meeting this moment. Standing in our way is a permitting process mired in duplication, endless litigation and uncertainty that has hobbled U.S. competitiveness with the second longest timeline in the world to bring a mine online. Our elected officials on both sides of the aisle have long acknowledged that the status quo cannot continue. We applaud the work that has been done to date and urge Congress to pass commonsense, much-needed reforms that will benefit all Americans,” said Rich Nolan, President and CEO of the National Mining Association.

“The Senate's progress toward a comprehensive, bipartisan permitting reform deal brings us one step closer to streamlining the outdated process that is holding up critical projects of all kinds, from energy and water infrastructure to roads, broadband, and manufacturing,” said Rodney Davis, senior vice president and head of government affairs at the U.S. Chamber. “We appreciate the leadership of Senators Capito, Whitehouse, Lee, and Heinrich to bring us to this point, and now we urge swift action in Congress to get this bill to the President’s desk as soon as possible.”

State and Local Government

“The National Governors Association and its partners are encouraged by the introduction of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 and look forward to working with Congress to further develop this legislation. Working with governors, NGA has long championed commonsense permitting reform to build the infrastructure our country needs. With priorities centered on federal partnership, interstate cooperation, and sound energy and environmental policy, NGA worked across the aisle and across sectors to deliver federal reform recommendations to Congress, using states as proving ground. Reform will help grow our economy, reduce costs, and improve quality of life for all Americans,” said Brian Tatum, CEO of the National Governors Association.

“Counties are on the front lines of delivering the energy, water and transportation infrastructure projects that residents depend on,” said National Association of Counties Executive Director Matthew Chase. “The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act recognizes counties as cooperating agencies in federal environmental protection statutes. This legislation would modernize the federal permitting process, reduce unnecessary delays, accelerate project delivery and ensure local expertise is incorporated into federal decision-making. Counties applaud Senators Lee, Heinrich, Capito and Whitehouse for their leadership and urge Congress to advance this bipartisan permitting reform package.”

“Unfortunately, outdated federal bureaucracy continues to delay critical energy and infrastructure projects and drive up costs for hardworking families at a time when speed and efficiency matter most. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is an opportunity to change that. By bringing greater certainty and accountability to the permitting process, we can unleash American energy dominance, strengthen our grid, bring manufacturing and investment back home, and ensure the United States leads the next generation of economic growth,” said 21 governors in a statement.

title: Senator Coons statement on third anniversary of October 7 attacks
text:
WILMINGTON, Del. – U.S. Senator Chris Coons (D-Del.) released the following statement on the anniversary of the October 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attacks on Israel:

“Three years on, the wounds left from Hamas’ brutal attack on Israeli civilians are still just as painful and devastating. One thousand two hundred souls were ripped away from their families and their futures, and 251 more were taken hostage in an attempt to destroy Israel’s spirit. In that, the attack failed. In meetings with the families of hostages and victims of the attacks, I’ve seen a strength and will to turn pain into progress I could not have imagined. Their perseverance in their search for justice has touched so many lives and cannot be forgotten. Together, we must continue to work toward a just and lasting peace in the region.

“May the memory of those lost always be a blessing, and may they continue to live on in the hearts of those who loved them – and in the hearts of all of us who remember them around the world.”

title: Cortez Masto, Rosen Release Joint Report Detailing How Trump’s Economy is Hurting Nevada Latino Families
text:
Las Vegas, Nev. – During the final week of Hispanic Heritage Month, U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) released a new report detailing the harm that President Donald Trump’s policies are causing Latino families in Nevada.

“This report confirms what Nevada families have known for months: under the Trump economy, it’s getting harder to put food on the table and a roof over your head,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “From his blanket tariffs to his reckless war in Iran, everything this President is doing has driven up costs for Latinos in Nevada. Every family deserves the chance to get ahead, and I’m going to keep doing everything I can to reverse President Trump’s disastrous policies.”

“Donald Trump’s economy is a disaster for Latinos in Nevada. Anyone who’s willing to work hard should have a fair shot at getting ahead, but that’s become almost impossible under Trump’s leadership,” said Senator Rosen. “Families are paying more for gas, groceries, health care, and housing, all while our tourism industry declines as a result of Trump’s policies. I’m committed to helping every Nevadan live the American Dream, and I’ll keep working to bring down costs and expand opportunities for Nevada families.”

Because of Trump’s tariffs, the war in Iran, and Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill, Latino families are paying more for everyday essentials and seeing fewer opportunities to get ahead. Below is a breakdown of how Trump and Washington Republicans’ policies are hurting Latino families in Nevada.

Gas and Groceries

Trump’s war in Iran has cost Latinos in Nevada about $230 million extra at the gas pump since the war began, which breaks down to an additional $659 per family.

Latinos account for more than a quarter of Nevada SNAP recipients, including over 48,000 Latino children.

As a result of Donald Trump’s cuts to SNAP in the “One Big Beautiful Bill,” 38,000 Latino Nevadans have lost their SNAP benefits, including as many as 16,000 children.

Trump’s first year in office cost Latinos in Nevada an additional $108 million on groceries, which is $310 per family.

Trump’s mass deportation agenda is taking immigrant workers off the job, and as a result, prices are rising in sectors like agriculture that depend on immigrant labor.

More than 60% of farm laborers nationwide are Latino, and the vast majority are immigrants. Targeting of this workforce has led to a 32.1% increase in lettuce prices, a 7.1% increase in apple prices, a 6.3% increase in fresh citrus prices, and a 7.9% increase in canned fruit prices.

Economic Opportunity

The tax provisions in Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” disproportionately benefit the top one percent of earners and leave the working class behind.

Individuals working in food preparation and service will lose about $820 in 2026. More than half of Nevada’s hospitality workforce is Latino.

Maids and housekeeping cleaners will lose about $830 in 2026. Latinos make up nearly half of this workforce nationally.

Nevada is home to more than 72,000 Latino-owned small businesses, accounting for over 22% of all Nevada small businesses. Trump’s across-the-board tariffs have cost these businesses a total of $8.6 billion.

Leisure and hospitality small businesses have seen a 15.2% decline in monthly revenue.

Construction small businesses have seen an 18% decline in revenue.

Since Trump returned to office, tourism to Las Vegas has declined by about ten percent, with Canadian tourism – the number one source of international visitation to Las Vegas – down even more as a result of Trump’s tariffs and attacks directed at Canada.

Latinos make up 54% of Nevada’s hospitality workforce and are seeing fewer shifts and fewer tips as a result of the decline in tourism.

Trump’s mass deportation agenda, including delays in work permit processing leading to loss of work authorization and the proposed termination of Temporary Protected Status for Salvadorans, will lead to 15,000 Nevadans losing their legal status by the end of this year.

Thousands of construction, hospitality, and health care workers will lose their ability to work, and Nevada will lose out on $341 million in economic contributions and $40 million in tax revenue.

Health Care

For the approximately 33,200 Latinos who buy health insurance through Nevada Health Link, premiums have risen over 50% on average due to Donald Trump and Washington Republicans’ refusal to extend the Affordable Care Act’s enhanced premium tax cuts.

Latinos account for around 36% of Medicaid beneficiaries in Nevada and are less likely to have employer-sponsored or private health insurance than other groups, despite having the highest labor force participation.

As Washington Republicans’ Medicaid cuts continue to take effect, up to 25,560 Latinos in Nevada could lose their Medicaid coverage.

Housing

Latino families in Nevada have spent an additional $184 million – or an additional $491 per family – on housing costs, including rent and mortgage payments, since Trump took office.

title: Sen. Cruz Statement on Third Anniversary of October 7th Terrorist Attack
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) released the following statement commemorating the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack.

Sen. Cruz said, “Today's anniversary is a day for mourning but also for renewing resolve. Over the last three years, Israel has demonstrated extraordinary courage, resolve, and skill in destroying the Hamas terrorists who committed the October 7th attack and in dismantling the Iranian-controlled terrorist armies that the Iranian regime had built across the Middle East. These operations were a necessary, measured, and just response to the attack, in which Hamas murdered and kidnapped dozens of Americans alongside over 1,200 Israelis and other nationals, and have immeasurably enhanced Israeli and American national security. As I said immediately after the attack, I am committed to doing everything in my power and using every resource at my disposal to ensure that America's policy is absolutely unequivocal: to ensure Israel has the military and diplomatic support to utterly eradicate Hamas, for as long as it takes.”

BACKGROUND:

In October 2023, Sen. Cruz introduced the Hamas Sanctions Act, legislation to impose sanctions on Hamas, its members and affiliates, and countries that provide funding and territory for Hamas operations.

In April 2025, Sen. Cruz introduced the LIABLE Act, legislation to allow American victims of terrorism, including victims of the terrorist attack on October 7th, to sue international organizations that provide material support to designated terrorist groups.

title: Durbin Joins Shaheen For Final Codel To Western Balkans
text:
SARAJEVO – This week, U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) is joining U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, for a congressional delegation trip to Bosnia and Herzegovina, Albania, Montenegro, Croatia, and Kosovo. This will be Durbin’s final congressional delegation trip as a United States Senator. Durbin previously traveled to the Balkans in 1999 and 2009.

During the trip, the Senators will meet with government officials, U.S. diplomatic personnel, civil society representatives, and young leaders to discuss regional security, democratic institutions, economic opportunity, and relations with the United States. Meetings will address the European Union accession processes, NATO cooperation, energy diversification, and implementation of the Western Balkans Democracy and Prosperity Act, enacted as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act. The delegation will visit the Srebrenica Memorial Center and Cemetery at Potocari and attend a performance by the House of Good Tones.

“Senator Shaheen has been a champion in the Senate at keeping attention on the Balkan region, and I am pleased to join her for this timely trip—just days after an election in Bosnia and Herzegovina,” said Durbin. “Many have forgotten about the terrible violence in the region after the breakup of the former Yugoslavia. And while a number of the ensuing independent nations have notably joined NATO and the European Union, many challenges remain three decades after the signing of the Dayton Accords. Our visit will demonstrate continued U.S. interest in seeing progress and continued healing in the region.”

“I first traveled to the Western Balkans as a Senator in 2010 with Senator George Voinovich, and I’m glad that my final delegation as Ranking Member will be to this critical region,” said Shaheen. “On this visit, Senator Durbin and I will meet with officials, young leaders and civil society representatives to discuss security, economic opportunity and their countries’ relationships with the United States.”

title: As USS Lincoln Nears Return to America’s Shores, Gallego Calls for Review, Oversight of the Ship’s Record-Breaking Deployment
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), a Marine Corps combat veteran who served in Iraq, wrote to the Department of Defense (DoD) Inspector General (IG) Platte B. Moring and Acting Comptroller General of the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) Orice W. Brown requesting reviews of the USS Abraham Lincoln’s deployment.

The more than 300-day deployment, among the longest for a U.S. aircraft carrier since the Vietnam War, initially focused on the Indo-Pacific but was later extended to support President Trump’s war in Iran. It drew condemnation from officials and servicemembers’ families amid reports of mental health concerns and deteriorating conditions on board. The letter comes as the USS Lincoln returned to U.S. soil for the first time in nine months, when the carrier stopped at Naval Base Guam last month.

Senator Gallego, in his letter to the DoD IG, wrote to urge an “independent investigation” of the “decisions and systems behind the reported shortages of food and basic supplies, sustained crew fatigue, and limited access to mental-health resources aboard the ship.” Reports from the deployment also described water contamination, plumbing failures, and sailors threatening to jump overboard, among other problems. Specifically, the senator requests the DoD IG “provide written findings, including any determination of policy noncompliance, systemic deficiency, or recommended accountability measures.”

In his letter to the GAO, Senator Gallego wrote to request a report on “the Department of the Navy’s ability to safely and effectively sustain extended ship deployments, and the effect of increasingly prolonged deployments on logistics, maintenance, sailor welfare, readiness, and retention.” Specifically, the senator requests that the GAO “recommend measurable standards or benchmarks that Congress and Navy leadership can use to determine when an extended deployment has exceeded sustainable limits.”

“The Lincoln’s crew met extraordinary operational demands and performed a critical mission. That makes it all the more important to determine whether the Navy’s systems were adequate to sustain sailors and maintain readiness under these conditions,” concluded Senator Gallego.

In August, Senator Gallego reacted to reports of poor conditions aboard the USS Lincoln on an ABC News appearance, saying, “this administration did not plan for this war, did not plan how to get out of this war, did not really understand how this war was going to escalate.” That same month, Senator Gallego called for an official congressional oversight visit to the USS Lincoln to investigate reported conditions and joined.

The full letter to DoD IG Moring can be found HERE.

The full letter to GAO Acting Comptroller General Brown can be found HERE.

title: Gallego, Banks Urge Trump Administration to Shore Up 6G Security
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Jim Banks (R-IN) wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging him to coordinate with allies to secure next-generation mobile telecommunications systems and infrastructure in the United States and around the globe. Specifically, the senators called on the Trump administration to name a U.S. head of delegation for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference (WRC-27), coordinate with allies on the security threat posed by China and strengthen U.S. leadership on 6G and satellite technology.

The letter comes ahead of the WRC-27, slated to begin in Shanghai in October 2027, where nations will decide standards governing the 6G networks that will underpin global communications for the next decade or more. It also follows Senator Gallego’s attendance at the United Nations General Assembly in New York and comes after President Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping for a summit in Washington.

“Designating a delegation lead would help the United States avoid a repeat of WRC-23, when the then-head of the U.S. delegation had to be replaced on short notice mid-preparation,” wrote the senators. “We cannot afford to enter WRC-27 under similar conditions.”

In 2012, Congress identified China-based Huawei, one of the four major network equipment manufactures globally, as a security risk, and the largest U.S telecommunications service providers — including AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon — chose not to use Chinese-made network equipment. However, smaller U.S. providers continued to purchase Huawei and ZTE for their networks, asserting the Chinese providers offered less expensive equipment and end-to-end support. Huawei also maintains a large footprint in Europe and Africa, where its equipment carries vast amounts of sensitive communications and data, giving China a potential avenue into critical infrastructure and greater leverage over networks the United States and its allies depend on.

Naming a U.S. head of delegation now, before those standards are set, will help ensure those standards reflect U.S. and allied interests rather than Chinese influence.

title: Gallego, Kelly Sound Alarm on Proposed Rule Change to Head Start Program
text:
Arizona senators urge the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to not change requirements for the Head Start Program

WASHINGTON — Today, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) wrote a letter to Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy and Assistant Secretary Alex J. Adams voicing concerns regarding a proposed rule, “Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs,” that would remove federal requirements for classroom sizes, instruction, and health screenings. In the letter, the senators urged the department to preserve the standards for the Head Start Program.

“Head Start offers a place to learn, build relationships, and receive care during years that are important to a child’s development,” the senators wrote. “These programs are an important part of Arizona communities and give families in need the support they may struggle to find or afford.”

In Arizona, Head Start and Early Head Start serve 16,172 children across 332 program sites, providing early education, meals, and health services at no cost to families. These programs also help parents maintain employment and continue their education, with 76 percent of Head Start parents working, attending school, or participating in job training.

Head Start and Early Head Start is especially important to communities where families have few child care options — including rural Arizona. There the programs provide about 17 percent of child care and serve 1,943 children eligible for services under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, 1,291 children experiencing homelessness, and 459 children in foster care statewide.

The senators also included letters from Arizona elected officials and organizations to highlight their concerns and show the importance of the Head Start program, including the Office of the Governor of Arizona and the Arizona Head Start Association, among others.

title: Gallego Unveils Sweeping Economic Agenda to Restore America’s Middle Class
text:
“Saving the Middle Class and Restoring the American Dream” details five pillars of the senator’s economic policy plan

WASHINGTON — Today, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) released his sweeping economic policy plan to rebuild America’s middle class. The five-pillar plan, “Saving the Middle Class and Restoring the American Dream,” includes a tax on data centers and AI, a New-Deal style public service jobs program, and raising the minimum wage to $20-per-hour to build an economy by-and-for the middle class — not the elites.

“For far too long, we’ve had a broken economy where hard work just isn’t nearly enough. The federal government let giant corporations, billionaires, and elites write the rules, and we’re living with the results: costs have soared, wages have stalled, and jobs have left. This bipartisan, failed status quo must end,” said Senator Gallego. “Working-class Americans aren’t asking for handouts. They don’t resent anyone else’s success — they just want a fair system. Work hard enough, and you should be able to get ahead, provide for your kids, take a vacation, and even get rich.”

Pillar 1, titled “Raise Wages and Improve Benefits,” outlines the senator’s plan to bring the American Dream back within reach by:

Moving to sectoral bargaining and increasing union membership: The senator wants to move beyond the PRO Act and toward sectoral bargaining. Senator Gallego is the among the first Democrats to call for sectoral bargaining and is the first politician to state that it should be the goal of the U.S. government to triple union density by 2035.

Raising the minimum wage to $20-per-hour and require companies to pay double for overtime work — not time-and-a-half.

Cracking down on worker misclassification by ending the ability of employers, like Uber and DoorDash, to misclassify employees as “independent contractors” to skirt minimum wage, overtime, unemployment insurance, and workers’ compensation responsibilities.

Creating an Office of Worker Empowerment and Office of Worker Advocacy: Sen. Gallego is the first federal politician to call for the creation of these offices.

Pillar 2, titled “Create and Protect Quality Blue Collar Jobs” would safeguard and grow job opportunity by:

Creating a trade policy for the working class by:

Repealing President Trump’s reckless, across-the-board global tariffs and ending his trade war with Canada.

Pursuing a strategic trade policy targeting unfair practices by chronic-surplus countries like China.

Combining trade and other industrial policies to effectively grow domestic industry.

Creating an Industrial Policy Council at the Executive Office of the President: Similar to the National Security Council, the plan calls for the creation of an entity to coordinate government industrial policy initiatives and ensure all efforts reflect worker-first, community-first growth.

Pillar 3, titled “Restoring Worker Trust in Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence” would ensure workers have a voice in how AI shapes the workforce and get a fair share of the prosperity it creates by:

Creating a New-Deal style public service jobs program: The program would fund jobs that allow AI-displaced workers to serve the public, funded by taxing AI. Sen. Gallego is one of the first Democrats to call for a large-scale public jobs program.

Requiring industry and workers to negotiate over AI: Sen. Gallego is among the first politicians to propose this idea. This approach mirrors the way in which actors and writers negotiated with Hollywood after the strike in 2023 over AI, guaranteeing workers have a seat at the table.

Creating a corporate “robot” tax to discourage job dislocation and maintain company payroll contributions for automated-away jobs.

Pillar 4, titled “Expand Job-Creating Entrepreneurship, Focusing Outside of Superstar Cities” would grow Main Street communities by:

Creating a data center tax:Senator Gallego is calling for a 10% excise tax on data centers and for the removal of many data center tax breaks like bonus depreciation and deductions for state and local taxes. Specifically, Senator Gallego is calling on data centers to benefit communities by:

Using excise tax revenue to fund community investments.

Requiring data centers to cover the full cost of needed generation, transmission, and distribution upgrades to the grid rather than shifting costs to families and businesses.

Requiring data centers to bring additional energy to the grid, preventing energy cost increases for consumers and creating new production jobs —and require them to sustain energy investments even if they abandon the project.

Preventing data centers from using key chips and components from China to spur domestic manufacturing.

Pushing data centers to pay high wages and use union labor.

Protecting small businesses from giant corporations by modernizing and enforcing antitrust laws.

Pillar 5, titled “Help Workers Find Jobs Faster” would improve the job search process by:

Cracking down on fake job postings known as “ghost jobs,” prohibiting companies from posting job advertisements that they have no intention of actually filling.

Giving laid-off workers more time to find a new job: The plan calls for requiring companies to provide affected workers with 120-day notice in the event of a mass layoff or closure. Currently, the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act only requires companies to give employees 60-day notice.

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues File Amicus Brief In Lawsuit Against Trump’s Department Of Housing And Urban Development For Attacking Fair Housing Program
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Transportation, Housing and Urban Development (THUD) Subcommittee, joined 20 of her Senate colleagues in submitting an amicus brief supporting a federal judge’s ruling that the Trump administration’s Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) unlawfully restricted funding to groups that investigate and enforce laws against housing discrimination. The amicus brief argues that HUD’s unprecedented attempt to direct $46 million away from fair housing organizations – while diverting an additional $10 million to government agencies with separate appropriations – has no lawful justification and would harm the nation’s fair housing enforcement infrastructure.

“Fair housing organizations work every day to protect New Yorkers from discrimination when they rent or buy a home,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Without the federal funding Congress appropriated, these groups could be forced to shut their doors, allowing housing discrimination to go unchecked and leaving families with nowhere to turn. I am proud to join this amicus brief and will keep fighting to make sure the Trump administration follows the law and delivers the funds as Congress intended.”

The senators began the brief, “Congress intended [the Fair Housing Initiatives Program (FHIP)] to foster a nationwide network of private organizations, like Plaintiffs, that can aid the federal government in uncovering and eliminating housing discrimination. Since Congress piloted FHIP in 1988 and codified it in 1992, FHIP has consistently sustained private fair housing organizations through three grant streams: the Private Enforcement Initiative (‘PEI’) to support investigative and enforcement activities; the Education and Outreach Initiative (‘EOI’); and the Fair Housing Organization Initiative (‘FHOI’) to build organizational capacity. With this funding, private organizations handle most housing discrimination complaints and enforcement nationwide.”

“HUD’s July 2, 2026 Notices of Funding Opportunity (‘NOFOs’) endanger fair housing organizations and their vital work. The NOFOs deviate from FHIP’s authorizing statute, decades of FHIP practice, and Congress’s intent. For the first time since FHIP’s codification in 1992, the FY2025 NOFOs provide no new awards for PEI or EOI—the lifeblood of fair housing organizations—nor do they fulfill existing multi-year PEI awards. Instead, HUD attempts to direct $46 million—the vast majority of funds—away from existing qualified organizations in favor of organizations with no experience in fair housing enforcement, while diverting the remaining $10 million to governmental agencies for which Congress separately appropriated. These unprecedented actions have no lawful justification and would seriously harm the nation’s fair housing enforcement infrastructure. The district court rightly vacated HUD’s unlawful notices and directed funding to flow under the prior framework. HUD’s request to stay that well-founded order should be denied,” the senators argued.

The senators concluded, “The Doles Memo’s stated aims are misleading and contrary to FHIP’s purposes as well. It claims the FY2025 NOFOs will ‘expand geographic coverage,’ ‘broaden’ expertise, and ‘strengthen the long-term resilience of the national fair housing infrastructure.’ HUD’s NOFOs do the opposite—losing geographic coverage, expertise, and organizational resilience by concentrating FHIP funding in a handful of grants that existing organizations cannot receive. Worse, the Doles Memo treats fair housing organizations like maligned welfare recipients—charging them with ‘perpetual dependence’ on federal funding. FHIP’s goal always has been to sustain these organizations as a vital organ of the fair housing enforcement system, particularly in areas underserved without federal resources. HUD’s NOFOs, if unaddressed, would set fair housing enforcement back decades. Defendants’ Motion for Stay should be denied.”

The brief was submitted to the United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit in the case of Massachusetts Fair Housing Center; National Fair Housing Alliance v. Department of Housing and Urban Development. Senator Gillibrand was joined by Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Patty Murray (D-WA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Mark Warner (D-VA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Edward Markey (D-MA), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Tina Smith (D-MN), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Peter Welch (D-VT), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), and Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD).

Senator Gillibrand has repeatedly held the Trump administration and HUD accountable for their failures on fair housing:

In August, she wrote to HUD urging the Trump administration to immediately rescind the FY25 and FY26 Notices of Funding Opportunity for the Fair Housing Initiatives Program (FHIP), which are the subject of this court case, and instead re-issue NOFOs consistent with the law and congressional intent.

Earlier this year, she secured $86 million for fair housing programs, including $56 million for FHIP, when negotiating the Fiscal Year 2026 funding bill to support the critical work fair housing organizations do in New York and across the country. The Trump administration proposed eliminating FHIP entirely.

Last year, she called out HUD for its failures to enforce our nation’s fair housing laws – a letter HUD has still not responded to nearly one year later.

Last year, she led Senate Democrats in pushing HUD to halt plans to overhaul a key homelessness program, which could have forced nearly 200,000 people back onto the streets. In May, she called out HUD Secretary Scott Turner over his failure to show measurable progress on housing affordability and to release HUD’s long-overdue report on homelessness data. Two weeks later, the administration released the report.

Full text of the argument in the brief can be viewed here.

title: Grassley-Backed Legislation to Improve Taxpayer Service Advances

title: Grassley, Lee, Collins Call on Trump Administration to Issue Emergency Scheduling Order for 7-OH, Initiate Permanent Scheduling Proceedings for Kratom
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and U.S. Sens. Mike Lee (R-Utah) and Susan Collins (R-Maine) are urging the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to take immediate action to protect Americans from deadly kratom and related semi-synthetic substances.

Specifically, the senators are requesting the Trump administration:

Immediately issue the emergency scheduling order for 7-hydroxy mitragynine (7-OH).

Permanently place all harmful substances found in kratom, including 7-OH, MGM-15, MGM-16 and mitragynine psyeudoindoxyl, into Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, meaning they have no accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse.

Develop a permanent scheduling recommendation for the full kratom plant and its derivatives.

“We frequently hear from constituents and concerned parents who have lost loved ones, and recovering users who warn us constantly about the addictive nature of kratom and its analogues. We worry the availability of these products is providing consumers with a false sense of security because they are readily available and marketed as natural,” the lawmakers wrote. “It is imperative that the final emergency scheduling order for 7-OH be expeditiously promulgated.”

“We urge DEA, in consultation with FDA, to initiate proceedings to permanently schedule all harmful substances found in kratom, including 7-OH, MGM-15, MGM-16, and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl. Furthermore, we urge the Food and Drug Administration to conduct the necessary scientific and medical evaluations of these substances and provide a permanent scheduling recommendation to the Drug Enforcement Administration for the full kratom plant, its derivatives, and all levels of the semi-synthetic analogues like mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, MGM-15, and MGM-16 that are being marketed as natural products,” the lawmakers concluded.

Read the full letter HERE.

Background:

Kratom is an unregulated substance – sold across the country as an over-the-counter energy booster, mood lifter or pain reliever – that is known to be approximately 14 times more potent than morphine when given orally. Kratom-derived concentrates and semi-synthetic analogues, including 7-OH, have been identified by the DEA as more potent than schedule II opioids. The FDA warns Americans not to consume kratom due to severe health effects, including liver toxicity, seizures and substance abuse disorder.

According to the National Drug Early Warning System and National Poison Data System, suspected nonfatal overdose encounters involving 7-OH, mitragynine or kratom were recorded across 38 states from 2023 to 2026. Further, between 2015 and 2025, poison control centers received 14,449 kratom exposure reports, with a 1,200% increase in exposure reports over the last 10 years. Kratom-related exposures in Iowa have increased approximately 120% from 2023 to 2025.

title: Grassley Welcomes Expanded Farm Safety Net Support Under Republicans’ Working Families Tax Cuts Act
text:
USDA launches “Farmers First” page to streamline resources for Rural America

BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) is welcoming major updates in the farm safety net from Republicans’ Working Families Tax Cuts Act which are expanding support for family farmers across Iowa.

This month, family farmers will begin receiving $13.8 billion in benefits through the Agriculture Risk Coverage (ARC) and Price Loss Coverage (PLC) programs, more than double what farmers were expected to receive before Republicans enacted the Working Families Tax Cuts Act. These historic improvements will help producers better protect against economic uncertainty and market volatility, so they can continue to feed and fuel the world while keeping family farms in the family.

The law also strengthened the farm safety net by increasing reference prices, modernizing payment limitations and allowing for the addition of up to 30 million new base acres nationwide. This base-acre increase is the first in 20 years. More information on how the Working Families Tax Cuts Act is delivering for Iowa family farmers can be found HERE or on the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) “Farmers First” webpage.

“Republicans strengthened the farm safety net through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act to stand with Rural America. Democrats didn’t lift a finger to support this bill – in fact, they fought tooth and nail to try and stop farmers from receiving this critical funding. Democrats in the Senate also voted against the Farm Bill that would deliver additional relief for the ag economy. Thankfully, family farmers will continue to feel the benefits from Republicans' historic legislation, and I’m going to keep working to bring down input costs and make life more affordable for Iowans,” Grassley said.

Background:

In addition to expanding the ARC and PLC programs, USDA is implementing additional provisions in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act that strengthen support for farmers. This includes making crop insurance more affordable and expanding access to standing disaster programs, such as the Emergency Assistance for Livestock, Honeybees and Farm-Raised Fish Program (ELAP) and the Livestock Forage Program (LFP).

title: PASSED THE SENATE: Hassan Bill to Help More Businesses Provide Child Care to Employees
text:
WASHINGTON – Legislation led by U.S. Senators Maggie Hassan (D-NH) and Dan Sullivan (R-AK) to help more businesses and working families access federal child care tax benefits recently passed the Senate. The Child Care Tax Benefit Outreach and Assistance Act would create a Business Child Care Liaison at the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to help more businesses take advantage of existing federal child care tax incentives that are underutilized. The bill now heads to the House for consideration.

In June, the U.S. Congress Joint Economic Committee – Minority, of which Senator Hassan serves as the Ranking Member, issued a report that calculated that a sample business could save $820,000 over 5 years using the credits, and a parent working for the company could save nearly $10,000 on child care costs.

“Child care costs are crushing working families across the country and making it harder for businesses to find and retain the workforce that they need. Federal child care tax incentives can help businesses better support working families by lowering the cost of providing child care, but too often, businesses do not know that these incentives are available,”said Senator Hassan. “This commonsense, bipartisan bill will help cut through the confusion around federal child care tax incentives, increase awareness among businesses about these incentives, and make it easier for Granite State businesses and employers across the country to invest in the child care that their employees need to stay in the workforce. I am pleased to see this pass the Senate and urge my House colleagues to support it so that it can be signed into law.”

“Quality child care is not only essential for the well-being of families, it is also key to a thriving economy and a strong workforce,” said Senator Sullivan. “I hear repeatedly from Alaska parents that the lack of affordable child care is one of their top concerns, and the data backs that up. Sixty-one percent of Alaskans are living in communities classified as child care ‘deserts,’ and too many families struggle to find reliable, affordable care close to home. This legislation will help employers, providers, and other nonprofits better utilize federal tools for employees—specifically the significant expansion of federal incentives in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act for child care facilities and the provisions that expand opportunities and support for working families. It was great to see this important legislation pass the Senate, and I look forward to seeing this bipartisan bill advance through the House and signed into law.”

Federal tax incentives designed to help businesses provide child care benefits are underutilized, even as working parents across the country struggle with the cost and availability of child care. Greater utilization of these incentives by businesses could help expand access to child care for many working families – and help more businesses hire and retain workers. The bipartisan Hassan-Sullivan legislation would direct the IRS to appoint a Business Child Care Liaison who would be responsible for building relationships between the child care sector and business community, coordinating with other federal agencies to help employers use child care tax incentives, and identify and recommend to Congress potential legislative and administrative changes to improve the utilization of these incentives.

Senator Hassan leads several bipartisan efforts to help more families access and afford child care. She introduced the bipartisan After Hours Child Care Act to improve access to affordable child care for parents working nontraditional hours. Additionally, Senator Hassan helped introduce the Child Care for Working Families Act, which would cap child care costs at 7 percent of a family’s income, make high-quality preschool universally accessible for all 3-and 4-year olds, and increase wages for early childhood workers.

title: Heinrich Joins Jake Tapper on CNN To Discuss How Bipartisan American Affordability & Jobs Act Will Hold Data Centers Accountable, Force Data Centers to Pay For Electricity Grid Upgrades
text:
Watch video here

ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, appeared on CNN’s The Lead with Jake Tapper today where he discussed his landmark legislation that will hold data centers accountable for the costs they impose on the electricity grid, helping to ensure families and small businesses aren’t stuck footing the bill. Heinrich also discussed reports of a deadly illness at a research facility in Russia.

“In the permitting bill, that we just released text on a little over a week ago, we mandate that [data centers] have to pay for both the electricity and for any grid upgrades. And we prohibit passing those costs along to average ratepayers, be those residential customers or small businesses,” said Heinrich.

VIDEO: U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, discusses with CNN’s Jake Tapper his landmark legislation that will hold data centers accountable for the costs they impose on the electric grid and reports of a suspected plague exposure at a research facility in Russia, October 7, 2026.

On Heinrich’s Bill to Make Data Centers Pay their Fair Share of Grid Costs:

Jake Tapper: “Senator, you're also the top Democrat on the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. And I don't need to tell you the debate over data centers is huge — especially on your Committee. You're pushing to make data center owners pay for the electricity that their buildings require, and not families who live nearby. How would you do that?”

Senator Heinrich: “Well, actually, in the permitting bill, that we just released text on a little over a week ago, we mandate that [data centers] have to pay for both the electricity and for any grid upgrades. And we prohibit passing those costs along to average ratepayers, be those residential customers or small businesses.”

For more information on Heinrich’s landmark legislation to require data centers to fully pay for costs they create, click here.

On Reports of a Deadly Illness at a Research Facility in Russia:

Heinrich: “We have a long history of Russia kind of coloring outside the lines, going all the way back to the Soviet Union. I would be very concerned if this were an engineered pathogen. I don't have any unique information saying that is the case. But if it were the case, that would be cause for alarm. And, you know, one of the things that I think is incredibly important that's related is just the fact that we have a CDC right now in the United States that is sort of running on fumes. Between the Trump administration and the actions of DOGE here a little over a year ago, the CDC is just simply not the agency that it should be for things like surveillance for any kind of international pathogen. And so, I'm not going to add fuel to that fire, but certainly I would be deeply concerned if we were to learn of any sort of engineered pathogen.”

“In the short term, what I'd really like to see is a hand-in-glove approach between Russia and the World Health Organization. That would tell us a lot. I want to know what tests were administered to the lab worker. What were the results of those tests? You know, if this were the plague, that would actually assuage a lot of my concerns because we all know how to deal with the plague. We've been dealing with the plague for hundreds of years. Even, even pneumonic plague is something that, because it has a relatively short incubation period, we know precisely how to intervene. If it's something else, then that, that is the concern that I think a lot of people are expressing.”

title: Hickenlooper, Colleagues Urge U.S. Department of Agriculture and U.S. Forest Service to Protect National Forests
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper, Martin Heinrich, Jeff Merkley, Alex Padilla, Jacky Rosen, Ben Ray Luján, Catherine Cortez Masto, Chris Van Hollen, Ruben Gallego, and Dick Durbin urged U.S. Department of Agriculture Under Secretary Michael Boren and U.S. Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz to maintain consistent environmental protections and local input mechanisms in any attempted revision of the 2005 Travel Management Rule.

“For years, the current rule has successfully balanced the use of motorized vehicles with other uses on public lands—ensuring that motorized use in our forests is managed responsibly, centering forest-level decision-making with state and local input, and protecting the environment,” the senators wrote. “Many of the proposed changes in the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s recently published Notice of Intent (NOI) would significantly alter the overarching framework that protects our lands and waters and supports our nation’s wildlife, clean water, and outdoor recreation economy.”

The letter identifies six core principles that the administration should maintain in any revisions to the 2005 Travel Management Rule:

Provide Meaningful Guidance that Helps Avoid Environmental Impacts;

Center State, Tribal, and Local Input;

Consider Impacts to All Types of Recreation and Uses;

Ensure Adequate Resources for Maintaining all Open Trails and Roads;

Continue to Provide Clear Information; and

Maintain Flexibility that Incorporates Public Input

“We urge the Forest Service to approach these revisions with those principles in mind and to work closely with Congress, Tribal Nations, State and local governments, and the broad range of stakeholders that depend on our national forests. We stand ready to work with you to ensure that any final rule gives land managers the tools to keep our forests accessible, safe, and healthy for generations to come,” the senators concluded.

Hickenlooper has been a consistent advocate for the preservation and expansion of public land protections. The senator introduced the Sarvis Creek Wilderness Completion Act to expand the Sarvis Creek Wilderness Area in the Routt National Forest by 6,817 acres. Hickenlooper is also a cosponsor of the CORE act which would protect approximately 420,000 acres of public land in Colorado, establish new wilderness areas, and safeguard existing outdoor recreation opportunities.

Full text is available HERE and below:

Dear Under Secretary Boren and Chief Schultz:

We write to highlight key issues and principles regarding the Administration’s proposed revision of the 2005 Travel Management Rule. For years, the current rule has successfully balanced the use of motorized vehicles with other uses on public lands—ensuring that motorized use in our forests is managed responsibly, centering forest-level decision-making with state and local input, and protecting the environment. Many of the proposed changes in the U.S. Department of

Agriculture’s recently published Notice of Intent (NOI) would significantly alter the overarching framework that protects our lands and waters and supports our nation’s wildlife, clean water, and outdoor recreation economy.

Our national forests serve a wide range of users, including hunters, anglers, hikers, horseback riders, motorized recreationists, livestock operators, outfitters, and local communities. Based on more than twenty years of experience with the Travel Management Rule in place, we know that these uses can coexist when travel management decisions are made thoughtfully and with meaningful input from the people who know these landscapes best. The 2005 Travel Management Rule was developed to allow motorized use within our national forests as a form of recreation while avoiding conflicts among users, damage to wildlife habitat or water resources, disturbance to cultural resources, and the need for new maintenance. Two decades later, these priorities are more critical than ever.

For these reasons, we urge you to ensure that any revisions to the 2005 Travel Management Rule maintain the following core principles:

Provide Meaningful Guidance that Helps Avoid Environmental Impacts: For over 20 years, the Travel Management Rule has provided a framework that helps protect fish and wildlife habitat, riparian areas, water quality, and cultural resources. The Administration’s proposal to presume that routes are open, unless required to be closed, could lead to networks of user-created trails—with significant implications for wildlife, water, and vegetation. We urge the administration to examine the types of environmental impacts that the 2005 Rule responded to, and ensure that any final rule minimizes negative impacts to habitat and ecosystems across the National Forest System.

Center State, Tribal, and Local Input: Travel management decisions should continue to be informed by robust public engagement and local input. Communities, Tribal Nations, recreationists, permittees, and other stakeholders should have a meaningful say in how they access and use their public lands. The 2005 Travel Management Rule ensures that Forest Service designations of trails and routes happen close-to-the-ground with robust local input. This core tenet should be maintained. Coordination with state and Tribal wildlife managers is particularly essential to benefit species and to support hunting access.

Consider Impacts to All Types of Recreation and Uses: Durable, well-informed travel management decisions are critical to sustaining America’s $1.3 trillion outdoor recreation economy. The existing Travel Management Rule has helped reduce conflicts between public land uses such as camping, hiking, hunting, and grazing. Many visitors to our National Forests wish to recreate in a quiet, non-motorized environment; a Travel Management Rule that helps avoid conflicts between uses will ultimately benefit our outdoor recreation economy.

Ensure Adequate Resources for Maintaining all Open Trails and Roads: The Forest Service should consider the long-term cost of properly maintaining, staffing, and administering its transportation system before adding new routes or expanding motorized use. Expanding the system without the resources necessary to maintain it would risk increasing the already significant road and trail maintenance backlog.

Continue to Provide Clear Information: The agency should continue to clearly identify where motorized travel is permitted. Clear designations, accurate Motor Vehicle Use Maps, user education, adequate signage, and reasonable enforcement are essential for visitors, land managers, and our natural resources. We support using technology to improve public access to information, including continued modernization and digitization of Motor Vehicle Use Maps.

Maintain Flexibility that Incorporates Public Input: Individual routes may warrant

reconsideration where local conditions justify it. The current rule allows for

modifications to the road and trail system through a public process and requires annual updates to the Motor Vehicle Use Maps. We believe this public input is essential to maintain.

We urge the Forest Service to approach these revisions with those principles in mind and to work closely with Congress, Tribal Nations, State and local governments, and the broad range of stakeholders that depend on our national forests. We stand ready to work with you to ensure that any final rule gives land managers the tools to keep our forests accessible, safe, and healthy for generations to come.

title: ICYMI: Hickenlooper Meets with Coloradans, Talks Food & Energy Affordability
text:
WASHINGTON – Yesterday, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper called out Trump administration policies that are increasing costs across the Denver Metro area. He stopped at Aurora’s Ahorra Mucho Supermercado for a roundtable discussion with grocers and locals about the impact of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) cuts and rising grocery prices. He then spoke to Coloradans in Globeville struggling with rising energy bills as a result of supply-chain disruptions from the War in Iran.

In Aurora, Hickenlooper toured Ahorra Mucho before sitting down with local grocers and community members to discuss grocery prices, which are up over 4% since the beginning of 2025, with some items like beef and coffee up over 16%. Hickenlooper has been a staunch opponent of Republican SNAP cuts, which have kicked 34,000 Coloradans off SNAP, including 13,000 children. He has led the charge against new provisions that require states to spend more of their state budgets to cover SNAP benefits and administrative costs associated with them.

In Denver, Hickenlooper hosted a discussion with residents and energy assistance leaders to hear how soaring energy bills are hitting Colorado families, as Trump’s Iran war and growing demand push costs higher. Residents voiced concerns about footing the bill for data centers and electricity costs continuing to rise right as Coloradans struggle with growing inflation.

Hickenlooper noted his strong support for full funding levels for energy assistance programs like the Low Income Home Energy Affordability Program (LIHEAP), which provides funding for Colorado’s Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP).
