title: Husted, Capito visit Centrus to discuss Ohio’s future in nuclear energy
text:
“This plant is creating good-paying Ohio jobs close to home for people in Piketon, strengthening our domestic nuclear fuel supply and helping position Ohio at the center of America’s nuclear future.”

WATCH HERE.

PIKETON, Ohio – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) today joined U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee Chairman Shelley Moore Capito in Piketon to tour Centrus and discuss Ohio’s future in nuclear energy.

“I’m glad to host Senator Capito here in Ohio to see firsthand the work being done at Centrus to rebuild America’s nuclear fuel supply. Centrus is the only U.S.-owned company currently enriching uranium with American technology right here in Piketon. This plant is creating good-paying Ohio jobs close to home for people in Piketon, strengthening our domestic nuclear fuel supply and helping position Ohio at the center of America’s nuclear future. I’ll keep working to expand this operation, grow our workforce and make sure Ohio is leading the way in American energy production,” said Husted.

“It was a pleasure to join Senator Husted here at Centrus Energy’s American Centrifuge Plant in Piketon, Ohio to see how federal investments in nuclear energy are transforming Ohio’s energy landscape. Through his work on the Environment and Public Works Committee, Senator Husted has been a strong advocate for nuclear energy as we’ve worked hard to reduce regulatory burdens and permitting inefficiencies so that we can deploy clean, reliable nuclear energy in Ohio and across the country,” said Capito.

In late 2023, Centrus began uranium enrichment operations at the American Centrifuge Plant in Piketon, Ohio—the first U.S.-owned, U.S.-technology enrichment plant to start production since 1954. Under contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), Centrus is pioneering production of High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium (HALEU) in Piketon.

HALEU is an advanced nuclear fuel that can power many next-generation nuclear reactors. Establishing a domestic supply of HALEU will help reduce America’s reliance on foreign sources of nuclear fuel and strengthen the U.S. nuclear energy supply chain.

In January 2026, Husted announced that the DOE will invest $2.7 billion to strengthen domestic enrichment services over the next ten years. This funding includes $900 million for Centrus Energy’s American Centrifuge Plant in Piketon, Ohio.

This announcement came after Husted sent two letters to the DOE in support of funding for the plant. In April and September 2025, he joined colleagues in writing to DOE Secretary Chris Wright, advocating for the American Centrifuge Plant and domestically produced uranium enrichment.

title: Kelly, Gallego Push to Protect Head Start Services for Arizona Families
text:
Arizona Senators urge the Department of Health and Human Services to not dilute quality, requirements for the Head Start Program

Today, Arizona Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego called on the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to protect the quality of Head Start services that more than 16,000 Arizona children and their families rely on.

In a letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Assistant Secretary Alex J. Adams, Kelly and Gallego raised concerns about a proposed rule, “Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs,” that would remove federal requirements for classroom sizes, instruction, and health screenings. The senators urged HHS to preserve standards that help ensure Arizona children receive quality early education and care.

“Head Start offers a place to learn, build relationships, and receive care during years that are important to a child’s development,” the senators wrote. “These programs are an important part of Arizona communities and give families in need the support they may struggle to find or afford.”

In Arizona, Head Start and Early Head Start serve 16,172 children across 332 program sites, providing early education, meals, and health services at no cost to families. These programs also help parents maintain employment and continue their education, with 76 percent of Head Start parents working, attending school, or participating in job training.

Head Start and Early Head Start is especially important to communities where families have few child care options — including rural Arizona. There the programs provide about 17 percent of child care and serve 1,943 children eligible for services under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, 1,291 children experiencing homelessness, and 459 children in foster care statewide.

The senators also included letters from Arizona elected officials and organizations to highlight their concerns and show the importance of the Head Start program, including the Office of the Governor of Arizona and the Arizona Head Start Association, among others.

“We urge the Department to carefully review the enclosed letters and work with Arizona organizations to address their concerns before moving forward with changes to the program. Head Start is essential to thousands of Arizona families, and any changes must protect the quality of the education and services they receive,” the senators concluded.

Kelly also joined today 38 Senate colleagues to highlight the national impact of the proposed rule’s changes on children, educators, and families.

title: Lankford in Washington Examiner: “The world of Oct. 8: Where antisemitism didn’t just return — it became trendy”
text:
OKLAHOMA CITY, OK — US Senator James Lankford (R-OK), co-chair of the Senate Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, today marked the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attacks in a new Washington Examiner column analyzing the rise of antisemitism since the attacks and the need to confront it wherever it appears. You can read it below or find it HERE.

The world of Oct. 8: Where antisemitism didn’t just return — it became trendy

By: James Lankford

Wednesday marks the three-year anniversary of one of the most brutal terrorist attacks in history: the deadly Oct. 7, 2023, attacks. Hamas terrorists flooded into Israel and murdered over 1,200 innocent Jewish men, women, and children, including 46 Americans. In addition to the death toll, Hamas captured and tormented 254 hostages, among them 12 Americans.

On Oct. 7, the world united against the horrors of antisemitism. Across the globe, people posted messages such as “Pray for Israel” and “We stand with Israel.” However, by the next morning, antisemitic propaganda was already flooding social media and college campuses around the country. People took to the streets to celebrate the “liberation” of Israel. A speaker at a rally in Philadelphia proclaimed, “I think that we should all give an applause right now to Hamas for a job well done,” and a rally in New York City chanted, “Globalize the intifada” and “smash the settler Zionist state.”

Within a few weeks of the Oct. 7 slaughter, it inexplicably became trendy on the political Left and the supposed “New Right” to say dumb and violent things about Jews and Israel. The rhetoric exceeded well beyond simple disagreement with the political or military decisions of the Israeli government. Without question, the U.S. Constitution protects the right of people in America to say epically dumb things. The Constitution also protects my right to call their rhetoric what it is — racist, ignorant, and antisemitic.

Hatred isn’t new for the Jewish people. For thousands of years, they have suffered racism, slavery, and genocide. From Egyptian slavery to Haman, Roman Occupation, the pogroms, and the Holocaust, irrational hatred toward Jewish people has persisted over millennia. But, in a more educated American society, you would hope that the lessons of the past would be applied and the scourge of antisemitism would finally end. That may be so someday, but today the social media algorithm teaches people to join in the centuries-old bias. We still have hope delayed.

Earlier this year, I visited Auschwitz-Birkenau, where Jews were unloaded from trains and sent to their death. I walked through the muddy streets that day and saw the evidence of the atrocities at the death wall and the crematoria. Hitler and his Nazi apparatus spread their vile antisemitic propaganda, then murdered 6 million Jews and absurdly declared that their brutality was justified because the Jews were “the problem.”

We are now living in the world of Oct. 8, where antisemitism is growing, and antisemitic incidents involving harassment, assault, and vandalism are more frequent now than they were before Oct. 7, 2023. Recent data from the FBI’s 2025 Hate Crimes Report shows that more than 62% of religiously-motivated hate crimes in 2025 targeted Jewish Americans — more than any other religious group. 2025 was the third-highest year of anti-Jewish hate crimes on record.

How we talk about antisemitism matters for the next generation. A recent study found that a single classroom lesson for middle and high school students on antisemitism reduces their willingness to agree with antisemitic tropes. Fact-based education matters in a free society. If you want to dive deeper into the past and help your classroom or family explore the consequences of antisemitism, the United States Holocaust Museum has excellent free online videos, visuals, and teaching materials. The deceit online needs a good dose of truth.

As a Christian and the co-chairman of the Senate Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, it is my mission to work for justice for all people. I collaborate with my colleagues, law enforcement, the White House, federal agencies, state and local governments, educators, advocates, and clergy against irrational Jewish hatred. In the Oct. 8 world, we each have the responsibility to call out antisemitism wherever we see it, to defend human dignity, and to speak out for the inherent right of religious liberty for all people.

title: Luján, Bennet, Ansari, Padilla, Hickenlooper, Schiff Introduce Legislation to Protect Public Lands and Taxpayers from Orphaned Oil and Gas Wells
text:
Santa Fe, N.M. – U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) joined U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, U.S. Representative Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.), and U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) to introduce the Stop Orphaned Wells Act, legislation that would prevent oil and gas companies from abandoning oil wells on public lands, a practice that shifts well cleanup costs from oil and gas companies to the American taxpayer.

“In New Mexico and across the country, abandoned wells pose serious environmental harm and threaten the health of our communities,” said Senator Luján. “We must ensure that oil and gas companies are held accountable and that taxpayers are not on the hook for the cost of cleanup. I’ve long fought to address abandoned wells, including championing the REGROW Act that was passed into law, and continue to work to ensure we identify and plug the thousands of abandoned wells nationwide. That’s why I’m cosponsoring this legislation to prevent companies from abandoning their wells and help reduce the number of abandoned wells in New Mexico and across the country.”

“For too long, taxpayers have footed the bill to clean up abandoned wells after companies walk away from their responsibilities,” said Senator Bennet. “As the Trump administration moves to weaken the safeguards that hold companies accountable, Congress must protect taxpayers and the public lands that power Colorado’s outdoor economy, while making sure oil and gas companies pay the cost of cleanup, rather than Colorado’s future generations.”

“Trump asked oil and gas executives to bankroll his campaign with a $1 billion contribution in exchange for a big payback. Meanwhile, Americans are left footing the bill for the damage they leave behind,” said Representative Ansari. “Orphaned wells threaten our water, wildlife, and air. I’m proud to lead the effort alongside Senator Bennet to make the oil and gas industry clean up its own mess. Our bill would ensure oil and gas companies pay to clean up the wells they abandon.”

Until 2024 when the Biden administration added agency rules, oil and gas fiscal assurance requirements were minimal, leading companies to abandon wells instead of remediating the land after drilling. The Trump administration is now rolling back these essential protections for public lands and American taxpayers. Nationwide, there are currently over 140,000 documented orphaned wells, including more than 15,000 on federal lands, and hundreds of thousands more that may be orphaned. Additionally, the number of documented orphaned wells in the United States has more than doubled since 2020. These sites are not only a significant liability for taxpayers and a growing threat to water resources, air quality, wildlife habitat, and private lands, but also jeopardize public health, ecosystems, grazing lands, outdoor recreation sites, and cultural resources that are at high risk from contamination. The Stop Orphaned Wells Act would ensure operators, not taxpayers, pay for cleanups and aligns directly with the interests of Western voters, nearly 9 in 10 of whom believe oil and gas companies should cover reclamation costs once drilling ends.

“Across California, there are over 5,000 orphaned oil wells that pose a threat to the health and safety of our communities and the environment,” said Senator Padilla. “When wells are left abandoned, drinking water is polluted, greenhouse gases are emitted, and the climate crisis is accelerated. This bill will help ensure orphaned oil and gas wells are plugged so Californians and communities across the country are protected from toxic emissions and contaminated air and water.”

“Abandoned wells put Colorado communities in danger,” said Senator Hickenlooper. “As Governor, we capped as many of these wells as we could, and that work continues here in the Senate, where we’re protecting taxpayers from getting stuck with the bill. Capping wells creates jobs and lowers pollution. It’s a win-win.”

“Oil companies can’t just walk away from abandoned oil and gas wells and leave taxpayers to bear the cleanup costs,” said Senator Schiff. “I’m joining Senator Bennet and other colleagues to make sure that Big Oil is responsible for cleaning up their messes. Americans should not have to deal with the consequences of an oil company’s negligence.”

“When an oil and gas company goes bankrupt, New Mexicans shouldn’t be the ones left to pick up the tab for cleanup costs,” said Senator Heinrich. “Right now, the Trump administration is making it easier for these companies to walk away without enough money set aside to clean up their wells. The Stop Orphaned Wells Act ensures that companies set aside money to meet their cleanup responsibilities, so taxpayers aren’t left paying the bill.”

Senator Luján has long fought to identify and remediate abandoned gas and oil wells. Senators Luján’s REGROW Act was adopted in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and put skilled energy workers back to work to plug abandoned wells. Additionally, Senator Luján has introduced the bipartisan Abandoned Well Remediation Research and Development Act (AWRRDA) to identify and remediate abandoned gas and oil wells, which can leak methane, contaminate groundwater, and create community safety risks.

This legislation is supported by 20 organizations, including Earthjustice Action, Colorado Fiscal Institute, Conservatives for Responsible Stewardship, Conservation Colorado, Montana Wildlife Federation, National Parks Conservation Association, Natural Resources Defense Council, Nevada Wildlife Federation, New Mexico Wildlife Federation, Public Land Solutions, Rocky Mountain Wild, San Juan Citizen’s Alliance, Sierra Club, Taxpayers for Common Sense, Trout Unlimited, Western Colorado Alliance, Western Organization of Resource Councils, Western Resilience Center, Wild Montana, Wilderness Workshop, and The Wilderness Society. In addition, this legislation was endorsed by U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.

The text of the bill is available HERE. A summary of the bill is available HERE.

title: McConnell Statement on Third Anniversary of October 7th Attacks
text:
WASHINGTON, DC -- U.S Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY), issued the following statement on the third anniversary of the October 7th attacks:

“Three years on from October 7th, 2023, it is important to distinguish what that day was, and what it was not.

“The deadliest attempted genocide of Jews since the Holocaust was not merely a new chapter in some intractable ethnic squabble.

“The invasion of peaceful homes to slaughter infants, rape women, and bludgeon elders was not the desperate act of noble freedom fighters.

“The hiding of hostages for over two years in dark tunnels, built for terror, was not the behavior of legitimate belligerents seeking peace.

“On this solemn anniversary, it is more important than ever for America and her allies to maintain clear eyes about the true impediments to lasting security for Israel and its neighbors: the web of terror that links Hamas, Hizballah, and fellow proxies with Iran, the architect of regional chaos.

“What more urgent call to remember and condemn the horrific violence of October 7th, 2023, than the emboldened anti-Semitism to which it has given license here at home? Jewish Americans, for their part, will remember which leaders made excuses for the deranged crowds chanting in the streets for the eradication of the world’s only Jewish state, and which ones declined to condemn the cowardly reprobates cashing in on anti-Semitism online.

“I refuse to be one of them. I refuse to treat October 7th as anything but what it is: a sickening reminder of the oldest hatred the world has ever known, the responsibility to confront it, and the importance of a resilient Jewish state in a world bent on its destruction.”

title: Wyden, Merkley, Bonamici, Salinas, Hoyle, Dexter Announce $4.3 Million to Support Public Safety Across Oregon
text:
Programs in Gresham, Beaverton, Salem and Cottage Grove to benefit

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici, Andrea Salinas, Val Hoyle, and Maxine Dexter, today announced more than $4.3 million in federal awards to support public safety programs across Oregon.

“It is absolutely essential to ensure communities across Oregon are safe, and young people are able to get the support they need in times of crisis,” Wyden said. “These federal grants will help support local police agencies, youth support programs and resources for foster youth. I’ll keep fighting to secure the federal resources Oregon communities need to thrive and stay secure.”

“Every Oregon community needs the resources to keep young people safe, support children who have experienced abuse and neglect, and build stronger relationships between families and those who serve them,” said Merkley, who helped secure funding for these community-initiated projects as a senior member of the Senate Appropriations Committee. “These federal investments will expand mentorship and opportunities for young people, ensure children have access to critical advocacy and medical services, and strengthen public safety infrastructure in several communities across the state. I’ll keep fighting to bring these federal resources home to Oregon and support the local organizations working every day to make our communities safer.”

“Beaverton’s Behavioral Health Court is doing important work to help people with mental health challenges who encounter the justice system and put them on a path to recovery,” said Bonamici. “I’m grateful this grant will support this initiative, improve lives, and make our communities safer.”

“Investments in emergency response capabilities strengthen our communities,” said Hoyle. “This funding for the Cottage Grove Police Department will replace aging equipment and bolster our emergency preparedness, prioritizing public safety and making it easier for officers to do their jobs.”

“Every child deserves to be safe, cared for, and heard. I’m thrilled to have helped secure over $2 million to protect children across Oregon. Because of this funding, children who have experienced abuse or neglect will not have to navigate some of the hardest moments of their lives alone. They will have an advocate in their corner and a safe place to turn to when they need emotional or medical support. I’m proud to see these federal dollars coming home to support the people doing this vital work in our communities,” Salinas said.

“Our young people deserve to grow up safe, supported and hopeful about their future,” said Dexter, M.D. “I fought hard to bring this $1 million investment to Gresham because children deserve opportunities to succeed. This funding will connect them with mentors, workforce readiness and programs that prevent and reduce involvement in violent crime and strengthen public safety efforts for youth and families in East Multnomah County. Investing in our children makes Oregon stronger.”

The $4.3 million in federal awards from the Department of Justice’s Byrne Discretionary Community Project Grants program will be distributed as follows:

$1.05 million to the City of Gresham to expand the East Multnomah Outreach Prevention Intervention initiative to prevent and combat juvenile delinquency, reduce youth involvement in violent crime, and strengthen coordinated public safety efforts for youth and families in East Multnomah County.

$1 million to Liberty House in Salem to increase medical clinic services to children who are victims of abuse or neglect in Marion and Polk Counties.

$1.03 million to the Oregon CASA Network in Salem to support its work to provide foster children the advocacy and support of an assigned Court Appointed Special Advocate.

$500,000 to the City of Beaverton to support the Behavioral Health Court program that targets defendants with criminal cases in the Beaverton Municipal Court who are the top utilizers of legal, jail or emergency room services living in the Beaverton area.

$800,000 to the City of Cottage Grove to support modernizing the Cottage Grove Police Department fleet and communications infrastructure to facilitate a department-wide transition to community-oriented policing practices.

“This funding will support Court Appointed Special Advocate programs across the state in recruiting and retaining volunteers who provide advocacy, encouragement, and a sense of stability to children impacted by abuse and neglect,” said Stephanie Brown, State Director, Oregon CASA Network. “Our advocates are in every corner of the state, getting to know the unique needs of each child they serve, and advocating for them in court, in school, and in the community. We appreciate the efforts of our elected officials to make this valuable investment in Oregon’s future which will help many of the state’s most vulnerable reach their full potential.

“Recovery takes time, care and support,” said Beaverton Mayor Lacey Beaty. “Our Behavioral Health Court team understands that and helps participants get treatment and rebuild their lives. I’m proud of the work Judge Britton and her team do every day, and grateful to Senator Wyden and Congresswoman Salinas for supporting it. This investment will make a real difference for our neighbors and the safety of our community.”

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Welcomes More than 60 Florida Veterans to Washington, D.C. for Honor Flight
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.— Senator Ashley Moody recently welcomed a group of more than 60 Florida veterans taking part in an Honor Flight to the nation’s capital. Senator Moody met with the group at the Lincoln Memorial, thanking the men and women for their service to our country.

“Florida is home to some of the bravest men and women who answered the call to serve our nation. We will ensure their service will never be forgotten. I am grateful to welcome these heroes to Washington and to personally thank them for all they have done for our country,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

Florida is home to more than 1.4 million veterans, one of the largest populations in the nation.

Senator Moody is committed to fighting for U.S. military members and veterans.

When Senator Moody served as Florida’s Attorney General, she oversaw the Florida Military and Veterans Assistance Program to assist service members and their families who have been affected by scams.

Earlier this year, the Florida Veterans Foundation awarded Villages Honor Flight a $15,000 grant as part of its support for 10 Honor Flight hubs across Florida.

Honor Flights are special trips planned for veterans of America’s wars to travel to Washington, D.C. from across the country to visit the monuments of the respective wars they fought in and honor the service and sacrifice of the veterans and their loved ones.

Senator Moody is a proud supporter of the U.S. Armed Forces, veterans, and military families. Since becoming a United States Senator, Moody has:

Recently cosponsored the Veterans Bill of Rights Act. The Veterans Bill of Rights Act would require the U.S. Secretary of Veterans Affairs to ensure veterans are clearly informed of their existing rights regarding VA-administered health care, benefits, and services.

Cosponsored the Major Richard Star Act, which seeks to fix unjust disability policies for retired combat veterans;

Supported the Veterans Education and Technical Skills (VETS) Opportunity Act, which would expand educational benefits for veterans;

Supported the Restore VA Accountability Act of 2025, which would help ensure that only the most dedicated individuals can serve veterans;

Held a town hall with VA Secretary Collins in Tampa to discuss issues facing veterans;

Recognized 200 years of U.S. Navy presence in Pensacola and discussed the critical importance of the Navy and Coast Guard’s presence in the Florida Panhandle; and more.

Senator Moody recently joined the Senate Armed Services Committee.

Senator Moody is proud to be part of a military family.

title: Murphy Denied Access to Military Facility by Hegseth in Unprecedented Move, Meets with Saudi Crown Prince
text:
RIYADH, SAUDI ARABIA – As Saudi Arabia is under heightened security risk amid the Iran War, U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) issued the following statements after departing Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on a Congressional Delegation (CODEL) trip to the Middle East, where he also visited Doha, Qatar.

In an unprecedented move, the U.S. Department of Defense (DOD) under Secretary Pete Hegseth’s leadership denied Murphy access to the Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, despite decades of precedent for DOD supporting CODELs to American military bases under active threat to uphold Congress’s oversight duties. Prior to his CODEL, Murphy requested access to the base via a letter and direct appeal to U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) leadership to no avail. While DOD denied him access to U.S. military facilities, the U.S. Department of State supported Murphy’s trip to the region.

“This is one of our biggest and most important facilities in the Gulf region. I’ve been to the Middle East at least a dozen times as a Member of Congress, and I’ve never been denied access to military facilities. This is part of a coordinated, deliberate campaign by the Department of Defense to hide the consequences and the true costs of the Iran war,” said Murphy of the denial.

Murphy also met with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Saudi Arabia.

“I’ve been a vocal critic of Saudi Arabia and the Crown Prince. But, I think it’s important to be here to disagree and be honest and candid about those disagreements. It’s important to recognize there are things we need to work on together: ending the war in Iran and a pathway to Palestinian statehood. We had an honest, provocative conversation, particularly about the Gulf countries’ decisions to invest in the Trump family. It’s important for the Crown Prince to hear not just from the Trump Administration, but from people who want a different path,” said Murphy of the meeting.

Additionally, Murphy met with Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud; toured the damage done to the U.S. embassy in Riyadh; engaged with economic and cultural leaders; and talked with University of New Haven students at the first American university campus in Saudi Arabia, among other things.

In Qatar, Murphy met with His Highness the Emir of the State of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. Additionally, Murphy met with Ali Al Thawadi, Qatari Minister for Strategic Affairs and a key diplomat who coordinates U.S.-Iran shuttle diplomacy; Qatari royal and Qatar Foundation Vice Chair Sheikha Hind Al Thani in Education City to discuss the presence of American universities in Qatar; and Qatar Energy CEO Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi, among others.

Sen. Murphy is the first Democratic Senator to visit the Gulf since the start of the Iran War.

title: Government Watchdog: Trump Illegally Blocked Health Research Funding
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray, Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, issued the following statement on a Government Accountability Office (GAO) decision issued today, which concludes that President Trump and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. illegally impounded fiscal year 2025 funding for health research conducted by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) in violation of the Impoundment Control Act (ICA):

“This decision confirms what we’ve long known: President Trump lit health research funding on fire last year, and it’s clear as day he’s just done the same again this year. In fact, President Trump announced to the world just a few days ago that he was illegally cutting nearly $30 million more, and HHS has failed to detail to the Committee exactly how it has spent down AHRQ funding for fiscal year 2026.

“This is research that has saved tens of thousands of lives and saved billions of dollars in health care costs—but President Trump and Secretary Kennedy are intent on breaking the law to cut it off, and Republicans in Congress have all but let them do it. It’s past time Congress imposes real consequences on this administration for killing lifesaving health research—I’ll keep fighting to do just that.”

In its decision today, GAO concluded:

“Congress appropriated lump-sum amounts to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) to carry out various research initiatives for fiscal year 2025. .… We conclude that HHS withheld funds when it declined to obligate or expend more than $78 million of its FY 2025 appropriation before the close of the fiscal year. We further conclude that this withholding constituted an impoundment under the ICA rather than a programmatic delay. Because HHS did not submit a special message proposing to rescind AHRQ funds, HHS’s actions violated the ICA.”

GAO’s decision examines how the Trump administration illegally impounded fiscal year 2025 funding provided to AHRQ for health research after the Trump administration sabotaged the agency, pushing out 80% of all staff and cancelling grants en masse. It’s clear, however, that this administration has once again illegally withheld and misspent AHRQ funding provided by Congress for fiscal year 2026, as well. Senator Murray and Senator Tammy Baldwin, Ranking Member of the Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education Subcommittee, raised alarm bells about the fate of fiscal year 2026 AHRQ funds several weeks ago. Then, just days after HHS Deputy Secretary Nominee Chris Klomp vowed to senators that virtually all of the agency’s funding would be spent—while failing to provide details to back up that assertion—President Trump moved to permanently impound nearly $30 million in AHRQ funding in his “pocket rescission.” Republicans have repeatedly blocked Democrats’ efforts to prevent presidents from attempting to use “pocket rescissions.”

title: Murray on Trump and Duffy’s Plans to Tie Transit Funding to Birth Rates
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray, Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, released the following statement after the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) proposed new guidance for the Capital Investment Grants (CIG) program that would increase funding for projects based on their region’s average birth and marriage rates compared to the nationwide averages. The CIG program funds infrastructure investments to expand public transit—including for bus transit and light rail and commuter rail improvements. Under the new proposal, the FTA would steer more grant funding to parts of the country where only more men and women choose to get married and more babies are born—providing an up to 10% boost.

“Tying funding for transit projects to marriage rates and how many babies a woman has is the sort of bizarre and dystopian idea you’d expect in a TV show, not actual policy put forth by the U.S. government—yet here we are. President Trump wants to weaponize federal grants to wage his backward culture wars and punish Democrats, and it’s past time Republicans join us to stand against this historically corrupt administration’s efforts to rob our communities of resources they are owed—because it’s already clear as day they are holding up projects in blue states while moving ahead with projects elsewhere.”

The new proposal would apply to 40 projects across the country already in the CIG program, forcing transit agencies and local and state governments that have already spent years planning and designing projects to follow a whole slew of new rating and cost-share requirements. This could force entities to re-design projects and re-do environmental reviews, which will increase costs and delay construction, and in the worst case potentially makes projects ineligible for CIG funding. The new requirements could reduce CIG funding for important transit projects below the 40% floor set by Congress in the annual funding bills, which has been in place since fiscal year 2020.

These significant changes to the CIG program are another attempt by the Trump administration to penalize blue states and slow down and delay transit projects. Recently, the Trump administration advanced a CIG project in a red state while it continues to hold back two projects in blue states that have been ready for much longer.

Studies conducted last year when the Department of Transportation issued an order updating its governing principles to include a general preference to communities with higher marriage and birth rates showed that such prioritization would disproportionally hurt low-income, non-white residents.

title: Senator Murray Launches Public Health for America Working Group to Determine What Comes Next After Trump & RFK Jr.
text:
A working group of leading national experts and Washington state public health leaders will develop a blueprint to build America’s public health system stronger, more resilient, and insulated from political interference

The efforts of the working group—listening sessions, roundtables, direct outreach to key stakeholders, and more—will inform new legislative proposals to help build and improve public health in America

Murray: “We can’t just put back what was there before… We have to build something that can’t be broken the next time someone decides science is inconvenient.”

NYT: A Public Health-Minded Senator Asks: What Comes After Trump and Kennedy?

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and a senior member and former Chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, announced the launch of the Public Health for America Working Group: an initiative to develop the ideas, safeguards, and legislation needed to build and improve the nation’s public health system after nearly two years of unprecedented attacks on the agencies, scientists, and institutions that save lives and keep Americans safe and healthy.

Since taking office, President Trump and Secretary Kennedy have taken unprecedented steps to politicize public health agencies, overrule experts, promote misinformation, and undermine trust in the nation’s public health infrastructure. Secretary Kennedy has fired thousands of federal public health experts–including a Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Director who refused to go along with his anti-vaccine views. Under Secretary Kennedy, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has halted promising research, taken down data for deadly diseases, refused to accurately report measles deaths, promoted false anti-vaccine information, and more. These steps have severely undermined public trust–with polls showing trust in CDC recommendations dropping from 77% to 50% over Trump’s first year in office this term.

The working group brings together some of the nation’s and Washington state’s most respected public health leaders to respond to these challenges. The mission of Murray’s working group is not simply to restore what existed before January 2025, but to design a public health system that is stronger, more resilient, and structurally protected from political interference—no matter who holds the White House or controls Congress.

Senator Murray on the announcement of the working group:

“In public health, we say an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. That’s not just true of disease, it’s also true of corruption, incompetence, and political interference—threats it is clear our system was simply not adequately prepared for.

“Right now, Trump and RFK Jr. have put our public health system on life support. The tragic evidence of their failures is overwhelming—foodborne outbreaks met by a sluggish response that resulted in fatalities, measles cases surging to new records, and causes of death scrubbed from agency data to try and mislead the public.

“As someone who has led the charge to strengthen our public health system, learn the lessons of the COVID-19 pandemic, and stop Trump and RFK Jr.’s sabotage—it is clear to me we have a big undertaking ahead. All of us who care about the future of public health need to come to grips with a hard reality—the system was underfunded, already stretched thin, and far too vulnerable to politics. And now, that system, and the public’s trust in it, is broken far beyond a simple repair.

“We can’t just put back what was there before. We need to make sure our future public health system is immune to political interference. We have to build something that can’t be broken the next time someone decides science is inconvenient. Public health policy can’t become a political football—it can’t shift drastically every four years based on political ideology, it has to be reliably grounded in science and facts.

“That’s why I’m bringing together some of the best minds in the country in this Working Group to help me chart a course for how Congress can build trust, protect science, and safeguard the health of all Americans. I am sincerely determined to talk to anyone and everyone about what comes next to rebuild public health in America.”

The Working Group will convene roundtables with researchers, providers, state, local, and Tribal health officials, and former career federal scientists; host public conversations on the future of public health; engage directly with communities and trusted messengers; and respond in real time as key public health decisions unfold. Its findings will inform nonpartisan policy proposals as Murray works to build consensus around legislation to build stronger public health infrastructure in America.

Members of the Working Group

Dr. Joshua M. Sharfstein – Distinguished Professor of the Practice in Health Policy and Management at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health; former Principal Deputy Commissioner of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration; former Secretary of the Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene; former Commissioner of the Baltimore City Health Department.

“Successful public health efforts help families to thrive, communities to flourish, and the nation to grow stronger,” said Dr. Joshua M. Sharfstein. “I very much look forward to developing a blueprint for a public health system that protects every American — and I thank Senator Murray for her leadership.”

Patty Hayes, RN, MN –Chair of the Washington State Board of Health; former Director of Public Health – Seattle & King County from 2014 to 2021, where she led the response to the nation’s first COVID-19 outbreak; former Assistant Secretary at the Washington State Department of Health.

“I am delighted to serve on this important working group with my colleagues,” said Patty Hayes. “Public Health must be there every day to address critical health issues alongside the health care system. As Chair of the WA State Board of Health, I see the impact of the politicization of public health and cuts to funding. Everyone counts on clean water, safe food, and a strong public health response when a crisis occurs. I want to thank Senator Murray’s for her continued leadership and willingness take on this critical issue.”

Dr. Jeffrey Levi – Professor Emeritus of Health Policy and Management at The George Washington University Milken Institute School of Public Health; former Executive Director of Trust for America’s Health; former Chair of the Advisory Group on Prevention, Health Promotion, and Integrative and Public Health; former Deputy Director of the Office of National AIDS Policy under the White House Domestic Policy Council.

“I am honored to work with Senator Murray and my colleagues on this critically important project,” said Dr. Jeffrey Levi. “Senator Murray is uniquely positioned to help bring about the transformational policies and investments along with the community engagement and partnership that will strengthen our nation’s public health system and restore the public’s trust.”

Dr. Helen Chu – Professor of Medicine and Epidemiology and Associate Dean for Research at the University of Washington Schools of Medicine of Public Health; led the Seattle Flu Study, which identified the first known case of community-spread COVID-19 in the United States in February 2020; served on the CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) untilSecretary Kennedy dismissed the committee’s entire membership in June 2025.

“I am honored to serve as part of this committee. As a physician and a scientist who has spent my career ensuring people have access to safe and effective vaccines, it has been a challenging few years to watch the public health systems that keep Americans safe be dismantled,” said Dr. Helen Chu. “I am very much looking forward to contributing expertise on vaccines, pandemic preparedness, and academic research to this committee, and helping to rebuild our public health systems for a better future.”

Dr. Vin Gupta –Pulmonologist and critical care physician; Distinguished Scholar at the University of Washington, Evans School; Senior Medical Analyst for MS NOW; Managing Director at Manatt Health; National Board Member of the American Lung Association; and Major in the U.S. Air Force Reserve Medical Corps.

“Public health works best when people can trust that the guidance they receive is grounded in evidence, communicated honestly, and protected from political interference,” said Dr. Vin Gupta. “This is an opportunity not simply to rebuild what has been lost, but to design a stronger and more durable system—one that earns public trust, prioritizes prevention, and is ready to protect every community when the next threat emerges. I’m grateful to Senator Murray for bringing together this group and honored to contribute to that work.”

Guiding Principles of the Working Group

The Working Group’s work will be organized around six principles:

Building a System the Public Trusts: Building public confidence in science and medicine through transparency, rigorous and unbiased data, honest communication, robust opportunities for public engagement, trusted local messengers, and real partnership to ensure public health serves all communities.

Science That Can’t Be Silenced: Building durable, enforceable guardrails so that decisions are based on high-quality evidence, expert advice, transparent processes, and public input — not political interference —no matter who controls the White House or Congress.

Prevention at the Core: Investing in prevention saves lives, and it saves money. The federal public health system should focus on prevention and work so all individuals and families have the opportunity to thrive by providing resources, education, and communication about preventing infectious and chronic disease.

Strong Public Health Everywhere: Modernizing federal public health agencies so they are stable, expert-driven, and accountable institutions that the American people can rely on. That includes supporting responsibilities uniquely suited to the federal government’s ability to solve complex challenges, while ensuring the federal government is a valuable partner by rebuilding local institutions and infrastructure through dedicated, stable funding tied to a core set of capabilities for state, local, Tribal, and territorial health departments, as well as reinstating the United States as a leader in global health security.

Ready for the Next Threat: Strengthening the systems that detect and respond to emergencies to make sure America is never caught flat-footed again—modern data and laboratory infrastructure that is interoperable, a surge-ready workforce, a resilient medical supply chain, strong global partnerships, and a cutting-edge biomedical research enterprise.

Health for All, Not Just Some: Guaranteeing that where you live and who you are doesn’t determine whether your health department can protect you. Public health communication and resources should work in cities, rural areas, Tribal nations, and every community in every part of America to ensure every person—no matter their race, income, or gender—has the same access to health information and services.

Background: Senator Murray’s Record on Public Health

Senator Murray has been one of Congress’s leading champions of public health for three decades, and has led the fight against the Trump administration’s dismantling of the nation’s health agencies from the start, including through his disastrous mishandling of the COVID-19 pandemic to his unprecedented elevation of RFK Jr., a well-known anti-vax conspiracy theorist who has decimated America’s public health infrastructure.

Standing up to Trump and RFK Jr.: Senator Murray forcefully opposed Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s nomination to lead HHS and has been one of the leading voices in Congress holding him accountable ever since. She has fought back against his purge of the CDC’s vaccine advisory committee, his mass firings of career scientists and public health experts, his cancellation of lifesaving research, and his sidelining of independent expert panels that Americans rely on for sound, evidence-based guidance. She has confronted Kennedy directly in multiple Senate HELP and Appropriations Committee hearings, led her colleagues in demanding he reverse actions that have left the nation less prepared for emerging outbreaks, and called for his firing multiple times after he ousted the CDC Director and drove the agency’s senior leadership to resign—a call she continues to reiterate loudly and consistently. Following RFK Jr.’s campaign of destruction at CDC, Senator Murray was supportive of many states, including Washington state, standing up for public health and forming their own regional health authorities—but emphasized that diseases don’t recognize borders, and there must be functioning and trustworthy leadership at the federal level.

Protecting public health funding as Appropriations Vice Chair: As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and former longtime top Democrat on the subcommittee that funds public health and medical research, Senator Murray successfully fought to ensure the fiscal year 2026 appropriations bills rejected President Trump’s proposal to cut CDC funding by more than half and slash medical research at NIH by nearly 40 percent, and she continues to push for robust funding of public health and infectious disease programs across all government funding bills. In fiscal year 2026, this included a $415 million increase for NIH research, including targeted increases for cancer research, Alzheimer’s disease, women’s health, and ALS, among others. Since Murray became the top appropriator of public health and medical research funds in 2015, she increased NIH funding by roughly $18 billion, or 60%. Within CDC, the fiscal year 2026 bill increased funding for the Public Health Infrastructure grant program by $10 million and also included a $10 million increase to data modernization to continue to help build state public health departments and their data infrastructure. It also included a $60 million increase for key programs supported by the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR) focused on increasing the nation’s stockpile of medical countermeasures and bolstering advanced research and development of select treatments and cures to ensure our health system is prepared to respond when disaster strikes.

Building the nation’s public health infrastructure: Senator Murray first introduced the Public Health Infrastructure Saves Lives Act (PHISLA)in 2019 and has reintroduced it most recently in July 2023. PHISLA would establish a dedicated program, ramping up to $4.5 billion annually, to fund a core set of capabilities at state, local, Tribal, and territorial health departments and end the “cycle of crisis and complacency” in public health funding. Murray’s bill represents the most comprehensive legislation to build up America’s public health infrastructure in Congress so far. While Murray continues to push for a landmark investment in public health infrastructure, in fiscal year 2022 she established the Public Health Infrastructure grant program at CDC with annual funding of $200 million, which Murray has since increased to $360 million in fiscal year 2026.

Strengthening pandemic preparedness: As Chair of the HELP Committee, Senator Murray authored and passed into law the bipartisan PREVENT Pandemics Act in 2022, which strengthened the nation’s public health and medical preparedness and response systems, authorized ARPA-H, and, among other provisions, required for the first time that the CDC Director be confirmed by the Senate. She previously helped lead reauthorization of the Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act and fought for emergency funding to respond to Ebola in 2014 and Zika in 2016.

Leading the response to COVID-19: When Washington state became the first epicenter of COVID-19, Senator Murray was among the first, and most insistent, in Congress to demand widespread testing and to introduce emergency paid sick leave legislation so workers could stay home without losing a paycheck—a provision later enacted in the Families First Coronavirus Response Act. Throughout the pandemic, she pressed the Trump Administration and its officials about the issues with their COVID-19 response from her position as HELP Ranking Member, later as HELP Chair, in addition to her bipartisan work on pandemic preparedness, she helped deliver the American Rescue Plan Act’s historic investments in public health, including $7.66 billion to hire and train public health workers.

Fighting political interference in science: During the first Trump administration, Senator Murray launched the “Save Our Science” Political Interference Tracker to document interference in the COVID-19 response, introduced the STOP Act to investigate political meddling at HHS’s scientific agencies, and joined Senators Warren and Peters in securing a Government Accountability Office (GAO) investigation into political interference at CDC and FDA. That GAO review found in 2022 that CDC, FDA, NIH, and ASPR had no procedures to define, report, or address political interference in scientific decision-making. Most recently, Murray secured language to prevent the Trump administration from implementing the Office of Management and Budget’s (OMB) proposed grants rule to politicize all federal grants, especially health and science grants, through the duration of the current continuing resolution. Murray also helped pressure the administration to back off its plan to draft an executive order that would give Russ Vought a veto over medical research grants.

Responding to public health threats in a bipartisan way: Murray has worked successfully for decades to fund and authorize key public health programs with her colleagues on both sides of the aisle. In recent years, bipartisan public health efforts were frequent and noncontroversial–as Ranking Member of the HELP Committee, Senator Murray co-led a bipartisan hearing on vaccine hesitancy and spoke about the importance of addressing vaccine skepticism and getting people the facts they need to keep their families and communities safe and healthy. Ahead of the hearing, as multiple states were facing measles outbreaks in under-vaccinated areas, Murray sent a bipartisan letter with former HELP Committee Chair Lamar Alexander (R-TN) pressing the CDC Director and HHS Assistant Secretary for Health on their efforts to promote vaccination and vaccine confidence. Senator Murray will continue to work to build broad-based consensus around any and all public health policies she champions.

Advancing prevention and biomedical research: As HELP Ranking Member, Senator Murray negotiated and passed the bipartisan 21st Century Cures Act in 2016, which delivered a major federal investment in biomedical research and clinical trials at the FDA and NIH. In 2018, Murray negotiated and helped pass the largest legislative response to the opioid crisis to date. In 2019, as the top Senate appropriator of public health funds, Murray helped secure the first dedicated federal funding for gun violence prevention research at CDC and NIH since the Dickey Amendment was enacted in 1996.

Strengthening global health response: Senator Murray is a leading voice on global health issues, emphasizing the importance of continuing the United States’ record of strong investments in global health security. Murray participated as a member of the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) Commission following its establishment in 2018, recognizing how global health security impacts families in Washington state, across the country, and across the world. Murray has consistently fought to promote global health programs and American leadership abroad, understanding that disease does not recognize borders. In 2025, Murray was vocal in her opposition to the decimation of USAID and American-funded global health programs that not only benefit our partners around the world, but also keep Americans safe.

title: ON THE JOB FOR MICHIGAN: Flint Leaders Discuss Storied History of Berston Field House, Highlight Peters’ Support for the Expansion & Renovation Project
text:
FLINT, MI – In a new “On the Job for Michigan” video from U.S. Senator Gary Peters’ (MI) office, community leaders in Flint highlight Peters’ support for the expansion and preservation of Berston Field House, a historic landmark and community center in north Flint. Efforts are currently underway to preserve the 100-year-old building, and Peters secured a $6.3 million federal investment to support the project earlier this year.

“You hear Berston, and you think about all these athletes and these others have come through here,” said James Avery, Executive Director of Berston Field House. “I think that's the memory I really have just continued to speak upon, is the history.”

“The big thing for me is that the community needs to see that something of this magnitude is theirs. That's a one stop shop of education, health, performing arts, athletics,” Avery continued.

“Berston has always been what we call, ‘The Mainstage,’” said Justus Thigpen Sr., former NBA Player and past Executive Director of Berston Field House.“I’ve been coming here ever since I was 10 years old, my dad taught me how to swim in the swimming pool that was here, everyone associates with Berston.”

Watch the “On the Job” video here.

“For more than a century, Berston Field House has been a gathering place for Flint residents. It’s important that this historic landmark continues to serve the community for generations to come,” said Peters. “I commend James Avery, Justus Thigpen Sr., and all the folks who are leading the charge on this revitalization project, and I was proud to be a federal partner in their efforts.”

The federal funding secured by Peters will support revitalization efforts, which include building renovations and construction of a new recreation center. In August, Peters kicked off his 2026 Motorcycle Tour at Berston Field House to celebrate the project and tour ongoing construction.

title: NEWS: Schiff, Padilla, and Carbajal Probe Corrupt Career Move as Former White House Energy Adviser that Fought to Reopen California Pipeline Takes Executive Position at Oil Company Pushing the Restart
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) and U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-Calif.-24) are seeking answers from former White House energy adviser Brittany Kelm who, after spending months advancing the interests of Sable Offshore Corporation’s (Sable) unlawful California project in her capacity at the White House, has now taken a top job as Vice President of Policy and Commercial Programs at Sable.

“To understand whether your transition directly from the White House and Department of Interior to Sable – including your work on Administration policies before you left office and at Sable on matters related to your role on the NEDC after your separation – complies with the federal ethics laws, we seek detailed information regarding your interactions with the company during your government service, as well as documents and communications about your recent hiring by and employment with the company,” the lawmakers wrote.

While at the White House, Kelm publicly championed and supported efforts to advance the restart of Sable’s pipeline in California, a project that has not been permitted under California law, has incurred fines, and had court orders against it. Sable CEO Jim Flores thanked Kelm for her work helping to restart the company’s oil production, a move the lawmakers argue is a violation of state law.

“These public statements leave the distinct impression that you were closely working on the Sable deal at a time when you could leverage the work you did advancing Sable’s business interests to secure private employment or other financial benefits from the very company you supported as a government official. To move from a high-level government office to its direct beneficiary, especially for the purpose of personal gain, is both ethically improper and potentially unlawful,” the lawmakers continued.

The lawmakers emphasize that “federal law prohibits any government employees from participating in any particular government matter, including permitting decisions, contracts, and other matters involving the interests of named parties, in which a company with whom they are seeking or negotiating for future employment has a financial interest.”

The lawmakers demand Kelm preserve all records of communications between her and Sable and question whether she received any ethics or conflicts of interest guidance.

Senator Schiff has been a strong opponent of restarting oil drilling off the California coast and has repeatedly pressed Sable for answers on the company’s collaboration with the Trump administration to invoke the Defense Production Act (DPA) in relation to this project.

The full text of the letter can be found hereand below.

Dear Ms. Kelm,

We write to you in your personal capacity to seek information related to your recent move from the White House’s National Energy Dominance Council (NEDC) to the oil industry as Vice President of Policy and Commercial Programs at Sable Offshore Corporation (Sable), where you will reportedly oversee their Washington, D.C., policy office. Your new role, considering your prior close relationship with Sable while serving as a White House Senior Policy Adviser for Oil and Gas, raises serious questions about your compliance with federal ethics laws, compounding the many existing legal issues with the federal government’s unilateral grant of approval of pipeline rights to Sable. To understand whether your transition directly from the White House and Department of Interior to Sable – including your work on Administration policies before you left office and at Sable on matters related to your role on the NEDC after your separation – complies with the federal ethics laws, we seek detailed information regarding your interactions with the company during your government service, as well as documents and communications about your recent hiring by and employment with the company.

During your tenure at NEDC, you and others made several statements suggesting that you were instrumental to the White House’s efforts to advance Sable’s pipeline in California by utilizing the Defense Production Act to override California’s objections to the pipeline. For instance, at a June 2026 press conference, Sable Chief Executive Officer Jim Flores reportedly thanked you personally for helping restart the company’s oil production, and you thanked Sable for “trusting the Trump Administration.” According to your own LinkedIn posts, you also visited Sable’s operations on at least two occasions and, while still in your role as a government official, you even appeared in photographs wearing Sable-branded merchandise. After Department of Energy Secretary Chris Wright signed a secretarial order directing Sable to open its Santa Ynez Unit pipeline, you posted online “[w]e are bringing more US production online ASAP us🛢️let’s go Sable Offshore Corp.” When announcing your departure from the White House, only days before beginning work at Sable, you referred to yourself as a “deal closer,” while a White House colleague praised you for “never [giving] up on Sable Offshore Corp.” These public statements leave the distinct impression that you were closely working on the Sable deal at a time when you could leverage the work you did advancing Sable’s business interests to secure private employment or other financial benefits from the very company you supported as a government official. To move from a high-level government office to its direct beneficiary, especially for the purpose of personal gain, is both ethically improper and potentially unlawful.

As you must know, federal ethics laws and regulations restrict certain conduct by current and former executive branch employees. In particular, federal law prohibits any government employees from participating in any particular government matter, including permitting decisions, contracts, and other matters involving the interests of named parties, in which a company with whom they are seeking or negotiating for future employment has a financial interest. After an employee leaves government, they are permanently restricted from communicating to or appearing before the federal government on behalf of any other person concerning any particular matters involving specific parties in which a former employee participated “personally and substantially” while serving in government. Additionally, ethics laws impose a two-year restriction on representing private entities regarding specific matters that were pending under an employee’s “official responsibility” during their final year of federal service, as well as establish “cooling off” periods that prohibit senior officials from contacting high-ranking White House personnel to influence official actions, regardless of whether they worked on those matters previously.

Against this legal backdrop, your public involvement in matters affecting Sable and rapid transition from the White House to Sable raise serious questions regarding your compliance with federal ethics requirements governing impartiality, employment negotiations, recusals, and post-government employment. Sable’s conduct in recruiting and hiring you also may bear on the legality of their efforts to secure federal government approval of a dangerous oil pipeline project whose operation has run afoul of state laws and court orders.

We therefore request that you preserve all records and communications relating to Sable or any of their officers, employees, or agents, from March 1, 2025, to the present and continue preserving such materials on an ongoing basis. This preservation hold applies to all relevant records within your possession related to all communications with Sable, any person representing or purporting to be acting on behalf of Sable, or any consulting firms associated with Sable. This includes, but is not limited to, records and communications via email, whether official or personal; mobile devices; encrypted or disappearing messaging applications; social media; calendar entries; meeting notes; and voicemail and text messages. To the extent that you use any autodelete functions, you should immediately suspend auto-delete functions and notify persons with control over potentially relevant records of similar preservation obligations.

Given your reported involvement with Sable during your tenure at NDEC, please provide written responses to the following questions, including requested documents and communications, by October 21, 2026:

What role did you play in efforts to restart Sable’s project during your time in government, and what actions did you take to assist Sable? Please provide detail about your role, titles, and a complete timeline of communications between yourself, Sable, or any person affiliated with Sable.

What matters relating to Sable fell within your responsibility as NEDC’s Senior Policy Adviser for Oil and Gas?

Did anyone at the White House, NEDC, or any federal agency discuss with you your obligations under applicable ethics laws, regulations, and policies at any point in your tenure? If so, identify each person involved and please describe what was communicated and when did those communications begin?

When did you first communicate with Sable or its representatives regarding potential employment? Please detail those communications and provide all related records.

Did you file a financial disclosure report, including a public report (OGE 278e) or confidential disclosure report (OGE 450)? If so, please provide the last copy of the report that you filed with any agency of the United States including the Executive Office of the President or the Department of the Interior.

title: Senator Schmitt Leads Bipartisan Effort to Protect Broadband Infrastructure from Theft and Vandalism
text:
Schmitt’s Bill Would Strengthen Federal Protections for Copper, Fiber, and Coaxial Cables

U.S. SENATE — U.S. Senators Eric Schmitt (R-MO) and Alex Padilla (D-CA) introduced the “Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act,” bipartisan legislation to combat the growing problem of theft and vandalism targeting broadband and telecommunications infrastructure. The bill would strengthen federal protections for privately owned broadband networks and make the willful or malicious theft, destruction, or damage of copper, fiber, and coaxial cables used to provide telecommunications and broadband internet services a federal criminal offense.

“Missouri families and businesses rely on broadband every day, and when critical infrastructure is vandalized or stolen, they are the ones who ultimately pay the price through service disruptions and higher costs. My bill gives law enforcement another tool to protect the infrastructure that keeps communities connected and holds those who deliberately damage these networks accountable,” said Senator Schmitt.

The “Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act” would amend Section 1362 of Title 18 of the United States Code, which currently provides federal protections for certain communications facilities. Schmitt’s legislation would expand those protections to include facilities used to provide broadband internet access services and facilities operated by private entities.

The “Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act” Would:

Protect broadband infrastructure: Explicitly include copper, fiber, and coaxial cables used to provide telecommunications and broadband internet access services within the federal statute.

Cover privately owned networks: Extend federal protections to facilities operated by private entities, including privately owned broadband networks.

Criminalize theft and vandalism: Prohibit the willful or malicious injury, destruction, or theft of covered copper, fiber, and coaxial cables, as well as attempts or conspiracies to commit those offenses.

Establish penalties: Violations would be punishable by a fine, imprisonment for up to 10 years, or both.

Protect lawful activities: The legislation maintains protections for certain lawful concerted activities and excludes customer premises equipment from the new cable provisions.

Protecting Missouri’s Broadband Infrastructure:

Missouri has experienced multiple incidents of copper theft and vandalism at critical communications sites. Such vandalism can disrupt essential internet service and result in costly repairs that are often ultimately borne by consumers through higher service costs.

According to a recent industry report, at least 5,770 incidents of targeted theft and vandalism against communications networks were reported in 2024, disrupting internet service for more than 1.5 million Americans and causing millions of dollars in damage.

Missouri’s predominant broadband providers, Spectrum/Charter and Xfinity/Comcast, have been actively supporting efforts to strengthen federal protections against broadband infrastructure vandalism.

Read the text of the bill HERE.

Statements of support:

“We applaud Sens. Schmitt and Padilla for introducing the Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act, building important bipartisan, bicameral momentum to address the growing threat of vandalism to our nation’s critical communications infrastructure. These networks are essential to public safety, national security, and daily life, yet increasing copper theft and intentional damage are disrupting emergency services, harming communities, and leaving consumers without vital connectivity. Strengthening federal law with tougher deterrents and penalties will help protect these critical networks and the millions of Americans who rely on them every day.” —NCTA, The Internet & Television Association

“We’re grateful to Senators Schmitt and Padilla for stepping up to protect the critical communications networks Americans rely on every day. The Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act takes meaningful action to update federal law to ensure all networks are protected.” —Spectrum

“We appreciate the leadership of Senators Schmitt and Padilla in introducing the Combating Critical Infrastructure Vandalism Act. America’s broadband networks are the backbone of our small businesses, hospitals, schools, and homes, and this legislation is an important step to securing them.” — Elad Nafshi, Chief Network Officer, Comcast.

title: Sen. Tim Scott introduces legislation to encourage investment in new nuclear facilities, bring manufacturing back to U.S.
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) introduced the Opportunities for Nuclear Energy Investment Act, which is designed to encourage investment into the construction of new nuclear facilities and bring grid equipment manufacturing back to the United States.

“American energy dominance requires more nuclear facilities and a modernized energy grid,” said Sen. Scott. “The Opportunities for Nuclear Energy Investment Act would create jobs, strengthen American manufacturing, and unleash American energy by encouraging private investment in new nuclear facilities. Keeping production at current levels would leave our country dependent on foreign energy sources, but by expanding nuclear energy here at home, America can power our future and pave our own way forward.”

The Working Families Tax Cuts established bonus tax incentives for nuclear energy, but they only applied to the production of nuclear energy and not to investments in new facilities. The Opportunities for Nuclear Energy Investment Act would address this imbalance by expanding the 10% bonus credit for nuclear energy production to include the building of nuclear facilities under Section 48E (48E), also allowing for non-metropolitan areas to qualify.

In addition, the legislation would expand the 45X Advanced Manufacturing Tax Credit to include distribution transformers and larger power transformers manufactured in the U.S. to speed up grid modernization efforts. These transformers are necessary to deliver electricity to homes and businesses. Currently, both transformers are backlogged by approximately two years.

Background:

“Nuclear communities” represent areas where unemployment is above the national average and 0.17% of employment comes from legacy energy sources.

Under this bill, construction jobs to build a new nuclear facility would count toward the 0.17% employment requirement to qualify for the 10% bonus credit.

South Carolina is a top U.S. nuclear power producer and serves as home to four major facilities:

Catawba Nuclear Station

Oconee Nuclear Station

H.B. Robinson Nuclear Plant

Virgil C. Summer Nuclear Station

President Trump has called for 10 new nuclear facilities to be built within the decade and, to reach that goal, the nuclear community must be expanded.

Endorsements:

“The Palmetto Nuclear Coalition applauds Senator Scott’s leadership in advancing legislation to support investment in the next generation of nuclear energy,” said Ethel Bunch, founder, Palmetto Nuclear Coalition. “South Carolina has the workforce, infrastructure, and experience to lead this effort. Expanding energy community eligibility would help build on those strengths and attract new nuclear investment and jobs to our state. We appreciate the opportunity to work with Senator Scott’s office on this legislation and look forward to supporting its passage.”

“Transformers are critical to meeting our nation’s rising demand for electricity and ensuring a safe, reliable, and resilient electric grid,” said Will Hupman, senior vice president for government affairs, National Electric Manufacturers Association (NEMA). “NEMA thanks Senator Scott for his leadership in including critical support for domestic transformer manufacturing in the Opportunities for Nuclear Energy Investment Act. This legislation ensures American-made transformers qualify for the 45X tax credit, strengthening domestic manufacturing while mitigating persistent supply chain challenges for distribution transformers. This approach will drive continued investment in U.S. production of critical electrical equipment needed to modernize our nation’s infrastructure to meet today’s growing demand.”

Chris Colbert, chairman and CEO, Elementl Power, said, “We strongly support Senator Scott’s legislation to address critical gaps in the current energy tax credit framework. By extending the nuclear communities bonus to the investment tax credit, this bill builds on Representative Newhouse’s legislation from last year and will help accelerate the deployment of new nuclear plants to meet our country’s growing power demands, unlocking investment, job creation, and local economic growth in communities that have long supported America’s energy leadership. We look forward to working with Senator Scott and his Finance Committee colleagues to advance these necessary changes to section 48E.”

Kodwo Ghartey-Tagoe, executive vice president and chief executive officer, Duke Energy Carolinas, said, “Nuclear energy has helped power the Carolinas for generations. As more families and businesses choose to call the Carolinas home, always-on nuclear energy remains an important option for meeting our region’s growing energy needs while helping keep costs as low as possible for customers. We applaud Senator Scott’s leadership on policies that support potential new nuclear projects and a strong nuclear energy future.”

“Meeting America’s growing energy needs will require investment across the energy ecosystem and the infrastructure that supports it. Eaton is investing $340 million in Jonesville, South Carolina to create 700 new jobs and help solve one of the grid’s most urgent challenges: manufacturing distribution transformers. Policies supporting energy infrastructure investment and domestic manufacturing can accelerate grid modernization and ensure reliable power for homes, businesses, and critical industries. We appreciate Senator Scott’s leadership in advancing policies to help build a stronger, more resilient energy system,” said Mike Yelton, president, electrical sector, Americas, Eaton.

The full text of the bill is available here.

title: Shaheen Applauds Senate Passage of Bipartisan Resolution to Establish October 7 as Energy Efficiency Day
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) applauded the unanimous Senate passage of her bipartisan resolution to designate today, October 7, 2026, as Energy Efficiency Day. Amid ongoing attacks by the Trump Administration on energy efficiency initiatives that lower costs, this resolution celebrates and promotes the economic and environmental benefits gained from investing in energy efficiency.

“Energy efficiency is one of the most effective tools we have to help Granite State families save money, support good-paying jobs and build a cleaner energy future,” said Senator Shaheen. “With diesel prices at historic highs and energy costs rising as a direct result of the President’s war in Iran, I’m proud to continue fighting to protect energy efficiency initiatives and am pleased the Senate came together to pass this bipartisan resolution recognizing Energy Efficiency Day and reaffirming its importance.”
